docs.title: MOTCO
docs.text: Multi-omics Trajectory Comparison — a Python package for building latent spaces from multi-omics data and testing whether two groups follow different molecular trajectories in those spaces.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
To analyse your own data, use motco analyze or motco.analysis.analyze_trajectories (Real-Data Analysis). It runs the measurement the simulation studies validated, in one step: pooled standardization, a stage-supervised PLS-DA latent space with the double-CV rank, delta / angle / shape with the net-displacement orientation estimator, and RRPP p-values.

  • Measurement visibility — which group differences the stage-supervised PLS measurement can see, and the tests for those it cannot
  • Scientific roadmap — what is established, what is not, and what comes next
  • End-to-end example notebook
  • GitHub repository

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install motco
# or with uv:
uv add motco

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Module Purpose Real-Data Analysis analyze_trajectories: the validated pipeline on your own blocks, metadata and covariates, with its record and artifact PLS-DA Supervised latent spaces via double cross-validated PLS discriminant analysis, including sparse stage-PLS SNF Fuse multiple omics layers into a single similarity network Trajectory Analysis Estimate and test differences in trajectory magnitude, orientation and shape; the split interaction test and the per-feature interaction scan Orientation Driver Attribution Explain shared-PLS trajectory orientation differences with signed feature, module and pathway effects Simulations The numpy semi-synthetic generator (no R at runtime), the evaluation harness and the declarative power study CLI motco plsr, motco snf, motco simulate, motco de, motco analyze

docs.title: What the stage-supervised measurement can see
docs.text:
MOTCO's production measurement fits one PLS-DA to the stage label on both groups pooled, chooses its rank by double cross-validation (floor 2), and measures delta, angle and shape on the group × stage means of the latent scores. This page states which group differences that measurement can see, why a rotation of the stage program onto other features can vanish from it, and what a non-rejection therefore means. Each claim links to the study that measured it.

The latent space defines the question. A space fitted to the stages with both groups pooled asks: does each group traverse the shared stage program the same way? Its blindness to other differences is the scope of that question, not a defect of the tests. A different question needs a different space.

docs.title: The span principle
docs.text:
The latent scores are a linear map of the standardized features, t = (x − x̄) R / s, with R the fitted rotations (one column per component). A mean difference d between the groups moves the latent stage means by dᵀR. Any part of d orthogonal to the span of R moves them by nothing. The measurement sees a group difference only through its component inside the fitted basis's span.

The basis is fitted to separate the stages, both groups pooled, so its span is built from the pooled stage means. At rank K − 1 with balanced cells it is close to the span of the centred pooled stage means. The plasmode diagnostic measured this on the SEA-AD export: the pooled stage displacement keeps 99.94 % of its norm inside the rank-5 span (plasmode report, §4).

docs.title: Why an equal-length rotation cancels: the rhombus
docs.text:
Take two stages. Group A's step is a and group B's step is b, of equal length ‖a‖ = ‖b‖ but along different features: B's stage program has been rotated onto other features, which is what the orientation surgery does when it relocates stage-changing CpGs. The pooled step is (a + b)/2, the group difference is b − a, and

(a + b) · (b − a) = ‖b‖² − ‖a‖² = 0.

These are the two diagonals of a rhombus, which are perpendicular. A basis built from the pooled step contains a + b and is orthogonal to b − a: in it, both groups' steps project onto the same vector, so the latent angle is 0 and the rotation has cancelled.

Three or more stages need a stronger condition. With steps a_s and b_s, the difference at one stage must be orthogonal to the pooled step of every stage:

(a_t + b_t) · (b_s − a_s) = (b_t · b_s − a_t · a_s) + (a_t · b_s − b_t · a_s) = 0  for all s, t.

The cancellation is exact when B's steps keep the lengths and mutual angles of A's (the first bracket is 0) and are orthogonal to every one of A's steps (the second is 0): B's program has moved onto features A's program does not use, which is what a relocation does. A rotation within A's own features does not satisfy it and is partly or wholly visible. The stage-span rotation, made in the plane of A's own configuration, is the wholly visible case: it keeps 0.85–0.97 of its energy in the span (see the pilot table below). The latent-space comparison's alignment axis (span_alignment) moves one rotation continuously between these two cases at a fixed intended geometry (Simulations).

The repository has measured the consequence three times:

  • The orientation probe's Phase 5 latent angle at full relocation was 6.1°, against a population angle of 90° (orientation probe, §4; the test still rejected, because the anchor's latent angle was 0.3°).
  • The plasmode's sparse plant kept 2.2 % of its norm inside the rank-5 span, what a random direction keeps (√(5/10,000) = 2.24 %) (plasmode report, §4).
  • Orientation/angle power tracks the CV-selected rank rather than the effect size (design-guidance pilot, §3.2 and §3.4).

docs.title: Which differences are visible
docs.text:
A difference is visible when it lies inside the span, which means it re-weights the stage program both groups share:

  • Scaling the program (magnitude): B's stage steps are a multiple of A's, so the difference is parallel to the pooled steps and lies in the span. This is why delta is the well-powered component in every operating study.
  • Rotating or bending the program inside its own span: the stage-span construction (below) makes exactly these edits, and the measurement recovers them in the target statistic.
  • A constant offset (translation) is invisible to all three statistics by design. It moves the group main effect, which MOTCO does not test, so it is the negative control.

A difference whose direction is orthogonal to the span is not visible, however large.

Blindness is a direction, not a set of features. The question is where the difference vector points relative to the span, not which features it touches. The same features can carry both kinds of difference:

  • Re-weighting stage-program features along the program is visible.
  • Moving them in a direction orthogonal to it is not.
  • A difference on features the program does not use is visible to the extent its direction correlates with the span, which for an unrelated feature set is about the random share. A direction on a few such features keeps several times that share, because the sample scaler rescales them, and is still not detected (see the visibility profiles below).

The three measured cases are all orthogonal directions. The relocation of stage-changing sites (the orientation and shape surgeries) points B's steps away from A's, and the rhombus places the difference outside the pooled span. A sparse plant on a few random features (the plasmode) points in an effectively random direction.

docs.title: The incidental routes, and their mixed signature
docs.text:
An out-of-span difference can still register when the measurement departs from the balanced rank-(K − 1) picture:

  • Rank above K − 1. When CV keeps more components, the extra ones follow within-stage covariance and can pick up part of the group difference. In the Phase 6 study the latent angle at full relocation was 32.1° at rank ≤ 3 and 76.0° at rank > 3, with angle power 0.082 against 0.506 (orientation probe, §1).
  • Unequal cell sizes. The pooled means are weighted by the cells, so the rhombus becomes a kite and the diagonals are no longer perpendicular. The SEA-AD table [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]] is such a design.
  • Unequal feature scales. Standardization rescales each feature by its pooled SD, so a relocation onto features of a different scale changes the steps' lengths.
  • Correlated noise. PLS weights tilt toward the noise covariance, so the span is not exactly that of the stage means.
  • Nonlinear units. Methylation enters as M-values and drives expression through the cascade, so relocated sites need not keep their step length.

Through these routes a rotation registers as a mix of delta, angle and shape, not as angle alone. In the design-guidance pilot, the orientation surgery at e = 1.0 moved delta (0.12–0.92) and shape (0.19–1.00) as well as angle (design-guidance pilot, §3.2).

docs.title: Score coordinates: the span is seen through a shear
docs.text:
The statistics are not measured on an orthonormal projection onto the span. They are measured in the PLS score coordinates that scikit-learn's transform returns:

T = X·R,   R = W·(PᵀW)⁻¹,

where W holds the weights and P the loadings. PᵀW is unit upper triangular, so R is W followed by a shear. The scores span the same subspace as an orthonormal basis of the weights, but the map is not an isometry of it. Lengths and angles inside the span are not preserved: two configurations equal in the standardized feature space are equal in score coordinates, but two of the same path length or shape need not stay so.

  • Size is unaffected. Under the null both groups share one population trajectory. Any linear map keeps two equal configurations equal, and RRPP permutes inside the same coordinates. The paper-grade anchors and translation controls read 0.002–0.062 against 0.0695 (stage-span paper grade, §5).
  • Specificity is affected. A difference that is pure in the standardized feature space can move the other statistics in score coordinates. A bend that keeps B's path length exactly can still lengthen or shorten it once the span is sheared, and so leak into delta.
  • The residual is measured. The paper-grade leak decomposition measured the bend at e = 0.5 under the planted scale, where B's population path length equals A's exactly. The table gives the median B − A path-length difference as a share of A's path, on the same population rows and through the same fitted basis.
column planted-scale coordinates orthonormal span PLS scores n = 200, two blocks −0.00 % +0.05 % +0.03 % n = 80, two blocks −0.00 % +0.11 % −0.02 % SEA-AD table, two blocks −0.00 % −0.01 % −0.48 % n = 200, three blocks −0.00 % +0.06 % +0.10 % n = 200, four stages −0.00 % +0.06 % −0.59 %

The residual is largest on the unequal SEA-AD table and at four stages. The rotation shows it more strongly: the 45° stage-span rotation on the SEA-AD table reads −3.35 % in scores against +0.66 % in the orthonormal span. At paper grade these residuals did not produce a delta leak (the bend's delta reads 0.016–0.036), but they are the one remaining route that the construction cannot remove.

docs.title: Orthonormal span coordinates: measured, not adopted
docs.text:
Orthonormal span coordinates measure on X_in·Q, with Q = qr(R) an orthonormal basis of the fitted span (equal to W up to column signs), rather than on the scores. delta, angle and shape are invariant to any orthogonal map, so every orthonormal basis of the span gives the same statistics and p-values.

MOTCO 0.19.0 offers them in the harness as the opt-in SimulationEvaluationParams.latent_coordinates = "orthonormal". The setting keeps the fit, rank and permutation draws. It is not available in motco analyze, in study configurations or with attribution. Without it every output is unchanged.

The 2026-11-09 validation measured both coordinate systems on the same units: the stage-span paper grade's 32,500 units and the weak design's 1,000 controls, with the same data, fit and draws, at 500 × 999. Its verdict is power_loss.

  • Size holds. The orthonormal coordinates read 0.000–0.066 at the 60 paper-grade controls and 0.010–0.050 at the weak design's 6, none above its bound.
  • The leak is removed. The watched cells are the 45° rotation's off-target shape: 0.070 → 0.000 at n = 200 and 0.086 → 0.000 at four stages (paired p ≤ 6e-11). The bend's planted-scale residual stays within 0.11 % of A's path, against −0.38 % and −0.60 % in scores on the SEA-AD table and at four stages. No off-target rate rises, and 1 of 90 is above the bound (6 are allowed).
  • Target power is lost. 19 of 45 target cells lose, 16 of them beyond the Bonferroni ceiling. All of them are at n = 80, on the SEA-AD table and at four stages, except two at n = 200. The largest losses:
  • the SEA-AD table's 45° rotation, angle 0.962 → 0.760;
  • the 22.5° rotation at four stages, 0.744 → 0.519;
  • the e = 0.25 bend at n = 80, shape 0.724 → 0.518;
  • the e = 0.1 magnitude on the SEA-AD table, delta 0.542 → 0.416.

The three-block column loses nothing. - Why the scores have more power is open. The scores do not see a larger target orientation or shape: the population angle and shape are equal in both coordinate systems. They do stretch a planted magnitude by up to 5 %. Where the orthonormal coordinates lose, their angle null is wider: at the SEA-AD anchor the 95th percentile is 34.6° against 26.1°.

Production and motco analyze stay on score coordinates. The scores' shear is a measured trade-off. It lets a 45° rotation leak into shape at up to 0.086, and it buys up to 0.23 of target power at small, unequal or four-stage designs. An off-target shape or delta rejection beside a strong angle or shape rejection can be the shear's.

Only an adopt_orthonormal verdict would have permitted a separate change to adopt orthonormal coordinates. This run did not return it (roadmap, item 15).

docs.title: Measurement spaces that keep the rotation, and what they cost
docs.text:
Every linear latent space is a projection of the standardized, concatenated features (concat). So it can only lose trajectory information relative to concat, never add it: a projection cannot see a difference concat does not contain. It can still have more power than concat, because it discards noise directions along with the differences it cannot see. In the orientation probe's Phase 6 design the shape construction at e = 1.0 was rejected on shape in 0.19 of replicates by pls_cv and in 0.00 by concat (orientation probe, §3). Choosing a space chooses which directions of difference count, and how much noise is measured with them.

The orientation probe crossed five measurement spaces on matched datasets (orientation probe, §3–§6). At full relocation the population angle is 90°:

space Phase 6 latent angle Phase 5 latent angle cost recorded by the probe pls_cv (production, net displacement) 56.7° 6.1° — pca at rank 2(K − 1) (label-free) 90.5° 90.2° Phase 6 shape power 0.19 → 0.00; angle leaks into the shape cell (0.39 under PC1) pls_within_group (two-sided, fixed basis) 90.3° 90.2° invalid without a refit per permutation: anchor angle 0.48–0.88; a refit multiplies the cost by the permutation count

The label-free and two-sided spaces keep the full rotation because their bases are not built only from the pooled stage means. Neither replaces the production space: pca loses the shape test at small n, and the two-sided basis needs a refit inside every permutation to be valid. The stage-PLS space stays the production measurement.

docs.title: Measuring visibility: span capture and the stage-span construction
docs.text:
Two opt-in tools of the simulation harness (0.15.0) measure visibility directly:

  • span_capture (SimulationEvaluationParams(span_capture=True), study key evaluation.span_capture) records, for every replicate, the shares of the population group difference (group_difference) and of the pooled stage means (pooled_stage) inside the fitted basis's span, beside the random-direction share rank / n_features. It also records the population means measured through the fitted basis (population_latent). The shares are energy shares: for one direction, the plasmode's 2.2 % norm share is an energy share of 0.05 %, equal to its random reference 5/10,000. See Simulations.
  • The stage-span construction (construction="stage_span") plants group B's difference inside the span of B's own stage configuration: a scaling, a rotation in the configuration's own plane, a bend at fixed size and direction, or an offset along the progression. It is circular by design, because it plants where the measurement looks. It answers how sensitive the test is to a difference it can see, not how visible the surgeries are. See Simulations.

docs.title: What a non-rejection means
docs.text: A non-rejection of angle or shape means no detectable difference inside the stage-supervised span. It answers the space's question (whether the groups traverse the shared stage program the same way) and nothing wider. It does not mean the groups follow the same direction, or have the same shape, in feature space. A rotation of the stage program onto other features, or a sparse difference on features outside the program, can be large and leave every statistic at its null. The span-capture shares below are the evidence for each simulator construction. Report the selected rank beside any angle reading, as the real-data analysis record does. The split interaction test asks the wider question directly.

docs.title: Capture shares measured by the stage-span pilot
docs.text:
The 2026-11-04 pilot (report, 100 replicates per cell) measured every mode under both constructions. It ran at three stages on methylation + expression, at n = 200, n = 80 and the SEA-AD table. The table gives the median group_difference energy share. A random direction keeps rank / 498 = 0.004–0.006.

mode effects feature-set surgery stage-span construction magnitude 0.02–0.1 0.934–0.970 0.934–0.970 orientation 0.25, 0.5 0.002–0.008 0.924–0.971 orientation 1.0 0.004–0.006 (0.215 on the SEA-AD table) 0.849–0.946 shape 0.25–1.0 0.004–0.011 0.917–0.969 translation 0.25–1.0 null (constant over stages) null

The pooled stage means keep 0.93–0.97 under every construction.

  • The surgeries' orientation and shape plants are invisible. They sit at the random-direction share, so their low angle and shape power measures visibility, not the tests.
  • Given a visible difference, the tests are sensitive. The stage-span 45° rotation and half-step bend are rejected in 0.95–1.00 of replicates at n = 80 and above. The surgeries reach 0.06–0.40 at the same effects.
  • Through the fitted basis the stage-span rotation reads close to its intended value: 45° reads 43.7–45.3°. The surgery's full relocation reads 4.4–4.8° at the balanced columns, against a population 90°.
  • The only partial exception is the kite route. On the unequal SEA-AD table the full relocation keeps 21.5 % and reaches angle power 0.67, registering as a mix (delta 0.31, shape 0.52).

The retrofit check found that an edit made in a replicate's own fitted basis and pulled back to the features has cosine 0.965–0.984 with the population stage-span plant. A basis-defined plant and the population-defined one nearly coincide.

docs.title: Visibility profiles across alignment
docs.text:
The 2026-11-04 latent-space comparison (report, 100 replicates × 199 permutations per cell) measured five spaces on identical data. It moved a 45° stage-span rotation from inside the stage span (φ = 0) to orthogonal to it (φ = 90) at a fixed intended geometry (span_alignment). The designs had three stages on methylation + expression: n = 200 and the SEA-AD table at the generator's stage effect (δ = 2.0), and the SEA-AD table at a δ calibrated to SEA-AD's held-out stage AUROC (δ = 0.11, AUROC 0.617). The table gives the median group_difference capture and the angle rejection rate at φ = 0 / 30 / 60 / 90, at n = 200 and on the SEA-AD table.

space capture, n = 200 angle, n = 200 capture, SEA-AD angle, SEA-AD pls_cv (production) 0.97 / 0.82 / 0.40 / 0.008 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.79 / 0.08 0.93 / 0.79 / 0.41 / 0.026 0.96 / 0.73 / 0.43 / 0.11 pca_matched (PCA at the pls_cv rank) 0.97 / 0.85 / 0.22 / 0.006 0.89 / 0.79 / 0.26 / 0.05 0.93 / 0.83 / 0.45 / 0.032 0.72 / 0.54 / 0.10 / 0.06 pca_fixed (PCA at rank 4) 0.97 / 0.86 / 0.45 / 0.024 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.67 / 0.09 0.94 / 0.83 / 0.47 / 0.051 0.75 / 0.53 / 0.15 / 0.09 pls_residual_pca (pls_cv + 2 residual axes) 0.97 / 0.83 / 0.41 / 0.024 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.54 / 0.17 0.93 / 0.81 / 0.45 / 0.075 0.93 / 0.79 / 0.35 / 0.18 concat (all 498 features) 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 0.81 / 0.85 / 0.89 / 0.90
  • Every low-dimensional space has the same profile. Capture falls to the random-direction share at φ = 90, and so does angle power. Neither a label-free basis nor within-stage residual components recover an out-of-span rotation; only concat does.
  • Size holds in every space but one. The anchor and translation controls read at most 0.08 (bound 0.0936) in every space except concat. Its angle is liberal at the SEA-AD-like stage signal (0.21 and 0.22).
  • Extra directions cost in-span power. pls_residual_pca shares pls_cv's coordinates and adds two near-empty ones. Magnitude delta falls from 0.74 to 0.37 (n = 200) and from 0.23 to 0.07 (SEA-AD table), and a 22.5° in-span rotation's angle from 0.84 to 0.41. concat and pca_fixed lose as much. pca_matched at rank 2 misses the stage program altogether: its leading axes keep 0.53–0.54 of the pooled stage means, against pls_cv's 0.93–0.97.
  • Support at a fixed norm. A 20-feature out-of-span direction keeps 0.108 (n = 200) and 0.116 (SEA-AD table) of its energy in the pls_cv span, against 0.008 and 0.026 dense: differences +0.102 and +0.091, SE 0.002 and 0.003. Its angle power is the same: −0.02 against SEs of 0.036 and 0.042. So blindness is a matter of direction for detection, while capture depends somewhat on the support. Through concat the sparse rotation reads 32–34° against an intended 45°, which shows the sample scaler shrinking the 20 planted features.
  • At SEA-AD's stage signal the span is mostly noise. At δ = 0.11 the fitted stage-PLS span keeps 0.10 of the population stage program (rank 3, random share 0.006), and no space has power for any plant.

The advisory reading was document_tradeoff: no space gains on the out-of-span rotation without losing what the production space sees. The production stage-PLS space stays the measurement, and its question stays the one stated at the top of this page.

docs.title: Sensitivity given visibility at paper grade
docs.text:
The 2026-11-04 paper grade (report, 500 replicates × 999 permutations per cell) repeated the stage-span measurement under the planted scale (span_scale: "planted", which makes each edit exact where the sample scaler looks) at five columns. Its predeclared decision is sensitivity_established: size holds at every column, every stage-span plant keeps at least 0.90 of its energy in the fitted span, and the off-target rates stay within the bound rule.

Target power of the stage-span plants (angle for the rotation, shape for the bend, delta for the scaling), at the three effects of each mode:

column orientation, 9° / 22.5° / 45° shape, e = 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5 magnitude, e = 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.1 n = 200, two blocks 0.74 / 0.88 / 1.00 0.70 / 0.97 / 1.00 0.23 / 0.69 / 0.94 n = 80, two blocks 0.40 / 0.41 / 0.99 0.21 / 0.72 / 0.97 0.04 / 0.24 / 0.62 SEA-AD table, two blocks 0.38 / 0.38 / 0.96 0.21 / 0.68 / 0.97 0.06 / 0.19 / 0.54 n = 200, three blocks 0.98 / 1.00 / 1.00 0.91 / 1.00 / 1.00 0.43 / 0.88 / 0.99 n = 200, four stages 0.48 / 0.74 / 1.00 0.48 / 0.96 / 1.00 0.17 / 0.65 / 0.94
  • Capture. The plants keep 0.92–0.97 of their energy in the span (median per cell). Through the fitted basis the rotation reads its intended angle to within 1.3° (SEA-AD, 45° reads 43.7°).
  • The visibility contrast. At e = 0.5 the surgeries reach angle 0.11–0.49 and shape 0.08–0.67 at the same columns, keeping 0.2–0.8 % of their energy in the span (three-block surgery capture was not measured).
  • Remaining specificity. The rotation's shape rises with the angle: at n = 200 it reads 0.030 / 0.046 / 0.070 and at four stages 0.004 / 0.030 / 0.086, at or just above the 0.0695 per-cell bound at 45°. The bound rule allows these (3 of 90 rates above it, 6 allowed, none above the ceiling), but this is the cell to watch in any larger effect.
  • Excluded configurations. The planted fixed point has no solution when the configuration's two in-plane directions nearly tie. It failed for 12 of the 1,000 four-stage orientation units, which were reported as failures; those two cells read over 497 and 491 replicates.

docs.title: Which stage-supervised space: weighting and sparsity
docs.text:
The latent-space comparison kept the stage-PLS span as the production measurement. It also showed how little of the stage program that span keeps at SEA-AD's stage signal (0.10 at the weak design). Two opt-in settings change the fitted span without changing its stage objective:

  • Block weighting (block_weighting: equal_variance; API) multiplies each standardized block by 1/√p_b. Unweighted, a block's share of the joint variance, and so of every stage-PLS direction, grows with its feature count; weighted, each block has unit total variance. The fit then runs without per-feature rescaling, so delta is in the weighted metric. When the blocks have equal feature counts the weights are equal, and the only change is that sklearn no longer re-standardizes each CV fold.
  • Sparse stage-PLS (sparsity: {scope: block}; API) lets each component load on a budget of features per block, chosen with the rank by the same held-out AUROC. A budget can drop features that carry only noise, at the price of any stage signal they carry.

Neither setting can see outside the stage span; both can only change which stage-supervised span is fitted. The production latent-space selection (2026-11-10, report) compared them with production on matched units: the latent-space comparison's three designs and the SEA-AD plasmode export with a stage-span plant on real noise. Its predeclared decision is keep_production:

  • No gain where production has none. At the weak design every arm rejects at 0.01–0.07 and keeps 0.08–0.10 of the stage program at the anchor. On the plasmode plant the largest gain, sparse_block at e = 0.5 (delta 0.51 → 0.62), misses the Bonferroni threshold. weighted reads no_gain.
  • Size. Every arm holds size in simulation (0.00–0.06). On the plasmode anchor the sparse arms read delta 0.11, above the ceiling at 100 replicates, and production reads 0.11 on the same replicates. The decision counts it as size_excess for the sparse arms; the paper grade would have resolved it.
  • A gain at a strong stage signal. At δ = 2.0 every candidate rejects more often than production where production is below saturation: angle 0.46 → 0.90–1.00 for the SEA-AD table's 22.5° rotation. Production's CV picks rank 3 in those cells and the candidates rank 2, while every arm keeps 0.92–0.98 of the stage program. The gain follows the selected rank, not a better view of the program.

Both settings stay opt-in. A case study may declare block weighting as a sensitivity analysis, with delta in the weighted metric. Sparse stage-PLS costs seven to nine production fits and has shown no gain that would justify it.

docs.title: The measured dimension: fit rank against predictive subspace
docs.text:
The production statistics are computed in as many dimensions as the cross-validation selects components. The rank A does two jobs: it regularizes the stage fit, and it sets the dimension of the measurement. Dimensions beyond the stage program cost power on what the span sees:

  • ranks above K − 1 lose shape power at the Phase 5 design (rank ladder);
  • two near-empty added components halve magnitude delta (the latent-space comparison, 0.74 → 0.37 at n = 200);
  • the production selection's candidates gained where they chose rank 2 and production's CV chose 3.

The predictive subspace. The stage labels are one-hot, so the fit's Y loadings have rank K − 1 whatever A is, and the fitted stage labels move only along K − 1 directions of the score space: the row space of the Y loadings. Measuring there keeps the fit, the CV and the rank, and drops the score directions that do not move the fitted labels. At A ≤ K − 1 it is the score measurement. MOTCO 0.24.0 offers three coordinate systems on that subspace as an opt-in setting, in the harness and in motco.analysis (latent_coordinates; API, analysis):

  • predictive: the scores projected on the subspace;
  • predictive_orthonormal: the input coordinates on an orthonormal basis of it;
  • predictive_fitted: the fitted stage indicators.

Why a lower fit rank is not the same thing. Forcing the fit to K − 1 components truncates it, and the later components are what aim the K − 1 directions. In the predictive-subspace pilot (report §7) the forced rank-2 fit keeps 0.34–0.48 of the pooled stage program in the stage-effect band, against 0.73–0.88 for production and 0.67–0.87 for the predictive subspace. It loses the power the subspace gains: the n = 200 rotation at δ = 0.5 and e = 0.1 reads 0.11, against production's 0.06 and the predictive subspace's 0.94.

What the predictive subspace gives up.

  • What production sees through its extra components. The Phase 6 feature-set orientation surgery at e = 1.0 is read by production's extra components (group_difference capture 0.20 at a median rank of 4), and by the predictive subspace barely (capture 0.002). Production reads its angle at 0.66 and the predictive arms at 0.48–0.49.
  • The size of the difference in the band. At n = 200 and δ = 0.25 the predictive arms read a 45° rotation as 18–20° where the population reads 43–45° through the same map. At δ = 2.0 they agree within about 4°.

The pilot's verdict: keep_production. All three coordinate systems read size_excess.

  • Size fails on real noise. On the SEA-AD plasmode's anchor (500 permuted-label replicates, the case-study configuration) they reject delta at 0.13–0.136 and shape at 0.076–0.078, where production reads 0.042 and 0.026 on the same replicates. Size holds at every simulated design, the weak one included at 500 replicates.
  • No protected power is lost, and the gains are large. All three gain in 10 of the 18 δ = 2.0 target cells at the Bonferroni threshold: the SEA-AD table's 22.5° rotation goes from 0.41 to 1.00. In the stage-effect band, where the CV rank grows to 4–11 while the held-out AUROC stays at its ceiling, they gain in 29–30 of 36 target cells. On the plasmode's real-noise plant delta goes from 0.51 to 0.79–0.82 at e = 0.5.
  • Specificity depends on the metric. predictive adds to production's rotation-into-shape leak in the band, and predictive_fitted leaks at δ = 2.0. predictive_orthonormal passes both families and removes most of production's own band leak: 0.80 → 0.41 and 0.57 → 0.04 at n = 200, δ = 0.5.
  • The CV rank sits next to a leak. One more fit component turns the 45° rotation's off-target shape at δ = 2.0 from 0.03–0.04 into 0.92–0.99.

Production and motco analyze therefore measure in the fitted span's scores. The predictive values stay opt-in diagnostics and are not tests a case study should report. Only a paper grade after a propose_paper_grade verdict could adopt another measurement, and that needs the real-noise excess understood first.

docs.title: The real-noise size excess, diagnosed
docs.text:
A diagnosis re-read the pilot's 800 plasmode units with their labels and RRPP seeds (report). Its four reference arms reproduced the pilot's counts exactly. The guess under test: the two predictive directions of the rank-5 fit hold its in-sample stage fit (stage R² 0.84 against a held-out AUROC of 0.636), and the reduced model's residuals in them are not exchangeable across stages, which RRPP's draws assume. Two checks separate the parts of that guess:

  • Within-stage draws change the null and keep the coordinates. RRPP's residuals are permuted among the donors of each stage only. If the excess comes from mixing residuals across stages, it goes away.
  • Out-of-fold coordinates change the coordinates and keep the null. Each donor's fitted stage indicators come from a stage-PLS model fitted without that donor. If the excess needs coordinates fitted on the donors they measure, it goes away.

Verdict: both_restore. Each check alone brings the anchor rates within the size rule the pilot applied. Rejections in 500 anchor units for delta / angle / shape:

coordinates pilot (unrestricted draws) within-stage draws predictive 68 / 11 / 38 31 / 17 / 33 predictive_orthonormal 67 / 9 / 38 29 / 17 / 32 predictive_fitted 65 / 10 / 39 28 / 17 / 33 out-of-fold fitted indicators — 8 / 7 / 17 (unrestricted draws) production (pls_cv) 21 / 24 / 13 19 / 27 / 19

Three readings qualify the verdict:

  • shape holds by a small margin. The within-stage draws remove the whole delta excess, but little of the shape excess, which stays near the size bound and above production's rate.
  • The out-of-fold coordinates carry almost no stage signal. They hold size, but out of fold the stage fit explains about 2 % of the stage indicators' variance at the anchor.
  • Production gains under the same draws. On the real-noise plant, production under within-stage draws gains about as much delta power as the predictive coordinates keep. A comparison of measurement spaces therefore has to use the same null for both.

The predictive values stay opt-in diagnostics; the diagnosis validates no test. The verdict opens a separate change: within-stage draws as an opt-in option of RRPP, the harness and motco analyze, with their own size and power readings in simulation and on this anchor. Only that change's verdict could re-read predictive_orthonormal.

docs.title: Testing outside the span: the split interaction test
docs.text:
The production statistics cannot see a difference outside the fitted span, and no measurement space sees it without losing in-span power (above). The split interaction test (motco.stats.interaction.interaction_split_test; motco analyze --span-split-test) asks the out-of-span question without a space. It takes the group × stage interaction energy of the standardized features, in the fitted PLS model's input coordinates, and splits it exactly into three parts, each tested by a trace pseudo-F under Freedman–Lane permutation:

  • total: is there a group × stage difference anywhere in the measured features?
  • span: is there one inside the fitted span, where delta, angle and shape decompose it?
  • complement: is there one outside it, where they cannot see it?

The basis is the fitted stage-PLS span. It never sees the group labels and is never refitted, so its draws are RRPP's at the same seed.

"Span" means the fitted span, not the population stage program. At a strong stage signal the two nearly coincide: the fitted span keeps 0.90–0.97 of the pooled stage means. At a SEA-AD-like stage signal the fitted span keeps only 0.10 of the population program (comparison, §9). There a difference along the true program can fall outside the fitted span.

Reading the parts.

  • A complement rejection means the groups differ by stage with energy outside the fitted span. It does not mean one group uses a different molecular program. Part of an in-span difference can reach the complement: the 3–7 % of its energy the fitted span misses, plus what the sample scaler moves there. A 45° in-span rotation is rejected by the complement in 0.35 (n = 200) and 0.32 (SEA-AD table) of replicates. At a weak stage signal the complement also contains whatever the fitted span missed of the program.
  • A span rejection means the difference has energy inside the fitted span. There delta, angle and shape say how it differs; the span part only says that it does. It is less powerful than the targeted statistics: magnitude 0.56 against delta's 0.74, a half-step bend 0.72 against shape's 1.00 (n = 200).
  • A non-rejection of complement or total is uninformative unless power has been shown at the design and for the kind of difference. On the SEA-AD blocks, a planted difference on 20 of 10,000 features at 2–3 within-stage SDs is rejected by no part above the null rate (0.02–0.05), as by angle. An energy test spreads over every coordinate, so a sparse difference does not register.
  • The in-span share (span_share) is descriptive. It must be read against the share a null analysis gives at the same rank and design, never against 0. Components beyond K − 1 follow the total covariance, where the noise's interaction energy also sits. At the plasmode anchor (rank 5) the null share is 0.24; at a two-component span at n = 200 it is 0.006.

Why a ratio. RRPP permutes the reduced model's residuals, whose mean square is RSS/n, not RSS/(n − r). An energy statistic carries that shrinkage into its null, and summed over thousands of coordinates the null concentrates, so a few percent of scale becomes many null standard deviations. The pseudo-F computes its numerator and denominator from the same permuted residuals, so the scale cancels. At the plasmode anchor the uncorrected interaction SS rejects the null complement in 0.268 of replicates; the pseudo-F on the same draws rejects in 0.012.

What it does not provide. No geometry: the split test says whether and where the groups differ, never how. It does not replace delta, angle or shape, and it does not find sparse differences: the per-feature interaction scan does. A group-aware space refitted per permutation is roadmap item 16's remaining follow-up (roadmap).

Validation: split_validated (2026-11-05, report, 500 × 999 at the controls, 100 × 999 elsewhere, on the latent-space comparison's and the plasmode's own units):

  • Size holds on three simulated designs (the 18 control rates read 0.032–0.058, against a per-cell bound of 0.0695) and on the SEA-AD blocks at the case study's configuration (total 0.040, span 0.050, complement 0.012).
  • Out-of-span power. The complement rejects the 45° out-of-span rotation in 1.00 (n = 200) and 0.68 (SEA-AD table) of replicates, where angle reads 0.08 and 0.10.
  • Localization. As the rotation tilts out of the span, the span part falls (1.00 → 0.52) and the complement rises (0.35 → 1.00).
  • At SEA-AD's stage signal no part has power for any plant, and the complement holds size there (0.05–0.06), where concat's angle did not.

docs.title: Testing feature by feature: the interaction scan
docs.text:
Every test above pools the group difference over many dimensions: delta, angle and shape over the fitted span, the split test's parts over their coordinates. A difference confined to a few features does not register in any of them. The SEA-AD plasmode's 20-feature plant was rejected at the null rate by all six. The per-feature interaction scan (motco.stats.interaction.interaction_feature_scan; motco analyze --interaction-scan) tests the group × stage interaction of each standardized feature on its own:

  • Per feature, the interaction F with the covariate-adjusted full and reduced trajectory models, the effect RRPP and the split test test.
  • Globally, the permutation p-value of the largest F over the features.
  • Feature by feature, a Westfall–Young step-down max-T adjusted p-value, which controls the familywise error rate over all scanned features. A hit is a feature with adjusted p ≤ 0.05.

The draws are RRPP's Freedman–Lane draws at the analysis's seed, with its residual correction. The scan uses neither the latent space nor the bootstrap, so latent adjustment and attribution leave it unchanged.

Reading a hit. A hit says that this feature's covariate-adjusted group difference changes across stages, with the familywise error rate over all scanned features controlled at 0.05. The per-stage differences in interaction_scan.csv (the second group minus the first, at each declared stage, in standardized units) show how. A hit does not say that the feature drives a latent trajectory difference, and correlated neighbours of a differing feature can be hits too.

Reading a non-rejection. A scan without hits is uninformative unless power has been shown at the design and effect. At the plasmode's design (n = 80, six covariates, 10,000 features), a ramp to 2 within-stage SDs on 20 features is detected in 0.692 of replicates, and the median scan names one of the 20. A ramp to 3 SDs is detected in every replicate, and half the 20 are named.

Why the maximum, not the sum. The split test's complement sums interaction energy over thousands of coordinates, and the noise in that sum grows with their number, so a few features' energy is lost. A maximum pays only for the search: its threshold grows like the logarithm of the feature count. The scan therefore targets differences on few features, and the complement targets differences spread over many. The simulation shows the division (report, §6). The scan is weak where a difference spreads thinly: magnitude 0.09 against delta's 0.74, and a weak bend on the SEA-AD table 0.20 against shape's 0.70. With 498 features the search is cheap, so the scan also matches or beats the complement on a 45° out-of-span rotation (1.00 / 0.96 against 1.00 / 0.68). The complement still wins at half that rotation on the SEA-AD table (0.31 against 0.16).

The scan, attribution and the split test make different claims.

  • Attribution ranks features by their contribution to a latent difference that was already detected, and makes no error-rate claim.
  • The scan tests each feature's interaction directly, under familywise control, without a latent space. On the plasmode its 20 largest F hold 0.473 / 0.887 of the plant at 2 / 3 SDs, against attribution's 0.227 / 0.432. The plasmode's attribution verdict (attribution_leg_failed) is unchanged: the scan is a new test with its own predeclared rule, not a rescue of attribution's.
  • The split test says whether the groups differ by stage inside or outside the fitted span; the scan says on which features.

What it does not provide. No geometry: the scan names features whose stage pattern differs between the groups, never how the trajectories differ. It is not a driver analysis. Its F is the plain per-feature F, not a variance-moderated one. Its familywise threshold is common to all features, and on the SEA-AD export one block's null is heavier: ATAC gives 0.618 of the null maxima with half the features, so the threshold leans on ATAC. The by-block scan (below) gives each block its own share of the error.

Validation: scan_validated (2026-11-09, report, on the split-test validation's own units, which it reproduced exactly):

  • Size holds on three simulated designs (the six control rates read 0.048–0.058, against a per-cell bound of 0.0695) and on the SEA-AD blocks at the case study's configuration (0.042).
  • Familywise control. Under the plasmode's partial null, a feature outside the planted set is a hit in 0.042 of replicates at 2 and at 3 SDs.
  • Sparse gain. At 3 SDs the scan rejects in 1.000 of replicates, against 0.016–0.048 for delta, angle, shape and the three split parts on the same units. At 3 SDs, 0.995 of its hits are planted features.

docs.title: Scanning by block
docs.text:
One maximum over every feature lets the block that most often gives the largest null F set every block's bar. A block with many features, or with heavier-tailed noise, takes most of the familywise error, and a small block's features face a threshold set by the large block's search. The by-block scan (motco analyze --interaction-scan-by-block; API) runs the same step-down within each declared block, on the same draws, and tests each of the K blocks at 0.05/K.

Reading a by-block hit. The claim is the joint scan's: this feature's covariate-adjusted group difference changes across stages, with the familywise error over all scanned features controlled at 0.05. What changes is who carries the error. Each block gets 0.05/K whatever its size or noise, so each block has about the same chance of a false hit.

When to use it. When the blocks differ in size, or their noise is known to differ. With equal blocks it mostly moves detection from the heavier-tailed block to the other at the same total. Only K = 2 has been measured; with many small blocks each gets only 0.05/K.

Validation: by_block_validated (2026-11-10, report, on the interaction-scan validation's units, whose joint scan it reproduced exactly, plus an unequal export with RNA cut to 500 of its 5,000 features):

  • Size and familywise control hold. The six simulation controls read 0.046–0.058. On real noise the global rate reads 0.040 (SEA-AD export) and 0.044 (unequal export), and a feature outside the planted set is a hit in 0.040 and 0.044 of units.
  • The error is shared. At the unequal export's anchor the joint scan puts its false hits almost all in ATAC (0.052 of units against RNA's 0.004); by block they read 0.030 and 0.016.
  • No global power is lost, and the small block gains. On the unequal export the global rate at 2 SDs rises from 0.760 to 0.892. RNA recall rises from 0.069 to 0.158 (2 SDs) and from 0.570 to 0.755 (3 SDs), while ATAC's falls from 0.076 to 0.058 and from 0.575 to 0.500. On the SEA-AD export the two blocks' mean recall is unchanged (0.059 at 2 SDs).
  • Bonferroni costs little at K = 2. The block maxima are weakly correlated (median Spearman 0.18–0.20 on the exports), and a minP combination would have rejected at most 2 more units of 500.

The joint scan stays the default; the by-block combination is opt-in.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Develop MOTCO into a scientifically defensible workflow that can:

  1. detect whether groups follow different multivariate molecular trajectories;
  2. distinguish progression magnitude and orientation reliably;
  3. treat shape with an explicitly validated interpretation; and
  4. identify stable feature and pathway drivers after a global trajectory difference is detected.

The roadmap prioritizes interpretability and validation before larger simulations or additional integration methods. The evidence for each statement below is in its dated report under reports/; the measurement visibility page explains what the production measurement can and cannot see.

docs.title: Established
docs.text:
• Methylation is converted from B values to M values before standardization and PLS integration.
  • PLS is the production measurement space. One pooled, stage-supervised PLS-DA fit, its rank chosen by double cross-validation with a floor of 2 (item 4), and delta / angle / shape measured in its score coordinates. Block weighting and sparse stage-PLS (item 17, keep_production) and orthonormal span coordinates (item 15, power_loss) were measured against it and not adopted.
  • Magnitude is specific under the joint construction at paper grade: magnitude/delta 1.000 at the top effect, magnitude/angle 0.024 and magnitude/shape 0.000 (addendum).
  • Shape invariance is audited and corrected. Production shape removes translation, uniform scale and any orthogonal transformation; reflections are aligned away at every ambient dimension (unify-shape-reflection-policy, resolving audit finding F3).
  • Orientation is measured by net displacement, the harness and motco analyze default since 2026-10-15. It holds size at paper grade and raises orientation/angle power from 0.300 to 0.648 at the Phase 6 design and from 0.840 to 0.924 at Phase 5, removing the shape → angle leak (report).
  • Given a difference inside the stage-supervised span, the tests are sensitive: a 45° rotation and a half-step bend are rejected in 0.96–1.00 of replicates at five designs at 500 × 999 (item 13 (a), sensitivity_established).
  • Covariates in the trajectory model hold size at the Phase 6 design (item 2). At the case study's configuration (six covariate columns at n = 80) the Freedman–Lane null needs the opt-in df residual correction, which is validated (item 8, adopt_df).
  • Two tests cover what the span cannot see, each validated for size in simulation and on SEA-AD's real blocks: the split interaction test for differences outside the span (item 16, split_validated) and the per-feature interaction scan for sparse ones (scan_validated; by block, by_block_validated).
  • Covariate-adjusted orientation attribution is validated on semi-synthetic data at the case study's configuration (item 11, adjusted_attribution_validated).
  • A controlled inverse-PLS study showed that latent interventions reconstruct reproducibly into feature space, with round-trip errors near machine precision; a 45° latent orientation change reconstructed as about 42° in feature space with negligible magnitude change. Latent orientation differences are different relative combinations of stage-associated molecular patterns, usually dense loading-aligned feature changes.
  • SNF is not intrinsically unsuitable for integration, but its graph-spectral geometry is not naturally aligned with MOTCO's Euclidean path-length and angle statistics.

docs.title: Not yet established
docs.text:
• The feature-set surgeries are not geometrically pure, and the measurement barely sees them. Orientation's shape response (0.998 at paper grade) is construction-present cross-talk of a per-omic feature permutation, present within each omic block; its predeclared "projection-associated" label is refuted (diagnostic, §1 and §4), and the paper must not repeat that framing. The surgeries' orientation and shape plants keep only the random-direction share of their energy in the stage-supervised span (0.2–1.1 %), so their low power measures visibility, not sensitivity (stage-span pilot).
  • The Phase 5 orientation claim is PC1's, and it is conditional. Under PC1 at n = 1,200, ρ = 0, orientation angle power is 0.840 ± 0.016 at paper grade (report, §5); it straddles the 0.80 floor by eigengap tercile (0.754 / 0.886 / 0.880), and it saturates at 0.84–0.88 from e = 0.25, so the strictly monotone form of the power claim is unsupported. Under PC1 the angle null tracks its own observed statistic (slope 0.811) and is load-bearing rather than corrigible (report). Under net displacement the eigengap no longer gates orientation power at the Phase 6 design; the CV-selected rank does, and it replaces the eigengap as the covariate reported beside any angle result (case studies below).
  • Cross-replicate driver stability has no design that holds the driver set fixed, so it is not claimable.
  • Specificity of the other magnitude constructions. The former default all (methylation δ alone) moves angle (0.276) and shape (0.742) far past the control bound at paper grade. Its off-target response is the geometry of concatenating one block that grew with two that did not (diagnostic); joint is the remedy and the default since 2026-10-09, and the historical configs pin all. Specificity stays unestablished for all, extremes and shape_kind='magnitude', so a magnitude result must name its construction. The acceptance-target reader's default two-sided rule records joint's conservative controls as not met; the opt-in bound: "upper" agrees with the gate.
  • Power at the Phase 6 design (n = 80, three stages, two blocks). Only delta has useful power (0.542 at a 10 % joint size change, 0.956 at 25 %), and no statistic is mode-specific for orientation or shape (small-n report). Under net displacement orientation/angle reaches 0.648 at the construction maximum (0.280 when CV keeps three or fewer components, 0.996 above) and 0.084–0.178 at e ≤ 0.75, so a non-rejection of angle at n = 80 stays uninformative.
  • Limits of the span measurement. The statistics are measured in sheared PLS score coordinates, which leave a path-length residual for the planted bend at e = 0.5 (−0.48 % of A's path on the SEA-AD table, −0.59 % at four stages); orthonormal coordinates remove it but lose target power (item 15), so the scores stay. The rotation's off-target shape rises to the per-cell bound at 45° (0.070 at n = 200, 0.086 at four stages). How much of a real difference the span sees is not established (item 13 (b)).
  • Real-noise evidence rests on one export. Every real-noise size and power reading comes from SEA-AD astrocytes at 80 donors on 10,000 features, where the anchor's replicates share one fit and the only in-span plant is a magnitude edit along the in-sample stage means. It is a fair size gate. It gave item 18 its verdict; in item 17 the arms it stopped had no gain either, and production read the same rate on those 100 replicates. Item 19 traced item 18's excess on it to the in-sample fit read under RRPP's unrestricted draws (both_restore): either within-stage draws or out-of-fold coordinates remove it, so a fix is an opt-in within-stage null still to be validated (open item 1). It does not rank measurement spaces, and no reading shows that its rates transfer to ADNI or ROSMAP (open item 2).
  • No real-data trajectory difference has been detected. Neither case study rejects any statistic (below). At ADNI's design the non-rejections are measured to be uninformative (item 9); at SEA-AD's they are bracketed to be uninformative. Orientation-driver attribution has therefore not run on a real-data claim, and on SEA-AD's real blocks a planted orientation on 20 of 10,000 features is not detected at up to 3 within-stage SDs, because it lies almost entirely outside the stage-PLS span (item 12). Neither the split test nor the interaction scan rejects on SEA-AD; at its stage signal no part of the split test has power for any plant, so those non-rejections are uninformative too.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text: The original sequence ran from closing the baseline studies through the shape and construction audits, attribution, a medium pilot and the paper-grade study to a real-data case study, with SNF-native methods optional at the end.

docs.title: Phase 0 — Close and preserve the baseline
docs.text: Done 2026-08-05. The latent-space metric-compatibility and inverse-PLS studies are archived and their capability specifications are canonical. The production contract is recorded: pooled PLS-DA, M-value methylation, a fixed shared coordinate system and per-statistic interpretation boundaries. The July M-value/PLS pilot predates the corrected shape estimator and the realized-geometry diagnostics; it is kept unchanged as historical evidence.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Shape invariance
docs.text: Resolved 2026-08-04 (audit). Translation, uniform scaling and proper rotation have documented expected outputs enforced by tests. The reflection policy was revisited on 2026-09-03 (unify-shape-reflection-policy): reflections are aligned away at every ambient dimension, and mirror pairs score zero at full rank and above.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Orientation and shape constructions before integration
docs.text: Resolved 2026-08-05 (findings). Every study mode has a documented realized geometry before PLS, and evaluations record analytic population, standardized population, observed standardized and PLS-latent checkpoints. Orientation is pure in native methylation but mixed after the biological cascade; both shape constructions are free or mixed bends, not shape-specific interventions.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Orientation-driver attribution
docs.text: Implemented 2026-08-27 (add-orientation-driver-attribution; extended 2026-09-04 by align-orientation-attribution; API). One pooled preprocessing and PLS model stays fixed for both groups. Attribution reports the observed normalized feature contrast q_observed = d_B/‖d_B‖ − d_A/‖d_A‖, its PLS-reconstructed counterpart q_PLS and their residual, for adjacent transitions and for the signed principal orientations that decompose the principal-axis angle (with a relative-eigengap degeneracy flag). It adds bootstrap sign, rank and top-k stability within design strata, correlated-feature module and caller-supplied pathway summaries, and standardized and original-unit effects. Pooled VIP is context only. The exit gate, a reproducible driver report for a significant orientation result, is exercised in simulation from Phase 4 on and has never been exercised on a real-data claim (Phase 6).

docs.title: Phase 4 — Medium pilot
docs.text: HOLD 2026-08-27 (report; 1,900 units at 100 × 199, n = 300, four stages). All 18 Type I controls passed, magnitude delta was 1.00 and specific, and shape shape was 0.94–1.00 and monotone. Orientation angle reached 0.65 against the 0.80 floor with a flat curve. A sign-anchor defect was found and fixed but did not explain the shortfall (report). The pivotality study explained it: each replicate's angle critical value tracks its own observed angle, a load-bearing property rather than a defect. The configuration spectrum records, on every replicate, the eigengap that makes it resolvable, and the geometry audit set the preconditions for Phase 5. Two findings carry forward: driver reports must use the observed contrast, because the PLS reconstruction keeps about 6 % of it (captured-component top-20 precision 0.15 against 1.00 observed); and a space supervised on stage is sized for stage separation, not for the group orientation contrast.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Paper-grade operating-characteristic study
docs.text: Closed 2026-09-10 as a conditional pass (exit review). The design point is ρ = 0, n = 1,200, four stages, p_dmp 0.1 (design-point pilot), and the rank rule is stage-supervised double CV (latent-rank ladder, keep_cv). The paper-grade run (9,500 units at 500 × 999, 0 failures; report) met all three power diagonals and all 21 Type I checks and held the gate at HOLD on the two magnitude controls. The magnitude-construction diagnostic traced that to the methylation-only all surgery, and the joint re-measurement lifted the magnitude claim on 2026-10-08 (addendum; 4,500 units, gate PROCEED). Sample size and block count at three stages are measured at paper grade by the design-guidance slice (item 7).

docs.title: Phase 6 — Real-data case study
docs.text: Closed 2026-11-02 on a size-controlled null, with the attribution leg reported failed (exit review). The exit gate (collaborators trace each global trajectory claim to stable drivers and reproduce it from documented inputs) is recorded as not met as written. Reproduction is met; driver tracing is unexercised because neither case study has a claim, and the vacuous pass is refused. Covariate-adjusted attribution was then validated (item 11), but the plasmode on SEA-AD's real blocks did not detect a 20-feature planted orientation (item 12, attribution_leg_failed). Phase 6 is not reopened. The case studies are described below.

docs.title: Phase 7 — SNF-native trajectory methodology (optional)
docs.text: Deferred; the question is closed rather than pending (Phase 5 exit review, §5). It awaits a decision to define graph-native path-length and angle statistics, which is independent of the PLS workflow. Candidate work: group-stage states on one pooled fused graph; diffusion or resistance path length as a magnitude analogue; transition profiles or diffusion flows as an orientation analogue; normalized stage-by-stage diffusion-distance matrices as a configuration analogue; a permutation scheme that rebuilds or conditions on the graph without breaking exchangeability; and validation on controlled nonlinear manifolds. Exit gate: an SNF-specific statistic has a graph-native estimand, calibrated Type I error, controlled power and no claim of preserving feature-space Euclidean geometry.

docs.title: Case studies
docs.text:
SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus astrocytes, with microglia as a positive-control cell type, in Omnia-Lab-UC/sead_sexdiff. Donor-level RNA + ATAC pseudobulks (TMM log2-CPM, top 5,000 variable features per block, chrX/Y/M removed); sex is the group and ADNC is merged into three stages (Not AD + Low / Intermediate / High). The primary cohort has ≥ 30 nuclei (astrocytes n = 80: F 11/10/28, M 9/10/12); the ≥ 50-nuclei cohort is a sensitivity analysis. Six donor covariate columns, rank floor 2, --residual-correction df.

ADNI serum metabolomics in Omnia-Lab-UC/adni_sexdiff: sex × stage (CN / MCI / AD) on Biocrates p180 (133 features) and Nightingale NMR (165), n = 1,501 (F 237/310/125, M 223/448/158), five covariates (six design columns), 9,999 permutations.

How a case study runs MOTCO. Through motco analyze or motco.analysis.analyze_trajectories (API), pinned to the release that contains every option it uses. That entry point is the harness's production measurement on caller-supplied blocks (a regression test checks it against the harness on identical data); it defaults to net displacement, requires an explicit stage order and records the selected rank, null summary and spectrum. Do not assemble the analysis from motco plsr + motco de or from the stats primitives: they are a different pipeline, and the primitives and motco de default to PC1. Carry the structural-analogue limitation (InterSIM blocks, 498 measured features).

Binding interpretability statement at the SEA-AD design (small-n report; angle revised 2026-10-15 from the power comparison §7):

  • delta. A rejection is evidence that the trajectories differ; it is consistent with a size difference but does not exclude a direction or shape difference. A non-rejection argues only against size differences of about 25 % or more.
  • shape. A rejection is evidence that the trajectories differ, but not of which kind. A non-rejection is uninformative at n = 80.
  • angle. The angle between the groups' net displacement vectors (last stage mean − first stage mean) in the latent space, so it reads only the endpoint stages. A rejection is evidence that the groups' net directions of change differ: Type I is controlled (anchor 0.050), and the size, shape and location constructions stay within the bound (0.024–0.068). Translation sits at 0.058–0.068, near the bound, so a rejection alongside a location difference warrants care. A non-rejection is uninformative at n = 80.
  • Selected rank. The cohort's CV-selected PLS rank is the covariate reported beside any angle result.

Results to date.

  • SEA-AD. No statistic is rejected in any of the 44 analyses: the four primaries, twelve forced ranks, sixteen preprocessing variants, eight latent-adjustment arms and four donor exclusions (re-issued under df, MOTCO 0.13.0, 2026-10-31). The primaries' delta / angle / shape p-values: astrocyte cohort_30 (CV rank 5, AUROC 0.636) 0.501 / 0.449 / 0.331; astrocyte cohort_50 (rank 2) 0.628 / 0.242 / 0.514; microglia cohort_30 (rank 2) 0.705 / 0.456 / 0.991; microglia cohort_50 (rank 4) 0.834 / 0.291 / 0.644. The split test's complement, its one confirmatory part, is rejected in none of the 40 analyses that carry it (0.18.0, 2026-11-06; cohort_30 astrocyte p = 0.886, microglia 0.795). The interaction scan's global p-value, read at α = 0.05 under a multiplicity policy fixed before any real-label scan, rejects in neither cohort_30 primary (0.20.0, 2026-11-10; astrocyte 0.962, microglia 0.956), and no feature is a hit in any primary. The positive control fails on the primary basis in cohort_30 and holds on the latent_adjusted basis. The stage latent adjustment is inadmissible at this configuration (residualized_basis), so its angle and shape p-values are reported but not read.
  • ADNI. The primary selects CV rank 8 at a held-out stage AUROC of 0.600 and rejects nothing (delta p 0.112, angle 0.688, shape 0.711). Across the sensitivities only delta rejects, at forced rank 6 (0.047) and under the nmr_all_columns export (0.045); adni_sexdiff reads both as dependence on that arm's setting. At ADNI's design no statistic reaches the 0.80 power floor (item 9), so its non-rejections are uninformative.

docs.title: Cross-cutting engineering work
docs.text:
• Preserve fitted preprocessing, PLS model, component count, feature order and loadings as a versioned analysis artifact. motco analyze --out-dir writes result.json, latent scores, PLS loadings and latent stage means, records units, the feature-order signature and software versions, and pickles no estimator.
  • Record seeds, configurations, parameter signatures, software versions and failed replicates in every study.
  • Keep fast deterministic invariance tests separate from slow operating-characteristic studies, and keep CI coverage for core geometry invariants and study-config validation.
  • Prefer structured CSV/JSON outputs plus concise Markdown reports over findings that exist only in notebooks.
  • Keep public documentation synchronized with methodological decisions and archived OpenSpec findings.
  • Preprocessing scope boundary (decided 2026-10-16): a step belongs in MOTCO only if it touches the model or the permutation null. Normalization stays upstream: it is omic-specific, and when it is blind to the labels it changes what is measured, not the validity of the test. Label-blind feature filtering stays upstream; supervised filtering (by group or stage) would bias the null unless repeated inside every permutation, so MOTCO documents it as forbidden. Imputation stays upstream; the finite-values contract stays, and missing covariates are handled only by the explicit missing_covariates policy. Block weighting is the one preprocessing step that belongs in MOTCO (item 5).

docs.title: Explicitly deferred
docs.text:
• Expanding SNF use before graph-native metrics are defined
  • Reading the pooled orientation power figure as applicable at any eigengap
  • Claiming angle or shape specificity against the methylation-only all magnitude construction (its controls fail; the claim holds for joint only — addendum)
  • Interpreting pooled VIP scores as orientation drivers
  • Fitting separate, unaligned PLS spaces per group
  • Claiming that a latent-space reconstruction is a unique or causal molecular inverse
  • Optimizing performance before the statistic and construction contracts are settled
  • Reading a non-rejection at an unmeasured design or stage signal as evidence that trajectories agree

docs.title: Open
docs.text:
Each is its own change; none is owed by Phase 6 (exit review §8). Open items 1–5 concern the measurement space and are ordered by how confident the results to date make their payoff (ordered 2026-11-12); open items 6–12 are independent follow-ups in no order of priority. Here and under On hold, a bare "item N" is the Done list's number and "open item N" is this list's.

  1. The predictive subspace: K − 1 measured dimensions on the production fit (from item 17; run 2026-11-12 as predictive-subspace-coordinates, item 18; report): keep_production. Production uses the CV rank both to regularize the stage fit and as the number of dimensions it measures. The pilot measured three coordinate systems on the fit's predictive subspace (the row space of its Y loadings, K − 1 dimensions) against production on 9,600 matched units, under a decision fixed in advance.
    • Size fails on real noise. All three read size_excess: on the SEA-AD plasmode anchor (500 replicates) they reject delta at 0.13–0.136 and shape at 0.076–0.078, where production reads 0.042 and 0.026. Size holds at every simulated design, the weak one included at 500 × 999.
    • The gains are real on simulated noise. No protected power is lost. All three gain in 10 of the 18 δ = 2.0 target cells at the Bonferroni threshold (the SEA-AD table's 22.5° rotation 0.41 → 1.00) and in 29–30 of 36 band cells (n = 200, δ = 0.5, rotation e = 0.1: 0.06 → 0.94). On the plasmode plant delta goes from 0.51 to 0.79–0.82 at e = 0.5. The weak design does not move.
    • The metric decides specificity. predictive adds to production's band leak, and predictive_fitted leaks at δ = 2.0. predictive_orthonormal passes both families and removes most of production's own band leak.
    • What it gives up. The surgery cell's angle falls from 0.66 to 0.48 (group_difference capture 0.20 → 0.002). In the band the observed angle is about half the population's.
    • The CV rank sits next to a leak. One more component turns the δ = 2.0 rotation's off-target shape from 0.03–0.04 into 0.92–0.99.
    • A lower fit rank is the wrong lever. The forced K − 1 control keeps 0.34–0.48 of the stage program in the band, against 0.73–0.88 for production, and loses the gains.
    • The excess, diagnosed (2026-11-13, item 19; report): both_restore. Either repair alone brings the anchor within the pilot's size rule. Restricting RRPP's draws within stage removes the whole delta excess (68 → 31, 67 → 29, 65 → 28 of 500), but shape only falls from 38–39 to 32–33, one or two counts under the threshold. The out-of-fold fitted indicators read 8 / 7 / 17, with almost no stage signal out of fold. Under within-stage draws production gains about as much plant power (delta 0.51 → 0.63 at e = 0.5) as the predictive coordinates keep (0.64–0.66).
    • What remains open. The three values stay opt-in diagnostics. The excess is understood but not fixed. The fix the verdict opens is within-stage draws as an opt-in option of RRPP, the harness and motco analyze, byte-identical when unset. Its change reads their size and power on the pilot's simulated designs, the weak design and this anchor, shape included, and pairs every measurement space under the same draws. The question why no simulated design reproduces the excess stays with open item 2. The verdict is a veto from one design. The simulations show no gain at SEA-AD's stage signal, and the designs where the arms gain have no real-noise reading. ADNI's design is the one where production measures the most dimensions beyond K − 1 (rank 8 on the data, 19 in its simulation, against 2), and whether the arms gain or hold size there is unmeasured. Two things would reopen predictive_orthonormal, either with a rank rule for a fixed measured dimension: the within-stage option validated, or size held on an ADNI or ROSMAP anchor together with a gain at that design in simulation, under a rule that scopes admissibility by design and is declared before the reading.
  2. Real-noise readings on more than one cohort, and a latent plasmode (item 13 (b); widened 2026-11-12 after item 18). Every real-noise reading so far comes from one export, SEA-AD astrocytes at 80 donors on 10,000 features, and its anchor read size_excess in both selections run on it (items 17 and 18), though only item 18's verdict turned on it.
    • What the SEA-AD plasmode is fair for. A size gate. The labels are permuted within stage, so the null is exact; every space is fitted without the group label and sees the same donors, labels and draws; and the configuration is the case study's.
    • What it cannot carry.
      • It is one dataset at one design, the extreme one (125 features per donor). The anchor's replicates share one fit, so a rate there is conditional on that fit.
      • Its in-span plant is a magnitude edit along the in-sample stage means (item 17), which rewards any space built on those means. The only other real-noise plant is item 12's sparse 20-feature orientation, almost entirely outside the span. No in-span rotation or bend exists on real noise, so the plasmode cannot rank measurement spaces on power.
      • It reads only the global null, so specificity on real noise is unmeasured.
      • Production's df correction came out of a size failure at this configuration (items 7 (c) and 8). No candidate has had such a repair, so a candidate's failure there may call for its own correction.
    • Cohorts. ADNI and ROSMAP are the cohorts MOTCO was first intended for; SEA-AD came first because analyses were already under way on it. ADNI's export exists in adni_sexdiff (1,501 donors on 298 features, 0.2 features per donor). ROSMAP has no export yet; its blocks, staging and covariates are fixed when one is defined. Each cohort is read in place through a contract like SEA-AD's, with labels permuted within stage and no donor id or label vector committed.
    • What a large cohort adds. Subsampling donors within cells gives independent real-noise datasets at a chosen n (80, 200, 500), each with its own fit, where SEA-AD gives one. A held-out half gives reference stage means, so plants and the capture are defined against something other than the sample they are measured on.
    • Cells, per cohort. The anchor; magnitude, rotation and bend plants in the reference stage span; an out-of-span plant; and each plant's off-target statistics, the real-noise specificity reading.
    • The latent plasmode stays as first written: a stage-span plant on real noise with a split-sample basis, because real data has no population means, measuring how much of a real difference the span sees. ADNI's cells can be split (the smallest has 125 donors); SEA-AD's barely can (9).
    • First reading: the predictive subspace's size excess (item 18), diagnosed on the SEA-AD anchor as both_restore (item 19, 2026-11-13). On the SEA-AD export the stage fit is mostly in-sample (stage R² 0.84 against a held-out AUROC of 0.636, and an out-of-fold share of 0.02), and a two-component fit is conservative on the same anchor (0.014 / 0.020 / 0.010). The guess was that the two predictive directions of the rank-5 fit hold the in-sample fit, and that its residuals are not exchangeable across stages. Both checks confirmed it there: RRPP's draws restricted within stage, and the predictive coordinates fitted out of fold, each bring the anchor within the size rule. In the predictive coordinates the largest stage (40 donors) has the narrowest residual dispersion, the reverse of the scores (descriptive). The guess predicts an excess that shrinks as donors per feature grow and is absent on ADNI; reading that prediction is this item's.
    • A covariate-free lead (item 19, descriptive). Without the six covariates in the trajectory model, production's delta rejects 0.082 on the same anchor (df kept), above the bound. The case study runs with the covariates; whether the reading holds beyond one fit is unread.
    • Why it is second. It pays off whatever it finds. It replaces the weak design's simulated capture (0.10, item 14) with real-noise ones, and it is where open items 1 and 4 read size before they say anything about a case study.
  3. Bias-corrected trajectory estimates in the full feature space (sketched 2026-11-12). An out-of-span difference is detected by the split test's complement (item 16) but not measured: no fixed low-dimensional space holds it (item 14), and the sample geometry of concat carries noise in every dimension. delta and angle are functions of the Gram matrix of the LS-mean vectors. Under one row covariance Σ the sample Gram exceeds the population one by tr(Σ)·L(XᵀX)⁻¹Lᵀ in expectation, up to p / n_cell on each squared norm without covariates. The full model's residuals estimate tr(Σ) without bias, so the excess is subtracted in closed form, with no basis, no group-aware fit and no refit.
    • What it is for. Measurement, the payoff open item 5 seeks: an estimate of the angle and of the path-length difference in the full space or in the complement, with a bootstrap interval within design strata as attribution has. It is not a test. The permutation null carries the same excess, so rejection rates are not expected to change, and detection stays with the complement.
    • A check needing no cluster: on the latent-space comparison's φ cells, the corrected angle beside the uncorrected one, both against the population angle through concat (45.1° / 44.5° / 42.7° / 41.7° at φ = 0 / 30 / 60 / 90, n = 200); then its spread on the SEA-AD table and at the weak design, where a corrected squared norm can be negative.
    • Limits. The correction assumes one covariance for both groups; a per-group trace is the extension, and open item 8's generator field would test it. shape needs the corrected Gram to stay positive semi-definite. At 10,000 features on 80 donors the estimate may be too variable to report.
  4. Noise-aware stage supervision (sketched 2026-11-12). At SEA-AD's stage signal the fitted span keeps 0.10 of the pooled stage program (item 14), and neither weighting nor sparsity raises it (item 17: 0.098, 0.085 and 0.082). Both keep stage-PLS's objective, which maximizes covariance and so leans toward high-variance noise. Two group-blind, fixed alternatives account for the noise covariance:
    • Shrinkage LDA (sklearn's LinearDiscriminantAnalysis with Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage) whitens by the within-stage covariance and gives K − 1 directions with no rank to select. They estimate the same stage-discriminant subspace as open item 1's predictive subspace under another regularizer (covariance shrinkage in place of the PLS fit rank), so this arm can pair against open item 1's coordinates on its driver. Open item 1's coordinates exceeded size on the SEA-AD plasmode while holding it in simulation, so this arm's real-noise size has to be read too.
    • Residual-factor removal projects the leading principal components of the stage-residualized features out before the stage-PLS fit. It is the inverse of pls_residual_pca, which appended them, and the unknown-covariate analogue of the latent adjustment (item 3).
    • A pre-check needing no cluster, and the gate: each variant's pooled_stage capture at the weak design's anchor against production's 0.100. If the capture does not rise, the item closes there.
    • Costs to read if it does. LDA's coordinates are whitened, so delta is in another metric, as under weighting. Removing residual factors removes any group difference lying along them, so the split test and the scan keep reading the unadjusted features. InterSIM's noise may lack the structured factors real blocks have, so on real noise the question waits for open item 2's split-sample capture.
    • Why it is fourth. Two changes to the stage-supervised fit have already left the capture where it was.
  5. A group-aware space refitted per permutation (thread 2 of item 16; sketched 2026-11-09, unblocked by item 17's keep_production, so it pairs against pls_cv). The question is a group-stratified stage space: stage-PLS fitted per group and merged into one basis, so each group's own stage program is in the span and a group-specific direction (the φ = 90 rotation every pooled space is blind to) becomes measurable, not only detectable.
    • Why it must refit. The harness has the construction as the diagnostic pls_within_group (K − 1 components per group, stacked rotations orthonormalized by pivoted QR, pooled-centred projection). The orientation probe (2026-10-12) found it keeps the planted rotation (90.3° against 90°) but, fitted once on the real labels, inflates anchor angle to 0.48–0.88: the union span is chosen where each group's noise aligns with stage, and RRPP's draws never see the fitting step. Any basis fitted with group labels has this problem, so a valid version refits the basis inside every draw: Freedman–Lane on the reduced model's feature residuals with RRPP's serial draws (the split test's scheme), two stage-PLS fits per draw at a rank chosen label-blind from the pooled CV and shared by both groups, projection, then delta / angle / shape. At fixed rank a fit takes milliseconds, so 999 refits cost seconds.
    • The pilot, when proposed: five arms on the latent-space comparison's designs and cells (its φ ∈ {0, 30, 60, 90} cells were built for this): pls_cv, within_group_fixed (to show the size failure on these cells), within_group_refit (the candidate), cell_pls_refit (one PLS on the group × stage cells refitted per draw; one basis, no QR tolerance) and within_group_crossfit (added 2026-11-12). Read for size at anchor and translation, out-of-span power against the complement's 1.00 / 0.68, and in-span cost on magnitude delta (two added near-empty dimensions cost 0.74 → 0.37 at n = 200 in the comparison; the QR tolerance is a knob the null depends on).
    • The cross-fitted arm.
