The basis is fitted on half of each group × stage cell and the statistics are measured on the other half, in both directions, with the two p-values combined by a rule valid under dependence. A basis independent of the measured samples needs no refit, at the price of half the sample. It is a simulation arm only: SEA-AD's smallest cell has 9 donors.
    • The bar: match the complement at held size with no in-span loss beyond the comparison's 2-pooled-SE rule, else the complement stays the answer. Its payoff is measurement (a measured angle, group-specific attribution), not detection, which the complement already provides; at SEA-AD the pooled span keeps 0.10 of the stage program on 80 donors, so per-group bases on 40 are expected to add little on real data.
    • A cheap pre-check needing no cluster: the principal angles between the two per-group spans on null datasets, which measure how ill-conditioned the merged basis is.
    • Why it is fifth. The merged basis has up to twice the pooled rank, and item 14 measured what two added near-empty dimensions cost, so the in-span bar is the likely failure. Open item 3 seeks the same payoff without a basis and is read first.
  6. A moderated per-feature statistic for the interaction scan (from item 16).
  7. Reading the SEA-AD scan by block in sead_sexdiff (pinning 0.23.0).
  8. Group-specific dispersion (item 7 (b), change B): an opt-in generator field scaling group B's covariance and a null-only study, the covariance and correlation scaling rows of the originally planned simulation grid.
  9. The df correction's follow-ups (item 8): whether df becomes the motco analyze default, a change that would re-issue the identity fixtures; and measuring size on the cohort_50 tables (microglia n = 63, κ = 1.090), which is inferred today. Nothing rejects there, so no rejection depends on it.
  10. Defaulting the null-dispersion materiality rule (item 6). It is opt-in so the committed Phase 5 report/ keeps regenerating byte-identically; switching the default is a reporting change needing a recorded re-issue of the affected localization output.
  11. The committed toy fixture (examples/data/toy/, deferred from docs-sync-audit, 2026-09-04). It predates the numpy generator: its truth.json records intersim_metadata and omits n_stages, p_dmp and baseline_continuity, and the current motco simulate at the same seed produces a different dataset. The choice is to regenerate it so the tutorial exercises the shipped code path, or to keep it pinned as a historical artifact. Regenerating touches the example data, examples/motco_example.ipynb, the toy-dataset spec scenarios and tests/test_toy_dataset.py.
  12. Open measurement questions, each a possible change: why the score metric narrows the angle null at weak, unequal or four-stage designs (report §6–§7); a four-stage design where an out-of-span bend is defined (report §11); and concat's p-padding question, which no comparison has measured (concat remains the ceiling reference only).

docs.title: On hold
docs.text:
Measurement-space candidates considered on 2026-11-12 and not proposed. Each entry gives the reason it waits and what would reopen it.

  • A stricter rank rule for the CV (from item 17; open item 1 as first written). Lowering the fit rank removes the components that aim the stage directions. In the 2026-11-12 probe (not a result; openspec/changes/archive/2026-11-12-predictive-subspace-coordinates/notes.md) a one-standard-error rule selected production's rank on every anchor and target unit at δ = 2.0 and 1.0, because the best candidate's fold SE is exactly zero at the AUROC ceiling. An absolute tolerance of 0.01 gained angle only (0.45 → 0.78 on the SEA-AD table, beside delta 0.23 → 0.17 and shape 0.68 → 0.55). At δ = 0.25 and at the weak design the rules changed the rank and no rate. Reopen if open item 1's pilot qualifies an arm whose rank-plus-one reading puts the CV rank next to the leak: the rule to study then is the fit rank under a fixed measured dimension, not a lower measured rank. The 2026-11-12 pilot found that leak (one more component turns the δ = 2.0 rotation's off-target shape from 0.03–0.04 into 0.92–0.99), but no arm qualified (size_excess on real noise).
  • The between-block agreement term of multi-block sPLS-DA (DIABLO). It optimizes agreement between blocks, not stage discrimination (a non-goal of regularized-stage-pls), and the two changes to the stage fit measured so far gained nothing at a weak stage signal (item 17). Reopen if open item 4's pre-check shows that changing the fit can raise the capture.
  • Supervision on a continuous progression score instead of discrete stages. The generator has no continuous progression, and whether a case-study export carries such a score has not been checked. One-hot labels already span every stage contrast, so the only gain is the ordering within a stage. Reopen when a case study supplies the score.
  • mfa weighting and joint-scope sparsity (implemented in 0.21.0 and 0.22.0, never run). Their siblings read no_gain and size_excess in item 17, the capture rose under neither, and a sparse arm costs seven to nine production fits. Reopen as extra arms of another paired run if weighting or sparsity gains anywhere.
  • Label-free factor models (MOFA+, JIVE, AJIVE). A label-free basis follows variance, not the stage program or the group difference: PCA at the production rank kept 0.53 of the stage program and was blind at φ = 90 (item 14), and a factor model shares both limits. Reopen only as a source of nuisance factors for open item 4, if the latent plasmode shows that structured noise dominates.
  • Nonlinear maps (kernel PLS, autoencoders) and graph networks. A nonlinear map turns an additive offset between groups into an apparent interaction, so the translation control would fail, and the generator plants mean shifts in Gaussian noise, which gives them nothing to find. Reopen with a nonlinear or cell-level generator, kernel PLS first; graph networks wait on Phase 7's graph-native statistics.
  • Multi-block PLS and supervised feature screening. Not waiting but already covered: with block scaling, multi-block PLS is PLS on the weighted concatenation (block_weighting), and screening features by stage association is a hard-threshold form of the sparse stage-PLS measured in item 17.

docs.title: Done
docs.text:
Before the numbered list: the joint magnitude default (default-joint-magnitude-construction, 2026-10-09; the historical configs pin "all"); the opt-in one-sided acceptance bound bound: "upper" (one-sided-acceptance-targets, 2026-10-14); the paper-grade estimator comparison (net-displacement-power-comparison, 2026-10-14, adopt_net_displacement, report); and the net-displacement harness default (default-net-displacement-orientation, 2026-10-15; every committed config and historical diagnostic pins "pc1", and the stats primitives keep PC1 as their default).

  1. Phase 6 real-data case study in sead_sexdiff: run through motco analyze, re-issued under df (2026-10-31), with the split test (2026-11-06) and with the interaction scan (2026-11-10); nothing rejects (case studies above). ADNI runs in adni_sexdiff.
  2. Covariate-adjusted trajectories (covariate-adjusted-trajectories, 0.8.0, 2026-10-16; report): covariates_validated. Covariates enter the full and reduced models, LS means are evaluated at a recorded reference row, missing covariates error or are dropped complete-case, never imputed. Adjusted delta 0.040, angle 0.062, shape 0.034 against 0.0695; the unadjusted arm rejects shape at 0.364.
  3. Covariate-aware latent construction (covariate-aware-latent-construction, 0.9.0, 2026-10-20): Type I adopt_stage (report; group_stage exceeds on angle, 0.082) and power candidate_fails for both arms (report; stage gains orientation power but loses shape and small-magnitude power). --latent-adjustment stage is a sensitivity analysis only, and it is inadmissible at the case study's configuration (item 7 (c)).
  4. Rank floor (minimum-latent-rank, 0.10.0, 2026-10-23; report): adopt_floor at δ = 0.05 and 0.1. CV could select rank 1, where angle is 0° or 180° by construction with a two-point null; both SEA-AD cohorts had. The floor of 2 holds size and defines angle and shape; it does not make them powerful.
  5. Block weighting (block-weighting, 0.21.0): measured no_gain by item 17, stays opt-in. A case study may declare it as a sensitivity analysis, with delta in the weighted metric.
  6. Open (above, item 10).
  7. Design-guidance pilot (design-guidance-grid, 0.11.0, 2026-10-28; report), which replaces the originally planned simulation grid (47,200 units). (a) The paper-grade slice (design-guidance-paper-grade-slice, 0.12.0, 2026-10-29; report): size holds at every column; delta reaches 0.62 / 0.94 / 1.00 at e = 0.1 for n = 80 / 200 / 500 with two blocks, shape is monotone in n, e and blocks, and angle is governed by n and block count with a flat response in e; below δ = 2.0 the CV rank inflates and delta / shape lose their power. (b) Open (above, item 8). (c) The Type I check at the case study's configuration (2026-10-29, report): diagnose_configuration_excess, diagnosed on 2026-10-30 (report) as residual_df_shrinkage for the primary's delta and residualized_basis for the stage arm.
  8. Residual-df corrected permutation (residual-df-corrected-permutation, 0.13.0, 2026-10-30; report): adopt_df. The opt-in residual_correction (df | leverage) rescales the reduced residuals; both hold every reading, leverage shows no paired power gain, and df reads 0.029–0.058 pooled. Follow-ups are open (above, item 9).
  9. Operating characteristics at the ADNI design (2026-11-02, report): non_rejections_uninformative. Size holds; magnitude/delta reaches 0.530 at most and angle / shape stay at the null rate, at a CV rank at the cap of 19.
  10. Phase 6 exit review (2026-11-02, review): closed on a size-controlled null with the attribution leg withheld until items 11–12.
  11. Covariate-adjusted attribution (covariate-adjusted-attribution, 0.14.0, 2026-11-02; report): adjusted_attribution_validated. Attribution from covariate-adjusted cell means; adjusted contamination is within 0.005 of an oracle's, against 0.43 of the top-20 unadjusted.
  12. Plasmode demonstration (plasmode-attribution-demonstration, 2026-11-02; report): attribution_leg_failed. Size holds on SEA-AD's real blocks, but a 20-feature planted orientation is rejected by angle in 0.036 of units at the 3-SD cap; it keeps 2.2 % of its norm in the rank-5 span.
  13. Stage-span constructions (stage-span-constructions, 0.15.0, 2026-11-04; report): revise_construction; visibility, not sensitivity, limits the surgeries. (a) The paper grade (stage-span-paper-grade, 0.17.0, 2026-11-04; report): sensitivity_established for stage-span effects up to e = 0.5 under the planted scale (12 of 1,000 four-stage orientation units failed, the planted fixed point cycling). (b) Open (above, item 2). (c) Done as item 14.
  14. Latent-space comparison across alignment (latent-space-comparison, 0.16.0, 2026-11-04; report): document_tradeoff. Every low-dimensional space is blind at φ = 90; only concat sees it, and extra dimensions cost in-span power.
  15. Orthonormal span coordinates (orthonormal-span-coordinates, 0.19.0, 2026-11-09; report): power_loss. The shear's leak is removed, but 19 of 45 target cells lose power, so the scores stay and the setting is an opt-in diagnostic.
  16. Split interaction test (span-split-interaction-test, 0.18.0, 2026-11-05; report): split_validated; the complement rejects the out-of-span rotation in 1.00 / 0.68 against angle's 0.08 / 0.10. Applied to SEA-AD 2026-11-06. Thread 3, the per-feature interaction scan (interaction-feature-scan, 0.20.0, 2026-11-09; report): scan_validated; the plasmode plant every other test misses is rejected in 0.692 / 1.000 at 2 / 3 SDs. By block (interaction-scan-block-maxima, 0.23.0, 2026-11-10; report): by_block_validated; the joint scan stays the default. The scan was applied to SEA-AD on 2026-11-10. Thread 2 is open (above, item 5).
  17. Production latent-space selection (production-latent-space-selection, 2026-11-10, on 0.22.0; report): keep_production. weighted → no_gain; sparse_block and weighted_sparse_block → size_excess on the plasmode anchor's delta (0.11 against the ceiling 0.10, where production also reads 0.11). Both settings stay opt-in. The δ = 2.0 gains that follow the selected rank are open (above, item 1).
  18. Predictive-subspace coordinates (predictive-subspace-coordinates, 0.24.0, 2026-11-12; report): keep_production. All three coordinate systems read size_excess on the SEA-AD plasmode anchor (delta 0.13–0.136, shape 0.076–0.078, against production's 0.042 and 0.026), while holding size in simulation, losing no protected power and gaining strongly at δ = 2.0 and in the stage-effect band. They stay opt-in diagnostics (open item 1).
  19. Predictive-subspace size-excess diagnosis (predictive-size-excess-diagnosis, 2026-11-13, on 0.24.0, no package change; report): both_restore. On item 18's 800 plasmode units, with the reference arms reproducing its counts exactly, restricting RRPP's draws within stage brings every predictive coordinate system within the anchor's size rule: delta 0.130–0.136 → 0.056–0.062, but shape only 0.076–0.078 → 0.064–0.066. The out-of-fold fitted indicators do too (0.016 / 0.014 / 0.034), with almost no stage signal out of fold. The fix the verdict opens, within-stage draws as an opt-in option, needs its own size and power readings (open item 1); keep_production stands.

docs.title: Real-Data Trajectory Analysis
docs.text:
motco.analysis runs the measurement the simulation studies validated on your own data: pooled per-feature standardization, a stage-supervised PLS-DA latent space with the double-CV rank rule, delta / angle / shape between two groups in that space with the net-displacement orientation estimator, and RRPP p-values. analyze_trajectories is the Python entry point and motco analyze the command-line one; both write the same analysis artifact.

Use this entry point rather than assembling motco plsr + motco de by hand. Those commands are a different pipeline: they skip the M-value contract, choose the rank without the parsimony tie-break, measure angle with PC1 by default, and record neither the selected rank, the null summary nor the spectrum.

docs.title: Input contract
docs.text:
• Blocks. One or more named omic blocks, each a samples × features table with string feature names. Blocks are concatenated in the order you declare them, and every joint feature is named "{block}__{feature}". Rows must equal the metadata's sample ids in the same order; every block needs at least one feature and only finite values.
  • Units. Each block declares a unit transform: identity (the default) or beta_to_mvalue (the logit of methylation beta values; values must lie in the open interval (0, 1)). MOTCO does not normalize counts, filter features or impute values. Supply blocks in the continuous units you want measured, for example log-normalized pseudobulk expression. The record states each block's declared units.
  • Metadata. A sample-id column, a group column with exactly two labels and a stage column, all named by you. Every group × stage cell must be observed.

  • Stage order. Required and explicit. Net displacement runs from the first to the last declared stage, and shape, the spectrum and every table follow this order. Stage order is never inferred by sorting labels, because High < Intermediate < Low alphabetically. Group order is optional and defaults to the labels sorted as strings.

  • Covariates (optional). covariate_cols names metadata columns, in model order; see Covariates.

Violations raise TrajectoryAnalysisError (a ValueError) naming the block, labels or cell at fault.

docs.title: What is measured and recorded
docs.text:
The latent space is fitted once on all samples, with the rank chosen by double cross-validation (the modal rank across outer repeats, the smaller rank winning ties) from the candidate ranks at or above the rank floor, min_components=2 by default (CLI --min-components), so angle and shape are measured in a space of at least two dimensions. min_components=1 restores the unfloored 0.9.0 rule and reproduces every 0.9.0 record and table byte for byte; a floor below 1 is rejected before anything is fitted. The CV defaults are the ones the operating studies ran: cv2_splits=4, cv1_splits=3, n_repeats=5, max_components=20, random_state=1203, each clamped to what the smallest stage can support (max_components to at least the floor plus one; a sample that cannot satisfy the floor is an error naming the counts). forced_components fixes the rank and skips cross-validation for the dimensionality sensitivity analysis, ignoring the floor; the record then says component_selection: "forced".

record (written as result.json) holds:

Key Contents statistics, p_values delta, angle, shape and their RRPP p-values (shape is null with two stages) null_summary per statistic: retained draws, mean, sd, 50/90/95/99 % quantiles of the permutation null config_spectrum eigenspectrum of the latent stage-mean configuration, pooled and per group, plus the permutation eigengap summary latent selected_lv, component_selection, CV settings (min_components beside them when the floor is above 1, block_weighting when set, sparsity and selected_keep_fraction when set), cv_mean_auroc, feature counts, feature_order_signature sparsity only with sparse stage-PLS: the scope, the ladder, the selected keep fraction and, per component, the support size per block design group and ordered stage levels, cell sizes per group × stage, contrast, analysed sample count covariates only when covariates are declared: names, kinds, factor levels and reference levels, design columns, the LS-mean reference row, missing policy, dropped samples, coefficients per latent component blocks each block's name, feature count, transform and units block_weighting only with a block weighting: the kind and each block's name, fitted weight and feature count measurement orientation estimator, selected rank, the predictive-subspace coordinates and their measured dimension when set, permutations, seed, the residual correction when one was applied, runtime span_split only with the split interaction test: per part (total, span, complement) the dimension, interaction and residual sums of squares, degrees of freedom, pseudo-F and, with permutations, the pseudo-F and interaction-SS p-values; the in-span share, the residual correction, permutations, seed and draws_match_rrpp interaction_scan only with the per-feature interaction scan: feature and degenerate counts, df, the maximum F with its feature and block and, with permutations, the global p-value, the hits at adjusted p ≤ 0.05 (block, feature, F, adjusted p, by F), per block the hit count and the share of null maxima, and draws_match_rrpp; permutations, seed and residual correction. By block it also gives combination, n_blocks_tested and per block the maximum F with its feature and the block's own p-value params, software resolved parameters; MOTCO, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas and Python versions attribution the compact attribution record, or a not_requested marker

The selected rank sits beside the angle result because orientation is only interpretable relative to the space it was measured in. The null summary shows how wide the observed statistic's own null was, and the relative eigengap in the spectrum indicates whether a group's orientation is resolvable at all. The space sees a group difference only through its component inside the fitted span, so a non-rejection of angle or shape means no detectable difference inside the stage-supervised span, not the same direction or shape in feature space; see Measurement visibility.

The floor guarantees two dimensions, not a second axis with signal. Under the unfloored rule a weak stage signal makes every candidate rank tie near an AUROC of 0.5 and parsimony selects rank 1, where the two groups' orientations are parallel or antiparallel by construction, angle is 0° or 180°, its RRPP null is a two-point distribution, and collinear stage means carry no bend for shape; both SEA-AD cohorts selected rank 1. With the floor, when the stage signal supports one component the second is the best of the remaining candidates, and angle's null widens accordingly. Read the record's config_spectrum relative eigengap and null_summary.angle together: they say how resolvable orientation is in each analysis. The floor was validated on a small-n construction calibrated to select rank 1 by scripts/rank_floor_check.py (rank_floor_decision.json), with the floor-1 arm reported beside it: the 2026-10-23 run returned adopt_floor at both calibrated strengths (report), with power at the null in both arms, so the floor defines angle and shape without making them powerful.

docs.title: Equivalence to the simulation harness
docs.text: analyze_trajectories and evaluate_semisynthetic_trajectory(..., integration_method="pls") call the same block-scaling cores and the same fit_pls_latent_space. On identical data, stage order and settings, the rank floor included, they return the same latent matrix, statistics, p-values, selected rank, null summary and spectrum. tests/test_analysis.py checks this for the default estimator, PC1 and a two-block layer selection, and tests/test_analysis_predictive_coordinates.py under each predictive-subspace coordinate system.

docs.title: Attribution
docs.text:
With attribution=AttributionDiagnosticSettings(enabled=True, ...) (CLI: --attribution), frozen-model orientation attribution runs on the fitted pooled estimator and the standardized joint matrix it was fitted to, with your stage order and group labels. The latent space is not refitted. Real data carry no generator truth, so the truth-recovery block is reported unavailable rather than invented. The full tables are written under attribution/.

With covariates, attribution uses covariate-adjusted cell means: the least-squares means of the cell-means model with the declared covariate design columns (record["covariates"]["design_columns"]), evaluated at the record's covariates.reference_row. They are the feature-space counterpart of the latent LS-means, so the attribution's observed means, projected through the fitted estimator, equal stage_means.csv. Its bootstrap resamples within cells exactly as without covariates and refits the covariate coefficients in every replicate; a resample whose covariates are collinear within cells (for example, one that omits the only donor at a rare factor level) is an invalid replicate and is counted. The record's attribution block then gains an adjustment block: mean_source (covariate_adjusted), design_columns, reference_row, rank_deficient_replicates and bootstrap_replicates. The CLI prints Attribution: covariate-adjusted means at the reference row; <k> of <B> bootstrap replicates rank-deficient. See covariate-adjusted means for the definition and its interpretation boundary.

Validation. scripts/adjusted_attribution_check.py returned adjusted_attribution_validated at the case study's configuration (astrocyte cohort_30 table, six covariate columns with one confounded and injected, rank floor 2, df, at the Phase 6 stage effect; 500 × 999 × B = 200). Against an oracle that removes the injection exactly, the adjusted attribution's top-20 contamination is within 0.005, its residual tilt toward the covariate is under 1 % of the unadjusted one, and truth precision and bootstrap stability are non-inferior. The PLS-captured and residual views keep 3–15 % of the confounding, so read drivers from the observed component. See the report.

On real blocks. The plasmode demonstration on SEA-AD astrocytes (scripts/plasmode_check.py) planted an orientation difference on 20 of the 10,000 RNA and ATAC features and returned attribution_leg_failed. Size held at the case study's configuration, but the plant was not detected at any strength up to 3 within-stage SDs: it lies almost entirely outside the stage-PLS latent space the statistics are measured in. Attribution's observed contrast recovered part of the planted set, unstably. A difference confined to a few features is therefore not something this analysis can detect or trace at n = 80. See the report.

Not with latent adjustment. Attribution together with covariate_latent_adjustment raises an error before any fitting: that basis is fitted on covariate-residualized features, and attribution on it is not defined.

The frozen measurement in memory. result.latent_artifacts holds the fitted estimator, the standardized joint feature matrix the latent scores are the projection of (latent_artifacts.model.transform(latent_artifacts.features) reproduces latent_scores to rounding) and the per-feature original scales. It exists for callers that attribute or probe in exactly the analysed coordinates. It is in memory only: it is not part of the record, and write_analysis_outputs never writes or pickles it.

docs.title: Analysis artifact
docs.text:
write_analysis_outputs(result, out_dir) writes:

  • result.json: the record above.
  • latent_scores.csv: samples × pls_*, indexed by sample id.
  • pls_loadings.csv: block, feature, pls_* (the PLS x_rotations_, in joint order).
  • stage_means.csv: group, stage, pls_*, the fitted latent LS-mean vectors in declared stage order. Pass these to motco.viz.plot_trajectories.
  • attribution/*.csv, when attribution ran.
  • interaction_scan.csv, when the per-feature interaction scan ran: one row per joint feature.

It refuses to replace an existing result.json unless overwrite=True (CLI: --overwrite). The fitted scikit-learn estimator is not pickled, because pickles are version-fragile. The scores, loadings and recorded feature order signature are enough to audit and re-project the fit.

docs.title: Covariates
docs.text:
Donor covariates such as age at death, PMI or RIN enter the trajectory regression in the latent space, so the stage means, the RRPP reduced model and therefore what is permuted all account for them. Declare them on the dataset:

dataset = TrajectoryDataset(
    ...,
    covariate_cols=["age_at_death", "pmi", "education_level"],
    categorical_covariates=["education_level"],   # optional; non-numeric columns are categorical anyway
    missing_covariates="complete_case",           # default "error"
)

CLI: --covariate age_at_death --covariate pmi --categorical-covariate education_level --missing-covariates complete_case.

  • Coding. A numeric (non-boolean) column enters as one design column holding its values. Any other column, or one listed in categorical_covariates (for numeric-coded factors), enters as drop-first indicators name[level], with levels ordered as strings (numerically when every label is an integer); the first level is the reference.
  • Model. The full model is group × stage + covariates and the reduced model group + stage + covariates. Covariates are additive: no interaction with group or stage. RRPP permutes the reduced model's residuals as before, so every permuted dataset keeps the fitted covariate effects.
  • LS-means. Every group × stage mean is evaluated at the pooled mean of each covariate design column (for a factor, its observed level proportions). The covariate term then adds the same vector to every stage mean, and delta, angle and shape are translation-invariant, so the statistics do not depend on the reference. Only stage_means.csv does, and the record states the reference row.
  • Missing values. missing_covariates="error" (the default) rejects any missing covariate value, naming the column and up to ten samples. "complete_case" drops those samples from the metadata and every block before standardization, the latent fit and the design, and records the dropped ids. A deletion that empties a group × stage cell is an error. Covariates are never imputed; blocks must still be complete.
  • Guards. A covariate that is also the sample, group or stage column, a constant numeric covariate, a factor with one observed level, a non-finite numeric value, and a model with covariates that is not of full column rank (for example a covariate collinear with group × stage) are rejected with an error naming the covariate(s).

By default the latent space is covariate-blind, and the adjustment is still exact. PLS-DA is fitted on the standardized features against stage alone, exactly as without covariates, so the latent scores, loadings and selected rank do not change. OLS commutes with a fixed linear map: regressing the scores T = XW on [design, covariates] gives the coefficients of regressing X on the same design, projected by W. The stage means are therefore adjusted exactly as in feature space; only the basis W was chosen without the covariates. If a covariate effect is large and aligned with stage, PLS may spend a component on it; latent adjustment chooses the basis with the covariates instead.

Attribution with covariates uses covariate-adjusted cell means at the same reference row; see Attribution.

Keep the covariate set parsimonious. Small cells (the SEA-AD MTG design has 9–28 donors per cell) and many covariate columns can make the model near-singular or the null unstable. The record's design_columns states the degrees of freedom used.

Type I validation. scripts/covariate_type_i_check.py measures size at the Phase 6 design with covariates confounded with group, stage and their interaction (adjusted vs unadjusted arms on a shared latent fit); see the report. Report covariate-adjusted results only under its covariates_validated decision.

Without covariates the record, the artifact and every output are identical to MOTCO 0.7.0 (except the runtime); the covariates key is absent and the schema version is unchanged (tests/test_analysis_identity.py).

docs.title: Latent adjustment
docs.text:
With covariates declared, the PLS-DA basis is still fitted on the features alone. A large technical axis aligned with stage (library quality, for example) can then take a whole component, and at a selected rank of 1 or 2 that leaves little room for the biology. covariate_latent_adjustment (CLI: --latent-adjustment) fits the basis on features residualized on the declared covariates instead:

params = TrajectoryAnalysisParams(permutations=999, seed=1, covariate_latent_adjustment="stage")

motco analyze ... --covariate age_at_death --covariate pmi --latent-adjustment stage
  • Conditional residualization. Every pooled-standardized joint feature is regressed on [1, D, C], where C holds the declared covariate design columns and D the conditioning design, and only the fitted covariate part C γ is subtracted. Under stage, D is the drop-first stage indicators; under group_stage, the group, stage and group × stage indicators. By Frisch–Waugh–Lovell, γ is the covariates' within-design effect, so stage signal that is merely correlated with a covariate stays in the features. Residualizing on the covariates alone would remove it: label-blind residualization upstream of MOTCO dropped the case study's held-out CV AUROC from 0.63 to 0.41. stage keeps the group label out of the basis; under group_stage the group enters only through the pooled within-cell slope. Use stage: it is the conditioning the Type I check admitted (see below).
  • Leak-free cross-validation. Inside the double CV, every outer rest set and inner training set estimates its own γ and residualizes its held-out samples as X_held_out − C_held_out γ, so held-out labels never enter the residualization. Both CV levels stratify their folds on the conditioning cells (stages under stage, group × stage cells under group_stage), so every training set can estimate the conditioning design. Under stage the folds equal those of the unadjusted analysis. The final basis uses γ estimated on all samples.
  • The pooled scale is kept. The residualized features are not re-standardized: every PLS fit on this path uses scale=False. A feature whose variance was mostly covariate is down-weighted, not inflated back to unit variance, and when the covariate effects are weak the basis approaches the unadjusted one.
  • The raw features are measured in the new basis. The latent scores are the pooled-standardized features (not the residuals), centered at the residuals' mean and projected onto the basis. The trajectory model, the LS-means, the RRPP reduced model and the permutations are exactly those of the covariate-adjusted analysis above. With the covariates in both RRPP models, projecting the raw or the residualized features gives identical statistics, p-values and null draws, because the difference (C − C̄) γ W lies in the models' column space. So only the choice of basis (and of CV rank) changes. Measuring the raw features keeps the covariates block's coefficients and stage_means.csv on the same footing as without the setting.
  • The same covariates in both places. The residualization covariates are exactly covariate_cols, which also enter the trajectory model; that equality is what makes the projection choice immaterial. To residualize on technical variables, declare them as covariates.
  • Guards. The setting without covariates is an error before any fitting. The full-sample residualization design must have full column rank, otherwise the error names the covariates and the conditioning. Every CV training design must too, otherwise the error names the repeat and fold; this happens when a rare factor level drops out of a training set, and depends on random_state. Merge rare levels upstream rather than relying on a minimum-norm fit, whose held-out shift would be arbitrary. Attribution is rejected with latent adjustment, before any fitting.
  • Record. result.json gains a latent_adjustment block after covariates, and latent.integration_params.latent_adjustment names the conditioning. The block holds conditioning, covariates, design_columns (conditioning then covariate columns, beyond the intercept), n_samples, residual_df (n − 1 − k − q), cv_min_training_df (the smallest training-set residual df seen in CV; null with forced_components), feature_scale (pooled_standardized) and feature_r2. That last field summarizes each feature's partial R² of the covariates given the intercept and conditioning (5/25/50/75/95 % quantiles, mean, fraction above 0.5), the share of variance the residualization removes. params.covariate_latent_adjustment is recorded only when set.

Mediator limitation. Residualizing a variable that mediates the stage effect removes real signal, and no simulation can tell a confounder from a mediator. Choosing and justifying the covariate set is the analysis's job, not MOTCO's: a technical variable that is itself downstream of disease stage (a cell-quality metric that worsens with pathology, say) is a mediator candidate.

Validation. scripts/latent_adjustment_type_i_check.py measures size at the Phase 6 design under a covariate-aligned nuisance axis calibrated so that the unadjusted basis spends its first component on it (median |Spearman| ≥ 0.8). It runs three arms per replicate (unadjusted basis, stage, group_stage) at 8 declared covariates, and its decision file names the admissible conditionings (adopt_stage | adopt_group_stage | diagnose_latent_excess). The 2026-10-20 run returned adopt_stage (report). stage held delta 0.031, angle 0.067 and shape 0.058 against 0.0706. group_stage exceeded the bound on angle (0.082) and is not admissible. About 10 % of replicates lost an arm to a rare factor level. scripts/latent_adjustment_power_comparison.py compares power with and without such an axis against the unadjusted basis. Its 2026-10-20 run (report) returned candidate_fails for both conditionings. stage raised orientation power (angle 0.92–0.93 against 0.64–0.78 at the top effect) but lost shape power when the nuisance axis was present, and small-magnitude power without it. group_stage lost most orientation and shape power. Residualizing on covariates confounded with the design removes signal even when they have no effect. Report latent-adjusted results only with stage conditioning, as a sensitivity analysis beside the covariate-adjusted analysis rather than as a replacement, under the conditions of both reports.

Validation at the case study's configuration. scripts/case_study_type_i_check.py measures size where the SEA-AD case study is actually run: the rank floor of 2, six numeric covariate design columns (one confounded with group × stage and injected into the features, five pure noise), a stage signal weakened to a held-out CV AUROC of 0.69–0.70 and a nuisance the covariate-blind basis follows (median |Spearman| 0.92), with three arms per unit on the same data and permutation draws: covariates in the trajectory model only (adjusted, the primary analysis), none (unadjusted, descriptive) and the stage latent adjustment (latent_stage, the fallback). Its decision names primary_validated | adopt_latent_stage | diagnose_configuration_excess over the anchor and the translation control. The 2026-10-29 run (500 × 999 at δ = 0.1 and 0.05, conjunction) returned diagnose_configuration_excess (report): the adjusted model held every statistic at δ = 0.05 and exceeded the 0.0695 bound on translation delta at δ = 0.1 (0.072; delta 0.060–0.072 in every reading, 0.066 pooled), and the stage adjustment exceeded at the anchor on angle (0.084–0.090) and shape (0.078–0.092) at both strengths. At that configuration, read covariate-adjusted delta p-values against a realized size of about 0.066, and do not interpret stage-adjusted angle or shape rejections, until the diagnosis the report names is done.

Diagnosis of that excess. scripts/case_study_diagnosis.py reran the same units, with the committed adjusted and latent_stage p-values reproduced exactly (0 mismatches over 6,000 per strength), under arms that separate the candidate causes:

  • on the covariate-blind basis, the confounded covariate estimated or its injection removed exactly, crossed with 0, 2 or 5 noise covariates;
  • each of those rerun with the Freedman–Lane residuals rescaled by √(n / (n − p_red));
  • the stage adjustment at a forced rank of 2.

The 2026-10-30 run (report) returned two verdicts:

  • residual_df_shrinkage for the adjusted delta. RRPP's permuted residuals shrink with the reduced model's column count, so pooled delta rises from 0.0545 to 0.066 between one and six covariate columns at n = 80. The corrected permutation holds every reading.
  • residualized_basis for the stage adjustment. It still exceeds on anchor angle at a fixed rank of 2 (0.084 / 0.082).

With many covariates at small n, use the opt-in residual correction df, which the corrected-permutation check validated at this configuration (roadmap, Next changes item 8). Without it, read covariate-adjusted p-values against their realized size.

Validation at the ADNI design. scripts/adni_design_check.py measures size and power where the second case study (ADNI serum metabolomics) is run:

  • The design. n = 1,501 in ADNI's sex × stage cells, two blocks, and six covariate design columns of ADNI's kinds. They are a confounded numeric, a three-level factor declared with categorical_covariates (two drop-first columns), a phase-like binary nuisance injected into one block, and two noise columns.
  • The regime. The stage signal is calibrated to ADNI's held-out AUROC (0.606 against 0.600), with a basis that follows the nuisance as ADNI's does.
  • The analysis. One covariate-adjusted analysis per unit, as the primary is issued: the rank floor of 2, net displacement and no residual correction.

The 2026-11-02 run (14 cells × 500 × 999; report) returned non_rejections_uninformative:

  • Size holds at the anchor and the translation control: every statistic reads 0.034–0.068 against the 0.0695 bound. delta is conservative (0.034), since six columns cost almost nothing in residual df at this n.
  • No statistic reaches the 0.80 power floor. Magnitude/delta reaches 0.530 at a doubled stage effect in one group. Orientation/angle (0.056–0.076) and shape/shape (0.034–0.062) stay at the null rate at every construction effect.
  • The rank. The CV-selected rank sits at the cap of 19 in 95–100 % of units, against ADNI's 8.

At a design of this kind (large n, a weak stage signal at AUROC ≈ 0.60), a non-rejection of delta, angle or shape is uninformative. The measurement covers this table, stage signal and covariate set only, on InterSIM-analogue blocks.

Without the setting, every output is identical to MOTCO 0.8.0 except the runtime, record["params"] included (tests/test_analysis_identity.py).

docs.title: Residual correction
docs.text:
RRPP permutes the reduced model's residuals (Freedman–Lane). Their mean square is RSS/n, not the unbiased RSS/(n − r), where r is the reduced model's rank, so the permuted noise is narrower than the real noise by a factor of √((n − r)/n). With many covariate columns at small n that factor matters: at n = 80 and r = 10 (intercept, group, two stage columns and six covariates) the permuted noise is about 6 % narrower in SD, the null of a scale-dependent statistic is too narrow, and delta rejects at about 0.066 at α = 0.05 (the diagnosis). The opt-in residual_correction rescales the residuals once before they are permuted:

params = TrajectoryAnalysisParams(permutations=999, seed=1, residual_correction="df")

motco analyze ... --covariate age_at_death --covariate pmi --residual-correction df
  • df multiplies every residual by κ = √(n / (n − r)): one scalar per analysis (κ = 1.069 at n = 80, r = 10). It is the correction the diagnosis measured.
  • leverage divides residual i by √(1 − h_ii), with h the reduced model's hat matrix, so samples in small cells or with extreme covariate values are inflated more. In a balanced one-factor design every sample has leverage r/n and the two corrections coincide.

r is the numerical rank of the reduced model with its covariates, so a rank-deficient model uses its rank, not its column count. The permutation draws (the same seed gives the same sample orders), the reduced fitted values, the full-model estimation and the observed statistics are unchanged: only the p-values and the null summary move. The latent scores, selected rank, stage means and every other block are identical with and without the setting. The correction does not need covariates: without them r = 4 (intercept, group, two stage columns at three stages), so κ = 1.026 at n = 80.

  • Errors. An unknown value is rejected before any fitting. df with n − r ≤ 0, and leverage with a sample of leverage 1 (the only member of a reduced-model category), raise an error naming the counts or the sample's row before any permutation.
  • Record. When the correction is set and permutations run, measurement.residual_correction states kind, n and reduced_rank, plus kappa for df, or leverage_min/leverage_max and scale_min/scale_max for leverage; the CLI prints it as RRPP null: residual correction …. params.residual_correction is recorded only when set. With permutations=0 the parameter is recorded but no correction entry is written, since nothing was applied.
  • The primitive. motco.stats.permutation.RRPP(..., residual_correction=) applies the same rescaling for any caller, and residual_correction_scale(model_reduced, correction) returns the per-sample multipliers.

Validation status: df validated (adopt_df, 2026-10-30). The corrected-permutation check (scripts/corrected_permutation_check.py; report) measured both corrections. It used a fresh seed family at the case study's configuration: six covariate columns, the rank floor of 2 and a weak stage signal, on both case-study cohort tables (n = 80 and 76) at 500 replicates × 999 permutations.

  • Size. Both corrections hold every pooled rate and every reading. Under df, delta reads 0.029–0.031, angle 0.0425–0.050 and shape 0.052–0.058 pooled per table, against a bound of 0.0597.
  • The uncorrected null. On the same data it was liberal: pooled shape 0.0675–0.0685, and anchor angle 0.086 at the Phase 6 stage effect.
  • Power cost. At the Phase 6 stage effect, df gives up 0.024–0.034 of angle and shape power, and up to 0.054 of delta power, against the uncorrected null.
  • leverage. It holds size as well but showed no paired power advantage, so df is the validated choice.

The validation covers n = 76–80 with six covariate columns. Smaller tables (for example n = 63) and other covariate sets are inferred, not measured. The correction stays opt-in, and the default is the uncorrected null.

Without the setting, every output is identical to MOTCO 0.12.0 except the runtime (tests/test_analysis_identity.py).

docs.title: Split interaction test
docs.text:
delta, angle and shape see a group difference only through its component inside the fitted stage-PLS span. The opt-in split interaction test asks the question the span cannot: do the groups differ by stage anywhere in the measured features, and is that difference inside the fitted span or outside it?

params = TrajectoryAnalysisParams(permutations=999, seed=1, residual_correction="df", span_split_test=True)

motco analyze ... --permutations 999 --seed 1 --residual-correction df --span-split-test

It runs motco.stats.interaction.interaction_split_test on the analysis's own inputs:

  • Outcome. The pooled-standardized joint features in the fitted PLS model's input coordinates, the coordinates in which qr(x_rotations_) is orthonormal and span capture is measured.
  • Basis. qr(x_rotations_): span has the selected rank as its dimension and complement the rest of the features.
  • Models. The full (group × stage) and reduced (group + stage) trajectory models with the declared covariates, so the tested effect is the group × stage interaction RRPP tests.
  • Null. Freedman–Lane permutation of the reduced residuals with RRPP's serial draws at the analysis's seed, the analysis's permutation count and its residual correction.

Per part the record's span_split block gives the dimension, the interaction sum of squares, the full model's residual sum of squares, df_int, df_res, the pseudo-F (SS_int / df_int) / (RSS / df_res) and, with permutations, the pseudo-F p-value (the test) and the interaction-SS p-value (a diagnostic). span + complement = total for both sums, and span_share is the observed share of the interaction energy inside the fitted span. draws_match_rrpp is true when RRPP ran serially (n_jobs 1), so the split test's draws are RRPP's; with more jobs RRPP draws a different sequence while the split test keeps the serial one. The CLI prints one line with the three pseudo-F p-values and the in-span share.

  • Unchanged outputs. Latent scores, rank, statistics, p-values, null summary and stage means are identical with and without the setting; without it every output equals MOTCO 0.17.0's (tests/test_analysis_identity.py, tests/test_analysis_span_split.py).
  • Latent adjustment. The test is defined on the covariate-blind basis, so requesting it with covariate_latent_adjustment (--latent-adjustment) is an error before fitting.
  • Reading. "Span" is the span fitted to the sample, not the population stage program. How a rejection or a non-rejection of each part is read, and the validation status, are on the measurement visibility page.

docs.title: Per-feature interaction scan
docs.text:
The split test's complement sums interaction energy over every coordinate outside the span, so a difference on a few features is lost in the noise of the rest. The opt-in scan tests the group × stage interaction of each feature on its own and combines the features by their maximum, so a difference confined to a few features can be detected and the features carrying it named.

params = TrajectoryAnalysisParams(permutations=999, seed=1, residual_correction="df", interaction_scan=True)

motco analyze ... --permutations 999 --seed 1 --residual-correction df --interaction-scan

It runs motco.stats.interaction.interaction_feature_scan on:

  • Outcome. The pooled-standardized joint features. Each feature's F ignores its location and scale, so the standardization does not matter; the declared unit transform (for example beta to M values) does.
  • Models. The full and reduced trajectory models with the declared covariates, the effect RRPP and the split test test.
  • Null. Freedman–Lane permutation of the reduced residuals with RRPP's serial draws at the analysis's seed, its permutation count and its residual correction (df cancels in every F).

The record's interaction_scan block gives the feature and degenerate counts, df_int and df_res, max_f with max_feature and max_block and, with permutations, p_value_global (the permutation p-value of the largest F), the hits (features with Westfall–Young step-down max-T adjusted p ≤ hit_alpha = 0.05, ordered by F) and per block the features, degenerate features, hits and null_max_share (the share of draws whose largest null F fell in that block, beside the block's share of features). draws_match_rrpp is true when RRPP ran serially. The CLI prints one line with the maximum F and its feature, the global p-value and the hit count.

interaction_scan.csv (TrajectoryAnalysisResult.interaction_scan) has one row per joint feature in joint order: block, feature, ss_interaction, rss, f, p_value_adjusted (with permutations), degenerate and difference[<stage>] per declared stage, the second group minus the first from the full model's LS means at the covariate reference row, in standardized units (the rows that give stage_means.csv in latent coordinates). Degenerate features (zero full-model residual variance, constant ones included) have no F or adjusted p-value and never enter the maximum.

  • Unchanged outputs. Latent scores, rank, statistics, p-values, null summary, stage means, any span_split block and any attribution output are identical with and without the setting; without it every output equals MOTCO 0.19.0's (tests/test_analysis_identity.py, tests/test_analysis_interaction_scan.py).
  • Latent adjustment, attribution and block weighting. The scan reads only the standardized features and the trajectory models, so it is allowed with all three and is identical with and without latent adjustment. It reads the unweighted standardized features, so a block weighting leaves its record and table unchanged.
  • Reading. A hit names a feature whose covariate-adjusted group difference changes across stages, with the familywise error rate over all scanned features controlled at 0.05; it does not say the feature drives a latent trajectory difference, and a scan without hits is uninformative unless power is shown. See measurement visibility for the reading and the validation status.

docs.title: By block
docs.text:
The joint scan's familywise bar is set by the block that most often gives the largest null F (on the SEA-AD export ATAC gave 0.62 of the null maxima with half the features). The opt-in by-block scan splits the familywise error equally between the declared blocks:

params = TrajectoryAnalysisParams(
    permutations=999, seed=1, residual_correction="df", interaction_scan=True, interaction_scan_by_block=True
)

motco analyze ... --permutations 999 --seed 1 --residual-correction df --interaction-scan --interaction-scan-by-block

It runs the same scan with the declared blocks as block labels (combination="block_bonferroni", see the primitive): the step-down within each block on the same draws, and each of the K blocks with a non-degenerate feature tested at α/K.

  • Requires the scan. interaction_scan_by_block=True without interaction_scan=True is rejected before any fitting, naming both (motco analyze exits with a clean error naming both flags). The setting is omitted from the resolved parameters while false.
  • Record. The interaction_scan block gains combination and n_blocks_tested after max_block, and each per-block entry gains max_f and max_feature (null for a wholly degenerate block) and, with permutations, p_value, the block's own global p-value before the factor K. p_value_global and hits are the by-block ones; max_f, max_feature, max_block, the per-block hit counts and null_max_share keep their meaning. The CLI's scan line names the combination and K.
  • Table. interaction_scan.csv keeps its columns; p_value_adjusted holds the by-block adjusted p-values, and the F and group differences are unchanged.
  • Unchanged outputs. Every output other than the scan's p-values and hits is identical between the joint and by-block scans, and without the setting every output equals MOTCO 0.22.0's (tests/test_analysis_scan_by_block.py, tests/test_analysis_identity.py).
  • Reading. A by-block hit keeps the familywise error over all scanned features at 0.05, now split equally across the blocks, so each block has the same chance of a false hit whatever its size or noise. Detection moves from the block with more features or heavier-tailed noise to the others. Validation status: see measurement visibility.

docs.title: Block weighting
docs.text:
The joint features are z-scored one by one and concatenated, so unweighted a block's influence on every fitted space grows with its feature count. The opt-in block weighting multiplies every standardized block by one label-blind scalar, so that weight is a declared choice:

params = TrajectoryAnalysisParams(permutations=999, seed=1, block_weighting="equal_variance")

motco analyze ... --permutations 999 --seed 1 --block-weighting equal_variance
  • Kinds. equal_variance multiplies block b by 1/√p_b (p_b its feature count, constant features included), so every block has unit total variance (the multi-block PLS block scaling). mfa multiplies it by the inverse standard deviation of the standardized block's leading principal component, so every block's dominant direction has unit variance (multiple factor analysis). The equal_variance weight depends only on the declared block; the mfa weight depends on the sample, so two cohorts weight differently. Neither reads a group or stage label, and both are fitted once on the pooled sample, like the standardization, so RRPP's null is unchanged in kind.
  • Metric. The PLS space is fitted without per-feature rescaling (every fit, the cross-validation's included), so the weights set the metric. delta is in the weighted metric and is not comparable with an unweighted analysis's; angle, shape and the p-values are. The rank can differ, because the weights change the space.
  • Record. A block_weighting block after blocks names the kind and each block's weight and feature count, latent.integration_params names the kind, and the CLI prints it beside the selected rank. Attribution's original-unit mapping and latent_artifacts.original_scales divide by the weights, so reconstructed features are in their original units. The split interaction test runs in the weighted metric of the fitted space; the per-feature scan does not depend on it.
  • Absent. Nothing is written and every output equals MOTCO 0.20.0's (tests/test_analysis_identity.py, tests/test_analysis_block_weighting.py).
  • Status. The setting is measured and stays opt-in. Its size and power check, the weighted arm of the production latent-space selection (report), read no_gain: size, protected power and specificity hold, and it gains no power at a weak stage signal or on the SEA-AD plasmode's stage-span plant. A case study may declare it as a sensitivity analysis. On blocks with equal feature counts the weights are equal, so the only change is the fit without per-fold re-standardization. An unknown kind is rejected before anything is fitted.

docs.title: Sparse stage-PLS
docs.text:
The production space loads every component on every feature. At a weak stage signal on many features the fitted span is mostly noise; the opt-in sparse stage-PLS-DA keeps the stage objective and the rank rule and adds one regularization, the number of features each component may load on, selected by the same held-out AUROC:

from motco.analysis import SparsitySettings

params = TrajectoryAnalysisParams(permutations=999, seed=1, sparsity=SparsitySettings("block"))

motco analyze ... --permutations 999 --seed 1 --sparsity block --sparsity-ladder 1.0,0.5,0.2,0.1,0.05
  • Budget. Every component's weight vector keeps the features with the largest absolute weights, shrunk by the largest discarded one (the sPLS-DA of Lê Cao et al.; SparsePLSDA). joint counts one budget over all features; block one per declared block, so every block keeps its share whatever its size. A keep fraction f keeps max(1, round(f · p)) features per group.
  • Selection. The cross-validation scores every pair of a candidate rank and a fraction of the ladder (default 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05; distinct, in (0, 1]) and keeps, on an exact tie, the smaller rank and then the fuller budget, so it leaves the ordinary fit only on strictly better held-out AUROC. The final model is fitted at the modal rank and the modal fraction. A ladder of 1.0 alone reproduces the ordinary analysis exactly. forced_components skips the cross-validation, so it needs a one-element ladder.
  • Record. A sparsity block after latent names the scope, the ladder, the selected fraction and each component's support per block; latent.integration_params carries the scope, the ladder and the selected fraction, and the CLI prints the fraction beside the selected rank. pls_loadings.csv shows the features no component loads on at zero.
  • Composition. Attribution, the split interaction test, the per-feature scan (which never reads the fit), latent adjustment and block weighting run unchanged on a sparse space.
  • Absent. Nothing is written and every output equals MOTCO 0.21.0's (tests/test_analysis_identity.py, tests/test_analysis_sparsity.py).
  • Status. The setting is measured and stays opt-in. The production latent-space selection's sparse_block arm (report) read size_excess: on the SEA-AD plasmode anchor delta reads 0.11 at 100 replicates, as production does on the same replicates, and it gains no Bonferroni-protected power at a weak stage signal or on the plasmode plant (best delta 0.51 → 0.62 at e = 0.5, p = 0.0096). It loses no protected power and costs about seven to nine production fits. A malformed setting is rejected before anything is fitted.

docs.title: Predictive-subspace coordinates
docs.text:
The cross-validated rank both regularizes the stage fit and sets the number of dimensions the statistics are measured in. The opt-in latent_coordinates keeps the fit and measures in the fitted model's predictive subspace, the min(rank, n_stages − 1) directions of its score space along which the fitted stage labels move (the row space of its Y loadings), as the simulation harness defines it:

params = TrajectoryAnalysisParams(permutations=999, seed=1, latent_coordinates="predictive")
  • Values. "predictive" (the scores projected on the subspace), "predictive_orthonormal" (the standardized features on an orthonormal basis of it) and "predictive_fitted" (the fitted stage indicators, one column per stage). "orthonormal" and "scores" are not offered here.
  • What moves. The statistics, the permutation draws, latent_scores.csv and stage_means.csv are in the measured coordinates. The selected rank, the held-out AUROC and pls_loadings.csv are those of the fit, which is unchanged.
  • Record. measurement.latent_coordinates gives the value and the measured dimension beside the selected rank, and latent.integration_params.latent_coordinates the value.
  • Rejections, all before any fitting: an unknown value, fewer than three stages, attribution and the split interaction test (both are defined on the fitted span). Covariates, latent adjustment, the residual correction, a forced rank, block weighting, sparsity and the interaction scan compose with it.
  • Absent. Nothing is written and every output equals MOTCO 0.23.0's (tests/test_analysis_identity.py).
  • Status. It has no CLI flag, and it is a diagnostic, not a test to report. The predictive-subspace pilot read keep_production on 2026-11-12 (report). On this entry point's own case-study configuration, on the SEA-AD plasmode, the three values reject delta at about 0.13 and shape at about 0.08 under permuted labels, where the scores read 0.042 and 0.026. motco analyze measures in the scores.

docs.title: Example: SEA-AD-style design
docs.text:
Two blocks (RNA and ATAC donor pseudobulks), sex as the group, three ADNC stages:

motco analyze \
  --block rna=rna_logcpm.csv --block atac=atac_logcpm.csv \
  --metadata donors.csv --sample-col donor_id --group-col Sex --stage-col ADNC \
  --stage-order "Not AD + Low,Intermediate,High" \
  --permutations 999 --seed 20261015 \
  --out-dir results/motco_mtg_astro

For the dimensionality sensitivity analysis, re-run with --forced-components 2, 3, … into separate output directories.

from motco.analysis import (
    OmicsBlock, TrajectoryAnalysisParams, TrajectoryDataset,
    analyze_trajectories, write_analysis_outputs,
)

dataset = TrajectoryDataset(
    blocks=[OmicsBlock("rna", rna), OmicsBlock("atac", atac)],
    metadata=donors,
    sample_col="donor_id", group_col="Sex", stage_col="ADNC",
    stage_order=["Not AD + Low", "Intermediate", "High"],
)
result = analyze_trajectories(dataset, TrajectoryAnalysisParams(permutations=999, seed=20261015))
write_analysis_outputs(result, "results/motco_mtg_astro")

docs.title: motco.analysis
docs.text:
Real-data trajectory analysis: the validated MOTCO measurement on your own data.

:func:analyze_trajectories runs the production pipeline the simulation harness characterizes — pooled per-feature standardization, a stage-supervised PLS-DA latent space whose rank is chosen by double cross-validation, delta / angle / shape between two groups in that space, and RRPP p-values — on caller-supplied omic blocks and sample metadata. It calls the same cores as :func:motco.simulations.evaluate_semisynthetic_trajectory (block scaling in :mod:motco.simulations.preprocessing, :func:~motco.simulations.evaluation.fit_pls_latent_space, the trajectory design and the record helpers), so the measurement exists once.

Two inputs are load-bearing and therefore explicit:

  • Stage order. Net displacement runs from the first to the last declared stage, and shape and the spectrum follow that order. It is never inferred by sorting labels.
  • Units. Each block declares its unit transform (identity or beta_to_mvalue). MOTCO does not normalize counts, filter features or impute values; blocks are analysed in the units supplied.

Declared covariates enter the trajectory model. By default the latent space is built without them; TrajectoryAnalysisParams.covariate_latent_adjustment ("stage" or "group_stage") instead fits the basis on features residualized on the covariates conditional on that design, and measures the raw features in it.

Attribution (TrajectoryAnalysisParams.attribution) explains the measured orientation on the fitted estimator. With declared covariates it attributes from covariate-adjusted cell means, the feature-space counterpart of the latent LS-means; it is not available with latent adjustment.

TrajectoryAnalysisParams.residual_correction ("df" or "leverage") rescales the reduced model's residuals before RRPP permutes them, so the null keeps the residual variance the reduced model's degrees of freedom remove. It moves only the p-values and the null summary.

TrajectoryAnalysisParams.span_split_test additionally tests the group × stage interaction of the standardized features inside the fitted PLS span and in its orthogonal complement (:func:motco.stats.interaction.interaction_split_test), recorded in a span_split block; every other output is unchanged.

TrajectoryAnalysisParams.block_weighting ("equal_variance" or "mfa") multiplies every standardized block by one label-blind scalar before the latent space is fitted, so a block's weight in the joint measurement is declared rather than set by its feature count; the space is fitted in the weighted metric, delta is measured in it, and a block_weighting record block names the kind and the weights. It is unvalidated until the production latent-space selection reads it.

TrajectoryAnalysisParams.sparsity (a :class:SparsitySettings: scope "joint" or "block" and a ladder of keep fractions) fits the latent space with sparse stage-PLS-DA (:class:motco.stats.sparse_pls.SparsePLSDA), whose components each load on a budget of features, cross-validated over the rank and the ladder jointly; a sparsity record block names the scope, the ladder, the selected fraction and the support per component and block. It is unvalidated until the production latent-space selection reads it.

TrajectoryAnalysisParams.interaction_scan additionally tests the group × stage interaction of every standardized feature on its own, combined by the maximum F with step-down max-T adjusted p-values (:func:motco.stats.interaction.interaction_feature_scan). It is recorded in an interaction_scan block and tabulated per feature with the covariate-adjusted group difference at each stage; every other output is unchanged. TrajectoryAnalysisParams.interaction_scan_by_block splits the scan's familywise error equally between the declared blocks (Bonferroni over within-block step-downs), so a large or heavy-tailed block no longer sets every block's bar; only the scan's p-values and hits move.

:func:write_analysis_outputs writes the result as plain JSON/CSV (record, latent scores, PLS loadings, latent stage means and, when requested, the attribution tables and the scan table) — the fitted estimator is never pickled.

docs.title: TrajectoryDataset dataclass
docs.text:
Aligned omic blocks plus sample metadata, validated on construction.

Every block's rows must equal metadata[sample_col] in order. The group column must hold exactly two labels; stage_order must list every observed stage label exactly once (labels are compared as strings), and every group × stage cell must be observed.

covariate_cols names metadata columns that enter the trajectory model additively, in declared order. A covariate is categorical when listed in categorical_covariates or when its dtype is not numeric (booleans are categorical); otherwise numeric. missing_covariates decides what a missing covariate value does: "error" rejects it, "complete_case" drops the sample from the metadata and every block before anything else is validated or fitted (dropped_sample_ids lists them). Covariates are never imputed.

Source code in src/motco/analysis.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TrajectoryDataset:
    """Aligned omic blocks plus sample metadata, validated on construction.

    Every block's rows must equal ``metadata[sample_col]`` in order. The group
    column must hold exactly two labels; ``stage_order`` must list every
    observed stage label exactly once (labels are compared as strings), and
    every group × stage cell must be observed.

    ``covariate_cols`` names metadata columns that enter the trajectory model
    additively, in declared order. A covariate is categorical when listed in
    ``categorical_covariates`` or when its dtype is not numeric (booleans are
    categorical); otherwise numeric. ``missing_covariates`` decides what a
    missing covariate value does: ``"error"`` rejects it, ``"complete_case"``
    drops the sample from the metadata and every block before anything else is
    validated or fitted (``dropped_sample_ids`` lists them). Covariates are
    never imputed.
    """

    blocks: Sequence[OmicsBlock]
    metadata: pd.DataFrame
    sample_col: str
    group_col: str
    stage_col: str
    stage_order: Sequence[str]
    group_order: Sequence[str] | None = None
    covariate_cols: Sequence[str] = ()
    categorical_covariates: Sequence[str] = ()
    missing_covariates: MissingCovariatePolicy = "error"
    _dropped_sample_ids: tuple[str, ...] = field(default=(), init=False, repr=False, compare=False)
    _covariate_design: CovariateDesign | None = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False, compare=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "blocks", tuple(self.blocks))
        object.__setattr__(self, "stage_order", tuple(str(stage) for stage in self.stage_order))
        if self.group_order is not None:
            object.__setattr__(self, "group_order", tuple(str(group) for group in self.group_order))
        object.__setattr__(self, "covariate_cols", tuple(self.covariate_cols))
        object.__setattr__(self, "categorical_covariates", tuple(self.categorical_covariates))
        self._validate_metadata()
        self._validate_covariate_declarations()
        cells_before = self._observed_cells()
        self._apply_missing_covariate_policy()
        self._validate_blocks(self.sample_ids)
        self._build_covariate_design()
        self._validate_design(cells_before)

    @property
    def sample_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        return self.metadata[self.sample_col].astype(str).tolist()

    @property
    def groups(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Group labels in analysis order (declared, else sorted as strings)."""

        if self.group_order is not None:
            return tuple(self.group_order)
        return tuple(sorted(set(self.metadata[self.group_col].astype(str))))

    @property
    def stages(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(self.stage_order)

    @property
    def dropped_sample_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Samples removed by complete-case deletion (empty under ``"error"``)."""

        return self._dropped_sample_ids

    @property
    def covariate_design(self) -> CovariateDesign | None:
        """The covariate design columns on the retained samples, or ``None`` without covariates."""

        return self._covariate_design

    def _observed_cells(self) -> set[tuple[str, str]]:
        return set(zip(self.metadata[self.group_col].astype(str), self.metadata[self.stage_col].astype(str)))

    def _validate_covariate_declarations(self) -> None:
        if self.missing_covariates not in MISSING_COVARIATE_POLICIES:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Unknown missing_covariates policy {self.missing_covariates!r}; allowed: "
                f"{list(MISSING_COVARIATE_POLICIES)}."
            )
        covariates = list(self.covariate_cols)
        repeated = sorted({name for name in covariates if covariates.count(name) > 1})
        if repeated:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Covariates must be declared once; repeated: {repeated}.")
        reserved = [name for name in covariates if name in {self.sample_col, self.group_col, self.stage_col}]
        if reserved:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Covariates must differ from the sample, group and stage columns; got {reserved}."
            )
        absent = [name for name in covariates if name not in self.metadata.columns]
        if absent:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"metadata is missing covariate column(s): {absent}.")
        undeclared = [name for name in self.categorical_covariates if name not in covariates]
        if undeclared:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"categorical_covariates must also be declared in covariate_cols; not declared: {undeclared}."
            )

    def _apply_missing_covariate_policy(self) -> None:
        if not self.covariate_cols:
            return
        missing = self.metadata[list(self.covariate_cols)].isna()
        if not missing.to_numpy().any():
            return
        sample_ids = self.metadata[self.sample_col].astype(str)
        if self.missing_covariates == "error":
            column = next(name for name in self.covariate_cols if missing[name].any())
            affected = sample_ids[missing[column].to_numpy()].tolist()
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Covariate {column!r} has missing values for {len(affected)} sample(s): {affected[:10]}. "
                "Pass missing_covariates='complete_case' to drop them; covariates are never imputed."
            )
        drop = missing.any(axis=1).to_numpy()
        keep = ~drop
        object.__setattr__(self, "_dropped_sample_ids", tuple(sample_ids[drop].tolist()))
        object.__setattr__(self, "metadata", self.metadata.loc[keep].reset_index(drop=True))
        retained = []
        for block in self.blocks:
            values = block.values
            if isinstance(values, pd.DataFrame) and values.shape[0] == keep.size:
                values = values.loc[keep]
            retained.append(OmicsBlock(block.name, values, block.transform))
        object.__setattr__(self, "blocks", tuple(retained))

    def _build_covariate_design(self) -> None:
        if not self.covariate_cols:
            return
        try:
            design = build_covariate_matrix(self.metadata, self.covariate_cols, self.categorical_covariates)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(str(exc)) from exc
        object.__setattr__(self, "_covariate_design", design)

    def _validate_metadata(self) -> None:
        if not isinstance(self.metadata, pd.DataFrame):
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("metadata must be a pandas DataFrame.")
        columns = {"sample_col": self.sample_col, "group_col": self.group_col, "stage_col": self.stage_col}
        missing = [f"{role}={name!r}" for role, name in columns.items() if name not in self.metadata.columns]
        if missing:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"metadata is missing column(s): {', '.join(missing)}.")
        if len({self.sample_col, self.group_col, self.stage_col}) != 3:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("sample_col, group_col and stage_col must name three different columns.")
        if self.metadata.shape[0] == 0:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("metadata must contain at least one sample.")
        for name in columns.values():
            if self.metadata[name].isna().any():
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"metadata column {name!r} contains missing values.")
        sample_ids = self.sample_ids
        duplicated = sorted({sid for sid in sample_ids if sample_ids.count(sid) > 1})
        if duplicated:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"metadata sample ids are not unique: {duplicated[:10]}.")

    def _validate_blocks(self, sample_ids: list[str]) -> None:
        if not self.blocks:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("At least one omic block is required.")
        names = [block.name for block in self.blocks]
        repeated = sorted({name for name in names if names.count(name) > 1})
        if repeated:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block names must be unique; repeated: {repeated}.")
        for block in self.blocks:
            if not isinstance(block.name, str) or not block.name:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block names must be non-empty strings, got {block.name!r}.")
            if block.transform not in UNIT_TRANSFORMS:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Block {block.name!r} declares unknown transform {block.transform!r}; "
                    f"allowed: {list(UNIT_TRANSFORMS)}."
                )
            values = block.values
            if not isinstance(values, pd.DataFrame):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block {block.name!r} must be a pandas DataFrame.")
            if values.shape[0] != len(sample_ids):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Block {block.name!r} has {values.shape[0]} rows but metadata has {len(sample_ids)} samples."
                )
            if values.index.astype(str).tolist() != sample_ids:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Block {block.name!r} rows are not aligned to metadata column {self.sample_col!r} "
                    "(same sample ids in the same order are required)."
                )
            if values.shape[1] == 0:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block {block.name!r} must contain at least one feature.")
            features = values.columns.astype(str).tolist()
            if len(set(features)) != len(features):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block {block.name!r} has duplicate feature names.")
            try:
                matrix = values.to_numpy(dtype=float)
            except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block {block.name!r} holds non-numeric values.") from exc
            if not np.all(np.isfinite(matrix)):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Block {block.name!r} contains missing or infinite values; complete matrices are "
                    "required and no imputation is performed."
                )
            if block.transform == "beta_to_mvalue" and not np.all((matrix > 0.0) & (matrix < 1.0)):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Block {block.name!r} declares beta_to_mvalue but holds values outside the open "
                    "interval (0, 1)."
                )

    def _validate_design(self, cells_before: set[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
        emptied = sorted(cells_before - self._observed_cells())
        if emptied:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Complete-case deletion of {len(self._dropped_sample_ids)} sample(s) with missing covariates "
                f"emptied group/stage combination(s): {emptied}."
            )
        observed_stages = sorted(set(self.metadata[self.stage_col].astype(str)))
        declared = list(self.stage_order)
        if len(set(declared)) != len(declared) or set(declared) != set(observed_stages):
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"stage_order must list every observed stage label exactly once; declared {declared}, "
                f"observed {observed_stages}."
            )
        if len(declared) < 2:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"At least two stages are required; observed {observed_stages}.")
        observed_groups = sorted(set(self.metadata[self.group_col].astype(str)))
        if len(observed_groups) != 2:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Exactly two groups are required in {self.group_col!r}; found {len(observed_groups)}: "
                f"{observed_groups}."
            )
        if self.group_order is not None:
            group_order = list(self.group_order)
            if len(set(group_order)) != len(group_order) or set(group_order) != set(observed_groups):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"group_order must list both observed groups exactly once; declared {group_order}, "
                    f"observed {observed_groups}."
                )
        present = self._observed_cells()
        missing = [(group, stage) for group in self.groups for stage in declared if (group, stage) not in present]
        if missing:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"metadata has no sample for group/stage combination(s): {missing}.")

docs.text:
Sparse stage-PLS-DA for the latent space: a budget scope and a ladder of keep fractions.

scope is "joint" (one budget over all features) or "block" (one budget per declared block, so every block keeps its share whatever its size). keep_fractions (default 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05) are fractions of the scope's feature count, distinct and in (0, 1]; they are held fullest first. The cross-validation selects the rank and the fraction jointly; on an exact tie it keeps the fuller budget, so it leaves the ordinary fit only on strictly better held-out AUROC.
