@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SparsitySettings:
    """Sparse stage-PLS-DA for the latent space: a budget scope and a ladder of keep fractions.

    ``scope`` is ``"joint"`` (one budget over all features) or ``"block"``
    (one budget per declared block, so every block keeps its share whatever
    its size). ``keep_fractions`` (default 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05) are
    fractions of the scope's feature count, distinct and in (0, 1]; they are
    held fullest first. The cross-validation selects the rank and the
    fraction jointly; on an exact tie it keeps the fuller budget, so it leaves
    the ordinary fit only on strictly better held-out AUROC.
    """

    scope: str
    keep_fractions: tuple[float, ...] = DEFAULT_KEEP_FRACTIONS

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.scope not in SPARSITY_SCOPES:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Unknown sparsity scope {self.scope!r}; allowed: {list(SPARSITY_SCOPES)}."
            )
        try:
            # The ladder is validated alone; the block sizes come from the declared blocks.
            ladder = SparsityDesign("joint", self.keep_fractions).keep_fractions
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"sparsity: {exc}") from exc
        object.__setattr__(self, "keep_fractions", ladder)

    def integration_param(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The core's ``integration_params["sparsity"]`` value."""

        return {"scope": self.scope, "keep_fractions": list(self.keep_fractions)}

docs.title: TrajectoryAnalysisParams dataclass
docs.text:
Measurement settings; the defaults are the simulation harness's.

forced_components fixes the latent rank (dimensionality sensitivity) and skips cross-validation; None selects it by double CV. seed seeds RRPP exactly as the harness does.

covariate_latent_adjustment (None, "stage" or "group_stage") opts into covariate-aware latent construction: the basis is fitted on features residualized on the declared covariates, conditional on the stage or the group × stage indicators. It requires declared covariates and is omitted from :meth:to_dict while None.

min_components is the rank floor of the cross-validated latent space (default 2, so angle and shape are measured in at least two dimensions). 1 restores the unfloored 0.9.0 rule and normalizes to None, which is omitted from :meth:to_dict and from the record's latent block, so a floor-1 analysis reproduces every 0.9.0 artifact. A floor below 1 is rejected before any fitting. The floor guarantees two dimensions, not a second axis with signal.

residual_correction (None, "df" or "leverage") rescales the reduced model's residuals before RRPP permutes them (see :func:motco.stats.permutation.RRPP): "df" by κ = √(n / (n − r)), "leverage" by 1 / √(1 − h_ii). The observed statistics, latent space and stage means are unchanged; only the null moves. An unknown value is rejected before any fitting, and the setting is omitted from :meth:to_dict while None.

span_split_test (default False) runs the split interaction test (:func:motco.stats.interaction.interaction_split_test) on the standardized features in the fitted PLS model's input coordinates, against qr(x_rotations_), with the trajectory models (covariates included), the seed, the permutations and the residual correction. It is omitted from :meth:to_dict while false and is not available with latent adjustment.

interaction_scan (default False) runs the per-feature interaction scan (:func:motco.stats.interaction.interaction_feature_scan) on the standardized features with the trajectory models (covariates included), the seed, the permutations and the residual correction. It uses neither the latent basis nor the bootstrap, so it is available with latent adjustment and with attribution, and it is omitted from :meth:to_dict while false. It reads the unweighted standardized features, so a block weighting leaves it unchanged.

interaction_scan_by_block (default False) runs that scan with the declared blocks as its block labels (combination="block_bonferroni"): the step-down runs within each block on the same draws, and with K blocks holding a non-degenerate feature each is tested at α/K, so every block has the same chance of a false hit whatever its size or noise. The F, the group differences and every non-scan output are unchanged; the global p-value, the adjusted p-values and the hits are the by-block ones. It requires interaction_scan (rejected before any fitting otherwise) and is omitted from :meth:to_dict while false.

block_weighting (None, "equal_variance" or "mfa") multiplies every standardized block by one label-blind scalar fitted on the pooled sample — 1/√p_b (unit total variance per block) or the inverse standard deviation of the block's leading principal component — and fits the PLS space without per-feature rescaling, so the weights set the metric. delta is in that metric; angle, shape and the p-values are comparable with an unweighted analysis. Attribution's original-unit mapping divides by the weights. An unknown kind is rejected before any fitting, and the setting is omitted from :meth:to_dict while None. Unvalidated until the production latent-space selection reads it.

sparsity (None or a :class:SparsitySettings) fits the latent space with sparse stage-PLS-DA: every component loads on the selected fraction of the features (joint) or of each declared block (block), the rank and the fraction are cross-validated jointly, and the final model is a :class:motco.stats.sparse_pls.SparsePLSDA. Attribution, the split test and the interaction scan run unchanged on it, and it composes with latent adjustment and block weighting; with forced_components the ladder must hold one fraction. A malformed setting is rejected before any fitting, and the setting is omitted from :meth:to_dict while None. Unvalidated until the production latent-space selection reads it.

latent_coordinates (None, "predictive", "predictive_orthonormal" or "predictive_fitted") measures the trajectories on the fitted model's predictive subspace, the row space of its Y loadings (min(rank, n_stages − 1) dimensions), as the simulation harness defines it: the scores projected on it, the input coordinates on an orthonormal basis of it, or the fitted stage indicators. The fit, the cross-validation and the rank are unchanged; the statistics, the permutation draws, the latent scores and the stage means are in the measured coordinates, and the loadings are the fitted model's. It needs three stages and is rejected with attribution and with the split interaction test, all before any fitting; it is omitted from :meth:to_dict while None. It has no CLI flag: it is a pilot measurement until the predictive-subspace validation reads it.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TrajectoryAnalysisParams:
    """Measurement settings; the defaults are the simulation harness's.

    ``forced_components`` fixes the latent rank (dimensionality sensitivity) and
    skips cross-validation; ``None`` selects it by double CV. ``seed`` seeds
    RRPP exactly as the harness does.

    ``covariate_latent_adjustment`` (``None``, ``"stage"`` or
    ``"group_stage"``) opts into covariate-aware latent construction: the
    basis is fitted on features residualized on the declared covariates,
    conditional on the stage or the group × stage indicators. It requires
    declared covariates and is omitted from :meth:`to_dict` while ``None``.

    ``min_components`` is the rank floor of the cross-validated latent space
    (default 2, so ``angle`` and ``shape`` are measured in at least two
    dimensions). ``1`` restores the unfloored 0.9.0 rule and normalizes to
    ``None``, which is omitted from :meth:`to_dict` and from the record's
    ``latent`` block, so a floor-1 analysis reproduces every 0.9.0 artifact.
    A floor below 1 is rejected before any fitting. The floor guarantees two
    dimensions, not a second axis with signal.

    ``residual_correction`` (``None``, ``"df"`` or ``"leverage"``) rescales the
    reduced model's residuals before RRPP permutes them (see
    :func:`motco.stats.permutation.RRPP`): ``"df"`` by κ = √(n / (n − r)),
    ``"leverage"`` by 1 / √(1 − h_ii). The observed statistics, latent space and
    stage means are unchanged; only the null moves. An unknown value is
    rejected before any fitting, and the setting is omitted from
    :meth:`to_dict` while ``None``.

    ``span_split_test`` (default ``False``) runs the split interaction test
    (:func:`motco.stats.interaction.interaction_split_test`) on the
    standardized features in the fitted PLS model's input coordinates, against
    ``qr(x_rotations_)``, with the trajectory models (covariates included), the
    seed, the permutations and the residual correction. It is omitted from
    :meth:`to_dict` while false and is not available with latent adjustment.

    ``interaction_scan`` (default ``False``) runs the per-feature interaction
    scan (:func:`motco.stats.interaction.interaction_feature_scan`) on the
    standardized features with the trajectory models (covariates included),
    the seed, the permutations and the residual correction. It uses neither
    the latent basis nor the bootstrap, so it is available with latent
    adjustment and with attribution, and it is omitted from :meth:`to_dict`
    while false. It reads the unweighted standardized features, so a block
    weighting leaves it unchanged.

    ``interaction_scan_by_block`` (default ``False``) runs that scan with the
    declared blocks as its block labels (``combination="block_bonferroni"``):
    the step-down runs within each block on the same draws, and with K blocks
    holding a non-degenerate feature each is tested at α/K, so every block has
    the same chance of a false hit whatever its size or noise. The F, the
    group differences and every non-scan output are unchanged; the global
    p-value, the adjusted p-values and the hits are the by-block ones. It
    requires ``interaction_scan`` (rejected before any fitting otherwise) and
    is omitted from :meth:`to_dict` while false.

    ``block_weighting`` (``None``, ``"equal_variance"`` or ``"mfa"``)
    multiplies every standardized block by one label-blind scalar fitted on
    the pooled sample — 1/√p_b (unit total variance per block) or the inverse
    standard deviation of the block's leading principal component — and fits
    the PLS space without per-feature rescaling, so the weights set the
    metric. ``delta`` is in that metric; ``angle``, ``shape`` and the p-values
    are comparable with an unweighted analysis. Attribution's original-unit
    mapping divides by the weights. An unknown kind is rejected before any
    fitting, and the setting is omitted from :meth:`to_dict` while ``None``.
    Unvalidated until the production latent-space selection reads it.

    ``sparsity`` (``None`` or a :class:`SparsitySettings`) fits the latent
    space with sparse stage-PLS-DA: every component loads on the selected
    fraction of the features (``joint``) or of each declared block
    (``block``), the rank and the fraction are cross-validated jointly, and
    the final model is a :class:`motco.stats.sparse_pls.SparsePLSDA`.
    Attribution, the split test and the interaction scan run unchanged on it,
    and it composes with latent adjustment and block weighting; with
    ``forced_components`` the ladder must hold one fraction. A malformed
    setting is rejected before any fitting, and the setting is omitted from
    :meth:`to_dict` while ``None``. Unvalidated until the production
    latent-space selection reads it.

    ``latent_coordinates`` (``None``, ``"predictive"``,
    ``"predictive_orthonormal"`` or ``"predictive_fitted"``) measures the
    trajectories on the fitted model's predictive subspace, the row space of
    its Y loadings (``min(rank, n_stages − 1)`` dimensions), as the simulation
    harness defines it: the scores projected on it, the input coordinates on
    an orthonormal basis of it, or the fitted stage indicators. The fit, the
    cross-validation and the rank are unchanged; the statistics, the
    permutation draws, the latent scores and the stage means are in the
    measured coordinates, and the loadings are the fitted model's. It needs
    three stages and is rejected with attribution and with the split
    interaction test, all before any fitting; it is omitted from
    :meth:`to_dict` while ``None``. It has no CLI flag: it is a pilot
    measurement until the predictive-subspace validation reads it.
    """

    permutations: int = 0
    seed: int | None = None
    n_jobs: int = 1
    orientation_estimator: str = "net_displacement"
    forced_components: int | None = None
    cv1_splits: int = 3
    cv2_splits: int = 4
    n_repeats: int = 5
    max_components: int = 20
    random_state: int = 1203
    attribution: AttributionDiagnosticSettings = field(default_factory=AttributionDiagnosticSettings)
    progress: bool = False
    covariate_latent_adjustment: str | None = None
    min_components: int | None = 2
    residual_correction: str | None = None
    span_split_test: bool = False
    interaction_scan: bool = False
    block_weighting: str | None = None
    sparsity: SparsitySettings | None = None
    interaction_scan_by_block: bool = False
    latent_coordinates: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        coordinates = self.latent_coordinates
        if coordinates is not None:
            if coordinates not in PREDICTIVE_COORDINATES:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Unknown latent_coordinates {coordinates!r}; allowed: {list(PREDICTIVE_COORDINATES)} or None."
                )
            if self.attribution.enabled:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"latent_coordinates={coordinates!r} cannot be combined with attribution: attribution is "
                    "defined on the fitted span's scores. Disable attribution or drop latent_coordinates."
                )
            if self.span_split_test:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"latent_coordinates={coordinates!r} cannot be combined with the split interaction test "
                    "(span_split_test): its span part is the fitted span. Drop one of the two settings."
                )
        floor = self.min_components
        if floor is not None:
            if isinstance(floor, bool) or not isinstance(floor, (int, np.integer)) or floor < 1:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"min_components must be an integer of at least 1, got {floor!r}.")
            # 1 is the unfloored 0.9.0 rule: held as ``None`` so the record stays byte-identical.
            object.__setattr__(self, "min_components", None if int(floor) == 1 else int(floor))
        if self.covariate_latent_adjustment is not None and self.covariate_latent_adjustment not in CONDITIONING_KINDS:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Unknown covariate_latent_adjustment {self.covariate_latent_adjustment!r}; allowed: "
                f"{list(CONDITIONING_KINDS)} or None."
            )
        if self.residual_correction is not None and self.residual_correction not in RESIDUAL_CORRECTIONS:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Unknown residual_correction {self.residual_correction!r}; allowed: "
                f"{list(RESIDUAL_CORRECTIONS)} or None."
            )
        if self.interaction_scan_by_block and not self.interaction_scan:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                "interaction_scan_by_block requires interaction_scan: the by-block combination is a way of "
                "running the per-feature scan. Set interaction_scan=True or drop interaction_scan_by_block."
            )
        if self.block_weighting is not None and self.block_weighting not in BLOCK_WEIGHTINGS:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Unknown block_weighting {self.block_weighting!r}; allowed: {list(BLOCK_WEIGHTINGS)} or None."
            )
        if self.sparsity is not None:
            if not isinstance(self.sparsity, SparsitySettings):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"sparsity must be a SparsitySettings or None, got {type(self.sparsity).__name__}."
                )
            if self.forced_components is not None and len(self.sparsity.keep_fractions) > 1:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"forced_components={self.forced_components} skips cross-validation, so the sparsity "
                    f"ladder {list(self.sparsity.keep_fractions)} cannot be selected over; give a single "
                    "keep fraction."
                )
        if self.orientation_estimator not in EVALUATION_ORIENTATION_ESTIMATORS:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Unknown orientation_estimator {self.orientation_estimator!r}; allowed: "
                f"{list(EVALUATION_ORIENTATION_ESTIMATORS)}."
            )
        if self.permutations < 0:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("permutations must be greater than or equal to 0.")
        if self.n_jobs == 0:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("n_jobs must be -1 or a non-zero integer.")
        settings = self.attribution
        if settings.enabled:
            if settings.bootstrap_replicates < 0:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("attribution.bootstrap_replicates must be greater than or equal to 0.")
            if settings.top_k < 1:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("attribution.top_k must be at least 1.")

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        data = asdict(self)
        if self.covariate_latent_adjustment is None:
            # Absent means the 0.8.0 analysis: its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("covariate_latent_adjustment")
        if self.min_components is None:
            # Floor 1 means the 0.9.0 rank rule: its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("min_components")
        if self.residual_correction is None:
            # Absent means the 0.12.0 null: its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("residual_correction")
        if not self.span_split_test:
            # Absent means the 0.17.0 analysis: its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("span_split_test")
        if not self.interaction_scan:
            # Absent means the 0.19.0 analysis: its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("interaction_scan")
        if self.block_weighting is None:
            # Absent means unweighted blocks (0.20.0): its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("block_weighting")
        if self.sparsity is None:
            # Absent means ordinary PLS-DA (0.21.0): its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("sparsity")
        if not self.interaction_scan_by_block:
            # Absent means the joint scan (0.22.0): its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("interaction_scan_by_block")
        if self.latent_coordinates is None:
            # Absent means the score measurement (0.23.0): its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("latent_coordinates")
        return data

    @property
    def resolved_min_components(self) -> int:
        """The rank floor the cross-validation runs with (1 when omitted)."""

        return self.min_components or 1

The analysis record plus the fitted representation.

record is JSON-safe. latent_scores are the per-sample PLS scores, pls_loadings the joint-feature rotations (block/feature columns first), stage_means the fitted latent LS-mean vector per group × stage in declared stage order, and attribution the full attribution result when it was requested.

latent_artifacts is the frozen measurement itself — the fitted PLS estimator, the standardized joint feature matrix the latent scores are its projection of, and the per-feature original scales — for callers that attribute or probe on exactly the analysed coordinates. It is held in memory only: it is never part of record, :meth:to_json or :func:write_analysis_outputs, and the estimator is never serialized.

interaction_scan is the per-feature scan table when the scan ran, one row per joint feature in the joint order: block, feature, ss_interaction, rss, f, p_value_adjusted (with permutations), degenerate and difference[<stage>] per declared stage (the second group minus the first, from the full model's LS means at the covariate reference row, in standardized units).

docs.title: analyze_trajectories(dataset, params=None)
docs.text:
Measure two groups' trajectories across ordered stages on real data.

Standardizes every block with pooled per-feature scalers (after its unit transform), concatenates the blocks in declared order as f"{block}__{feature}", builds the stage-supervised PLS-DA latent space (double-CV rank, or params.forced_components), estimates delta, angle (net displacement by default) and shape between the groups in that space and, when params.permutations > 0, their RRPP p-values. Records the selected rank, null summary, stage-mean spectrum, cell sizes, block units and software versions beside the statistics. Optionally runs frozen-model orientation attribution on the fitted estimator.

Declared covariates (dataset.covariate_cols) are appended additively to the full (group × stage) and reduced (group + stage) trajectory models, so RRPP permutes residuals of the reduced model with covariates. Every LS-mean is evaluated at the pooled covariate mean; delta, angle and shape do not depend on that reference. The latent space is fitted without the covariates unless params.covariate_latent_adjustment is set: then the pooled-standardized features are residualized on the covariates conditional on the stage ("stage") or group × stage ("group_stage") indicators before the basis is fitted (per training set inside the cross-validation, at the pooled scale), the raw features are projected onto that basis, and the trajectory model, LS-means and RRPP are unchanged.

With covariates, attribution uses the covariate-adjusted cell means at the record's covariate reference row (the same design columns), so its means project through the fitted estimator to the latent stage means, and its bootstrap refits the covariate coefficients in every resample. Attribution is not available with latent adjustment; the request is rejected before fitting.

params.residual_correction rescales the reduced model's residuals (covariates included) before RRPP permutes them; the record's measurement block then states the correction it applied.

params.span_split_test adds a span_split block after measurement: the group × stage interaction of the standardized features, split into the fitted PLS span and its orthogonal complement and tested with RRPP's serial draws at the analysis's seed. It is rejected with latent adjustment before fitting.

params.interaction_scan adds an interaction_scan block after measurement and any span_split block, and the per-feature table TrajectoryAnalysisResult.interaction_scan: each standardized feature's interaction F with the covariate-adjusted models, combined by the maximum with step-down max-T adjusted p-values under RRPP's serial draws at the analysis's seed. It reads the features and models only, so latent adjustment and attribution leave it unchanged. With params.interaction_scan_by_block the declared blocks share the scan's familywise error equally, and the block also names the combination, the number of blocks tested and each block's maximum and own p-value.

params.latent_coordinates measures on the fitted model's predictive subspace: latent_scores and stage_means are in the measured coordinates, pls_loadings stays the fitted model's, and the record's measurement block gains latent_coordinates (the value and the measured dimension).

def analyze_trajectories(
    dataset: TrajectoryDataset,
    params: TrajectoryAnalysisParams | None = None,
) -> TrajectoryAnalysisResult:
    """Measure two groups' trajectories across ordered stages on real data.

    Standardizes every block with pooled per-feature scalers (after its unit
    transform), concatenates the blocks in declared order as
    ``f"{block}__{feature}"``, builds the stage-supervised PLS-DA latent space
    (double-CV rank, or ``params.forced_components``), estimates ``delta``,
    ``angle`` (net displacement by default) and ``shape`` between the groups
    in that space and, when ``params.permutations > 0``, their RRPP p-values.
    Records the selected rank, null summary, stage-mean spectrum, cell sizes,
    block units and software versions beside the statistics. Optionally runs
    frozen-model orientation attribution on the fitted estimator.

    Declared covariates (``dataset.covariate_cols``) are appended additively to
    the full (group × stage) and reduced (group + stage) trajectory models, so
    RRPP permutes residuals of the reduced model with covariates. Every LS-mean
    is evaluated at the pooled covariate mean; ``delta``, ``angle`` and
    ``shape`` do not depend on that reference. The latent space is fitted
    without the covariates unless ``params.covariate_latent_adjustment`` is
    set: then the pooled-standardized features are residualized on the
    covariates conditional on the stage (``"stage"``) or group × stage
    (``"group_stage"``) indicators before the basis is fitted (per training set
    inside the cross-validation, at the pooled scale), the raw features are
    projected onto that basis, and the trajectory model, LS-means and RRPP are
    unchanged.

    With covariates, attribution uses the covariate-adjusted cell means at the
    record's covariate reference row (the same design columns), so its means
    project through the fitted estimator to the latent stage means, and its
    bootstrap refits the covariate coefficients in every resample. Attribution
    is not available with latent adjustment; the request is rejected before
    fitting.

    ``params.residual_correction`` rescales the reduced model's residuals
    (covariates included) before RRPP permutes them; the record's
    ``measurement`` block then states the correction it applied.

    ``params.span_split_test`` adds a ``span_split`` block after
    ``measurement``: the group × stage interaction of the standardized
    features, split into the fitted PLS span and its orthogonal complement and
    tested with RRPP's serial draws at the analysis's seed. It is rejected with
    latent adjustment before fitting.

    ``params.interaction_scan`` adds an ``interaction_scan`` block after
    ``measurement`` and any ``span_split`` block, and the per-feature table
    ``TrajectoryAnalysisResult.interaction_scan``: each standardized feature's
    interaction F with the covariate-adjusted models, combined by the maximum
    with step-down max-T adjusted p-values under RRPP's serial draws at the
    analysis's seed. It reads the features and models only, so latent
    adjustment and attribution leave it unchanged. With
    ``params.interaction_scan_by_block`` the declared blocks share the scan's
    familywise error equally, and the block also names the combination, the
    number of blocks tested and each block's maximum and own p-value.

    ``params.latent_coordinates`` measures on the fitted model's predictive
    subspace: ``latent_scores`` and ``stage_means`` are in the measured
    coordinates, ``pls_loadings`` stays the fitted model's, and the record's
    ``measurement`` block gains ``latent_coordinates`` (the value and the
    measured dimension).
    """

    params = params or TrajectoryAnalysisParams()
    if params.latent_coordinates is not None and len(dataset.stage_order) < 3:
        raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
            f"latent_coordinates={params.latent_coordinates!r} needs at least three stages: its subspace has "
            f"n_stages − 1 dimensions, and this dataset has {len(dataset.stage_order)} stage(s) "
            f"{list(dataset.stage_order)}."
        )
    covariates = dataset.covariate_design
    if params.covariate_latent_adjustment is not None and covariates is None:
        raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
            f"Latent adjustment ({params.covariate_latent_adjustment!r}) requires declared covariates; "
            "declare covariate_cols on the dataset or drop the setting."
        )
    if params.covariate_latent_adjustment is not None and params.attribution.enabled:
        raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
            "Attribution is not available with latent adjustment: that basis is fitted on "
            "covariate-residualized features, and attribution on it is not defined. Disable attribution or "
            "drop the latent adjustment."
        )
    if params.covariate_latent_adjustment is not None and params.span_split_test:
        raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
            f"The split interaction test (span_split_test) is not available with latent adjustment "
            f"(covariate_latent_adjustment={params.covariate_latent_adjustment!r}): it is defined on the "
            "covariate-blind basis. Drop one of the two settings."
        )
    start = perf_counter()
    # The residualization design is checked before the trajectory models, so its rank error comes first.
    nuisance = _latent_nuisance(_working_frame(dataset), covariates, params.covariate_latent_adjustment)
    inputs = _trajectory_inputs(dataset, params)
    blocks, order, transforms, scalers = inputs.blocks, inputs.order, inputs.transforms, inputs.scalers
    X = inputs.features
    working = inputs.working
    design = inputs.design
    group_levels, stage_levels = inputs.group_levels, inputs.stage_levels
    model_full, model_reduced, ls_means = inputs.model_full, inputs.model_reduced, inputs.ls_means

    integration_params: dict[str, Any] = {
        "cv1_splits": params.cv1_splits,
        "cv2_splits": params.cv2_splits,
        "n_repeats": params.n_repeats,
        "max_components": params.max_components,
        "random_state": params.random_state,
        "n_jobs": params.n_jobs,
    }
    if params.forced_components is not None:
        integration_params["forced_components"] = params.forced_components
    if params.block_weighting is not None:
        integration_params["block_weighting"] = params.block_weighting
    if params.sparsity is not None:
        integration_params["sparsity"] = params.sparsity.integration_param()
    sample_ids = dataset.sample_ids
    try:
        latent = fit_pls_latent_space(
            X,
            working[_STAGE],
            integration_params,
            stage_col=dataset.stage_col,
            sample_ids=sample_ids,
            layer_feature_counts={name: int(frame.shape[1]) for name, frame in blocks.items()},
            layers_metadata={},
            original_scales=_joint_original_scales(scalers, order, X.columns),
            methylation_units=_methylation_units(transforms),
            nuisance=nuisance,
            min_components=params.resolved_min_components,
            **({} if params.latent_coordinates is None else {"coordinates": params.latent_coordinates}),
        )
    except SimulationEvaluationError as exc:
        raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(str(exc)) from exc

    observed_deltas, observed_angles, observed_shapes, observed_spectra = estimate_difference(
        Y=latent.matrix,
        model_matrix=model_full,
        LS_means=ls_means,
        contrast=design.contrast,
        return_spectra=True,
        orientation_estimator=params.orientation_estimator,
    )
    config_spectrum = _config_spectrum_block(observed_spectra, group_levels)
    shape_available = len(stage_levels) >= 3
    pair_statistics = _extract_pair_statistics(
        observed_deltas, observed_angles, observed_shapes, shape_available=shape_available
    )

    p_values: dict[str, float] = {}
    null_summary: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    correction_record: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    if params.permutations > 0:
        if params.residual_correction is not None:
            try:
                correction_record = _residual_correction_record(model_reduced, params.residual_correction)
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(str(exc)) from exc
        dist_delta, dist_angle, dist_shape, dist_eigengap = RRPP(
            latent.matrix,
            model_full,
            model_reduced,
            ls_means,
            design.contrast,
            permutations=params.permutations,
            n_jobs=params.n_jobs,
            progress=params.progress,
            seed=params.seed,
            return_eigengaps=True,
            orientation_estimator=params.orientation_estimator,
            residual_correction=params.residual_correction,
        )
        null_values = _extract_null_distributions(
            dist_delta, dist_angle, dist_shape, shape_available=shape_available
        )
        p_values = {
            statistic: _empirical_p_value(null_values[statistic], observed)
            for statistic, observed in pair_statistics.items()
            if statistic in null_values and np.isfinite(observed)
        }
        null_summary = _summarize_null_distributions(null_values)
        config_spectrum["permutation_pooled_eigengap"] = _summarize_permutation_eigengaps(dist_eigengap)

    latent_scores = latent.matrix.copy()
    latent_scores.index.name = dataset.sample_col
    artifacts = latent.artifacts
    assert artifacts is not None  # the PLS core always returns its fitted artifacts
    span_split_record = (
        _span_split_record(artifacts, model_full, model_reduced, params) if params.span_split_test else None
    )
    scan_record, scan_table = (
        _interaction_scan_outputs(_scan_inputs(inputs), params) if params.interaction_scan else (None, None)
    )
    # The loadings are the fitted model's, one column per fitted component, whatever the measured coordinates.
    fitted_components = [f"pls_{i}" for i in range(np.asarray(artifacts.model.x_rotations_).shape[1])]
    pls_loadings = _loadings_frame(artifacts.model, X.columns, fitted_components)
    betas = np.asarray(estimate_betas(model_full, latent.matrix.to_numpy(dtype=float)), dtype=float)
    stage_means = _stage_means_frame(
        ls_means,
        betas,
        group_levels,
        stage_levels,
        list(latent.matrix.columns),
    )

    attribution_record, attribution_result = _run_attribution(dataset, params, latent, X, transforms, covariates)
    cell_sizes = {
        group: {
            stage: int(
                (
                    (dataset.metadata[dataset.group_col].astype(str) == group)
                    & (dataset.metadata[dataset.stage_col].astype(str) == stage)
                ).sum()
            )
            for stage in stage_levels
        }
        for group in group_levels
    }
    record: dict[str, Any] = {
        "schema_version": ANALYSIS_SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "statistics": pair_statistics,
        "p_values": p_values,
        "null_summary": null_summary,
        "config_spectrum": config_spectrum,
        "latent": latent.metadata,
        **({"sparsity": latent.metadata["sparsity"]} if "sparsity" in latent.metadata else {}),
        "design": {
            "group_col": dataset.group_col,
            "stage_col": dataset.stage_col,
            "sample_col": dataset.sample_col,
            "group_levels": group_levels,
            "stage_levels": stage_levels,
            "cell_sizes": cell_sizes,
            "contrast": design.contrast,
            "n_samples": len(sample_ids),
        },
        **(
            {"covariates": _covariate_record(dataset, covariates, betas, list(latent.matrix.columns))}
            if covariates is not None
            else {}
        ),
        **(
            {"latent_adjustment": _latent_adjustment_record(dataset, artifacts.latent_adjustment)}
            if artifacts.latent_adjustment is not None
            else {}
        ),
        "blocks": [
            {
                "name": block.name,
                "n_features": int(block.values.shape[1]),
                "transform": block.transform,
                "units": _TRANSFORM_UNITS[block.transform],
            }
            for block in dataset.blocks
        ],
        **(
            {"block_weighting": _block_weighting_record(params.block_weighting, dataset, scalers)}
            if params.block_weighting is not None
            else {}
        ),
        "measurement": {
            "orientation_estimator": params.orientation_estimator,
            "selected_lv": latent.metadata["selected_lv"],
            "component_selection": latent.metadata["component_selection"],
            **(
                {
                    "latent_coordinates": {
                        "value": params.latent_coordinates,
                        "measured_dimension": latent.metadata["measured_dimension"],
                    }
                }
                if params.latent_coordinates is not None
                else {}
            ),
            "permutations": params.permutations,
            "seed": params.seed,
            "n_jobs": params.n_jobs,
            **({"residual_correction": correction_record} if correction_record is not None else {}),
            "shape_available": shape_available,
            "runtime_seconds": perf_counter() - start,
        },
        **({"span_split": span_split_record} if span_split_record is not None else {}),
        **({"interaction_scan": scan_record} if scan_record is not None else {}),
        "params": params.to_dict(),
        "software": _software_versions(),
        "attribution": attribution_record,
    }
    return TrajectoryAnalysisResult(
        record=_json_safe(record),
        latent_scores=latent_scores,
        pls_loadings=pls_loadings,
        stage_means=stage_means,
        attribution=attribution_result,
        latent_artifacts=artifacts,
        interaction_scan=scan_table,
    )

Writes result.json, latent_scores.csv, pls_loadings.csv, stage_means.csv, when attribution ran, its tables under attribution/ and, when the interaction scan ran, interaction_scan.csv. Refuses to touch a directory that already holds result.json unless overwrite is set.

def write_analysis_outputs(
    result: TrajectoryAnalysisResult,
    out_dir: str | Path,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
) -> dict[str, Path]:
    """Write the analysis artifact to ``out_dir`` and return the written paths.

    Writes ``result.json``, ``latent_scores.csv``, ``pls_loadings.csv``,
    ``stage_means.csv``, when attribution ran, its tables under
    ``attribution/`` and, when the interaction scan ran,
    ``interaction_scan.csv``. Refuses to touch a directory that already holds
    ``result.json`` unless ``overwrite`` is set.
    """

    directory = Path(out_dir)
    result_path = directory / "result.json"
    if result_path.exists() and not overwrite:
        raise FileExistsError(f"{result_path} already exists; pass overwrite=True to replace the analysis.")
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    paths: dict[str, Path] = {}
    result_path.write_text(json.dumps(result.record, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    paths["result"] = result_path
    paths["latent_scores"] = directory / "latent_scores.csv"
    result.latent_scores.to_csv(paths["latent_scores"])
    paths["pls_loadings"] = directory / "pls_loadings.csv"
    result.pls_loadings.to_csv(paths["pls_loadings"], index=False)
    paths["stage_means"] = directory / "stage_means.csv"
    result.stage_means.to_csv(paths["stage_means"], index=False)
    if result.attribution is not None:
        for name, path in write_attribution_outputs(result.attribution, directory / "attribution").items():
            paths[f"attribution/{name}"] = path
    if result.interaction_scan is not None:
        paths["interaction_scan"] = directory / "interaction_scan.csv"
        result.interaction_scan.to_csv(paths["interaction_scan"], index=False)
    return paths

docs.title: Orientation Driver Attribution
docs.text:
Orientation attribution explains a two-group, multi-stage difference after an upstream trajectory analysis has identified the shared PLS space of interest. Pass the pooled, aligned feature matrix, matching group/stage metadata, and the one fitted PLS estimator to analyze_orientation_attribution.

The analysis orders groups and stages deterministically unless explicit levels are supplied. For every adjacent stage pair it reports each group's raw transition and path length, the unit directional contrast, the same contrast after PLS score projection and inverse transformation, and the signed residual observed - pls_captured. Observed feature values remain in the result; the reconstruction is a parallel, lossy view rather than a replacement.

docs.title: Two decompositions
docs.text:
Attribution reports two decompositions, and they explain different quantities.

The principal-orientation block decomposes the tested angle estimand: principal-axis divergence, the contrast between the groups' signed leading principal axes. It applies the same functional the statistic is built from (motco.stats.trajectory.principal_orientation) to each group's stage-mean configuration, observed and PLS-reconstructed, so the explanation and the test cannot drift apart.

The per-adjacent-transition blocks describe where along the trajectory the groups' step directions diverge. They are a per-step description, not the tested estimand; the two decompositions coincide only for a two-stage design, where the configuration is rank one and PC1 is the transition direction.

Both appear in the tabular outputs under the transition_id column — the transitions as from->to, the principal block under principal_component_id (default principal), which is validated against the stage-derived identifiers so the two can never collide.

docs.title: Degeneracy and availability
docs.text:
A principal axis exists for any configuration with variance, but it is only resolvable when one axis dominates. The result reports each contributing configuration's relative eigengap and flags the principal contrast degenerate when any falls below eigengap_threshold (default 0.05). The flagged contrast is still returned: degeneracy is a property of the data, so callers stratify on the flag rather than lose rows.

That is distinct from unavailability. A trajectory whose net displacement from first stage to last is at or below zero_tolerance is closed, and no direction is defined at all — that group's principal orientation is marked unavailable, exactly as a zero-length transition is.

docs.title: Units and stability
docs.text:
Effects are reported in the input coordinate units, normally pooled standardized units. Positive per-feature scales can be supplied to add original-unit columns. These scales only convert reported effects; they never change PLS geometry.

Bootstrap resampling is independent within every group-by-stage cell and uses the same fitted model and preprocessing contract in every replicate. The result records the seed, requested count, valid count, sign stability, and top-k selection frequency, for the principal-orientation block as well as the transitions. Each replicate's principal axis is signed by that replicate's own net displacement, so resampling noise cannot flip the axis; a replicate whose trajectory closes contributes no contrast and counts as invalid. Bootstrap is available for arithmetic and covariate-adjusted means (below); a precomputed mean table is accepted with stability marked unavailable.

docs.title: Covariate-adjusted means
docs.text:
Pass covariates (numeric design columns, row-aligned with X; code factors as indicator columns) to attribute from covariate-adjusted cell means instead of arithmetic ones. Each group × stage mean is then the least-squares mean of the cell-means model with the covariates added, evaluated at a reference covariate row c_ref (covariate_reference, by default the column means):

m̂_gs = x̄_gs − γ̂ᵀ (c̄_gs − c_ref)

where x̄_gs and c̄_gs are the cell's feature and covariate means and γ̂ holds the covariate coefficients estimated within cells. This is the model the real-data analysis fits in the latent space, here fitted in feature space, so projecting the adjusted means through the fitted PLS model gives the analysis's latent stage means. The reconstructed and residual components follow from the adjusted means as they do from arithmetic ones.

  • Reference-row invariance. c_ref shifts every cell by the same vector γ̂ᵀ c_ref, so transitions, path lengths and both contrast blocks do not depend on it. Only the means tables move.
  • Bootstrap refit. Each replicate draws the same within-cell resample as attribution without covariates for the same seed, refits γ̂ on the resampled rows and evaluates the means at the fixed full-sample c_ref. The fitted preprocessing and PLS model stay frozen, so stability includes the uncertainty of estimating the covariate coefficients.
  • Rank-deficient replicates. Covariates collinear within cells (for example, constant within every cell) are an error on the full sample. In a resample, for example one that omits the only sample carrying a rare factor level, they make the replicate invalid. Such a replicate contributes no contrast to any block, is excluded from every valid count, and is counted in the configuration row bootstrap_rank_deficient_replicates.

The configuration records mean_source = covariate_adjusted, the covariate columns in order and the reference row. The interpretation table adds an adjustment_boundary: adjusted effects assume an additive linear covariate model evaluated at the reference row, and adjustment does not remove unmeasured confounding. covariates cannot be combined with a precomputed mean table. Without covariates every output is unchanged.

docs.title: Labels and interpretation
docs.text:
Feature-to-module or feature-to-pathway labels are optional and must be a complete one-to-one mapping supplied by the caller. Aggregate tables preserve the labels and mark their source as caller-supplied. Aggregation is not a pathway annotation service and does not establish biological causality.

The result contains no p-values or significance decisions. Attribution should be run after the calling workflow has made any global orientation inference decision. It describes associations implied by one frozen shared PLS model; the inverse reconstruction is not unique, and bootstrap stability is conditional on that fitted representation.

Reports both decompositions described in the module docstring: the principal-orientation contrast, which decomposes the tested angle estimand and carries a relative-eigengap degeneracy qualifier, and the per-adjacent-transition contrasts, which describe where along the trajectory the group directions diverge. The two coincide only for a two-stage design.
