def analyze_orientation_attribution(
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    metadata: pd.DataFrame,
    model: Any,
    *,
    group_col: str = "group",
    stage_col: str = "stage",
    feature_cols: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    groups: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    stages: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    mean_table: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    precomputed_means: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    covariates: pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray | None = None,
    covariate_reference: Sequence[float] | pd.Series | Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    original_scales: Sequence[float] | pd.Series | Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    feature_scales: Sequence[float] | pd.Series | Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    feature_groups: Mapping[str, str] | pd.Series | pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    group_labels: Mapping[str, str] | pd.Series | pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    label_namespace: str = "module",
    bootstrap_replicates: int = 0,
    bootstrap_seed: int | None = 0,
    top_k: int = 10,
    zero_tolerance: float = 1e-12,
    eigengap_threshold: float = 0.05,
    principal_component_id: str = "principal",
    sample_id_col: str | None = None,
) -> OrientationAttributionResult:
    """Attribute two-group trajectory orientation differences.

    Reports both decompositions described in the module docstring: the
    principal-orientation contrast, which decomposes the tested ``angle``
    estimand and carries a relative-eigengap degeneracy qualifier, and the
    per-adjacent-transition contrasts, which describe where along the trajectory
    the group directions diverge. The two coincide only for a two-stage design.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X:
        Aligned feature matrix in the exact coordinate system consumed by
        ``model``. Observed values are never overwritten by reconstructions.
    metadata:
        Row-aligned metadata containing ``group_col`` and ``stage_col``.
    model:
        One already fitted pooled PLS estimator exposing ``transform`` and
        ``inverse_transform``. It is reused for all groups and replicates.
    mean_table, precomputed_means:
        Optional complete group-by-stage table. It may have a two-level
        MultiIndex or explicit group/stage columns. When supplied, bootstrap
        resampling is unavailable because row-level sampling semantics are not
        defined for precomputed means. Exclusive with ``covariates``.
    covariates:
        Optional numeric covariate design columns, row-aligned with ``X`` (a
        DataFrame must share its index; an array's columns are named
        ``covariate_0`` …). Every cell mean is then the least-squares mean of
        ``X ~ cells + covariates`` at ``covariate_reference`` (see the module
        docstring), and each bootstrap replicate refits the covariate
        coefficients on its resampled rows. Categorical covariates are the
        caller's to code as indicator columns. Covariates collinear within the
        group × stage cells are an error.
    covariate_reference:
        The covariate row the adjusted means are evaluated at: a mapping or
        Series over the covariate columns, or a sequence in their order. The
        default is the column means. It moves the means tables only.
    original_scales, feature_scales:
        Optional positive per-feature scale in canonical feature order. The
        aliases are accepted for readability at call sites; supplying both is
        an error.
    feature_groups, group_labels:
        Optional one-to-one caller-supplied feature-to-label mapping. The
        aliases are accepted for readability at call sites.
    eigengap_threshold:
        Relative-eigengap level at or above which a stage-mean configuration is
        treated as having a well-separated principal axis. A contributing
        configuration below it flags the principal-orientation contrast as
        degenerate; the contrast is still returned, so callers stratify rather
        than lose rows. The default (0.05) separates the audit's resolvable
        replicates from its near-isotropic independent-baseline draws.
    principal_component_id:
        Reserved identifier carrying the principal-orientation component in the
        tabular outputs' ``transition_id`` column. It is validated against the
        stage-derived transition ids so the two can never collide.

    Returns
    -------
    OrientationAttributionResult
        Frozen typed records and DataFrame views for means, transitions, the
        principal-orientation block, feature effects, aggregates, and bootstrap
        stability.
    """
    if mean_table is not None and precomputed_means is not None:
        raise AttributionError("Provide only one of mean_table and precomputed_means.")
    if covariates is not None and (mean_table is not None or precomputed_means is not None):
        raise AttributionError(
            "Provide only one mean source: a precomputed mean table, or covariates for adjusted means."
        )
    if original_scales is not None and feature_scales is not None:
        raise AttributionError("Provide only one of original_scales and feature_scales.")
    if feature_groups is not None and group_labels is not None:
        raise AttributionError("Provide only one of feature_groups and group_labels.")
    if not isinstance(label_namespace, str) or not label_namespace.strip():
        raise AttributionError("label_namespace must be a non-empty string.")
    if precomputed_means is not None:
        mean_table = precomputed_means
    if feature_scales is not None:
        original_scales = feature_scales
    if group_labels is not None:
        feature_groups = group_labels

    feature_frame, metadata_frame, feature_names = _validate_inputs(
        X,
        metadata,
        model,
        group_col,
        stage_col,
        feature_cols,
        sample_id_col,
    )
    ordered_groups = cast(
        tuple[str, str], _ordered_levels(metadata_frame[group_col], groups, 2, "groups")
    )
    ordered_stages = _ordered_levels(metadata_frame[stage_col], stages, 2, "stages")
    _validate_cells(metadata_frame, group_col, stage_col, ordered_groups, ordered_stages)
    scale_values = _validate_scales(original_scales, feature_names)
    label_values = _validate_feature_groups(feature_groups, feature_names)
    adjustment = _validate_covariates(covariates, covariate_reference, feature_frame.index)

    if adjustment is not None:
        cells = _cell_codes(metadata_frame, group_col, stage_col, ordered_groups, ordered_stages)
        try:
            means_array = _adjusted_means(
                feature_frame.to_numpy(dtype=float),
                adjustment.matrix,
                cells,
                adjustment,
                ordered_groups,
                ordered_stages,
            )
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise AttributionError(
                f"Covariates {list(adjustment.names)} are collinear with the group × stage cells or with one "
                f"another, so covariate-adjusted cell means are not identified: {exc}"
            ) from exc
        mean_source = "covariate_adjusted"
    elif mean_table is None:
        means_array = _arithmetic_means(
            feature_frame,
            metadata_frame,
            group_col,
            stage_col,
            ordered_groups,
            ordered_stages,
        )
        mean_source = "arithmetic"
    else:
        means_array = _precomputed_mean_array(
            mean_table,
            feature_names,
            ordered_groups,
            ordered_stages,
            group_col,
            stage_col,
        )
        mean_source = "precomputed"
        if bootstrap_replicates:
            raise AttributionError(
                "bootstrap_replicates must be zero when mean_table contains precomputed means; "
                "row-level bootstrap semantics are unavailable."
            )

    _validate_bootstrap_settings(bootstrap_replicates, top_k, zero_tolerance)
    _validate_principal_settings(eigengap_threshold, principal_component_id, ordered_stages)
    reconstructed_array = _reconstruct_means(means_array, model, feature_names)
    transitions = _build_transitions(
        means_array,
        reconstructed_array,
        ordered_groups,
        ordered_stages,
        zero_tolerance,
    )
    principal = _build_principal_orientation(
        means_array,
        reconstructed_array,
        ordered_groups,
        ordered_stages,
        zero_tolerance,
        eigengap_threshold,
        principal_component_id,
    )
    model_components = _model_components(model)
    bootstrap_records, rank_deficient = _bootstrap(
        feature_frame,
        metadata_frame,
        group_col,
        stage_col,
        ordered_groups,
        ordered_stages,
        model,
        feature_names,
        scale_values,
        bootstrap_replicates,
        bootstrap_seed,
        top_k,
        zero_tolerance,
        principal_component_id,
        adjustment,
    )
    config = AttributionConfig(
        group_column=group_col,
        stage_column=stage_col,
        feature_names=feature_names,
        groups=ordered_groups,
        stages=ordered_stages,
        mean_source=mean_source,
        input_units="standardized_input",
        original_units_available=scale_values is not None,
        zero_tolerance=float(zero_tolerance),
        bootstrap_replicates=int(bootstrap_replicates),
        bootstrap_seed=bootstrap_seed,
        top_k=int(top_k),
        model_components=model_components,
        label_namespace=label_namespace if label_values is not None else None,
        label_source="caller-supplied" if label_values is not None else None,
        eigengap_threshold=float(eigengap_threshold),
        principal_component_id=principal_component_id,
        covariate_columns=adjustment.names if adjustment is not None else None,
        covariate_reference=(
            dict(zip(adjustment.names, map(float, adjustment.reference))) if adjustment is not None else None
        ),
        rank_deficient_replicates=rank_deficient if adjustment is not None else None,
    )
    bootstrap_lookup = {
        (record.transition_id, record.component): record for record in bootstrap_records
    }
    feature_effects, feature_records = _feature_effect_table(
        transitions,
        principal,
        feature_names,
        scale_values,
        bootstrap_lookup,
        label_values,
        label_namespace,
        bootstrap_replicates,
    )
    aggregate_effects, aggregate_records = _aggregate_effect_table(
        feature_effects,
        feature_names,
        label_values,
        label_namespace,
        bootstrap_replicates,
    )
    transition_summaries, transition_vectors = _transition_tables(
        transitions,
        ordered_groups,
        feature_names,
    )
    principal_summaries, principal_vectors = _principal_tables(
        principal,
        ordered_groups,
        feature_names,
    )
    bootstrap_table = _bootstrap_table(bootstrap_records, feature_names)
    means_table = _means_table(means_array, ordered_groups, ordered_stages, feature_names)
    reconstructed_table = _means_table(
        reconstructed_array, ordered_groups, ordered_stages, feature_names
    )
    interpretation = InterpretationMetadata(
        statement="Attribution describes associations implied by one fitted shared PLS representation.",
        causal_boundary="Feature, module, and pathway effects are not causal claims.",
        significance_boundary=(
            "No p-values or significance decisions are produced; external orientation inference remains the caller's "
            "responsibility."
        ),
        reconstruction_boundary=(
            "PLS-captured effects are a lossy inverse-transform view and are not a unique inverse of measured features."
        ),
        bootstrap_boundary=(
            "Bootstrap stability is conditional on the fitted preprocessing contract and frozen PLS model."
        ),
        label_source="caller-supplied" if label_values is not None else None,
        decomposition_boundary=(
            f"The '{principal_component_id}' component decomposes the tested angle estimand — principal-axis "
            "divergence between the groups' signed leading principal axes — while per-adjacent-transition "
            "contrasts describe where along the trajectory the group directions diverge; the two coincide only "
            "for two-stage designs. A degenerate principal contrast is reported with its flag and MUST NOT be "
            "read as a well-defined orientation."
        ),
        adjustment_boundary=ADJUSTMENT_BOUNDARY if adjustment is not None else None,
    )
    return OrientationAttributionResult(
        config=config,
        means=means_table,
        reconstructed_means=reconstructed_table,
        transitions=tuple(transitions),
        principal_orientation=principal,
        feature_effects=feature_effects,
        transition_summaries=transition_summaries,
        transition_vectors=transition_vectors,
        principal_summaries=principal_summaries,
        principal_vectors=principal_vectors,
        aggregate_effects=aggregate_effects,
        bootstrap_summaries=bootstrap_table,
        interpretation=interpretation,
        feature_records=tuple(feature_records),
        aggregate_records=tuple(aggregate_records),
        bootstrap_records=tuple(bootstrap_records),
    )

docs.title: motco.stats.attribution.attribution_frames(result)
docs.text:
Return all findings-ready tables for result.

The covariate rows of configuration and the adjustment_boundary row of interpretation appear only for covariate-adjusted means.

Source code in src/motco/stats/attribution.py 
def attribution_frames(result: OrientationAttributionResult) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return all findings-ready tables for ``result``.

    The covariate rows of ``configuration`` and the ``adjustment_boundary`` row
    of ``interpretation`` appear only for covariate-adjusted means.
    """

    adjustment_settings: list[tuple[str, Any]] = []
    if result.config.covariate_columns is not None:
        adjustment_settings = [
            ("covariate_columns", list(result.config.covariate_columns)),
            ("covariate_reference", dict(result.config.covariate_reference or {})),
            ("bootstrap_rank_deficient_replicates", result.config.rank_deficient_replicates),
        ]
    adjustment_fields: list[tuple[str, Any]] = []
    if result.interpretation.adjustment_boundary is not None:
        adjustment_fields = [("adjustment_boundary", result.interpretation.adjustment_boundary)]
    configuration = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            ("group_column", result.config.group_column),
            ("stage_column", result.config.stage_column),
            ("feature_names", list(result.config.feature_names)),
            ("groups", list(result.config.groups)),
            ("stages", list(result.config.stages)),
            ("mean_source", result.config.mean_source),
            ("input_units", result.config.input_units),
            ("original_units_available", result.config.original_units_available),
            ("zero_tolerance", result.config.zero_tolerance),
            ("bootstrap_replicates", result.config.bootstrap_replicates),
            ("bootstrap_seed", result.config.bootstrap_seed),
            ("top_k", result.config.top_k),
            ("model_components", result.config.model_components),
            ("label_namespace", result.config.label_namespace),
            ("label_source", result.config.label_source),
            ("eigengap_threshold", result.config.eigengap_threshold),
            ("principal_component_id", result.config.principal_component_id),
            *adjustment_settings,
        ],
        columns=["setting", "value"],
    )
    interpretation = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            ("statement", result.interpretation.statement),
            ("causal_boundary", result.interpretation.causal_boundary),
            ("significance_boundary", result.interpretation.significance_boundary),
            ("reconstruction_boundary", result.interpretation.reconstruction_boundary),
            ("bootstrap_boundary", result.interpretation.bootstrap_boundary),
            ("label_source", result.interpretation.label_source),
            ("decomposition_boundary", result.interpretation.decomposition_boundary),
            *adjustment_fields,
        ],
        columns=["field", "value"],
    )
    return {
        "means": result.means.copy(),
        "reconstructed_means": result.reconstructed_means.copy(),
        "feature_effects": result.feature_effects.copy(),
        "transition_summaries": result.transition_summaries.copy(),
        "transition_vectors": result.transition_vectors.copy(),
        "principal_orientation": result.principal_summaries.copy(),
        "principal_orientation_vectors": result.principal_vectors.copy(),
        "aggregate_effects": result.aggregate_effects.copy(),
        "bootstrap_summaries": result.bootstrap_summaries.copy(),
        "configuration": configuration,
        "interpretation": interpretation,
    }

docs.title: motco.stats.attribution.write_attribution_outputs(result, output_dir)
docs.text:
Write attribution tables as CSV files and return their paths.

Source code in src/motco/stats/attribution.py 
def write_attribution_outputs(
    result: OrientationAttributionResult,
    output_dir: str | Path,
) -> dict[str, Path]:
    """Write attribution tables as CSV files and return their paths."""

    directory = Path(output_dir)
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    paths: dict[str, Path] = {}
    for name, frame in attribution_frames(result).items():
        path = directory / f"{name}.csv"
        frame.to_csv(path, index=False)
        paths[name] = path
    return paths

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
The motco command-line interface provides five subcommands.

usage: motco [-h] [--version] [--verbose] {plsr,snf,simulate,de,analyze} ...

MOTCO CLI: PLSR, SNF, group differences, and real-data trajectory analysis

positional arguments:
  {plsr,snf,simulate,de,analyze}
    plsr                Run PLS-DA with double cross-validation
    snf                 Similarity Network Fusion
    simulate            Generate a semi-synthetic multi-omics toy dataset
                        (numpy generator, no R)
    de                  Group differences on trajectories (estimate or RRPP)
    analyze             Real-data trajectory analysis with the validated
                        pipeline (PLS latent space, RRPP)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
  --verbose             Enable debug logging to stderr

For real data, use motco analyze. It runs the measurement the simulation studies validated, in one step. plsr and de are lower-level building blocks.

docs.title: motco plsr
docs.text:
Run PLS-DA with double cross-validation. Input is one of: omics layer CSVs (--input, repeated; standardized and concatenated) with a metadata CSV holding the label (--metadata, --label-col); a single CSV with predictors and the label column (--data, --label-col); or separate predictor/label CSVs (--x / --y). --out-scores writes the final model's latent scores, the input motco de takes as --Y.

usage: motco plsr [-h] [--input INPUT] [--metadata METADATA] [--data DATA]
                  [--label-col LABEL_COL] [--x X] [--y Y]
                  [--cv1-splits CV1_SPLITS] [--cv2-splits CV2_SPLITS]
                  [--n-repeats N_REPEATS] [--max-components MAX_COMPONENTS]
                  [--min-components MIN_COMPONENTS]
                  [--random-state RANDOM_STATE] [--out-table OUT_TABLE]
                  [--out-vips OUT_VIPS] [--out-scores OUT_SCORES]
                  [--n-components N_COMPONENTS]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --input INPUT         Omics layer CSV (repeat for multiple layers;
                        standardized and concatenated)
  --metadata METADATA   Metadata CSV with label column (required when using
                        --input)
  --data DATA           CSV with predictors and label column
  --label-col LABEL_COL
                        Label column name (used with --data or
                        --input/--metadata)
  --x X                 CSV with predictors (features)
  --y Y                 CSV with labels/outcomes
  --cv1-splits CV1_SPLITS
  --cv2-splits CV2_SPLITS
  --n-repeats N_REPEATS
  --max-components MAX_COMPONENTS
  --min-components MIN_COMPONENTS
                        Smallest number of latent variables CV considers;
                        candidates are MIN..MAX-1 (default: 1)
  --random-state RANDOM_STATE
  --out-table OUT_TABLE
                        Path to save the best models table (CSV)
  --out-vips OUT_VIPS   Path to save VIP scores per feature (CSV)
  --out-scores OUT_SCORES
                        Path to save latent space scores from final model
                        (CSV)
  --n-components N_COMPONENTS
                        Number of latent variables for final score model
                        (default: modal LV from CV)

Example:

motco plsr \
  --data data.csv --label-col group \
  --cv1-splits 5 --cv2-splits 5 --n-repeats 10 --max-components 5 \
  --out-table results/plsr_table.csv \
  --out-vips results/vips.csv

docs.title: motco snf
docs.text:
Similarity Network Fusion across two or more omics CSV files. Pass --input once per dataset (all must have the same number of rows in the same sample order).

usage: motco snf [-h] [--input INPUT] [--K K] [--eps EPS] [--k K] [--t T]
                 [--out-fused OUT_FUSED] [--out-embedding OUT_EMBEDDING]
                 [--spectral-components SPECTRAL_COMPONENTS]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --input INPUT         Input CSV (repeat for multiple omics)
  --K K                 K for affinity construction
  --eps EPS             Epsilon for affinity construction
  --k K                 k for sparse kernel in SNF
  --t T                 Number of SNF iterations
  --out-fused OUT_FUSED
                        Path to save fused matrix (CSV)
  --out-embedding OUT_EMBEDDING
                        Path to save spectral embedding (CSV)
  --spectral-components SPECTRAL_COMPONENTS
                        Number of spectral embedding components (default: 10)

Example:

motco snf \
  --input proteomics.csv --input metabolomics.csv \
  --K 20 --k 20 --t 20 \
  --out-fused results/fused.csv \
  --out-embedding results/embedding.csv \
  --spectral-components 10

docs.title: motco simulate
docs.text:
Generate one semi-synthetic multi-omic dataset with the numpy generator (no R at runtime). Group A follows a random baseline trajectory and group B the transform --trajectory-mode names, at --effect-size (0 is the null for every mode). See Simulations for what each mode changes.

usage: motco simulate [-h] --seed SEED --out-dir OUT_DIR
                      [--n-samples N_SAMPLES] [--n-stages N_STAGES]
                      [--trajectory-mode {none,translation,magnitude,orientation,shape}]
                      [--effect-size EFFECT_SIZE]
                      [--shape-kind {relocate,magnitude}]
                      [--magnitude-kind {joint,all,extremes}] [--p-dmp P_DMP]
                      [--cluster-mean-shift CLUSTER_MEAN_SHIFT]
                      [--delta-methyl DELTA_METHYL] [--delta-expr DELTA_EXPR]
                      [--delta-protein DELTA_PROTEIN]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --seed SEED           Random seed for reproducibility
  --out-dir OUT_DIR     Directory to write output files
  --n-samples N_SAMPLES
                        Total number of samples (default: 600)
  --n-stages N_STAGES   Number of trajectory stages (default: 3)
  --trajectory-mode {none,translation,magnitude,orientation,shape}
                        Group trajectory difference mode (default:
                        orientation)
  --effect-size EFFECT_SIZE
                        Group effect size: magnitude scale, extra-set size, or
                        relocated fraction (default: 1.0)
  --shape-kind {relocate,magnitude}
                        Shape-mode single-stage perturbation: relocate sites
                        or scale effect (default: relocate)
  --magnitude-kind {joint,all,extremes}
                        Magnitude-mode scope: joint (every omic's delta scaled
                        together), all (methylation delta alone at all
                        stages), or extremes (methylation endpoint indicators
                        only) (default: joint)
  --p-dmp P_DMP         Per-stage probability a methylation feature is
                        differential (default: 0.2)
  --cluster-mean-shift CLUSTER_MEAN_SHIFT
                        Per-omic mean shift (delta) applied to unspecified
                        per-omic delta flags (default: 2.0)
  --delta-methyl DELTA_METHYL
                        Methylation cluster mean shift; overrides --cluster-
                        mean-shift for methylation
  --delta-expr DELTA_EXPR
                        Expression cluster mean shift; overrides --cluster-
                        mean-shift for expression
  --delta-protein DELTA_PROTEIN
                        Proteomics cluster mean shift; overrides --cluster-
                        mean-shift for proteomics

The output directory holds methylation.csv, expression.csv, proteomics.csv and metadata.csv, the trajectory design (model_full.csv, model_reduced.csv, ls_means.csv, contrast.json) ready for motco de, and truth.json recording the generator parameters and the planted difference.

Example:

motco simulate \
  --seed 42 --n-samples 90 --n-stages 3 \
  --trajectory-mode orientation --effect-size 1.0 \
  --out-dir results/simulated/

docs.title: motco de
docs.text:
Estimate group trajectory differences, optionally with RRPP permutation testing.

Estimate only (no p-values): provide --model-matrix.

RRPP (with p-values): provide --model-full, --model-reduced, and --rrpp-permutations.

usage: motco de [-h] --Y Y --ls-means LS_MEANS --contrast CONTRAST
                [--model-matrix MODEL_MATRIX] [--model-full MODEL_FULL]
                [--model-reduced MODEL_REDUCED]
                [--rrpp-permutations RRPP_PERMUTATIONS] [--out-json OUT_JSON]
                [--out-observed OUT_OBSERVED]
                [--orientation-estimator {pc1,net_displacement}]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --Y Y                 Outcome matrix CSV (latent space coordinates)
  --ls-means LS_MEANS   Least-squares means CSV
  --contrast CONTRAST   JSON file with groups (list of index lists)
  --model-matrix MODEL_MATRIX
                        Model matrix CSV (with intercept) for
                        estimate_difference
  --model-full MODEL_FULL
                        Full model matrix CSV (with intercept) for RRPP
  --model-reduced MODEL_REDUCED
                        Reduced model matrix CSV (with intercept) for RRPP
  --rrpp-permutations RRPP_PERMUTATIONS
                        Number of permutations for RRPP
  --out-json OUT_JSON   Output JSON file
  --out-observed OUT_OBSERVED
                        Save predicted LS-mean vectors as CSV
  --orientation-estimator {pc1,net_displacement}
                        Orientation estimator for angles, observed and
                        permuted (default: pc1). net_displacement is the
                        estimator the simulation harness and the published
                        operating characteristics describe; when given, the
                        JSON records it.

--orientation-estimator selects how each group's orientation is measured, for the observed angles and for every RRPP permutation. The default stays pc1, so existing invocations produce the same output. When the flag is omitted, the JSON is unchanged and has no orientation_estimator key. net_displacement is the estimator the simulation harness and the published operating characteristics describe. When the flag is given, with either value, the JSON records it as "orientation_estimator". Only angles depend on it.

Example — estimate only:

motco de \
  --Y latent.csv --model-matrix model_full.csv \
  --ls-means ls_means.csv --contrast contrast.json \
  --out-json results/de.json \
  --out-observed results/ls_mean_vectors.csv

Example — RRPP:

motco de \
  --Y latent.csv \
  --model-full model_full.csv --model-reduced model_reduced.csv \
  --ls-means ls_means.csv --contrast contrast.json \
  --rrpp-permutations 999 \
  --out-json results/rrpp.json

docs.title: motco analyze
docs.text:
Real-data trajectory analysis with the validated pipeline. See Real-Data Analysis for the input contract, the record and the artifact layout.

usage: motco analyze [-h] --block NAME=PATH [--transform NAME=KIND] --metadata
                     METADATA --sample-col SAMPLE_COL --group-col GROUP_COL
                     --stage-col STAGE_COL [--stage-order STAGE_ORDER]
                     [--group-order GROUP_ORDER] [--covariate COL]
                     [--categorical-covariate COL]
                     [--missing-covariates {error,complete_case}]
                     [--latent-adjustment {stage,group_stage}]
                     [--permutations PERMUTATIONS] [--seed SEED]
                     [--n-jobs N_JOBS] [--forced-components FORCED_COMPONENTS]
                     [--residual-correction {df,leverage}] [--span-split-test]
                     [--interaction-scan] [--interaction-scan-by-block]
                     [--min-components MIN_COMPONENTS]
                     [--block-weighting {equal_variance,mfa}]
                     [--sparsity {joint,block}] [--sparsity-ladder F1,F2,...]
                     [--orientation-estimator {net_displacement,pc1}]
                     [--attribution]
                     [--bootstrap-replicates BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES]
                     [--bootstrap-seed BOOTSTRAP_SEED] [--top-k TOP_K]
                     [--cv1-splits CV1_SPLITS] [--cv2-splits CV2_SPLITS]
                     [--n-repeats N_REPEATS] [--max-components MAX_COMPONENTS]
                     [--cv-random-state CV_RANDOM_STATE] --out-dir OUT_DIR
                     [--overwrite]

Measure two groups' trajectories across ordered stages on your own multi-omic
data. Blocks are analysed in the units supplied: MOTCO does not normalize
counts, filter features or impute values.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --block NAME=PATH     Omic block CSV (samples x features, first column the
                        sample id); repeat per block, in the order the joint
                        feature matrix should follow
  --transform NAME=KIND
                        Unit transform for a declared block: identity
                        (default) or beta_to_mvalue
  --metadata METADATA   Sample metadata CSV
  --sample-col SAMPLE_COL
                        Metadata column with the sample ids
  --group-col GROUP_COL
                        Metadata column with the two groups
  --stage-col STAGE_COL
                        Metadata column with the stages
  --stage-order STAGE_ORDER
                        Required. Comma-separated stage labels, first to last
                        (never inferred by sorting)
  --group-order GROUP_ORDER
                        Comma-separated group labels (default: sorted as
                        strings)
  --covariate COL       Metadata column entering the trajectory model
                        additively; repeat per covariate, in model order (non-
                        numeric columns are categorical)
  --categorical-covariate COL
                        Like --covariate, but treat the column as a factor
                        whatever its dtype
  --missing-covariates {error,complete_case}
                        Missing covariate values: error (default) or
                        complete_case (drop those samples); never imputed
  --latent-adjustment {stage,group_stage}
                        Fit the PLS basis on features residualized on the
                        declared covariates, conditional on the stage (stage)
                        or group x stage (group_stage) indicators; requires a
                        covariate. Default: off (covariate-blind basis)
  --permutations PERMUTATIONS
                        RRPP permutations (default: 0, no p-values)
  --seed SEED           RRPP seed
  --n-jobs N_JOBS       Parallel jobs for CV and RRPP (-1 = all CPUs)
  --forced-components FORCED_COMPONENTS
                        Fix the latent rank and skip cross-validation
                        (dimensionality sensitivity)
  --residual-correction {df,leverage}
                        Rescale the reduced model's residuals before RRPP
                        permutes them: df (kappa = sqrt(n / (n - rank))) or
                        leverage (1 / sqrt(1 - h_ii)). Moves only the null.
                        Default: off
  --span-split-test     Also test the group x stage interaction of the
                        standardized features inside the fitted PLS span and
                        in its orthogonal complement (pseudo-F, RRPP draws at
                        --seed). Not available with --latent-adjustment.
                        Default: off
  --interaction-scan    Also test the group x stage interaction of every
                        standardized feature on its own (per-feature F, the
                        maximum's global p-value and step-down max-T adjusted
                        p-values, RRPP draws at --seed); writes
                        interaction_scan.csv. Default: off
  --interaction-scan-by-block
                        Split the interaction scan's familywise error equally
                        between the declared blocks (Bonferroni over within-
                        block step-downs), so a large or heavy-tailed block
                        does not set every block's bar. Requires
                        --interaction-scan. Default: off (one joint maximum)
  --min-components MIN_COMPONENTS
                        Rank floor of the cross-validated latent space: CV
                        considers ranks MIN..MAX-1 (default: 2; 1 restores the
                        unfloored 0.9.0 rule)
  --block-weighting {equal_variance,mfa}
                        Multiply every standardized block by one label-blind
                        scalar before the latent space is fitted:
                        equal_variance (1/sqrt(features), unit total variance
                        per block) or mfa (unit variance of each block's
                        leading principal component). delta is then in the
                        weighted metric. Unvalidated. Default: off
                        (unweighted)
  --sparsity {joint,block}
                        Fit sparse stage-PLS-DA: every component loads on a
                        budget of features, over all features (joint) or per
                        block (block); CV selects the rank and the keep
                        fraction jointly. Unvalidated. Default: off (ordinary
                        PLS-DA)
  --sparsity-ladder F1,F2,...
                        Keep fractions CV selects over, in (0, 1] (requires
                        --sparsity; default: 1.0,0.5,0.2,0.1,0.05)
  --orientation-estimator {net_displacement,pc1}
                        Orientation estimator (default: net_displacement)
  --attribution         Run frozen-model orientation attribution
  --bootstrap-replicates BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES
                        Attribution bootstrap replicates
  --bootstrap-seed BOOTSTRAP_SEED
                        Attribution bootstrap seed
  --top-k TOP_K         Attribution top-k feature count
  --cv1-splits CV1_SPLITS
                        Inner CV folds (default: 3)
  --cv2-splits CV2_SPLITS
                        Outer CV folds (default: 4)
  --n-repeats N_REPEATS
                        Outer CV repeats (default: 5)
  --max-components MAX_COMPONENTS
                        Largest rank CV considers (default: 20)
  --cv-random-state CV_RANDOM_STATE
                        CV random state (default: 1203)
  --out-dir OUT_DIR     Directory for the analysis artifact
  --overwrite           Replace an existing analysis in --out-dir

Blocks are analysed in the units supplied: MOTCO does not normalize counts, filter features or impute values. On success the command prints the selected rank with its floor, the estimator, the statistics with their p-values and the written paths; with covariates it also prints each covariate's kind and the number of samples complete-case deletion dropped, and with --latent-adjustment the conditioning and the residual degrees of freedom of the residualization, and with --residual-correction the correction it applied to the RRPP null (κ for df, the leverage and multiplier range for leverage). With --block-weighting the kind is printed beside the rank floor and recorded in a block_weighting block; see Block weighting for the metric it implies and its validation status. With --sparsity the scope and the selected keep fraction are printed beside the rank floor and recorded in a sparsity block; --sparsity-ladder without --sparsity, or a ladder that is not comma-separated fractions in (0, 1], exits non-zero before anything is fitted. See Sparse stage-PLS for its validation status. With --span-split-test it prints one line with the three pseudo-F p-values and the in-span share and records a span_split block; it exits non-zero with --latent-adjustment. With --interaction-scan it prints one line with the maximum F and its feature, the global p-value and the hits at adjusted p ≤ 0.05, records an interaction_scan block and writes interaction_scan.csv; --interaction-scan-by-block (which requires --interaction-scan) runs the scan within each block and adds the combination and the number of blocks tested to that line. See Split interaction test and Per-feature interaction scan. Covariates are declared in flag order across --covariate and --categorical-covariate. --latent-adjustment without a covariate flag exits non-zero before any data are read; see Latent adjustment for what it changes and the mediator caveat, and Residual correction for the corrected null and its validation status. Input and validation errors exit non-zero with an Error: … message.

Example:

motco analyze \
  --block rna=rna_logcpm.csv --block atac=atac_logcpm.csv \
  --metadata donors.csv --sample-col donor_id --group-col Sex --stage-col ADNC \
  --stage-order "Not AD + Low,Intermediate,High" \
  --permutations 999 --seed 20261015 \
  --out-dir results/motco_mtg_astro

docs.title: PLS-DA
docs.text: Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis with double cross-validation.

docs.title: Scale and nuisance residualization
docs.text:
plsda_doubleCV takes five keyword-only arguments whose defaults reproduce its earlier behaviour exactly:

  • scale (default True) is passed to every PLSRegression fit in the inner loop, the outer loop and the per-repeat refits. False fits in the metric the predictors are already in, for example pooled-standardized features that must keep their pooled scale.
  • nuisance (default None) takes a NuisanceDesign: row-aligned conditioning columns D (no intercept) and covariate columns C. Every training set (each outer rest set and each inner training set) regresses its predictors on [1, D, C], subtracts the fitted covariate part C γ, and residualizes its held-out rows as X_held_out − C_held_out γ. The held-out rows' conditioning (their labels) is never read. The per-repeat refits use coefficients estimated on all rows. Every training design must have full column rank, or the function raises a ValueError naming the repeat and fold, for example when a factor level is absent from a training set. The result gains "nuisance_min_training_df", the smallest training-set residual degrees of freedom.
  • strata (default None) names row-aligned labels both CV levels stratify on instead of y; the AUROC still scores y. Folds depend only on the partition the labels define, so labels that partition the rows like y reproduce the default folds. With a nuisance design, pass nuisance.cells() (its conditioning cells) so every training set contains every cell: the inner folds are not shuffled, and on rows sorted by group within stage a stage-only stratification can put a whole group × stage cell into one validation fold.

  • min_components (default 1) is the smallest number of latent variables the inner CV considers: the candidates are min_components … max_components − 1, so every outer-fold selection, every modal LV in the table and every refit model has at least that many components. It must satisfy 1 ≤ min_components < max_components, or the function raises a ValueError naming both values before any fold is fitted. The default is the unfloored rule; the trajectory latent space (fit_pls_latent_space, shared by the simulation harness and motco analyze) applies a floor of 2 by default, see Real-data analysis.

  • sparsity (default None) takes a SparsityDesign and selects a sparsity budget jointly with the rank; see below.

The real-data analysis uses scale, nuisance and strata together for covariate-aware latent construction; see Real-data analysis.

docs.title: Sparse PLS-DA
docs.text:
SparsePLSDA (motco.stats.sparse_pls, also importable from motco.stats) is a PLSRegression whose components each load on a budget of features (the sPLS-DA of Lê Cao et al., regression mode). Inside scikit-learn's NIPALS power iteration the X weight vector is soft-thresholded before it is normalized: the largest absolute weights are kept and shrunk toward zero by the largest discarded one, and every other weight is zero. Everything else is scikit-learn's: the model inherits transform, inverse_transform, predict, x_rotations_, x_scores_ and the input scaling, so every consumer of a fitted PLS-DA model in MOTCO (the latent map, span capture, attribution, VIPs, the split test) accepts it unchanged. At the full budget the fit is PLSRegression.fit, bit for bit. keep_ holds the count per component and group, support_ the non-zero weights (features × components). The fit agrees with mixOmics splsda on the committed fixture (tests/data/splsda_reference_fixture.npz, produced once by tests/data/reference/splsda_fixture.R): identical supports, weights and scores to 1e-6 up to column signs.

A SparsityDesign(scope, keep_fractions, feature_groups) describes the budget to select over:

  • scope is "joint" (one budget over all features) or "block" (one budget per block, so every block keeps its share whatever its size; a joint budget on blocks of unequal noise can empty a block). DIABLO's between-block agreement term is not part of it.
  • keep_fractions (default 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05) are fractions of the scope's feature count, distinct and in (0, 1], held fullest first. A fraction keeps max(1, round(f · p)) features per group (halves round up), so every block keeps at least one feature per component.
  • feature_groups are the block sizes in column order; the block scope needs them, and plsda_doubleCV rejects groups that do not cover the columns of X before any fold is fitted.

With sparsity=, the inner CV scores every (rank, fraction) pair by mean held-out AUROC, ordered rank ascending then fraction descending, so an exact tie goes to the smaller rank and, within it, to the fuller budget: the CV leaves production only on strictly better held-out AUROC. The outer fold is evaluated at the selected pair. Each repeat aggregates the rank by mode (smaller on ties) and the fraction by mode (fuller on ties), the table gains a keep_fraction column after LV, and every refit model is a SparsePLSDA at the repeat's pair. A ladder of [1.0] reproduces the run without sparsity exactly. Without sparsity the output is byte-identical to before (tests/data/plsda_doublecv_identity.json) and has no new column.

docs.title: motco.stats.pls.plsda_doubleCV(X, y, cv1_splits=7, cv2_splits=8, n_repeats=30, max_components=50, random_state=1203, n_jobs=1, progress=True, *, scale=True, nuisance=None, strata=None, min_components=1, sparsity=None)
docs.text:
Run canonical double-nested cross-validation for PLS-DA.

For each outer fold, the inner CV averages AUROC across its V folds and selects the n_LV with the highest mean. The outer fold's selected n_LV is then evaluated on its held-out test set. Per repeat, the K outer-fold test AUROCs are aggregated by mean (and sample std), and the per-fold n_LV choices are aggregated by mode (parsimony tie-break). One final model is refit per repeat on the full input using the modal n_LV.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default X DataFrame

The predictor variables.

required y Union[DataFrame, Series]

The outcome variable.

required cv1_splits int

Number of folds in the CV1 (inner) loop. Default: 7.

7 cv2_splits int

Number of folds in the CV2 (outer) loop. Default: 8.

8 n_repeats int

Number of repeats of the K-fold outer CV. Default: 30.

30 max_components int

Maximum number of LV to test (candidates are min_components..max_components-1). Default: 50.

50 random_state int

For reproducibility. Default: 1203.

1203 n_jobs int

Number of parallel workers for the inner CV loop. Use -1 for all available CPUs. Default: 1 (serial).

1 progress bool

Whether to display a tqdm progress bar over outer folds. Default: True.

True scale bool

Keyword-only. Whether every PLS fit (inner, outer and the per-repeat refits) rescales the predictors to unit variance. False fits in the metric X is already in. Default: True.

True nuisance NuisanceDesign | None

Keyword-only. When given (row-aligned to X), every training set — each outer rest set and each inner training set — estimates the covariate coefficients of X on [1, conditioning, covariates] from its own rows (:func:fit_nuisance_coefficients), residualizes its own rows, and residualizes the held-out rows with the same coefficients and the held-out covariate columns alone, so held-out labels never enter the residualization. The per-repeat refits use coefficients estimated on all rows. Every training design must have full column rank; otherwise a ValueError names the repeat and fold. Default: None (no residualization).

None strata Union[ndarray, Series, Sequence[str], None]

Keyword-only. Row-aligned labels the outer and inner folds are stratified on instead of y (for example the conditioning cells of nuisance, so that every training set contains every cell). Folds depend only on the partition the labels define, so labels that partition the rows like y reproduce the default folds. Default: None (stratify on y).

None min_components int

Keyword-only. The smallest number of latent variables the inner CV considers, so the candidates are min_components..max_components-1 and every outer-fold selection, every modal LV and every refit model has at least this many components. Must satisfy 1 <= min_components < max_components; otherwise a ValueError names both values before any fold is fitted. Default: 1 (the unfloored rule; the trajectory latent space applies its own floor, see :func:motco.simulations.evaluation.fit_pls_latent_space).

1 sparsity SparsityDesign | None

Keyword-only. When given, every fit is a :class:~motco.stats.sparse_pls.SparsePLSDA and the inner CV scores every pair of a candidate rank and a keep fraction of the design's ladder, ordered rank ascending then fraction descending, so the first-occurrence argmax breaks an exact tie of mean inner AUROC toward the smaller rank and, within it, toward the fuller budget. The outer fold is evaluated at the selected pair; each repeat aggregates the rank by mode (smaller on ties) and the fraction by mode (fuller on ties) and refits a sparse model at that pair. The design's feature groups must cover the columns of X (a joint design without groups is completed with one group); otherwise a ValueError is raised before any fold is fitted. A ladder of [1.0] reproduces the run without sparsity exactly (the full budget is PLSRegression). Default: None (ordinary PLS-DA; byte-identical output, no new column).

None

Returns:

Type Description dict

With two keys:

  • "table": pd.DataFrame with one row per repeat and four columns — "rep" (int), "LV" (int, modal across K outer folds with parsimony tie-break), "AUROC" (float, mean across K outer folds), "AUROC_std" (float, sample std across K outer folds; NaN if K < 2).
  • "models": list of length n_repeats. Each entry is a PLSRegression refit on the full input (X, one-hot(y)) with the corresponding row's modal n_LV.

With sparsity given, the table gains a "keep_fraction" column after "LV" (float, the repeat's modal fraction) and every model is a SparsePLSDA at the row's rank and fraction.

With nuisance given, a third key "nuisance_min_training_df" holds the smallest residual degrees of freedom of any training-set residualization fit.

Source code in src/motco/stats/pls.py 
def plsda_doubleCV(
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    y: Union[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series],
    cv1_splits: int = 7,
    cv2_splits: int = 8,
    n_repeats: int = 30,
    max_components: int = 50,
    random_state: int = 1203,
    n_jobs: int = 1,
    progress: bool = True,
    *,
    scale: bool = True,
    nuisance: NuisanceDesign | None = None,
    strata: Union[np.ndarray, pd.Series, Sequence[str], None] = None,
    min_components: int = 1,
    sparsity: SparsityDesign | None = None,
) -> PLSDAResult:
    """
    Run canonical double-nested cross-validation for PLS-DA.

    For each outer fold, the inner CV averages AUROC across its V folds and
    selects the n_LV with the highest mean. The outer fold's selected n_LV is
    then evaluated on its held-out test set. Per repeat, the K outer-fold test
    AUROCs are aggregated by mean (and sample std), and the per-fold n_LV
    choices are aggregated by mode (parsimony tie-break). One final model is
    refit per repeat on the full input using the modal n_LV.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X: pd.DataFrame
        The predictor variables.
    y: Union[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]
        The outcome variable.
    cv1_splits: int
        Number of folds in the CV1 (inner) loop. Default: 7.
    cv2_splits: int
        Number of folds in the CV2 (outer) loop. Default: 8.
    n_repeats: int
        Number of repeats of the K-fold outer CV. Default: 30.
    max_components: int
        Maximum number of LV to test (candidates are
        ``min_components..max_components-1``). Default: 50.
    random_state: int
        For reproducibility. Default: 1203.
    n_jobs: int
        Number of parallel workers for the inner CV loop. Use -1 for all
        available CPUs. Default: 1 (serial).
    progress: bool
        Whether to display a tqdm progress bar over outer folds. Default: True.
    scale: bool
        Keyword-only. Whether every PLS fit (inner, outer and the per-repeat
        refits) rescales the predictors to unit variance. ``False`` fits in the
        metric ``X`` is already in. Default: True.
    nuisance: NuisanceDesign | None
        Keyword-only. When given (row-aligned to ``X``), every training set —
        each outer rest set and each inner training set — estimates the
        covariate coefficients of ``X`` on ``[1, conditioning, covariates]``
        from its own rows (:func:`fit_nuisance_coefficients`), residualizes its
        own rows, and residualizes the held-out rows with the same coefficients
        and the held-out covariate columns alone, so held-out labels never
        enter the residualization. The per-repeat refits use coefficients
        estimated on all rows. Every training design must have full column
        rank; otherwise a ``ValueError`` names the repeat and fold. Default:
        None (no residualization).
    strata: array-like | None
        Keyword-only. Row-aligned labels the outer and inner folds are
        stratified on instead of ``y`` (for example the conditioning cells of
        ``nuisance``, so that every training set contains every cell). Folds
        depend only on the partition the labels define, so labels that
        partition the rows like ``y`` reproduce the default folds. Default:
        None (stratify on ``y``).
    min_components: int
        Keyword-only. The smallest number of latent variables the inner CV
        considers, so the candidates are ``min_components..max_components-1``
        and every outer-fold selection, every modal ``LV`` and every refit
        model has at least this many components. Must satisfy
        ``1 <= min_components < max_components``; otherwise a ``ValueError``
        names both values before any fold is fitted. Default: 1 (the
        unfloored rule; the trajectory latent space applies its own floor,
        see :func:`motco.simulations.evaluation.fit_pls_latent_space`).
    sparsity: SparsityDesign | None
        Keyword-only. When given, every fit is a
        :class:`~motco.stats.sparse_pls.SparsePLSDA` and the inner CV scores
        every pair of a candidate rank and a keep fraction of the design's
        ladder, ordered rank ascending then fraction descending, so the
        first-occurrence ``argmax`` breaks an exact tie of mean inner AUROC
        toward the smaller rank and, within it, toward the fuller budget. The
        outer fold is evaluated at the selected pair; each repeat aggregates
        the rank by mode (smaller on ties) and the fraction by mode (fuller on
        ties) and refits a sparse model at that pair. The design's feature
        groups must cover the columns of ``X`` (a joint design without groups
        is completed with one group); otherwise a ``ValueError`` is raised
        before any fold is fitted. A ladder of ``[1.0]`` reproduces the run
        without sparsity exactly (the full budget is ``PLSRegression``).
        Default: None (ordinary PLS-DA; byte-identical output, no new column).

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        With two keys:

        - ``"table"``: pd.DataFrame with one row per repeat and four columns —
          ``"rep"`` (int), ``"LV"`` (int, modal across K outer folds with
          parsimony tie-break), ``"AUROC"`` (float, mean across K outer folds),
          ``"AUROC_std"`` (float, sample std across K outer folds; NaN if K < 2).
        - ``"models"``: list of length ``n_repeats``. Each entry is a
          PLSRegression refit on the full input (X, one-hot(y)) with the
          corresponding row's modal n_LV.

        With ``sparsity`` given, the table gains a ``"keep_fraction"`` column
        after ``"LV"`` (float, the repeat's modal fraction) and every model is
        a ``SparsePLSDA`` at the row's rank and fraction.

        With ``nuisance`` given, a third key ``"nuisance_min_training_df"``
        holds the smallest residual degrees of freedom of any training-set
        residualization fit.
    """
    _X_arr = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    _y_arr = np.asarray(y)
    _n_x = _X_arr.shape[0]
    _n_y = _y_arr.shape[0]
    if _n_x != _n_y:
        raise ValueError(
            f"X has {_n_x} rows but y has {_n_y} rows — number of rows must match."
        )
    _n_classes = len(np.unique(_y_arr))
    if _n_classes < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"y has {_n_classes} unique class(es); at least 2 are required."
        )
    if max_components > _X_arr.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"max_components={max_components} exceeds the number of features in X "
            f"({_X_arr.shape[1]}); reduce max_components."
        )
    try:
        floor_ok = int(min_components) == min_components and 1 <= min_components < max_components
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        floor_ok = False
    if not floor_ok:
        raise ValueError(
            f"min_components={min_components!r} must be an integer with "
            f"1 <= min_components < max_components={max_components}; the candidates are "
            "min_components..max_components-1."
        )
    min_components = int(min_components)
    design: SparsityDesign | None = None
    if sparsity is not None:
        if not isinstance(sparsity, SparsityDesign):
            raise ValueError(f"sparsity must be a SparsityDesign or None, got {type(sparsity).__name__}.")
        design = sparsity.resolve(_X_arr.shape[1])
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(_X_arr)):
        raise ValueError("X contains NaN or Inf values.")
    if nuisance is not None and nuisance.n_samples != _n_x:
        raise ValueError(f"X has {_n_x} rows but the nuisance design has {nuisance.n_samples}.")
    folds_on: Union[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series] = y
    if strata is not None:
        folds_on = pd.Series(np.asarray(strata))
        if folds_on.shape[0] != _n_x:
            raise ValueError(f"X has {_n_x} rows but strata has {folds_on.shape[0]}.")
    encoder = OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False)
    yd_arr = encoder.fit_transform(np.array(y).reshape(-1, 1))
    yd = pd.DataFrame(yd_arr)
    cv2 = RepeatedStratifiedKFold(
        n_splits=cv2_splits, n_repeats=n_repeats, random_state=random_state
    )
    cv1 = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=cv1_splits)

    # Candidates are (rank, keep fraction) pairs, rank ascending then fraction
    # fullest first; without sparsity the fraction is None (ordinary PLS).
    fractions: tuple[float | None, ...] = (None,) if design is None else design.keep_fractions
    candidates: list[tuple[int, float | None]] = [
        (n_lv, fraction) for n_lv in range(min_components, max_components) for fraction in fractions
    ]
    n_candidates = len(candidates)

    rep_means: list[float] = []
    rep_stds: list[float] = []
    rep_lvs: list[int] = []
    rep_fractions: list[float] = []

    outer_aurocs: list[float] = []
    outer_n_lv: list[int] = []
    outer_fractions: list[float] = []
    fold_in_repeat = 0
    training_dfs: list[int] = []
    auroc = partial(_candidate_auroc, scale=scale, sparsity=design)

    cv2_iter = tqdm(
        cv2.split(X, folds_on),
        total=cv2_splits * n_repeats,
        desc="PLS-DA CV2",
        unit="fold",
        disable=not progress,
    )
    for rest, test in cv2_iter:
        X_rest = X.iloc[rest, :]
        X_test = X.iloc[test, :]
        folds_on_rest = folds_on.iloc[rest]
        yd_rest = yd.iloc[rest, :]
        yd_test = yd.iloc[test, :]
        outer_where = f"repeat {len(rep_lvs) + 1}, outer fold {fold_in_repeat + 1}"
        X_rest_fit, X_test_fit = X_rest, X_test
        if nuisance is not None:
            X_rest_fit, X_test_fit, rest_df = _fit_and_residualize(
                X_rest, X_test, nuisance, rest, test, outer_where
            )
            training_dfs.append(rest_df)

        # Inner CV: average AUROC across V folds for each candidate n_LV.
        inner_aurocs = np.zeros((cv1_splits, n_candidates))
        for v_idx, (train, validation) in enumerate(cv1.split(X_rest, folds_on_rest)):
            X_train = X_rest.iloc[train, :]
            yd_train = yd_rest.iloc[train, :]
            X_val = X_rest.iloc[validation, :]
            yd_val = yd_rest.iloc[validation, :]
            if nuisance is not None:
                # Coefficients from the inner training rows of the raw predictors.
                X_train, X_val, train_df = _fit_and_residualize(
                    X_train,
                    X_val,
                    nuisance,
                    rest[train],
                    rest[validation],
                    f"{outer_where}, inner fold {v_idx + 1}",
                )
                training_dfs.append(train_df)
            args = zip(
                candidates,
                repeat(X_train),
                repeat(yd_train),
                repeat(X_val),
                repeat(yd_val),
            )
            fold_aurocs: list[float]
            if n_jobs == 1:
                fold_aurocs = [auroc(*a) for a in args]
            else:
                n_workers = (
                    (multiprocessing.cpu_count() or 1) if n_jobs == -1 else max(1, n_jobs)
                )
                with multiprocessing.Pool(processes=n_workers) as pool:
                    fold_aurocs = pool.starmap(auroc, args)
            inner_aurocs[v_idx, :] = fold_aurocs

        mean_per_candidate = inner_aurocs.mean(axis=0)
        # np.argmax returns the first occurrence on ties → parsimony (the
        # smaller rank, then the fuller budget). Select by value so the floor
        # is a property of the candidate set.
        candidate_star = candidates[int(np.argmax(mean_per_candidate))]

        outer_score = float(
            auroc(candidate_star, X_rest_fit, yd_rest, X_test_fit, yd_test)
        )
        outer_aurocs.append(outer_score)
        outer_n_lv.append(candidate_star[0])
        if candidate_star[1] is not None:
            outer_fractions.append(candidate_star[1])

        fold_in_repeat += 1
        if fold_in_repeat == cv2_splits:
            mean_auroc = float(np.mean(outer_aurocs))
            std_auroc = (
                float(np.std(outer_aurocs, ddof=1))
                if len(outer_aurocs) > 1
                else float("nan")
            )
            mode_lv = _modal_int_with_parsimony(outer_n_lv)
            rep_means.append(mean_auroc)
            rep_stds.append(std_auroc)
            rep_lvs.append(mode_lv)
            if design is not None:
                rep_fractions.append(_modal_fraction_fullest(outer_fractions))
            outer_aurocs = []
            outer_n_lv = []
            outer_fractions = []
            fold_in_repeat = 0

    model_table = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "rep": list(range(1, n_repeats + 1)),
            "LV": rep_lvs,
            "AUROC": rep_means,
            "AUROC_std": rep_stds,
        }
    )
    model_table["rep"] = model_table["rep"].astype(int)
    model_table["LV"] = model_table["LV"].astype(int)
    model_table["AUROC"] = model_table["AUROC"].astype(float)
    model_table["AUROC_std"] = model_table["AUROC_std"].astype(float)
    if design is not None:
        model_table.insert(2, "keep_fraction", np.asarray(rep_fractions, dtype=float))

    X_full = _X_arr
    if nuisance is not None:
        try:
            full_coefficients, _ = fit_nuisance_coefficients(_X_arr, nuisance)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"Nuisance residualization failed on the full input: {exc}") from exc
        X_full = residualize(_X_arr, nuisance.covariates, full_coefficients)

    best_models: list[PLSRegression] = []
    rep_pairs = zip(rep_lvs, rep_fractions) if design is not None else zip(rep_lvs, repeat(None))
    for lv, fraction in rep_pairs:
        model = _plsda_estimator(lv, scale=scale, sparsity=design, keep_fraction=fraction).fit(X_full, yd_arr)
        best_models.append(model)

    if nuisance is not None:
        return {"models": best_models, "table": model_table, "nuisance_min_training_df": min(training_dfs)}
    return {"models": best_models, "table": model_table}

def calculate_vips(
    model,
    components: Union[None, list[int]] = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Estimates Variable Importance in Projection (VIP)
    in Partial Least Squares (PLS)

    Parameters
    ----------
    model: PLSRegression
        model generated from the PLSRegression function
    components: Union[None, list[int]]
        if not None, a list of integers indicating the components to compute
        the VIPs from. If None, all components are taken into account.
        Default None.

    Returns
    -------
    vips: np.array
        variable importance in projection for each variable
    """
    if components is not None:
        t = model.x_scores_[:, components]
        w = model.x_weights_[:, components]
        q = model.y_loadings_[:, components]
        p, h = w.shape
    else:
        w = model.x_weights_
        t = model.x_scores_
        q = model.y_loadings_
        p, h = w.shape

    vips = np.zeros((p,))
    s = np.diag(np.matmul(np.matmul(np.matmul(t.T, t), q.T), q)).reshape(h, -1)
    total_s = np.sum(s)
    for i in range(p):
        weight = np.array([(w[i, j] / np.linalg.norm(w[:, j])) ** 2 for j in range(h)])
        vips[i] = np.sqrt(p * np.matmul(s.T, weight)[0] / total_s)
    return vips

class SparsePLSDA(PLSRegression):
    """PLS regression (PLS-DA on one-hot labels) with a feature budget per component.

    Per component the power iteration's X weight vector is soft-thresholded in
    every group: the ``keep`` largest absolute entries are kept and shrunk
    toward zero by the largest discarded absolute entry, every other entry is
    zero, and the vector is then normalized. Deflation is regression mode, so
    the fitted attributes and methods are those of ``PLSRegression`` with the
    same meanings (``x_rotations_ = W·(PᵀW)⁺``, ``transform``,
    ``inverse_transform``, ``predict``). When every count equals its group's
    size the fit is ``PLSRegression.fit``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_components : int, default=2
        Number of components.
    keep : int | sequence of int | None, default=None
        Features each component's X weight vector may load on: one count
        (one group) or one count per group of ``groups``, each in
        ``[1, group size]``. ``None`` keeps every feature, i.e. ordinary PLS.
    groups : sequence of int | None, default=None
        Sizes of consecutive column groups (blocks) the budget is counted in.
        ``None`` is one group of all features.
    scale : bool, default=True
        As :class:`~sklearn.cross_decomposition.PLSRegression`.
    max_iter : int, default=1000
        As ``PLSRegression`` (MOTCO's setting rather than sklearn's 500).
    tol : float, default=1e-06
        As ``PLSRegression``: the iteration stops when the squared change of
        the X weight vector is below ``tol``.
    copy : bool, default=True
        As ``PLSRegression``.

    Attributes
    ----------
    keep_ : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_groups)
        The resolved count per component and group.
    support_ : ndarray of shape (n_features, n_components)
        Boolean; the features each component's weight vector loads on
        (its non-zero entries).
    """

    _parameter_constraints: dict = {
        **PLSRegression._parameter_constraints,
        "keep": "no_validation",
        "groups": "no_validation",
    }

    def __init__(
        self,
        n_components: int = 2,
        keep: int | Sequence[int] | None = None,
        *,
        groups: Sequence[int] | None = None,
        scale: bool = True,
        max_iter: int = 1000,
        tol: float = 1e-06,
        copy: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(n_components=n_components, scale=scale, max_iter=max_iter, tol=tol, copy=copy)
        self.keep = keep
        self.groups = groups

    @_fit_context(prefer_skip_nested_validation=True)
    def fit(self, X: Any, y: Any) -> SparsePLSDA:
        """Fit the sparse model; the budget is validated before any component is fitted."""

        n_features = int(np.shape(X)[1]) if np.ndim(X) == 2 else -1
        if n_features < 1:
            raise ValueError("SparsePLSDA: X must be a 2-D matrix with at least one column.")
        sizes, counts = _resolve_budget(self.keep, self.groups, n_features)
        if counts == sizes:
            # The full budget: the threshold is zero, so this is ordinary PLS.
            super().fit(X, y)
        else:
            self._fit_sparse(X, y, sizes, counts)
        n_components = self.x_weights_.shape[1]
        self.keep_ = np.tile(np.asarray(counts, dtype=int), (n_components, 1))
        self.support_ = self.x_weights_ != 0.0
        return self

    def _fit_sparse(self, X: Any, y: Any, groups: tuple[int, ...], counts: tuple[int, ...]) -> None:
        """``sklearn.cross_decomposition._PLS.fit`` (regression mode, NIPALS) with the thresholded power method."""

        check_consistent_length(X, y)
        X = validate_data(self, X, dtype=np.float64, force_writeable=True, copy=self.copy, ensure_min_samples=2)
        y = check_array(y, input_name="y", dtype=np.float64, force_writeable=True, copy=self.copy, ensure_2d=False)
        if y.ndim == 1:
            self._predict_1d = True
            y = y.reshape(-1, 1)
        else:
            self._predict_1d = False

        n, p = X.shape
        q = y.shape[1]
        n_components = self.n_components
        rank_upper_bound = min(n, p)
        if n_components > rank_upper_bound:
            raise ValueError(
                f"`n_components` upper bound is {rank_upper_bound}. "
                f"Got {n_components} instead. Reduce `n_components`."
            )
        self._norm_y_weights = False
        Xk, yk, self._x_mean, self._y_mean, self._x_std, self._y_std = _center_scale_xy(X, y, self.scale)

        self.x_weights_ = np.zeros((p, n_components))
        self.y_weights_ = np.zeros((q, n_components))
        self._x_scores = np.zeros((n, n_components))
        self._y_scores = np.zeros((n, n_components))
        self.x_loadings_ = np.zeros((p, n_components))
        self.y_loadings_ = np.zeros((q, n_components))
        self.n_iter_ = []

        y_eps = np.finfo(yk.dtype).eps
        for k in range(n_components):
            yk_mask = np.all(np.abs(yk) < 10 * y_eps, axis=0)
            yk[:, yk_mask] = 0.0
            try:
                x_weights, y_weights, n_iter_ = _sparse_power_method(
                    Xk, yk, groups, counts, max_iter=self.max_iter, tol=self.tol
                )
            except StopIteration as e:
                if str(e) != "y residual is constant":
                    raise
                warnings.warn(f"y residual is constant at iteration {k}")
                break
            self.n_iter_.append(n_iter_)
            _svd_flip_1d(x_weights, y_weights)

            x_scores = np.dot(Xk, x_weights)
            y_ss = np.dot(y_weights, y_weights)
            y_scores = np.dot(yk, y_weights) / y_ss
            x_loadings = np.dot(x_scores, Xk) / np.dot(x_scores, x_scores)
            Xk -= np.outer(x_scores, x_loadings)
            y_loadings = np.dot(x_scores, yk) / np.dot(x_scores, x_scores)
            yk -= np.outer(x_scores, y_loadings)

            self.x_weights_[:, k] = x_weights
            self.y_weights_[:, k] = y_weights
            self._x_scores[:, k] = x_scores
            self._y_scores[:, k] = y_scores
            self.x_loadings_[:, k] = x_loadings
            self.y_loadings_[:, k] = y_loadings

        self.x_rotations_ = np.dot(
            self.x_weights_, pinv(np.dot(self.x_loadings_.T, self.x_weights_), check_finite=False)
        )
        self.y_rotations_ = np.dot(
            self.y_weights_, pinv(np.dot(self.y_loadings_.T, self.y_weights_), check_finite=False)
        )
        self.coef_ = np.dot(self.x_rotations_, self.y_loadings_.T)
        self.coef_ = (self.coef_ * self._y_std).T / self._x_std
        self.intercept_ = self._y_mean
        self._n_features_out = self.x_rotations_.shape[1]
        self.x_scores_ = self._x_scores
        self.y_scores_ = self._y_scores

    def support_sizes(self, groups: Sequence[int] | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
        """Non-zero weights per component (rows) and group (columns); ``groups`` default to the fit's."""

        requested = groups if groups is not None else self.groups
        sizes = (self.support_.shape[0],) if requested is None else tuple(int(size) for size in requested)
        if sum(sizes) != self.support_.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError(f"groups {list(sizes)} do not cover the model's {self.support_.shape[0]} features.")
        bounds = np.cumsum((0,) + tuple(sizes))
        return np.array(
            [[int(self.support_[bounds[g] : bounds[g + 1], k].sum()) for g in range(len(sizes))]
             for k in range(self.support_.shape[1])],
            dtype=int,
        )

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SparsityDesign:
    """A sparsity budget to select over: scope, keep-fraction ladder and block sizes.

    ``scope`` is ``"joint"`` (one budget over all features) or ``"block"``
    (one budget per block, so every block keeps its share whatever its size).
    ``keep_fractions`` are fractions of the scope's feature count, distinct and
    in (0, 1]; they are held fullest first. ``feature_groups`` are the block
    sizes in column order; the block scope requires them, the joint scope uses
    them only to report support per block. A joint design without groups is
    completed by :meth:`resolve` once the feature count is known.
    """

    scope: str
    keep_fractions: tuple[float, ...] = DEFAULT_KEEP_FRACTIONS
    feature_groups: tuple[int, ...] | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.scope not in SPARSITY_SCOPES:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown sparsity scope {self.scope!r}; allowed: {list(SPARSITY_SCOPES)}.")
        if isinstance(self.keep_fractions, (str, bytes)):
            raise ValueError(f"keep_fractions {self.keep_fractions!r} must be a sequence of fractions.")
        try:
            raw = tuple(self.keep_fractions)
        except TypeError:
            raise ValueError(f"keep_fractions {self.keep_fractions!r} must be a sequence of fractions.") from None
        if not raw:
            raise ValueError("keep_fractions must hold at least one fraction.")
        fractions = tuple(_validate_fraction(value, where="SparsityDesign") for value in raw)
        if len(set(fractions)) != len(fractions):
            raise ValueError(f"keep_fractions {list(raw)} repeat a fraction; they must be distinct.")
        object.__setattr__(self, "keep_fractions", tuple(sorted(fractions, reverse=True)))
        if self.feature_groups is None:
            if self.scope == "block":
                raise ValueError("The block sparsity scope needs feature_groups (the block sizes in column order).")
        else:
            object.__setattr__(self, "feature_groups", _validate_groups(self.feature_groups, where="SparsityDesign"))

    @property
    def n_features(self) -> int | None:
        """The total feature count the groups cover (``None`` while unresolved)."""

        return None if self.feature_groups is None else sum(self.feature_groups)

    def resolve(self, n_features: int) -> SparsityDesign:
        """This design checked against ``n_features`` columns (a joint design without groups gets one group)."""

        if self.feature_groups is None:
            return SparsityDesign(self.scope, self.keep_fractions, (int(n_features),))
        if sum(self.feature_groups) != int(n_features):
            raise ValueError(
                f"The sparsity feature groups {list(self.feature_groups)} cover {sum(self.feature_groups)} "
                f"features, but X has {n_features}."
            )
        return self

    @property
    def budget_groups(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        """The groups a budget is counted in: the whole feature set (joint) or every block (block)."""

        if self.feature_groups is None:
            raise ValueError("The sparsity design is unresolved; call resolve(n_features) first.")
        return (sum(self.feature_groups),) if self.scope == "joint" else self.feature_groups

    def counts(self, fraction: float) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        """The features kept per budget group at ``fraction``: ``max(1, round(f·p_g))``."""

        value = _validate_fraction(fraction, where="SparsityDesign.counts")
        return tuple(keep_count(value, size) for size in self.budget_groups)

    def estimator(self, n_components: int, fraction: float, *, scale: bool = True) -> SparsePLSDA:
        """An unfitted :class:`SparsePLSDA` at ``n_components`` and ``fraction``."""

        return SparsePLSDA(
            n_components, keep=self.counts(fraction), groups=self.budget_groups, scale=scale, max_iter=1000
        )

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The setting as recorded: scope and ladder (fullest first)."""

        return {"scope": self.scope, "keep_fractions": list(self.keep_fractions)}

The residualization regresses each predictor on [1, conditioning, covariates] and subtracts only the covariate part, so signal collinear with the covariates but explained by the conditioning design is kept (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell). kind optionally names the conditioning design for callers that record it.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NuisanceDesign:
    """Row-aligned nuisance design for covariate residualization.

    ``conditioning`` (``n × k``) holds the design the covariate coefficients
    are estimated conditional on (for example drop-first stage indicators),
    without an intercept; ``covariates`` (``n × q``) holds the covariate
    columns whose fitted part is removed. The residualization regresses each
    predictor on ``[1, conditioning, covariates]`` and subtracts only the
    covariate part, so signal collinear with the covariates but explained by
    the conditioning design is kept (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell). ``kind`` optionally
    names the conditioning design for callers that record it.
    """

    conditioning: np.ndarray
    covariates: np.ndarray
    conditioning_names: tuple[str, ...]
    covariate_names: tuple[str, ...]
    kind: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        conditioning = np.asarray(self.conditioning, dtype=float)
        covariates = np.asarray(self.covariates, dtype=float)
        if conditioning.ndim != 2 or covariates.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError("NuisanceDesign conditioning and covariates must be 2-D matrices.")
        if conditioning.shape[0] != covariates.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError(
                f"NuisanceDesign conditioning has {conditioning.shape[0]} rows but covariates have "
                f"{covariates.shape[0]}."
            )
        if covariates.shape[1] == 0:
            raise ValueError("NuisanceDesign needs at least one covariate column.")
        if conditioning.shape[1] != len(self.conditioning_names) or covariates.shape[1] != len(
            self.covariate_names
        ):
            raise ValueError("NuisanceDesign column names do not match its matrices.")
        object.__setattr__(self, "conditioning", conditioning)
        object.__setattr__(self, "covariates", covariates)
        object.__setattr__(self, "conditioning_names", tuple(self.conditioning_names))
        object.__setattr__(self, "covariate_names", tuple(self.covariate_names))

    @property
    def n_samples(self) -> int:
        return int(self.covariates.shape[0])

    @property
    def column_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Design column names beyond the intercept: conditioning, then covariates."""

        return self.conditioning_names + self.covariate_names

    def matrix(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """The full residualization design ``[1, conditioning, covariates]``."""

        return np.column_stack([np.ones(self.n_samples), self.conditioning, self.covariates])

    def cells(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """One label per row naming its conditioning cell (its distinct conditioning row).

        Under stage indicators these are the stages; under group × stage
        indicators, the group × stage cells. Used to stratify cross-validation
        folds so that every training set contains every conditioning cell.
        """

        return np.array(["|".join(f"{value:g}" for value in row) for row in self.conditioning], dtype=object)

    def rows(self, index: Union[np.ndarray, Sequence[int]]) -> "NuisanceDesign":
        """The design restricted to ``index`` (positional rows)."""

        index = np.asarray(index)
        return NuisanceDesign(
            self.conditioning[index], self.covariates[index], self.conditioning_names, self.covariate_names, self.kind
        )
