docs.title: motco.stats.pls.fit_nuisance_coefficients(X, design)
docs.text:
Estimate the covariate coefficients of X conditional on the design.

Regresses every column of X on [1, conditioning, covariates] by least squares and returns the covariate block of the coefficients (q × p) and the residual degrees of freedom n − 1 − k − q.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If X and the design differ in rows, or the design does not have full column rank; the message names the design columns.

Source code in src/motco/stats/pls.py 
def fit_nuisance_coefficients(
    X: Union[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame],
    design: NuisanceDesign,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
    """Estimate the covariate coefficients of ``X`` conditional on the design.

    Regresses every column of ``X`` on ``[1, conditioning, covariates]`` by
    least squares and returns the covariate block of the coefficients
    (``q × p``) and the residual degrees of freedom ``n − 1 − k − q``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``X`` and the design differ in rows, or the design does not have
        full column rank; the message names the design columns.
    """

    X_arr = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    if X_arr.shape[0] != design.n_samples:
        raise ValueError(f"X has {X_arr.shape[0]} rows but the nuisance design has {design.n_samples}.")
    M = design.matrix()
    rank = int(np.linalg.matrix_rank(M))
    if rank < M.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The residualization design [intercept, {', '.join(design.column_names)}] is not of full rank "
            f"(rank {rank} of {M.shape[1]} columns on {M.shape[0]} samples); a covariate is collinear with "
            "the conditioning design or with another covariate, or a factor level is absent."
        )
    coefficients = np.linalg.lstsq(M, X_arr, rcond=None)[0]
    k = design.conditioning.shape[1]
    return coefficients[1 + k :, :], int(M.shape[0] - M.shape[1])

def residualize(
    X: Union[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame],
    covariates: np.ndarray,
    coefficients: np.ndarray,
) -> Union[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Subtract the fitted covariate part: ``X − covariates @ coefficients``.

    Only the covariate columns are read, so held-out rows can be residualized
    with training coefficients without their labels. A DataFrame keeps its
    index and columns.
    """

    shift = np.asarray(covariates, dtype=float) @ np.asarray(coefficients, dtype=float)
    if isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame):
        return X - pd.DataFrame(shift, index=X.index, columns=X.columns)
    return np.asarray(X, dtype=float) - shift

docs.text:
Per-feature partial R² of the covariates given the intercept and conditioning.

1 − RSS([1, D, C]) / RSS([1, D]) for every column of X: the share of the variance left after the conditioning design that the covariates explain, i.e. what the residualization removes. A column with no variance left after the conditioning design gets 0.

Source code in src/motco/stats/pls.py 
def nuisance_partial_r2(X: Union[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame], design: NuisanceDesign) -> np.ndarray:
    """Per-feature partial R² of the covariates given the intercept and conditioning.

    ``1 − RSS([1, D, C]) / RSS([1, D])`` for every column of ``X``: the share
    of the variance left after the conditioning design that the covariates
    explain, i.e. what the residualization removes. A column with no variance
    left after the conditioning design gets 0.
    """

    X_arr = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    full = design.matrix()
    reduced = full[:, : 1 + design.conditioning.shape[1]]
    rss_full = _residual_sum_of_squares(full, X_arr)
    rss_reduced = _residual_sum_of_squares(reduced, X_arr)
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        r2 = np.where(rss_reduced > 0.0, 1.0 - rss_full / rss_reduced, 0.0)
    return np.clip(r2, 0.0, 1.0)

docs.title: Trajectory Analysis
docs.text: Group trajectory differences: magnitude, orientation, and shape.

docs.title: Assumptions about the measurement space
docs.text:
The trajectory statistics use Euclidean geometry in the supplied outcome matrix. Their interpretation therefore depends on how that matrix was built.

Representation What the statistics directly describe Interpretation Standardized concatenation The complete standardized feature space A transparent baseline, but feature weighting depends on standardization and block dimensionality PCA or PLS scores A linear projection of the feature space Path length and direction can be related to the original features through the fitted loadings; omitted components still make the projection lossy SNF spectral coordinates A nonlinear embedding of a fused affinity graph Euclidean length, angle, and Procrustes shape describe the embedding and are not guaranteed to preserve feature-space geometry

delta and angle are most directly aligned with linear measurement spaces. When using SNF, validate the intended geometric interpretation by simulation and see Interpreting trajectory geometry in SNF space. Graph-native diffusion, connectivity, or transition-profile statistics would be a separate methodology and are not implemented by the current trajectory API.

docs.title: Interpreting shape
docs.text:
shape is a strict geometric-morphometric residual configuration statistic. For each group trajectory, MOTCO centers the stage configuration and scales it to unit centroid size. Pairwise shape distance is then the residual norm after aligning one trajectory to the other over the full orthogonal group — the alignment is unconstrained in determinant, so reflections are aligned away rather than retained.

Under this contract, translation, positive uniform scale, and any orthogonal transformation — proper rotation or reflection — do not produce nonzero shape distance beyond numerical tolerance. Genuine configuration changes, such as moving an interior stage so relative stage-to-stage distances change after size normalization, remain positive.

The reflection policy is uniform: it does not depend on whether the stage configuration spans the ambient space, so the statistic means the same thing at every measurement checkpoint. (A trajectory of k stages has rank at most k − 1, so in feature space a proper-rotation constraint would be satisfiable for free in the null space and therefore vacuous — the previous "reflections retained" contract bound only in a full-rank latent space.) A genuine mirror difference is an orientation difference and is reported by angle.

docs.title: Interpreting orientation and identifying feature drivers
docs.text:
In a shared linear PLS space, a trajectory orientation difference means that the groups progress through different relative combinations of the molecular patterns retained by PLS. Different stage-associated feature sets are one possible cause, but not the only one: the same features can change in different proportions or signs, or one group can recruit an additional correlated feature module.

For two stages, let each group's standardized feature-space transition be

d_g = mean(X | group=g, stage=1) - mean(X | group=g, stage=0)

or use covariate-adjusted LS means in place of raw means. To isolate direction from magnitude, normalize each transition and calculate

u_g = d_g / ||d_g||
q   = u_B - u_A

Large positive or negative values of q[j] identify features that contribute relatively more to one group's progression direction. With more than two stages, calculate this contrast for each adjacent transition and for the signed principal feature-space orientation used to summarize the complete path.

A production attribution analysis should:

  1. Keep the pooled preprocessing and PLS model fixed; do not fit independently aligned latent spaces for the two groups.
  2. Reconstruct each group's stage-to-stage PLS score displacement through the fitted X loadings, then compare the reconstructed normalized feature steps.
  3. Compare that loading-derived contrast with the directly observed or LS-mean-adjusted feature contrast q. Their agreement describes the part of the group difference captured by the retained PLS space; their residual describes feature variation that PLS omitted.
  4. Bootstrap samples to assess feature-rank and sign stability, especially for correlated features, and summarize stable signals at module/pathway level.
  5. Report standardized effects alongside original-unit effects. PLS geometry is defined after preprocessing, so raw-unit contributions need not have the same ranking.

Pooled VIP scores alone are insufficient for this question: they identify features important to the pooled stage model, not features whose normalized stage association differs between groups. Orientation drivers require the group-specific transition contrast above.

For a production attribution result from a detected orientation difference, use the shared fitted PLS model and the aligned pooled-standardized matrix with Orientation Driver Attribution. The attribution API supports adjacent transitions for multi-stage data, optional covariate- adjusted mean tables, frozen-model bootstrap stability, and caller-supplied module/pathway labels. It reports standardized and optional original-unit effects separately and does not produce p-values, causal claims, or a unique inverse of the measured features.

Coding scheme

  • Group main effects: one-hot with drop-first for groups (G-1 columns).
  • Level main effects: one-hot with drop-first for levels (L-1 columns).
  • If full=True, include all interaction terms between group and level dummies: (G-1) × (L-1) columns.

The category order is deterministic: numeric when every distinct label of a factor parses as an integer (so 10+ levels order correctly), otherwise sorted by string representation.

Parameters:

required group_col str

required level_col str

required full bool

Type Description ndarray

def get_model_matrix(
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    group_col: str,
    level_col: str,
    full: bool = True,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Build a design (model) matrix for group × level factors.

    Coding scheme
    -------------
    - Intercept (column of ones).
    - Group main effects: one-hot with drop-first for groups (G-1 columns).
    - Level main effects: one-hot with drop-first for levels (L-1 columns).
    - If `full=True`, include all interaction terms between group and level
      dummies: (G-1) × (L-1) columns.

    The category order is deterministic: numeric when every distinct label of
    a factor parses as an integer (so 10+ levels order correctly), otherwise
    sorted by string representation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X: pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame containing `group_col` and `level_col`.
    group_col: str
        Name of the group column.
    level_col: str
        Name of the level/state column.
    full: bool
        Whether to include interaction terms.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Model matrix with intercept.
    """
    for col, param in [(group_col, "group_col"), (level_col, "level_col")]:
        if col not in X.columns:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{param}='{col}' not found in X. Available columns: {list(X.columns)}."
            )
        n_unique = X[col].nunique()
        if n_unique < 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{param}='{col}' has {n_unique} unique value(s); at least 2 are required."
            )
    # Determine deterministic category order
    g_levels = _sort_levels(pd.unique(X[group_col].astype(str)).tolist())
    l_levels = _sort_levels(pd.unique(X[level_col].astype(str)).tolist())
    # Wrap in Series to preserve X.index; pd.get_dummies on a bare Categorical
    # returns integer-indexed DataFrames, which causes pd.concat to outer-join with
    # the string-indexed Intercept part and double the row count.
    g = pd.Series(
        pd.Categorical(X[group_col].astype(str), categories=g_levels, ordered=True),
        index=X.index,
    )
    lc = pd.Series(
        pd.Categorical(X[level_col].astype(str), categories=l_levels, ordered=True),
        index=X.index,
    )

    G = pd.get_dummies(g, drop_first=True, dtype=int)
    L = pd.get_dummies(lc, drop_first=True, dtype=int)

    parts = []
    # Intercept
    parts.append(pd.DataFrame({"Intercept": np.ones(len(X))}, index=X.index))
    # Main effects
    if G.shape[1] > 0:
        parts.append(G)
    if L.shape[1] > 0:
        parts.append(L)
    # Interactions
    if full and G.shape[1] > 0 and L.shape[1] > 0:
        inter_cols = {}
        for g_col in G.columns:
            for l_col in L.columns:
                inter_cols[f"{g_col}:{l_col}"] = np.asarray(G[g_col]) * np.asarray(L[l_col])
        parts.append(pd.DataFrame(inter_cols, index=X.index))

    model_mat = pd.concat(parts, axis=1).to_numpy()
    return model_mat

def build_ls_means(
    group_levels: Sequence[str],
    level_levels: Sequence[str],
    full: bool = True,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Generate LS-mean rows for every group × level cell consistent with
    `get_model_matrix` coding.

    Parameters
    ----------
    group_levels: Sequence[str]
        Sorted group labels; first is baseline.
    level_levels: Sequence[str]
        Sorted level labels; first is baseline.
    full: bool
        Whether to include interaction terms.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        LS-mean design matrix with shape (G×L, 1 + (G-1) + (L-1) + I), where
        I = (G-1)×(L-1) if `full=True` else 0. Row order is by group major,
        then level minor.
    """
    g_levels = list(group_levels)
    l_levels = list(level_levels)
    Gm1 = max(len(g_levels) - 1, 0)
    Lm1 = max(len(l_levels) - 1, 0)
    n_rows = max(len(g_levels), 1) * max(len(l_levels), 1)
    n_cols = 1 + Gm1 + Lm1 + (Gm1 * Lm1 if full else 0)
    M = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)

    def row_for(i_g: int, i_l: int) -> int:
        return i_g * len(l_levels) + i_l

    # Column indices
    col = 0
    INTERCEPT = col
    col += 1
    G_START = col
    col += Gm1
    L_START = col
    col += Lm1
    I_START = col if full else None

    for gi, g_val in enumerate(g_levels):
        for li, l_val in enumerate(l_levels):
            r = row_for(gi, li)
            # Intercept
            M[r, INTERCEPT] = 1.0
            # Group dummies (drop first)
            if gi > 0 and Gm1 > 0:
                M[r, G_START + (gi - 1)] = 1.0
            # Level dummies (drop first)
            if li > 0 and Lm1 > 0:
                M[r, L_START + (li - 1)] = 1.0
            # Interactions
            if full and gi > 0 and li > 0 and (Gm1 > 0 and Lm1 > 0):
                assert I_START is not None
                idx = (gi - 1) * Lm1 + (li - 1)
                M[r, I_START + idx] = 1.0
    return M

def center_matrix(
    dat: pd.DataFrame,
    group_col: str,
    level_col: str,
    feature_cols: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Center feature columns by per-group means.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dat: pd.DataFrame
        Original, non-centered dataframe.
    group_col: str
        Column in `dat` indicating the group (between-subject factor).
    level_col: str
        Column in `dat` indicating the level/state (within-group factor).
    feature_cols: Sequence[str] | None
        Feature columns to center. If None, all numeric columns except
        `group_col` and `level_col` are used.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        A copy of `dat` with selected feature columns centered within groups.
    """
    if feature_cols is not None:
        missing = [c for c in feature_cols if c not in dat.columns]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"feature_cols contains column(s) not found in dat: {missing}."
            )
    datc = dat.copy()
    if feature_cols is None:
        feature_cols = [
            c
            for c in datc.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
            if c not in {group_col, level_col}
        ]
    if not feature_cols:
        return datc
    # Center within groups using group-wise means
    datc.loc[:, feature_cols] = (
        datc.loc[:, feature_cols]
        - datc.groupby(group_col)[feature_cols].transform("mean")
    )
    return datc

def estimate_betas(
    X: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray], Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
) -> Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Estimate the beta coefficients between an outcome matrix
    and a model matrix

    Parameters
    ----------
    X: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Model matrix with intercept.
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Outcome matrix.

    Returns
    -------
    betas: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Beta coefficients
    """
    # Convert inputs to arrays for linear algebra while preserving Y's metadata
    X_arr = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    if isinstance(Y, pd.DataFrame):
        Y_arr = Y.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        y_cols = Y.columns
    else:
        Y_arr = np.asarray(Y, dtype=float)
        y_cols = None

    # Solve normal equations using factorization with robust fallbacks
    XtX = X_arr.T @ X_arr
    XtY = X_arr.T @ Y_arr
    try:
        # Cholesky is fastest and most stable for SPD XtX
        L = np.linalg.cholesky(XtX)
        tmp = np.linalg.solve(L, XtY)
        betas_arr = np.linalg.solve(L.T, tmp)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        logger.warning("Cholesky decomposition failed; falling back to direct solve. Check for near-singular XtX.")
        try:
            # Fall back to a direct solve of the normal equations
            betas_arr = np.linalg.solve(XtX, XtY)
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            logger.warning("Direct solve failed; falling back to lstsq. Model matrix may be rank-deficient.")
            # Final fallback: least-squares without forming normal equations
            # This handles rank deficiency and ill-conditioning better.
            betas_arr, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X_arr, Y_arr, rcond=None)

    if y_cols is not None:
        # Return a DataFrame so downstream matmul with numpy yields a DataFrame
        # and index/column handling stays consistent with previous behavior.
        return pd.DataFrame(betas_arr, columns=y_cols)
    return betas_arr

def get_observed_vectors(
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    group_col: str,
    level_col: str,
    full: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Get LS-mean vectors for each group × level cell.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X: pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame containing factors `group_col` and `level_col` for each row
        corresponding to `Y`.
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Outcome matrix (n_samples × n_features).
    group_col: str
        Group column name in `X`.
    level_col: str
        Level/state column name in `X`.
    full: bool
        Whether to include interactions in the model.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        LS means arranged with a MultiIndex (group, level). Columns follow `Y`.
    """
    model_full = get_model_matrix(X[[group_col, level_col]], group_col, level_col, full)
    betas = estimate_betas(model_full, Y)

    g_levels = _sort_levels(pd.unique(X[group_col].astype(str)).tolist())
    l_levels = _sort_levels(pd.unique(X[level_col].astype(str)).tolist())
    ls_matrix = build_ls_means(g_levels, l_levels, full)
    means = np.matmul(ls_matrix, np.asarray(betas, dtype=float))

    # Build a clear index and columns
    idx = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([g_levels, l_levels], names=[group_col, level_col])
    if isinstance(Y, pd.DataFrame):
        cols = Y.columns
    else:
        cols = [f"f{i}" for i in range(means.shape[1])]  # type: ignore[assignment]
    return pd.DataFrame(means, index=idx, columns=cols)

def estimate_difference(
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    model_matrix: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    LS_means: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    contrast: list[list[int]],
    *,
    return_spectra: bool = False,
    orientation_estimator: str = "pc1",
) -> tuple:
    """
    Estimate parameters angle, delta, and shape given an outcome
    matrix, model matrix, and contrast to compare. This is a comparison
    of more than two states.

    Parameters
    ----------
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Outcome matrix.
    model_matrix: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Model matrix with intercept.
    LS_means: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Least-squares means to estimate.
    contrast: list[list[int]]
        Indices indicating the groups to compare based on LS means.
        Each list must contain the cohorts that belong to the same group.
    return_spectra: bool
        When ``True``, additionally return the pooled and per-group stage-mean
        configuration spectra (:func:`configuration_spectra`) computed from the
        LS-mean vectors this call already fits. Off by default: the returned
        tuple is then exactly the historical three-element one.
    orientation_estimator: str
        How each group's orientation is estimated for ``angles``: ``"pc1"``
        (default; :func:`_estimate_orientation`) or ``"net_displacement"``
        (:func:`_estimate_net_displacement`). Only ``angles`` depends on it. A
        net displacement of zero length has no direction, and its pairwise
        angles are ``NaN``.

    Returns
    -------
    deltas: np.ndarray
        Symmetric matrix (n_groups x n_groups) with differences in magnitude.
    angles: np.ndarray
        Symmetric matrix (n_groups x n_groups) with differences in direction (degrees).
    shapes: np.ndarray
        Symmetric matrix (n_groups x n_groups) with Procrustes shape distances
        after removing translation, uniform scale, and any orthogonal
        transformation. Reflections are aligned away at every ambient
        dimension; a mirror difference is an orientation difference and
        surfaces in ``angles``.
    spectra: dict[str, Any]
        Only when ``return_spectra=True``. A recorded covariate — it enters no
        statistic and no decision rule.

    Notes
    -----
    See [1]_ for more information on trajectory analysis.

    References
    ----------
    .. [1] Adams, Dean C., and Michael L. Collyer.
           "A general framework for the analysis of phenotypic trajectories in
           evolutionary studies."
           Evolution: International Journal of Organic Evolution 63.5 (2009):
           1143-1154.
           https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1558-5646.2009.00649.x
    """
    # --- Input validation ---
    _Y = np.asarray(Y, dtype=float)
    _X = np.asarray(model_matrix, dtype=float)
    _LS = np.asarray(LS_means, dtype=float)
    if _Y.shape[0] != _X.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Y has {_Y.shape[0]} rows but model_matrix has {_X.shape[0]} rows — "
            "number of rows must match."
        )
    if _LS.shape[1] != _X.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"LS_means has {_LS.shape[1]} columns but model_matrix has {_X.shape[1]} columns — "
            "number of columns must match."
        )
    _n_ls = _LS.shape[0]
    for _gi, _group in enumerate(contrast):
        for _idx in _group:
            if not (0 <= _idx < _n_ls):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"contrast[{_gi}] contains index {_idx}, but LS_means only has {_n_ls} rows "
                    f"(valid indices: 0–{_n_ls - 1})."
                )
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(_Y)):
        raise ValueError("Y contains NaN or Inf values.")
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(_X)):
        raise ValueError("model_matrix contains NaN or Inf values.")
    if orientation_estimator not in ORIENTATION_ESTIMATORS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown orientation_estimator {orientation_estimator!r}; "
            f"expected one of {list(ORIENTATION_ESTIMATORS)}."
        )
    # --- End validation ---
    estimate_orientation = (
        _estimate_net_displacement if orientation_estimator == "net_displacement" else _estimate_orientation
    )
    n_groups = len(contrast)
    betas = estimate_betas(model_matrix, Y)
    # Compute LS-mean vectors; keep as DataFrame to minimize behavioral drift
    obs_vect = pd.DataFrame(
        np.matmul(np.asarray(LS_means, dtype=float), np.asarray(betas, dtype=float))
    )
    ys = []
    des = []
    angles = np.zeros((n_groups, n_groups))
    deltas = np.zeros((n_groups, n_groups))
    for i in range(n_groups):
        y = estimate_orientation(obs_vect, contrast[i])
        d = _estimate_size(obs_vect, contrast[i])
        des.append(d)
        ys.append(y)
    shapes = _estimate_shape(obs_vect, contrast)
    for i in range(n_groups):
        comp = i + 1
        while comp < n_groups:
            delta = np.abs(des[i] - des[comp])
            # When using SVD, no need to divide by size
            dot = np.clip(np.inner(ys[i], ys[comp]), -1.0, 1.0)
            angle = np.arccos(dot) * 180 / np.pi
            deltas[i, comp] = delta
            deltas[comp, i] = delta
            angles[i, comp] = angle
            angles[comp, i] = angle
            comp += 1
    if return_spectra:
        return deltas, angles, shapes, configuration_spectra(obs_vect, contrast)
    return deltas, angles, shapes

def pair_difference(
    dat: pd.DataFrame,
    group_col: str,
    level_col: str,
    groups: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
    levels: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
    feature_cols: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """
    Estimate difference in direction (angle, degrees) and magnitude (delta)
    between two groups across two levels.

    The change vector for a group is defined as `level1 - level2` over the
    selected feature columns.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dat: pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame containing features plus `group_col` and `level_col`.
    group_col: str
        Column with groups (between-subject factor).
    level_col: str
        Column with levels/states (within-subject factor).
    groups: tuple[str, str] | None
        Pair of group labels to compare. If None, infer and require exactly two.
    levels: tuple[str, str] | None
        Pair of level labels to use for the change vector. If None, infer and
        require exactly two.
    feature_cols: Sequence[str] | None
        Feature columns to use. If None, all numeric columns except `group_col`
        and `level_col` are used.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[float, float]
        (angle_degrees, delta_magnitude_difference)

    Notes
    -----
    See [1]_ for more information on two-state comparisons.

    References
    ----------
    .. [1] Collyer, Michael L., and Dean C. Adams. "Analysis of two‐state
           multivariate phenotypic change in ecological studies." Ecology 88.3
           (2007): 683-692. https://doi.org/10.1890/06-0727
    """
    if feature_cols is None:
        feature_cols = [
            c
            for c in dat.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
            if c not in {group_col, level_col}
        ]
    if not feature_cols:
        raise ValueError("No feature columns provided or detected.")

    g_vals = _sort_levels(pd.unique(dat[group_col].astype(str)).tolist())
    l_vals = _sort_levels(pd.unique(dat[level_col].astype(str)).tolist())
    if groups is None:
        if len(g_vals) != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected exactly 2 groups, found {len(g_vals)}: {g_vals}"
            )
        groups = (g_vals[0], g_vals[1])
    if levels is None:
        if len(l_vals) != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected exactly 2 levels, found {len(l_vals)}: {l_vals}"
            )
        levels = (l_vals[0], l_vals[1])

    # Compute per (group, level) means
    means = (
        dat.assign(
            __g=dat[group_col].astype(str), __l=dat[level_col].astype(str)
        )
        .groupby(["__g", "__l"])[feature_cols]
        .mean()
    )
    try:
        y_g1 = np.asarray(means.loc[(groups[0], levels[0])], dtype=float) - np.asarray(
            means.loc[(groups[0], levels[1])], dtype=float
        )
        y_g2 = np.asarray(means.loc[(groups[1], levels[0])], dtype=float) - np.asarray(
            means.loc[(groups[1], levels[1])], dtype=float
        )
    except KeyError as e:
        raise ValueError(
            "Missing combinations for the requested groups/levels in the data."
        ) from e

    d1 = float(np.linalg.norm(y_g1))
    d2 = float(np.linalg.norm(y_g2))
    delta = abs(d1 - d2)
    if d1 == 0 or d2 == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "Zero-magnitude change vector for at least one group; angle is undefined."
        )
    angle = float(np.degrees(np.arccos(np.inner(y_g1 / d1, y_g2 / d2))))
    return angle, delta

def RRPP(
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    model_full: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    model_reduced: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    LS_means: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    contrast: list[list[int]],
    permutations: int = 999,
    n_jobs: Optional[int] = None,
    progress: bool = True,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    return_eigengaps: bool = False,
    orientation_estimator: str = "pc1",
    residual_correction: Optional[str] = None,
) -> tuple:
    """
    Residual Randomization in a Permutation Procedure to evaluate
    linear models.

    Parameters
    ----------
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Outcome matrix.
    model_full: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Model matrix for full model, including intercept.
    model_reduced: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Model matrix for reduced model, including intercept.
    LS_means: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Least-squares means to estimate.
    contrast: list[list[int]]
        Indices indicating the groups to compare based on LS means.
        Each list must contain the cohorts that belong to the same group.
    permutations: int
        Number of permutations.
    n_jobs: Optional[int]
        If provided and > 1, run permutations in parallel using multiple
        worker processes. Use -1 to use all available CPUs. When None or 1,
        runs single-threaded (backward-compatible default).
    seed: Optional[int]
        Optional seed for reproducible residual randomization.
    return_eigengaps: bool
        When ``True``, additionally return the pooled stage-mean configuration
        relative eigengap of each permutation draw, so a replicate can locate its
        observed eigengap against its own permutation distribution. The spectrum
        consumes no randomness, so the permutation draws and the three returned
        null distributions are identical with the flag on or off. Off by default:
        the returned tuple is then exactly the historical three-element one.
    orientation_estimator: str
        Orientation estimator for every permuted ``angle`` (``"pc1"``, the
        default, or ``"net_displacement"``); see
        :func:`motco.stats.trajectory.estimate_difference`.
    residual_correction: Optional[str]
        Rescale the reduced model's residuals once before they are permuted:
        ``"df"`` multiplies each by κ = √(n / (n − r)) and ``"leverage"``
        divides each by √(1 − h_ii) (see :func:`residual_correction_scale`).
        The permutation indices, the reduced fitted values and the full-model
        estimation are unchanged, so only the null distributions move. ``None``
        (the default) permutes the raw residuals, exactly as before the
        setting existed. An unknown or undefined correction raises before any
        permutation is drawn.

    Returns
    -------
    dist_delta: list[float]
        Distribution of deltas.
    dist_angle: list[float]
        Distribution of angles.
    """
    # --- Input validation ---
    _Y = np.asarray(Y, dtype=float)
    _Xf = np.asarray(model_full, dtype=float)
    _Xr = np.asarray(model_reduced, dtype=float)
    _LS = np.asarray(LS_means, dtype=float)
    if _Y.shape[0] != _Xf.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Y has {_Y.shape[0]} rows but model_full has {_Xf.shape[0]} rows — "
            "number of rows must match."
        )
    if _Y.shape[0] != _Xr.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Y has {_Y.shape[0]} rows but model_reduced has {_Xr.shape[0]} rows — "
            "number of rows must match."
        )
    if _LS.shape[1] != _Xf.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"LS_means has {_LS.shape[1]} columns but model_full has {_Xf.shape[1]} columns — "
            "number of columns must match."
        )
    _n_ls = _LS.shape[0]
    for _gi, _group in enumerate(contrast):
        for _idx in _group:
            if not (0 <= _idx < _n_ls):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"contrast[{_gi}] contains index {_idx}, but LS_means only has {_n_ls} rows "
                    f"(valid indices: 0–{_n_ls - 1})."
                )
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(_Y)):
        raise ValueError("Y contains NaN or Inf values.")
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(_Xf)):
        raise ValueError("model_full contains NaN or Inf values.")
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(_Xr)):
        raise ValueError("model_reduced contains NaN or Inf values.")
    correction_scale = None if residual_correction is None else residual_correction_scale(_Xr, residual_correction)
    # --- End validation ---
    # Set Y to be pandas df
    Y = pd.DataFrame(Y)
    # Set-up permutation procedure
    betas_red = estimate_betas(model_reduced, Y)
    # Predicted values from reduced model
    y_hat = np.matmul(model_reduced, betas_red)
    y_hat.index = Y.index
    # Resdiuals of reduced mode (these are the permuted units)
    y_res = Y - y_hat
    # Prepare NumPy views to avoid pandas inside the permutation loop
    y_hat_np = np.asarray(y_hat)
    y_res_np = np.asarray(y_res)
    if correction_scale is not None:
        # Rescaled once, before either path: the draws below are untouched.
        y_res_np = y_res_np * correction_scale[:, None]
    # Prepare containers
    deltas: list[np.ndarray] = []
    angles: list[np.ndarray] = []
    shapes: list[np.ndarray] = []
    eigengaps: list[float | None] = []

    # Serial path
    if n_jobs in (None, 1):
        n = y_res_np.shape[0]
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        for _ in tqdm(range(permutations), desc="RRPP", unit="perm", disable=not progress):
            # Drawn before any spectrum work, and identically either way.
            idx = rng.permutation(n)
            y_random = y_hat_np + y_res_np[idx, :]
            if return_eigengaps:
                d, a, s, spectra = estimate_difference(
                    y_random,
                    model_full,
                    LS_means,
                    contrast,
                    return_spectra=True,
                    orientation_estimator=orientation_estimator,
                )
                eigengaps.append(pooled_relative_eigengap(spectra))
            else:
                d, a, s = estimate_difference(
                    y_random, model_full, LS_means, contrast, orientation_estimator=orientation_estimator
                )
            deltas.append(d)
            angles.append(a)
            shapes.append(s)
        if return_eigengaps:
            return deltas, angles, shapes, eigengaps
        return deltas, angles, shapes

    # Parallel path
    n_workers = (os.cpu_count() or 1) if n_jobs == -1 else max(1, n_jobs or 1)
    n_workers = min(n_workers, max(1, permutations))
    logger.info("Running %d permutations across %d workers", permutations, n_workers)
    base = permutations // n_workers
    rem = permutations % n_workers
    counts = [base + (1 if i < rem else 0) for i in range(n_workers)]

    ss = np.random.SeedSequence(seed)
    seeds = [int(s.generate_state(1)[0]) for s in ss.spawn(n_workers)]

    worker = _RRPPWorker(
        y_hat_np,
        y_res_np,
        model_full,
        LS_means,
        contrast,
        return_eigengaps=return_eigengaps,
        orientation_estimator=orientation_estimator,
    )
    with multiprocessing.Pool(processes=n_workers) as pool:
        parts = pool.starmap(worker, zip(counts, seeds))

    for part in parts:
        deltas.extend(part[0])
        angles.extend(part[1])
        shapes.extend(part[2])
        if return_eigengaps:
            eigengaps.extend(part[3])

    if return_eigengaps:
        return deltas, angles, shapes, eigengaps
    return deltas, angles, shapes

docs.title: motco.stats.permutation.residual_correction_scale(model_reduced, correction)
docs.text:
Per-sample multipliers a residual correction applies to the reduced model's residuals.

The reduced model's mean squared residual is RSS/n, not the unbiased RSS/(n − r), so permuting the raw residuals draws a null that is too narrow for scale-dependent statistics. The corrections restore that scale:

  • "df": every residual is multiplied by κ = √(n / (n − r));
  • "leverage": residual i is divided by √(1 − h_ii), with h the reduced model's hat matrix.

r is the numerical rank of model_reduced (numpy's matrix_rank tolerance on its thin SVD), so a rank-deficient model uses its rank, not its column count. A balanced one-factor model gives every sample the same leverage r/n, where both corrections coincide.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model_reduced Union[DataFrame, ndarray]

Model matrix of the reduced model, including intercept.

required correction str

One of :data:RESIDUAL_CORRECTIONS.

required

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

One multiplier per row of model_reduced.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For an unknown correction, for "df" when n − r ≤ 0, and for "leverage" when a row has leverage 1 to numerical tolerance.

def residual_correction_scale(
    model_reduced: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    correction: str,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Per-sample multipliers a residual correction applies to the reduced model's residuals.

    The reduced model's mean squared residual is RSS/n, not the unbiased
    RSS/(n − r), so permuting the raw residuals draws a null that is too
    narrow for scale-dependent statistics. The corrections restore that scale:

    - ``"df"``: every residual is multiplied by κ = √(n / (n − r));
    - ``"leverage"``: residual i is divided by √(1 − h_ii), with h the reduced
      model's hat matrix.

    r is the numerical rank of ``model_reduced`` (numpy's ``matrix_rank``
    tolerance on its thin SVD), so a rank-deficient model uses its rank, not
    its column count. A balanced one-factor model gives every sample the same
    leverage r/n, where both corrections coincide.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model_reduced: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Model matrix of the reduced model, including intercept.
    correction: str
        One of :data:`RESIDUAL_CORRECTIONS`.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        One multiplier per row of ``model_reduced``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For an unknown correction, for ``"df"`` when n − r ≤ 0, and for
        ``"leverage"`` when a row has leverage 1 to numerical tolerance.
    """
    if correction not in RESIDUAL_CORRECTIONS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown residual_correction {correction!r}; allowed: {list(RESIDUAL_CORRECTIONS)} or None."
        )
    X = np.asarray(model_reduced, dtype=float)
    n, p = X.shape
    U, s, _ = np.linalg.svd(X, full_matrices=False)
    tolerance = s.max() * max(n, p) * np.finfo(float).eps if s.size else 0.0
    rank = int(np.sum(s > tolerance))
    if correction == "df":
        if n - rank <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The df residual correction needs n - rank > 0, but the reduced model has n = {n} rows "
                f"and rank {rank}."
            )
        return np.full(n, np.sqrt(n / (n - rank)))
    complement = 1.0 - np.sum(U[:, :rank] ** 2, axis=1)
    saturated = np.flatnonzero(complement <= _LEVERAGE_TOLERANCE)
    if saturated.size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The leverage residual correction is undefined: row {int(saturated[0])} of the reduced model has "
            f"leverage 1 (1 - h_ii = {complement[saturated[0]]:.3g})."
        )
    return 1.0 / np.sqrt(complement)

docs.title: Interaction test inside and outside a span
docs.text:
delta, angle and shape see a group difference only through its component inside the latent span they are measured in. interaction_split_test asks whether the groups differ by stage at all, and where, without a latent space: it splits the group × stage interaction energy of the outcome exactly into the part inside a given orthonormal basis (span) and the part in its orthogonal complement (complement), beside the total. Each part is tested by a trace pseudo-F under Freedman–Lane permutation of the reduced model's residuals, with RRPP's serial draws at the same seed and its residual corrections.

The basis must stay fixed across permutations and be built without the group labels (for the production measurement, qr(x_rotations_) of the stage-supervised PLS model in its input coordinates). The pseudo-F is the statistic because its ratio cancels the residual scale the reduced model's degrees of freedom remove; the interaction-SS p-value is a diagnostic. See Measurement visibility for how the parts are read.

def interaction_split_test(
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    model_full: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    model_reduced: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    basis: np.ndarray,
    *,
    permutations: int = 0,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    residual_correction: Optional[str] = None,
    return_null: bool = False,
) -> InteractionSplitResult:
    """Test the group × stage interaction inside a span and in its orthogonal complement.

    Parameters
    ----------
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Outcome matrix, ``n × p``, in the coordinates the basis is orthonormal in.
    model_full: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Model matrix of the full model (group × stage, plus any covariates), including intercept.
    model_reduced: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Model matrix of the reduced model (group + stage, plus the same covariates), nested in the full one.
    basis: np.ndarray
        ``p × r`` matrix with orthonormal columns (tolerance 1e-8), ``1 ≤ r < p``.
    permutations: int
        Number of Freedman–Lane draws; 0 reports the observed quantities only.
    seed: Optional[int]
        Seed of ``np.random.default_rng``; each draw is one ``rng.permutation(n)``,
        RRPP's serial sequence, so the test pairs with a trajectory analysis at the same seed.
    residual_correction: Optional[str]
        ``"df"``, ``"leverage"`` or ``None``, applied to the reduced residuals before any draw
        (see :func:`motco.stats.permutation.residual_correction_scale`). The observed quantities
        do not depend on it; under ``"df"`` the pseudo-F null is unchanged and the SS null scales by κ².
    return_null: bool
        Keep the per-draw null pseudo-F and SS of every part.

    Returns
    -------
    InteractionSplitResult

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Before any draw, for inputs whose rows or columns disagree, non-finite values, a basis
        whose columns are not orthonormal, an empty basis or complement, models that are not
        nested, a non-positive df_int or df_res, a negative permutation count, or an unknown or
        undefined residual correction.
    """

    outcome = np.asarray(Y, dtype=float)
    full = np.asarray(model_full, dtype=float)
    reduced = np.asarray(model_reduced, dtype=float)
    Q = np.asarray(basis, dtype=float)
    _validate_shapes(outcome, full, reduced, Q)
    _check_permutations(permutations)
    n, p = outcome.shape
    r = Q.shape[1]
    spaces = _model_spaces(full, reduced)
    df_interaction = spaces.df_interaction
    df_residual = spaces.df_residual
    U_reduced = spaces.U_reduced
    scale = None if residual_correction is None else residual_correction_scale(reduced, residual_correction)

    residuals = outcome - U_reduced @ (U_reduced.T @ outcome)
    in_span = residuals @ Q
    # Formed directly: G_total − G_span would cancel badly when the span holds most of the energy.
    out_of_span = residuals - in_span @ Q.T
    grams = {
        "total": residuals @ residuals.T,
        "span": in_span @ in_span.T,
        "complement": out_of_span @ out_of_span.T,
    }
    dimensions = {"total": p, "span": r, "complement": p - r}
    weights = spaces.weights

    observed: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {
        name: _sums(gram, weights, df_interaction, float(np.trace(gram))) for name, gram in grams.items()
    }
    null_ss: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    null_rss: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    if permutations > 0:
        scaled = grams if scale is None else {name: gram * np.outer(scale, scale) for name, gram in grams.items()}
        traces = {name: float(np.trace(gram)) for name, gram in scaled.items()}
        for name in INTERACTION_SPLIT_PARTS:
            null_ss[name] = np.empty(permutations)
            null_rss[name] = np.empty(permutations)
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        for draw in range(permutations):
            idx = rng.permutation(n)
            # Row i of the permuted residuals is row idx[i], and Σ_ij w_i·G[idx_i, idx_j]·w_j = w'ᵀ·G·w'
            # with w' = w[argsort(idx)], so the permuted Gram matrix is never formed.
            permuted_weights = weights[np.argsort(idx)]
            for name, gram in scaled.items():
                ss, rss = _sums(gram, permuted_weights, df_interaction, traces[name])
                null_ss[name][draw] = ss
                null_rss[name][draw] = rss

    parts: dict[str, InteractionSplitPart] = {}
    for name in INTERACTION_SPLIT_PARTS:
        ss, rss = observed[name]
        f_value = _pseudo_f(np.array([ss]), np.array([rss]), df_interaction, df_residual)[0]
        p_value_f: float | None = None
        p_value_ss: float | None = None
        part_null_f: np.ndarray | None = None
        if permutations > 0:
            part_null_f = _pseudo_f(null_ss[name], null_rss[name], df_interaction, df_residual)
            p_value_ss = _p_value(null_ss[name], ss)
            p_value_f = _p_value(part_null_f, f_value) if np.isfinite(f_value) else None
        parts[name] = InteractionSplitPart(
            dimension=dimensions[name],
            ss_interaction=ss,
            rss=rss,
            df_interaction=df_interaction,
            df_residual=df_residual,
            f=float(f_value),
            p_value_f=p_value_f,
            p_value_ss=p_value_ss,
            null_f=part_null_f if return_null else None,
            null_ss=null_ss[name] if (return_null and permutations > 0) else None,
        )
    total_ss = parts["total"].ss_interaction
    span_share = None if total_ss <= 0.0 else float(np.clip(parts["span"].ss_interaction / total_ss, 0.0, 1.0))
    return InteractionSplitResult(
        parts=parts,
        span_share=span_share,
        permutations=int(permutations),
        seed=seed,
        residual_correction=residual_correction,
    )

class InteractionSplitPart:

    ``None`` without permutations (or for an undefined pseudo-F). ``null_f``

    """

    rss: float
    df_interaction: int
    df_residual: int

            "df_residual": self.df_residual,

docs.title: Per-feature interaction scan
docs.text:
The split test's complement sums interaction energy over every coordinate outside the span, so a difference confined to a few features is lost in the noise of the rest. interaction_feature_scan tests the same group × stage interaction one feature at a time: each outcome column gets the one-column F (SS_int / df_int) / (RSS / df_res), and the features are combined by their maximum. A sum pays for every noise dimension; a maximum pays only for the search, so the scan targets differences on few features and the split test's complement differences spread over many.

With permutations, the reduced model's residuals are permuted by Freedman–Lane with RRPP's serial draws at the same seed and its residual corrections (a constant multiplier such as df cancels in every F). The global p-value is the permutation p-value of the largest F, and each feature gets a Westfall–Young step-down max-T adjusted p-value, which controls the familywise error rate over the scanned features; the top feature's adjusted p-value is the global one. Features with zero full-model residual variance (constant ones included) are degenerate: they get no F or p-value and never enter a maximum. A draw costs one rank(F) × n by n × p product, so 999 draws over 10,000 features take seconds. A hit is a feature whose covariate-adjusted group difference changes across stages; it does not say the feature drives a latent trajectory difference. See Measurement visibility.

docs.title: By block
docs.text:
One maximum over every feature lets the block that most often gives the largest null F set every block's bar: a block with many features, or with a heavier-tailed null F, takes most of the familywise error. With blocks= (one label per column) the scan shares the familywise error equally between the blocks (combination="block_bonferroni"):

  • Within each block the same step-down runs on the block's features alone, on the same draws and the same per-draw F, giving each feature its within-block value p⁽ᵏ⁾ and each block its own global p-value p_k (its top feature's p⁽ᵏ⁾).
  • Across blocks each of the K blocks holding a non-degenerate feature is tested at α/K: a feature's adjusted p-value is min(1, K · p⁽ᵏ⁾) and the global p-value min(1, K · min_k p_k), the smallest adjusted p-value. The union bound keeps the familywise error over all features at α whatever the dependence between blocks.
  • The result adds n_blocks_tested (K), one InteractionScanBlock per label in order of first appearance (name, columns, n_degenerate, max_f, max_column, and with permutations p_value = p_k and null_max_f, every draw's block maximum) and null_block_max_f (draws × K). max_f, max_column, null_max_f and null_max_column stay the joint ones, and hits() reads the by-block adjusted p-values. A block whose columns are all degenerate has no maximum or p-value and does not count in K.
  • Identity. One label on every column gives the joint scan's p-values and hits exactly; without labels the scan, its result and its serialization are unchanged.

A label list whose length is not the number of outcome columns is rejected before any draw, naming both lengths. A hit at α/K needs at most ⌊(α/K)(1 + B)⌋ − 1 exceeding draws (24 of 999 at K = 2), so the split needs B ≫ K/α, not the B ≫ p/α a per-feature minP would.

docs.text:
Test the group × stage interaction feature by feature, combined by the maximum F.

For each outcome column y, the interaction sum of squares is ‖(H_F − H_R)·y‖², the residual sum of squares ‖(I − H_F)·y‖² and F = (SS_int / df_int) / (RSS / df_res), with df_int = rank(F) − rank(R) and df_res = n − rank(F). Each F ignores its column's location and scale, and the per-feature sums add to :func:interaction_split_test's total sums.

A column whose RSS is at most 1e-12 of its centred sum of squares, or that is constant, is degenerate: it gets no F and no p-value and never enters a maximum.

With permutations, the reduced residuals are permuted by Freedman–Lane with RRPP's serial index sequence (one rng.permutation(n) per draw from np.random.default_rng(seed)), and every feature's F is evaluated at every draw from the same permuted residuals. The global p-value is the permutation p-value of the largest F. Each feature's adjusted p-value is Westfall–Young step-down max-T: with features ordered by observed F (descending, ties by column index), rank j's raw value is (1 + #{draws whose largest null F over ranks ≥ j is ≥ the j-th observed F}) / (1 + B), and the adjusted p-value is the running maximum down the order. The top feature's adjusted p-value is the global p-value.

With blocks (one label per column), the familywise error is split equally between the K blocks that hold a non-degenerate feature. Within each block the same step-down runs on the block's features alone, on the same draws and the same per-draw F, giving p⁽ᵏ⁾; a feature's adjusted p-value is min(1, K · p⁽ᵏ⁾), block k's own global p-value p_k is its top feature's p⁽ᵏ⁾, and the global p-value is min(1, K · min_k p_k). Each block's step-down controls its familywise error, so testing each at α/K controls it over all features by the union bound, whatever the dependence between blocks. One label on every column gives the joint scan exactly.

def interaction_feature_scan(
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    model_full: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    model_reduced: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    *,
    permutations: int = 0,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    residual_correction: Optional[str] = None,
    return_null: bool = False,
    blocks: Optional[Sequence[Hashable]] = None,
) -> InteractionScanResult:
    """Test the group × stage interaction feature by feature, combined by the maximum F.

    For each outcome column y, the interaction sum of squares is
    ``‖(H_F − H_R)·y‖²``, the residual sum of squares ``‖(I − H_F)·y‖²`` and
    ``F = (SS_int / df_int) / (RSS / df_res)``, with ``df_int = rank(F) −
    rank(R)`` and ``df_res = n − rank(F)``. Each F ignores its column's location
    and scale, and the per-feature sums add to
    :func:`interaction_split_test`'s ``total`` sums.

    A column whose RSS is at most 1e-12 of its centred sum of squares, or that
    is constant, is degenerate: it gets no F and no p-value and never enters a
    maximum.

    With permutations, the reduced residuals are permuted by Freedman–Lane with
    RRPP's serial index sequence (one ``rng.permutation(n)`` per draw from
    ``np.random.default_rng(seed)``), and every feature's F is evaluated at
    every draw from the same permuted residuals. The global p-value is the
    permutation p-value of the largest F. Each feature's adjusted p-value is
    Westfall–Young step-down max-T: with features ordered by observed F
    (descending, ties by column index), rank j's raw value is ``(1 + #{draws
    whose largest null F over ranks ≥ j is ≥ the j-th observed F}) / (1 + B)``,
    and the adjusted p-value is the running maximum down the order. The top
    feature's adjusted p-value is the global p-value.

    With ``blocks`` (one label per column), the familywise error is split
    equally between the K blocks that hold a non-degenerate feature. Within
    each block the same step-down runs on the block's features alone, on the
    same draws and the same per-draw F, giving p⁽ᵏ⁾; a feature's adjusted
    p-value is ``min(1, K · p⁽ᵏ⁾)``, block k's own global p-value p_k is its
    top feature's p⁽ᵏ⁾, and the global p-value is ``min(1, K · min_k p_k)``.
    Each block's step-down controls its familywise error, so testing each at
    α/K controls it over all features by the union bound, whatever the
    dependence between blocks. One label on every column gives the joint scan
    exactly.

    Parameters
    ----------
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Outcome matrix, ``n × p``.
    model_full: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Model matrix of the full model (group × stage, plus any covariates), including intercept.
    model_reduced: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Model matrix of the reduced model (group + stage, plus the same covariates), nested in the full one.
    permutations: int
        Number of Freedman–Lane draws; 0 reports the observed F only.
    seed: Optional[int]
        Seed of ``np.random.default_rng``, so the scan pairs with a trajectory analysis at the same seed.
    residual_correction: Optional[str]
        ``"df"``, ``"leverage"`` or ``None``, applied to the reduced residuals before any draw
        (see :func:`motco.stats.permutation.residual_correction_scale`). The observed F do not depend on
        it, and a constant multiplier (``"df"``, or ``"leverage"`` at equal leverages) cancels in every F,
        so it leaves every null F and p-value unchanged.
    return_null: bool
        Keep the draws × columns null F.
    blocks: Optional[Sequence[Hashable]]
        One block label per outcome column, for the by-block combination (``block_bonferroni``); the
        blocks are named ``str(label)`` in order of first appearance. ``None`` runs the joint scan.

    Returns
    -------
    InteractionScanResult

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Before any draw, for inputs whose rows disagree, non-finite values, models that are not nested,
        a non-positive df_int or df_res, a negative permutation count, an unknown or undefined residual
        correction, block labels that do not give one label per column, or an outcome whose every column
        is degenerate.
    """

    outcome = np.asarray(Y, dtype=float)
    full = np.asarray(model_full, dtype=float)
    reduced = np.asarray(model_reduced, dtype=float)
    named = (("Y", outcome), ("model_full", full), ("model_reduced", reduced))
    _check_two_dimensional(named)
    _check_rows(outcome, full, reduced)
    labels = None if blocks is None else _block_labels(blocks, outcome.shape[1])
    _check_finite(named)
    _check_permutations(permutations)
    n, p = outcome.shape
    spaces = _model_spaces(full, reduced)
    df_interaction = spaces.df_interaction
    df_residual = spaces.df_residual
    scale = None if residual_correction is None else residual_correction_scale(reduced, residual_correction)

    residuals = outcome - spaces.U_reduced @ (spaces.U_reduced.T @ outcome)
    ss, rss = _feature_sums(residuals, spaces.weights, df_interaction, np.sum(residuals**2, axis=0))
    centred_ss = np.sum((outcome - outcome.mean(axis=0)) ** 2, axis=0)
    constant = np.all(outcome == outcome[:1], axis=0)
    degenerate = constant | (rss <= _DEGENERATE_TOLERANCE * centred_ss)
    valid = np.flatnonzero(~degenerate)
    if valid.size == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No feature has a defined F: all {p} outcome column(s) are degenerate (zero full-model residual "
            "variance)."
        )
    f_values = np.full(p, np.nan)
    f_values[valid] = _pseudo_f(ss[valid], rss[valid], df_interaction, df_residual)
    # Step-down order: F descending, ties by column index.
    order = valid[np.lexsort((valid, -f_values[valid]))]
    observed_sorted = f_values[order]
    max_column = int(order[0])
    max_f = float(observed_sorted[0])
    layout = None if labels is None else _block_layout(labels, valid, f_values)
    if permutations == 0:
        return InteractionScanResult(
            ss_interaction=ss,
            rss=rss,
            f=f_values,
            degenerate=degenerate,
            df_interaction=df_interaction,
            df_residual=df_residual,
            max_f=max_f,
            max_column=max_column,
            permutations=int(permutations),
            seed=seed,
            residual_correction=residual_correction,
            **({} if layout is None else _block_fields(layout, f_values, degenerate)),
        )

    permuted = residuals[:, order]
    if scale is not None and not np.all(scale == scale[0]):
        # A constant multiplier cancels in every F, so only a varying one is applied.
        permuted = permuted * scale[:, None]
    norms = np.sum(permuted**2, axis=0)
    exceed = np.zeros(order.size, dtype=np.int64)
    null_max_f = np.empty(permutations)
    null_max_column = np.empty(permutations, dtype=np.int64)
    null_f = np.full((permutations, p), np.nan) if return_null else None
    step_down = None if layout is None else _BlockStepDown(layout, order, f_values, permutations)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    for draw in range(permutations):
        idx = rng.permutation(n)
        # Row i of the permuted residuals is row idx[i], so Wᵀ·E[π] = W[argsort(idx)]ᵀ·E.
        draw_ss, draw_rss = _feature_sums(permuted, spaces.weights[np.argsort(idx)], df_interaction, norms)
        draw_f = _pseudo_f(draw_ss, draw_rss, df_interaction, df_residual)
        # 0 / 0 (a permuted column inside col(reduced)) carries no interaction.
        draw_f = np.where(np.isnan(draw_f), 0.0, draw_f)
        if step_down is None:
            suffix_max = np.maximum.accumulate(draw_f[::-1])[::-1]
            exceed += suffix_max >= observed_sorted
        else:
            step_down.add(draw, draw_f)
        position = int(np.argmax(draw_f))
        null_max_f[draw] = draw_f[position]
        null_max_column[draw] = order[position]
        if null_f is not None:
            null_f[draw, order] = draw_f
    adjusted = np.full(p, np.nan)
    block_fields: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if step_down is None:
        adjusted[order] = np.maximum.accumulate((1.0 + exceed) / (1.0 + permutations))
        p_value_global = _p_value(null_max_f, max_f)
    else:
        assert layout is not None
        within = step_down.within_block()
        n_tested = len(layout.segments)
        adjusted[layout.order] = np.minimum(1.0, n_tested * within)
        block_p_values = [float(within[start]) for _, start, _ in layout.segments]
        p_value_global = min(1.0, n_tested * min(block_p_values))
        block_fields = _block_fields(layout, f_values, degenerate, block_p_values, step_down.null_block_max_f)
    return InteractionScanResult(
        ss_interaction=ss,
        rss=rss,
        f=f_values,
        degenerate=degenerate,
        df_interaction=df_interaction,
        df_residual=df_residual,
        max_f=max_f,
        max_column=max_column,
        p_value_global=p_value_global,
        p_value_adjusted=adjusted,
        null_max_f=null_max_f,
        null_max_column=null_max_column,
        null_f=null_f,
        permutations=int(permutations),
        seed=seed,
        residual_correction=residual_correction,
        **block_fields,
    )

docs.title: motco.stats.interaction.InteractionScanResult dataclass
docs.text:
The per-feature interaction scan: one F per outcome column and their maximum.

ss_interaction, rss and f hold one value per outcome column; f is NaN where degenerate is true (zero full-model residual variance, a constant column included). max_f and max_column are the largest F over the non-degenerate columns and its column (ties go to the lower column index).

With permutations, p_value_global is (1 + #{draws whose largest null F ≥ max_f}) / (1 + permutations), p_value_adjusted holds each column's Westfall–Young step-down max-T adjusted p-value (NaN where degenerate), and null_max_f / null_max_column hold each draw's largest null F and the column attaining it. null_f (draws × columns, NaN where degenerate) is kept only when requested. Without permutations all of these are None.

combination is "joint" for a scan without block labels and "block_bonferroni" with them. A by-block scan also has blocks, one :class:InteractionScanBlock per label in order of first appearance, and n_blocks_tested (K, the blocks with a non-degenerate feature); its p_value_adjusted is min(1, K · the within-block step-down value), its p_value_global is min(1, K · the smallest block p-value) (the smallest adjusted p-value), and null_block_max_f (draws × K, the tested blocks in order) holds every draw's block maxima. max_f, max_column, null_max_f and null_max_column stay the joint ones.

Source code in src/motco/stats/interaction.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class InteractionScanResult:
    """The per-feature interaction scan: one F per outcome column and their maximum.

    ``ss_interaction``, ``rss`` and ``f`` hold one value per outcome column;
    ``f`` is ``NaN`` where ``degenerate`` is true (zero full-model residual
    variance, a constant column included). ``max_f`` and ``max_column`` are the
    largest F over the non-degenerate columns and its column (ties go to the
    lower column index).

    With permutations, ``p_value_global`` is ``(1 + #{draws whose largest null F
    ≥ max_f}) / (1 + permutations)``, ``p_value_adjusted`` holds each column's
    Westfall–Young step-down max-T adjusted p-value (``NaN`` where degenerate),
    and ``null_max_f`` / ``null_max_column`` hold each draw's largest null F and
    the column attaining it. ``null_f`` (draws × columns, ``NaN`` where
    degenerate) is kept only when requested. Without permutations all of these
    are ``None``.

    ``combination`` is ``"joint"`` for a scan without block labels and
    ``"block_bonferroni"`` with them. A by-block scan also has ``blocks``, one
    :class:`InteractionScanBlock` per label in order of first appearance, and
    ``n_blocks_tested`` (K, the blocks with a non-degenerate feature); its
    ``p_value_adjusted`` is ``min(1, K · the within-block step-down value)``,
    its ``p_value_global`` is ``min(1, K · the smallest block p-value)`` (the
    smallest adjusted p-value), and ``null_block_max_f`` (draws × K, the tested
    blocks in order) holds every draw's block maxima. ``max_f``,
    ``max_column``, ``null_max_f`` and ``null_max_column`` stay the joint ones.
    """

    ss_interaction: np.ndarray
    rss: np.ndarray
    f: np.ndarray
    degenerate: np.ndarray
    df_interaction: int
    df_residual: int
    max_f: float
    max_column: int
    permutations: int
    seed: int | None
    residual_correction: str | None
    p_value_global: float | None = None
    p_value_adjusted: np.ndarray | None = None
    null_max_f: np.ndarray | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
    null_max_column: np.ndarray | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
    null_f: np.ndarray | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
    combination: str = "joint"
    blocks: tuple[InteractionScanBlock, ...] | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
    n_blocks_tested: int | None = None
    null_block_max_f: np.ndarray | None = field(default=None, repr=False)

    @property
    def n_features(self) -> int:
        return int(self.f.size)

    @property
    def block_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
        """The block names in order of first appearance, ``None`` for a joint scan."""

        return None if self.blocks is None else tuple(block.name for block in self.blocks)

    @property
    def n_degenerate(self) -> int:
        return int(np.count_nonzero(self.degenerate))

    @property
    def degenerate_columns(self) -> np.ndarray:
        return np.flatnonzero(self.degenerate)

    def hits(self, alpha: float = INTERACTION_SCAN_ALPHA) -> np.ndarray:
        """Columns with adjusted p-value ≤ ``alpha``, by F descending (ties by column index).

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            When the scan ran without permutations.
        """

        if self.p_value_adjusted is None:
            raise ValueError("The scan ran without permutations; it has no adjusted p-values and no hits.")
        columns = np.flatnonzero(~self.degenerate & (self.p_value_adjusted <= alpha))
        return columns[np.lexsort((columns, -self.f[columns]))]

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Counts, df, the maximum and, with permutations, the global p-value and the hits by column index.

        A by-block scan adds ``combination``, ``n_blocks_tested`` and one entry per block.
        """

        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
            "n_features": self.n_features,
            "n_degenerate": self.n_degenerate,
            "degenerate_columns": [int(column) for column in self.degenerate_columns],
            "df_interaction": self.df_interaction,
            "df_residual": self.df_residual,
            "max_f": self.max_f,
            "max_column": self.max_column,
            "permutations": self.permutations,
            "seed": self.seed,
            "residual_correction": self.residual_correction,
        }
        if self.blocks is not None:
            payload["combination"] = self.combination
            payload["n_blocks_tested"] = self.n_blocks_tested
            drawn = self.p_value_adjusted is not None
            payload["blocks"] = [block.to_dict(with_p_value=drawn) for block in self.blocks]
        if self.p_value_adjusted is not None:
            assert self.p_value_global is not None
            payload["p_value_global"] = self.p_value_global
            payload["hit_alpha"] = INTERACTION_SCAN_ALPHA
            adjusted = self.p_value_adjusted
            payload["hits"] = [
                {"column": int(column), "f": float(self.f[column]), "p_value_adjusted": float(adjusted[column])}
                for column in self.hits()
            ]
        return payload

@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class InteractionScanBlock:
    """One block of a by-block feature scan.

    ``columns`` are the block's outcome columns (ascending). ``max_f`` and
    ``max_column`` are the largest F over its non-degenerate columns and the
    column attaining it (ties to the lower column index); both are ``None``
    when every column of the block is degenerate, and such a block is not
    tested. With permutations, ``p_value`` is the block's own global p-value
    ``(1 + #{draws whose largest null F over the block ≥ max_f}) / (1 +
    permutations)``, before the factor K, and ``null_max_f`` holds each draw's
    largest null F over the block.
    """

    name: str
    columns: np.ndarray = field(repr=False)
    n_degenerate: int
    max_f: float | None
    max_column: int | None
    p_value: float | None = None
    null_max_f: np.ndarray | None = field(default=None, repr=False)

    @property
    def n_features(self) -> int:
        return int(self.columns.size)

    @property
    def tested(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the block has a non-degenerate feature, and so counts in K."""

        return self.max_column is not None

    def to_dict(self, *, with_p_value: bool | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Name, counts, the maximum and, with permutations, the block's own global p-value.

        ``with_p_value`` says whether the scan drew permutations (an untested block then has a
        ``None`` p-value); by default it is read from the block's null maxima.
        """

        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
            "name": self.name,
            "n_features": self.n_features,
            "n_degenerate": self.n_degenerate,
            "max_f": self.max_f,
            "max_column": self.max_column,
        }
        drawn = self.null_max_f is not None if with_p_value is None else with_p_value
        if drawn:
            payload["p_value"] = self.p_value
        return payload
