docs.title: Simulations
docs.text: The numpy semi-synthetic generator, the evaluation harness that runs a generated dataset through MOTCO's measurement, and the grid and study orchestration behind the operating-characteristic studies. Generation needs no R at runtime: the generator samples from the cached InterSIM reference committed at src/motco/simulations/data/intersim_reference.npz. R and InterSIM are needed only to regenerate that cache and the fidelity fixtures; the Python bridge to R is kept as the legacy InterSIM bridge.

docs.title: Semi-synthetic trajectory generation
docs.text:
The semi-synthetic trajectory generator samples directly from the numpy-native InterSIM reimplementation (no R at runtime) and returns a MOTCO-ready dataset with:

  • aligned methylation, gene expression, and proteomics matrices
  • sample metadata containing sample_id, group, and stage
  • truth metadata recording trajectory mode, per-stage/group differential indicators, per-omic δ, and the generator seed

Group A is a random baseline trajectory; group B is a deterministic transform of group A's per-stage differential indicators selected by trajectory_mode.

from motco.simulations import (
    SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams,
    generate_semisynthetic_trajectory,
)

dataset = generate_semisynthetic_trajectory(
    SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams(
        seed=99,
        trajectory_mode="magnitude",
        n_samples=120,
        n_stages=3,
        group_effect_size=0.2,
        group_ratio=0.5,
    ),
)

sample_metadata = dataset.metadata
truth = dataset.truth

Supported trajectory modes (all governed by the unified group_effect_size knob, where 0 is the null for every mode):

Mode Injected group-specific pattern none Identical to baseline; useful for Type I error scenarios translation Constant observed-space location offset magnitude Scales δ (size); see the magnitude_kind table below orientation One global per-omic feature permutation (rotation) shape Permutes interior stages only (bend); requires at least three stages

magnitude_kind selects how magnitude scales group B (the motco simulate --magnitude-kind flag has the same default):

magnitude_kind Construction 'joint' (default) Scales every omic's δ (methylation, expression, proteomics) by the same 1 + e. Size-pure in the joint standardized space, not only within each block. This is the construction the Phase 5 magnitude re-measurement validated. 'all' Scales the methylation δ alone at every stage. Size-pure within the methylation block but rotates the concatenated trajectory. 'extremes' Scales only the endpoint stages' methylation indicators.

'extremes' and the shape mode's shape_kind='magnitude' remain methylation-only scalings; the joint default does not extend to them.

Explicit group × stage sizes. group_stage_sizes replaces proportional sizing (n_samples × stage_sample_prop × group_ratio) with an exact table: one tuple of per-stage counts per group, rows ordered as group_labels and columns as stages. Every group-stage cell gets exactly the stated number of samples, and truth metadata records the realized table under truth["group_stage_sizes"]. Use it when the imbalance varies by stage, as in a real cohort:

SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams(
    seed=1,
    n_stages=3,
    group_stage_sizes=((11, 10, 28), (9, 10, 12)),  # 80 samples, the SEA-AD MTG design
)

The table must have two rows of n_stages integers, each at least 1. Setting it together with a non-default n_samples, stage_sample_prop or group_ratio is an error that names the conflicting settings. When the table is absent (the default None), generation, truth metadata, cell ids and parameter signatures are byte-identical to the generator before the field existed: hash payloads omit the field while it is None.

Migration. Before default-joint-magnitude-construction the default was 'all'. Code that relied on the default and wants the old construction must pass magnitude_kind="all" (or --magnitude-kind all). The committed historical study configs under examples/trajectory_power_study/ already pin "all", so their cells, signatures and datasets are unchanged.

docs.title: Stage-span construction
docs.text:
The modes above are feature-set surgeries (the default, construction=None; "surgery" normalizes to it). construction="stage_span" is an opt-in, measurement-defined alternative: it edits group B's exact null population stage means inside the span of B's own stage configuration, so the planted difference lies where the stage-supervised PLS measurement looks. Use it to ask how sensitive the test is to a difference the measurement can see; the surgeries remain the biologically grounded constructions.

SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams(
    seed=1,
    trajectory_mode="orientation",
    group_effect_size=0.5,          # a 45° rotation
    construction="stage_span",
    span_layers=("methylation", "expression"),  # must equal the measured blocks
)

The edit is made over span_layers (default: all three blocks) in analysed units (methylation in M-values), each feature divided by its null population pooled SD: the within-cell variance (the reference covariance diagonal) plus the between-cell variance of the null means at the realized cell proportions. With z_s B's standardized stage means, centroid c, path length L, mean step L̄ = L / (S − 1) and u the unit net displacement:

Mode Stage-span edit Intended population geometry magnitude c + (1 + e)(z_s − c) path length ×(1 + e); angle = shape = 0 orientation rigid rotation about c by θ = 90°·e in the plane of u and the next principal direction v (e ≤ 2) net-displacement angle = θ; delta = shape = 0 shape the stage the shape surgery perturbs moves e·L̄ off the chord between its neighbours, then the path is rescaled to L and recentred on c shape > 0; delta = angle = 0 translation every stage moves e·L̄ along u all three statistics 0 (the in-span negative control)

The plant is mapped back to analysed units and added to group B's cell means before sampling (generate_omics(..., cell_shift_*=)); blocks outside span_layers are untouched. The construction draws no random numbers, so a stage-span dataset equals the none dataset at the same seed plus the plant: group A and B's sampling noise are shared with the surgery datasets of the same seed family. orientation and shape need a second in-span direction, so fewer than three stages, or a configuration whose second singular value is at most 1e-8 times its first, is an error; span_layers without stage_span, and unknown, duplicated or empty layers, are rejected.

Truth metadata records construction, span_layers, the effect parameters under transform (scale, rotation_degrees, shape_stage/displacement/rescale, or offset_length) and a stage_span block with the configuration's path_length and mean_step, the intended_geometry (net-displacement delta, angle, shape and path lengths in the null-standardized coordinates) and the plant_norm per stage. The population trajectories include the plant. Stage-span cells draw from no feature pool, so they have no surgery headroom and no realized-surgery summary. While both settings are unset every dataset, truth record, cell id and signature is byte-identical to the generator before they existed.

Alignment with the stage span. span_alignment (φ, in degrees, 0–90) tilts the stage-span orientation's rotation plane out of the stage span. The rotation is made in the plane of u and w_φ = cos φ·v + sin φ·o, where o is a unit direction on the span-layer features the null stage program does not use: those whose standardized null stage means are constant across stages (within 1e-10), so o is orthogonal to every centred null stage mean without a projection.

SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams(
    seed=1,
    trajectory_mode="orientation",
    group_effect_size=0.5,          # a 45° rotation
    construction="stage_span",
    span_layers=("methylation", "expression"),
    span_alignment=90.0,            # the rotation plane leaves the stage span
    span_support=20,                # o on 20 unused features (absent: all of them)
)
  • Fixed geometry. The intended population geometry is the same at every φ (net-displacement angle θ, delta = shape = 0). Only where the difference points changes, so differences in capture and power across φ are visibility, not effect size.
  • The two ends. φ = 0 normalizes to None, the in-span rotation, byte-identical to a dataset without the setting. At φ = 90 with balanced cells, B − A minus its mean over stages is orthogonal to the centred pooled stage means (the rhombus): the controlled analogue of the relocation surgery.
  • Support. span_support = k draws o on k unused features chosen uniformly; absent, o is dense over all of them. o is normalized either way, so dense and sparse cells plant the same energy.
  • Stream. o is drawn from np.random.default_rng([seed, SPAN_ALIGNMENT_STREAM]), never the sampling stream, so the dataset is still the null dataset plus the plant, and o is the same for every effect and every φ > 0 at a seed and support.
  • Scope. Both settings are accepted only under stage_span with orientation (or none). φ outside [0, 90], a support without φ > 0, a non-positive support and a k larger than the unused features are errors. Alignment applies to orientation only: at three stages a bend out of the plane makes a different triangle, so the intended shape would change with φ; magnitude and translation have no out-of-span version.

Truth records span_alignment and span_support (top level), span_alignment under transform, and a stage_span.out_of_span block: the span_layers, the support_size, the number of available_features and a direction_id (a hash of the drawn support and the stream seed). Both settings are omitted from cell ids, signatures and dumped configs while unset.

Planted scale (0.17.0). By default the stage-span edit is defined in coordinates divided by the null population pooled SD, which does not depend on the plant. The measurement's sample scaler estimates the planted population's pooled SD, which does, so under the null scale a bend shortens B's path where the scaler looks (−0.65 % to −1.06 % of A's path at e = 0.5 across the paper-grade columns). span_scale="planted" removes that route. The edit is solved as a fixed point under the planted pooled SD: planted_pooled_scale is the within-cell variance plus the between-cell variance of A's null and B's planted cell means at the realized sizes.

SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams(
    seed=1,
    trajectory_mode="shape",
    group_effect_size=0.5,          # a half-step bend
    construction="stage_span",
    span_layers=("methylation", "expression"),
    span_scale="planted",           # exact under the planted pooled SD
)
  • Exactness. At the fixed point B's planted-standardized configuration is the mode's edit of A's, so the bend, the rotation and the translation keep delta, and the off-target statistics, exactly in those coordinates.
  • Convergence. The iteration starts at the null SD and stops when no feature's SD moves by more than 1e-12 (relative). After 200 updates it raises a SemiSyntheticTrajectoryError naming the mode, the effect and the last change, rather than returning an inexact plant.
  • It converged at every paper-grade column in at most 67 updates.
  • It failed for 12 of 1,000 four-stage orientation units (e = 0.25, 0.5). In those, the configuration with the net displacement removed has two nearly tied singular values, so the rotation plane swings with the scale and the iteration cycles.
  • Magnitude needs no iteration: scaling about the centroid commutes with a per-feature scale, so the plant is the null-scale plant bit for bit.
  • Randomness. The dataset is still the null dataset plus the plant.
  • Scope. Accepted only under stage_span and not with span_alignment, whose out-of-span direction is drawn in null-standardized coordinates.

Truth gains span_scale, and the stage_span block reads units: "planted_standardized" with scale_iterations and scale_residual; its geometry is in the planted coordinates. The setting is omitted from cell ids, signatures and dumped configs while unset. The study key generator.span_scale is refused as an axis: scales are compared as sibling profiles.

docs.title: Evaluation harness
docs.text:
The evaluation harness runs one SemiSyntheticTrajectoryDataset through MOTCO integration and trajectory testing. It is the per-replicate layer used before larger Type I error or power grids.

from motco.simulations import (
    SimulationEvaluationParams,
    evaluate_semisynthetic_trajectory,
)

evaluation = evaluate_semisynthetic_trajectory(
    dataset,
    SimulationEvaluationParams(
        integration_method="concat",
        permutations=0,
    ),
)

observed_delta = evaluation.pair_statistics["delta"]
truth = evaluation.truth_metadata

Supported integration methods:

Method Behavior concat Column-binds methylation, expression, and proteomics matrices after deterministic per-feature standardization by default snf Builds per-omic affinity matrices, fuses them with SNF, and uses spectral embedding as the trajectory outcome matrix

Diagnostic integration methods. Three further spaces exist for comparing measurement designs. They are labelled integration_role="diagnostic", are never production, and reject attribution and the forced_components override:

Method Space Rank pca Label-free principal-component scores of the standardized concat matrix required integration_params["n_components"] pls_within_group Stage-supervised PLS fitted within each group, the stacked bases orthonormalized into one components_per_group (default n_stages − 1) per group pls_residual_pca The production pls scores, followed by principal-component scores of the stage-residualized features orthogonal to the PLS span the CV rank plus residual_components (default n_stages − 1)

pls_residual_pca fits the production pls space (CV rank, rank floor), then, in the model's input coordinates X_in = (X − x_mean) / x_std, subtracts the pooled stage means, projects the residuals off the span of the PLS rotations and appends X_in·W for their top residual_components right singular vectors W. Its first columns are exactly the pls latent matrix, so the arm differs from production only by the appended coordinates. The basis reads the features and stage labels, never the group labels, and is fitted once, never inside RRPP. residual_components must lie in [1, min(n_features − PLS rank, n_samples − n_stages)]. The metadata records pls_rank, residual_components and retained_dimensionality, and realized geometry measures the matrix as the pls_residual_pca_latent checkpoint. pls_residual_pca_from_pls(dataset, pls, params) builds the space from an existing pls integration of the same dataset without refitting the PLS model, so a comparison can share one fit between the production arm and this one.

Block selection. integration_params["layers"] names the omic blocks the evaluation measures, for every integration method: e.g. {"layers": ["methylation", "expression"]}. All three blocks are still generated; only the selected ones enter pooled preprocessing, integration, every realized-geometry checkpoint (per-block scopes for the selected blocks only, joint scopes over them) and orientation attribution. The selection is normalized to canonical order (methylation, expression, proteomics) and must be non-empty, duplicate-free and known; integration metadata records it as integration_params.layers. When the key is absent, all three blocks are measured and the evaluation result is byte-identical to the harness before the key existed (no layers metadata entry is added).

Block weighting. integration_params["block_weighting"] ("equal_variance" or "mfa"; 0.21.0) multiplies every pooled-standardized block by one label-blind scalar fitted once on the pooled sample with the scalers, so a block's weight in the joint measurement is declared rather than set by its feature count (unweighted, methylation's 367 features outweigh expression's 131 by 2.8 to 1 in total variance). equal_variance is 1/√p_b, constant features included, so every block of non-constant features has unit total variance; mfa is √n/σ₁(Z_b), the inverse standard deviation of the standardized block's leading principal component, so every block's dominant direction has unit variance (an mfa block with no variance is an error naming it). The weights live on the scalers (BlockScaler.weight, fit_block_scalers(..., weighting=), fit_omics_preprocessor(..., weighting=), FittedOmicsPreprocessor.block_weighting), so observed rows and analytic population means are weighted alike and every span-capture share and population_latent checkpoint is measured on the weighted inputs. Every PLS fit of a weighted pls space (the cross-validation's and the final one) uses scale=False, since scale=True would re-standardize each column and undo the weights; delta is then in the weighted metric, while angle, shape and the p-values are comparable with an unweighted evaluation. concat, pca, pls_within_group and pls_residual_pca measure the weighted blocks; snf and the unstandardized concat never read the standardized blocks and refuse the setting before any preprocessing, as does an unknown kind. A prebuilt preprocessor, latent integration or PLS fit with another weighting is refused, naming both. The kind is recorded as integration_params.block_weighting in the latent metadata only when set. Absent, every weight is 1 (multiplied exactly), and transforms, records, cell ids and signatures are byte-identical to 0.20.0; as an integration parameter it is already the study-config axis evaluation.integration_params.block_weighting. The setting is measured and stays opt-in: the weighted arm of the production latent-space selection (report) read no_gain (size, protected power and specificity hold; no gain at a weak stage signal or on the SEA-AD plasmode plant).

Sparse stage-PLS. integration_params["sparsity"] (0.22.0) fits the pls space with SparsePLSDA, whose components each load on a budget of features. The value is {"scope": "joint" | "block", "keep_fractions": [...]}: joint counts one budget over all measured features, block one per measured block (every block keeps its share whatever its size); the optional ladder of keep fractions (distinct, in (0, 1], held fullest first) defaults to 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, and a fraction keeps max(1, round(f · p)) features per group. The double CV selects the rank and the fraction jointly (plsda_doubleCV(..., sparsity=): ties to the smaller rank, then the fuller budget), the block membership is the measured blocks in concatenation order (layer_feature_counts, never parsed from column names), and the final model is fitted at the modal rank and the modal fraction (the fuller on ties) with the path's scale. The latent metadata records integration_params.sparsity (scope and ladder) and integration_params.selected_keep_fraction, and a top-level sparsity block adds, per component, the support size per block. It composes with the rank floor, the latent adjustment (residualized fit, raw projection), latent_coordinates="orthonormal" (the basis spans the sparse rotations) and block weighting (scale=False). A forced rank skips the CV, so it needs a one-element ladder (the model is fitted at it); a longer ladder is rejected before any preprocessing, naming both. pls_residual_pca builds its residual axes on the sparse PLS fit; pls_residual_pca_from_pls, pls_orthonormal_from_pls, span capture and attribution run unchanged on it, and a prebuilt latent or PLS fit with another sparsity setting is refused. Any other integration method, and a malformed value (not a mapping, an unknown key or scope, a fraction outside (0, 1], a repeated fraction, an empty ladder), is rejected before any preprocessing, naming the offence. Absent, nothing changes: no metadata entry is written, the production space is PLSRegression and records, cell ids and signatures are byte-identical to 0.21.0; as an integration parameter it is already the study-config axis evaluation.integration_params.sparsity. A ladder of [1.0] reproduces the production space exactly. The setting is measured and stays opt-in: the sparse_block arm of the production latent-space selection (report) read size_excess (the SEA-AD plasmode anchor's delta 0.11 at 100 replicates, production's rate on the same replicates) and gained no Bonferroni-protected power at a weak stage signal or on the plasmode plant.

Orientation estimator. orientation_estimator selects how each group's orientation is measured for the observed angle, every RRPP draw and every realized-geometry checkpoint angle. The default is "net_displacement" (the unit vector from the first to the last stage mean), adopted after the net-displacement power comparison; it is part of the cell id and parameter signature and is recorded in runtime_metadata["orientation_estimator"]. Pass orientation_estimator="pc1" to opt out to the principal-axis estimator: "pc1" normalizes to None, which is left out of every hash payload and record, so a PC1 evaluation is byte-identical to the harness before the selection existed. Every committed study config and historical diagnostic pins "pc1". Only angle depends on the selection. The stats primitives (estimate_difference, RRPP) keep "pc1" as their default.

Rank floor. min_components is the smallest rank the stage-supervised double CV may select for pls integration: the candidates are min_components … max_components − 1, so every outer-fold selection, the modal rank and the pooled fit are at or above it. The default is 2, so angle and shape are measured in a space of at least two dimensions (at rank 1 two orientations are parallel or antiparallel by construction and angle's null is a two-point distribution). The default is hashed into the cell id and parameter signature and recorded in runtime_metadata["min_components"] and in the latent metadata's integration_params.min_components. Pass min_components=1 for the unfloored rule: 1 normalizes to None, which is left out of every hash payload and record, so a floor-1 evaluation is byte-identical to the harness before the floor existed. Every committed study config pins "min_components": 1 beside "pc1", as do the historical diagnostics. max_components is clamped to [min_components + 1, min(n_features, n_samples)]; a sample that cannot satisfy the floor raises an error naming the floor and the counts. The diagnostic forced_components override keeps its own range ([2, max]) and ignores the floor; pca and pls_within_group have fixed ranks by construction. In a study config evaluation.min_components is a field and a design axis: null names the evaluator's default and 1 the unfloored rule, as distinct values. The floor guarantees two dimensions, not a second axis with signal; it was validated by scripts/rank_floor_check.py (the 2026-10-23 run returned adopt_floor at both calibrated strengths, report).

Latent coordinates. latent_coordinates names the coordinate system the pls latent space is measured in. Absent (the default) it is the PLS scores X_in·R, R = x_rotations_, which are a sheared image of the fitted span (see measurement visibility). Pass latent_coordinates="orthonormal" to measure X_in·Q instead, X_in = (X − x_mean) / x_std the final model's input coordinates and Q = qr(R), the basis span capture already uses. Q equals the PLS weights up to column signs, and delta, angle and shape are invariant to any orthogonal map of the latent coordinates, so every orthonormal basis of the span gives the same statistics and p-values. Only the coordinates change: the fitted model, the cross-validation and the selected or forced rank are those of the scores, and the span-capture shares are identical. The latent matrix, the pls_latent checkpoint, the configuration spectrum, every RRPP draw and the population_latent checkpoint are measured in the new coordinates. The setting is recorded as integration_params.latent_coordinates in the latent metadata and in runtime_metadata["latent_coordinates"]. It is rejected before any preprocessing or fit with any integration method other than pls and with attribution (attribution's PLS-captured reconstruction is defined only in score coordinates), and an unknown value is rejected naming the allowed values. "scores" normalizes to None, which is left out of every hash payload and record, so an evaluation without the setting is byte-identical to the harness before it existed (tests/data/orthonormal_coordinates_prechange_fixture.json). pls_orthonormal_from_pls(dataset, pls, params) builds the orthonormal integration from an existing score-coordinate pls integration of the same dataset without refitting, equal to the fit from scratch, so one fit can be measured in both coordinate systems; it refuses an integration that is not pls, has no fitted artifacts or is already orthonormal, and evaluate_semisynthetic_trajectory(..., latent=) refuses a prebuilt integration whose coordinates differ from its parameters. The setting is opt-in, and scripts/orthonormal_coordinates_check.py validated it on 2026-11-09. That run returned power_loss: size holds and the shear's off-target leak goes, but target power is lost at small, unequal and four-stage designs (report). The production measurement and motco analyze therefore use the scores, and the setting stays a diagnostic.

Predictive-subspace coordinates. The CV rank A does two jobs: it regularizes the stage fit, and it is the number of dimensions the statistics are measured in. Three further values of latent_coordinates keep the fit and measure in fewer dimensions. The stage labels are one-hot, so the final model's Y loadings Q (K × A) have rank K − 1 whatever A is, and the fitted stage indicators T·Qᵀ move only along the row space of Q. With V an orthonormal basis of that row space (numerical rank at 1e-10 of the largest singular value; predictive_directions(model)), the predictive subspace is span(V) in score space and span(R·V) in the model's input space, of dimension r = min(A, K − 1):

Value Latent matrix Columns "predictive" T·V, the scores projected on the subspace r (pred_<i>) "predictive_orthonormal" X_in·qr(R·V), the input coordinates on an orthonormal basis of it r (pred_<i>) "predictive_fitted" T·Qᵀ, the fitted stage indicators in the model's centred, scaled response units K of rank r (fitted_<i>)
  • One fit, one subspace. The fitted model, the cross-validation and the selected or forced rank are those of the scores; the step is a column map of the final fit, so it follows a forced rank, block weighting, sparsity and the latent adjustment (where T is the raw features projected on the basis). The three values share the basis qr(R·V), so their span-capture shares are equal, and at most the scores'. The fitted stage indicators recomputed from the subspace equal the model's.
  • Equal to the scores at A ≤ K − 1. V is then square and orthogonal, so "predictive" gives the scores' statistics and p-values.
  • What is measured there. The latent matrix, the pls_latent checkpoint, the configuration spectrum, every RRPP draw and the population_latent checkpoint (through LinearLatentMap.from_pls_predictive). The latent metadata gains integration_params.latent_coordinates and measured_dimension (r), its shape and n_features describe the measured matrix, and runtime_metadata["latent_coordinates"] names the value. A fit whose Y loadings have rank below r is an error naming the rank.
  • Rejections, all before any preprocessing or fit: any integration method other than pls, attribution, and fewer than three stages (the subspace would have one dimension, where angle is 0° or 180° by construction), each naming the value.
  • Absent, nothing changes. None is hash-omitted, so every committed cell id, signature and record is unchanged (tests/test_predictive_coordinates.py).
  • Prebuilt fit. pls_coordinates_from_pls(dataset, pls, params) builds the integration of any value other than the scores from an existing score-coordinate pls integration of the same dataset without refitting, equal to the fit from scratch, so one fit can be measured four ways; pls_orthonormal_from_pls is its orthonormal case. Both refuse an integration that is not pls, has no fitted artifacts or is not in score coordinates.
  • Status. Measured and not adopted. scripts/predictive_subspace_check.py, the paired pilot of the three values against production, read keep_production on 2026-11-12 (report). In simulation they hold size, lose no protected power and gain strongly. On the SEA-AD plasmode's real noise all three exceed size (delta 0.13, shape 0.08, against production's 0.042 and 0.026). Production and motco analyze measure in the scores, and the values stay diagnostics.

Set permutations=0 for observed statistics only. When permutations > 0, the harness runs RRPP and computes upper-tail empirical p-values with plus-one correction:

p = (1 + count(null >= observed)) / (1 + n_permutations)

The result includes observed delta, angle, and shape matrices, scalar two-group pair statistics, optional p-values, latent matrix metadata, generator truth metadata, runtime metadata, group/stage levels, and the trajectory contrast. Shape pair statistics and p-values are reported as unavailable for datasets with fewer than three stages.

docs.title: Realized-geometry decomposition
docs.text:
Generated semi-synthetic datasets also expose exact group-stage population means in integration units: methylation M-values and native expression/proteomics units. Evaluation uses one pooled fitted preprocessing artifact for both diagnostics and PLS, then reports:

Checkpoint Scopes Interpretation population_native each omic Exact construction and biological-cascade geometry without sampling noise population_standardized each omic and joint Exact means under the replicate's pooled fitted feature scaling observed_standardized each omic and joint Geometry actually presented to integration, including finite sampling pls_latent joint Geometry retained in the fitted production PLS representation population_latent joint Exact population means seen through the replicate's fitted linear map (only with span_capture)

Every applicable scope records both group path lengths, pairwise delta, angle, and shape, and explicit availability flags. Joint native-space geometry is intentionally omitted because the unstandardized omic blocks use incompatible units. Raw distances across feature and latent checkpoints are not scale-equivalent; use the decomposition to locate changes in behavior rather than subtracting distances across spaces.

Span capture. SimulationEvaluationParams(span_capture=True) (opt-in; False normalizes to the hash-omitted None) asks an evaluation in a linear space how much of the population trajectories its fitted basis sees. It reuses the evaluation's own fitted map and preprocessor — nothing is refitted, so the latent matrix, rank, statistics and p-values are identical with and without it — and adds the population_latent checkpoint above plus a span_capture block. Every linear integration carries its fitted map (LatentIntegrationResult.linear_map, a LinearLatentMap: the input centre and scale, an orthonormal basis of the kept directions in those coordinates, and the map to latent coordinates), and the block is computed in its input coordinates against that basis:

Method Input coordinates Basis pls (x − x_mean) / x_std of the fitted model QR of the rotations (as in 0.15.0, so PLS records are unchanged; the same basis in either latent_coordinates) pca x − column mean the retained principal axes pls_residual_pca the PLS model's QR of the rotations, then the residual axes concat (standardized) x the identity: every share is 1 and rank = n_features

The block's fields:

Field Meaning group_difference Share of Σ_s‖d_s‖² inside the span, d_s the population B − A difference at stage s minus its mean over stages; null when the difference is the same at every stage (the anchor, a translation), which none of the three statistics can see pooled_stage Share of the centred average stage means inside the span rank, n_features, random_share The fitted rank, the measured feature count and rank / n_features, the expected share of a random direction

The shares are energy (squared-norm) shares. For a single direction the plasmode check's latent_capture.py reported the norm share ‖Qᵀd‖/‖d‖, the square root of this one. snf, pls_within_group and the unstandardized concat carry no map, and they and datasets without population trajectories record neither the checkpoint nor the block.

Stage-span guard. A dataset generated with construction="stage_span" may only be measured on its span layers: the harness raises, before any preprocessing or fit, when integration_params["layers"] names other blocks, and the error names both block sets.

See the Phase 2 findings for the revised orientation and shape construction contracts and the matched-seed characterization command.

docs.title: Grid orchestration
docs.text:
The grid orchestration layer enumerates parameter cells, runs local replicates through the evaluation harness, persists one JSONL row per replicate, resumes completed work, and summarizes rejection rates for Type I error or power studies.

from pathlib import Path

from motco.simulations import (
    SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams,
    SimulationEvaluationParams,
    SimulationRunConfig,
    enumerate_type_i_grid,
    run_simulation_grid,
    summarize_rejection_rates,
)

grid = enumerate_type_i_grid(
    baseline_generator_params=SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams(seed=2, n_samples=60),
    evaluation_params=SimulationEvaluationParams(integration_method="concat", permutations=99),
    axes={
        "generator.n_samples": [60, 120],
        "generator.group_ratio": [0.5, 0.7],
    },
    n_replicates=3,
    base_seed=2026,
)

records = run_simulation_grid(
    grid,
    config=SimulationRunConfig(output_path=Path("simulation-results.jsonl")),
)
summaries = summarize_rejection_rates(records, alpha=0.05)

Each SimulationCell stores a stable cell_id, phase, SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams, SimulationEvaluationParams, replicate count, base seed, and metadata such as the varied axis. Axis names use explicit namespaces: generator.<field> or evaluation.<field>.

Initial persistence is JSON Lines. Each row records cell and replicate IDs, deterministic seeds, a parameter signature, status, p-values, pair statistics, realized-geometry diagnostics, truth metadata, runtime metadata, cell metadata, and optional error details. The diagnostic schema version participates in the parameter signature. With resume=True, completed rows with matching parameter signatures are skipped. A matching cell/replicate with a different parameter signature raises unless overwrite=True; legacy rows remain readable but have no realized-geometry payload.

summarize_rejection_rates groups completed replicate rows by cell and statistic, then reports available replicate count, rejection count, rejection rate, Monte Carlo standard error, and unavailable replicate count. Missing statistics, such as shape p-values for two-stage datasets, remain unavailable rather than being counted as non-significant.

docs.title: Legacy InterSIM bridge
docs.text: run_intersim calls the R InterSIM package and returns its matrices. Nothing in MOTCO's generation, harness or studies uses it. The cached reference is exported by src/motco/simulations/export_reference.R, and the fidelity fixtures are regenerated as described in src/motco/simulations/FIDELITY.md.

docs.title: R dependency
docs.text:
The bridge is optional and requires Rscript plus the R InterSIM package:

install.packages(
  "InterSIM",
  repos = c("https://cran.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)

Check availability before running a simulation:

from motco.simulations import check_intersim_available

availability = check_intersim_available()
if not availability.available:
    print(availability.message)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from motco.simulations import InterSIMParams, run_intersim

result = run_intersim(
    InterSIMParams(
        seed=1203,
        n_sample=100,
        cluster_sample_prop=(0.3, 0.3, 0.4),
        delta_methyl=1.0,
        delta_expr=1.0,
        delta_protein=1.0,
        p_dmp=0.1,
    )
)

methylation = result.methylation
expression = result.expression
proteomics = result.proteomics
clusters = result.clusters

docs.title: motco.simulations.SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams dataclass
docs.text:
Parameters for semi-synthetic trajectory generation.

group_ratio is the proportion assigned to the first label in group_labels within every stage. group_effect_size is the unified effect knob described in the module docstring (0 is null for all modes). p_dmp is the per-stage probability that a methylation feature is differential (InterSIM's p.DMP); expression/protein indicators are derived from it via the cross-omic maps. baseline_continuity (ρ) is the baseline stage-program continuity described in the module docstring: 0 draws each stage's program independently, higher values make a CpG's differential status persist across adjacent stages with correlation ρ while holding every stage's marginal at p_dmp. delta_* are the per-omic mean-shift sizes (InterSIM's delta.*). shape_kind selects the single-interior-stage perturbation used by shape. magnitude_kind selects whether magnitude scales every omic's effect size together (joint, the default), group B's methylation effect alone at all stages (all, a uniform methylation δ scale), or the methylation effect only at the extreme stages (extremes, first and last) leaving interior stages at the baseline effect. group_stage_sizes is the explicit alternative to n_samples / stage_sample_prop / group_ratio: one tuple of per-stage counts per group, rows ordered as group_labels and columns as stages, realized exactly. It may not be combined with a non-default proportional setting. None (the default) keeps proportional sizing, byte-identical to the generator before the table existed. surgery_censoring is the policy for pool-limited surgeries described in the module docstring: "error" (default) refuses to realize a partial surgery, "clamp" realizes the largest surgery the pool allows. Use "clamp" only to reproduce a historical run or for exploratory work where a partial surgery is acceptable — under it the requested effect no longer labels the realized construction. construction selects how the effect modes are realized: None (the default; "surgery" normalizes to it) is the feature-set surgery, "stage_span" the opt-in stage-span construction described in the module docstring. span_layers names the blocks the stage span is computed over (None = all three, canonical order) and is accepted only under stage_span. Both are omitted from cell ids and signatures while None. span_alignment (φ, degrees in [0, 90]) tilts the stage-span orientation's rotation plane out of the stage span, and span_support (a positive integer k, or None for every eligible feature) sets the support of the out-of-span direction; see the module docstring. φ = 0 normalizes to None. Both are accepted only under stage_span with orientation or none and are omitted from cell ids and signatures while None. span_scale selects the scale the stage-span edit is exact in: None (the default) the null population pooled SD, "planted" the planted population's pooled SD, solved as a fixed point; see the module docstring. It is accepted only under stage_span, not with span_alignment, and is omitted from cell ids and signatures while None.

Source code in src/motco/simulations/semisynthetic.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams:
    """Parameters for semi-synthetic trajectory generation.

    ``group_ratio`` is the proportion assigned to the first label in
    ``group_labels`` within every stage. ``group_effect_size`` is the unified
    effect knob described in the module docstring (``0`` is null for all modes).
    ``p_dmp`` is the per-stage probability that a methylation feature is
    differential (InterSIM's ``p.DMP``); expression/protein indicators are
    derived from it via the cross-omic maps. ``baseline_continuity`` (ρ) is the
    baseline stage-program continuity described in the module docstring: 0 draws
    each stage's program independently, higher values make a CpG's differential
    status persist across adjacent stages with correlation ρ while holding every
    stage's marginal at ``p_dmp``. ``delta_*`` are the per-omic
    mean-shift sizes (InterSIM's ``delta.*``). ``shape_kind`` selects the
    single-interior-stage perturbation used by ``shape``. ``magnitude_kind``
    selects whether ``magnitude`` scales every omic's effect size together
    (``joint``, the default), group B's methylation effect alone at *all*
    stages (``all``, a uniform methylation δ scale), or the methylation effect
    only at the *extreme* stages (``extremes``, first and last) leaving interior
    stages at the baseline effect.
    ``group_stage_sizes`` is the explicit alternative to ``n_samples`` /
    ``stage_sample_prop`` / ``group_ratio``: one tuple of per-stage counts per
    group, rows ordered as ``group_labels`` and columns as stages, realized
    exactly. It may not be combined with a non-default proportional setting.
    ``None`` (the default) keeps proportional sizing, byte-identical to the
    generator before the table existed.
    ``surgery_censoring`` is the policy for pool-limited surgeries described in
    the module docstring: ``"error"`` (default) refuses to realize a partial
    surgery, ``"clamp"`` realizes the largest surgery the pool allows. Use
    ``"clamp"`` only to reproduce a historical run or for exploratory work where
    a partial surgery is acceptable — under it the requested effect no longer
    labels the realized construction.
    ``construction`` selects how the effect modes are realized: ``None`` (the
    default; ``"surgery"`` normalizes to it) is the feature-set surgery,
    ``"stage_span"`` the opt-in stage-span construction described in the module
    docstring. ``span_layers`` names the blocks the stage span is computed over
    (``None`` = all three, canonical order) and is accepted only under
    ``stage_span``. Both are omitted from cell ids and signatures while
    ``None``.
    ``span_alignment`` (φ, degrees in ``[0, 90]``) tilts the stage-span
    orientation's rotation plane out of the stage span, and ``span_support``
    (a positive integer ``k``, or ``None`` for every eligible feature) sets the
    support of the out-of-span direction; see the module docstring. φ = 0
    normalizes to ``None``. Both are accepted only under ``stage_span`` with
    ``orientation`` or ``none`` and are omitted from cell ids and signatures
    while ``None``.
    ``span_scale`` selects the scale the stage-span edit is exact in: ``None``
    (the default) the null population pooled SD, ``"planted"`` the planted
    population's pooled SD, solved as a fixed point; see the module docstring.
    It is accepted only under ``stage_span``, not with ``span_alignment``, and
    is omitted from cell ids and signatures while ``None``.
    """

    seed: int
    trajectory_mode: TrajectoryMode = "none"
    n_samples: int = 600
    n_stages: int = 3
    group_effect_size: float = 0.0
    group_ratio: float = 0.5
    group_labels: tuple[str, str] = ("A", "B")
    p_dmp: float = 0.2
    baseline_continuity: float = 0.0
    delta_methyl: float = 2.0
    delta_expr: float = 2.0
    delta_protein: float = 2.0
    shape_kind: ShapeKind = "relocate"
    magnitude_kind: MagnitudeKind = "joint"
    surgery_censoring: SurgeryCensoring = "error"
    stage_sample_prop: tuple[float, ...] | None = None
    group_stage_sizes: tuple[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] | None = None
    construction: Construction | None = None
    span_layers: tuple[OmicsLayer, ...] | None = None
    span_alignment: float | None = None
    span_support: int | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.construction == "surgery":
            object.__setattr__(self, "construction", None)
        alignment = self.span_alignment
        if isinstance(alignment, int | float | np.integer | np.floating) and not isinstance(alignment, bool):
            if alignment == 0:
                # Zero alignment is the in-span rotation: the hash-omitted spelling.
                object.__setattr__(self, "span_alignment", None)
        layers = self.span_layers
        if layers is not None and not isinstance(layers, str | bytes) and isinstance(layers, Sequence):
            names = tuple(str(layer) for layer in layers)
            if set(names) <= set(_OMICS_LAYERS) and len(set(names)) == len(names):
                # Canonical order, so equal span sets hash equally.
                names = tuple(layer for layer in _OMICS_LAYERS if layer in names)
            object.__setattr__(self, "span_layers", names)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SimulationEvaluationParams:
    """Parameters for evaluating one semi-synthetic trajectory dataset."""

    integration_method: IntegrationMethod = "concat"
    integration_params: Mapping[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    permutations: int = 0
    n_jobs: int | None = 1
    seed: int | None = None
    progress: bool = False
    include_null_distributions: bool = False
    group_col: str = "group"
    stage_col: str = "stage"
    attribution: AttributionDiagnosticSettings = field(default_factory=AttributionDiagnosticSettings)
    # Orientation estimator for the observed ``angle``, every RRPP draw and every
    # realized-geometry checkpoint. The default is net displacement; it is hashed
    # into cell ids and signatures and recorded in ``runtime_metadata``. ``None``
    # is the hash-omitted spelling of PC1 (``grid._SIGNATURE_OMIT_WHEN_NONE``) and
    # an explicit ``"pc1"`` normalizes to it, so PC1 cell ids, signatures and
    # records equal those produced before the field existed.
    orientation_estimator: str | None = "net_displacement"
    # Rank floor of the PLS latent space: the double CV selects from the
    # candidates ``min_components … max_components − 1``. The default is 2, so
    # ``angle`` and ``shape`` are measured in at least two dimensions; it is
    # hashed into cell ids and signatures and recorded in ``runtime_metadata``.
    # ``None`` is the hash-omitted spelling of the unfloored rule (floor 1,
    # ``grid._SIGNATURE_OMIT_WHEN_NONE``) and an explicit ``1`` normalizes to it,
    # so floor-1 cell ids, signatures and records equal those produced before
    # the field existed. PLS only; the other integration methods ignore it.
    min_components: int | None = 2
    # Opt-in span-capture diagnostic: with a linear integration (``pls``, ``pca``,
    # ``pls_residual_pca``, ``concat``), realized geometry gains the
    # ``population_latent`` checkpoint and the ``span_capture`` shares, computed
    # from the evaluation's own fitted linear map (no refit; statistics are
    # unchanged). ``None`` (off) is hash-omitted and ``False`` normalizes to it,
    # so an evaluation without it is byte-identical to before the field existed.
    span_capture: bool | None = None
    # Opt-in coordinates of the PLS measurement: ``"orthonormal"`` measures the
    # final model's input coordinates on ``qr(x_rotations_)`` instead of its
    # (sheared) scores; ``"predictive"``, ``"predictive_orthonormal"`` and
    # ``"predictive_fitted"`` measure on the final model's predictive subspace
    # (the row space of its Y loadings, ``min(rank, n_stages − 1)`` dimensions):
    # the scores projected on it, the input coordinates on an orthonormal basis
    # of it, and the fitted stage indicators. The fit, the CV and the rank are
    # unchanged. PLS only, and not with attribution; the predictive values need
    # three stages. ``None`` (the scores) is hash-omitted and ``"scores"``
    # normalizes to it, so an evaluation without it is byte-identical to before
    # the field existed.
    latent_coordinates: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        coordinates = self.latent_coordinates
        if coordinates is not None:
            if coordinates not in LATENT_COORDINATES:
                raise SimulationEvaluationError(
                    f"Unknown latent_coordinates {coordinates!r}; allowed: {list(LATENT_COORDINATES)}."
                )
            if coordinates == "scores":
                object.__setattr__(self, "latent_coordinates", None)
        if self.span_capture is not None and not isinstance(self.span_capture, bool | np.bool_):
            raise SimulationEvaluationError(
                f"SimulationEvaluationParams.span_capture must be true or false, got {self.span_capture!r}."
            )
        if self.span_capture is not None:
            object.__setattr__(self, "span_capture", True if bool(self.span_capture) else None)
        floor = self.min_components
        if floor is not None:
            floor = _validate_min_components(floor, where="SimulationEvaluationParams.min_components")
            object.__setattr__(self, "min_components", None if floor == 1 else floor)
        estimator = self.orientation_estimator
        if estimator is None:
            return
        if estimator not in EVALUATION_ORIENTATION_ESTIMATORS:
            raise SimulationEvaluationError(
                f"Unknown orientation_estimator {estimator!r}; allowed: "
                f"{list(EVALUATION_ORIENTATION_ESTIMATORS)}."
            )
        if estimator == "pc1":
            object.__setattr__(self, "orientation_estimator", None)

    @property
    def resolved_orientation_estimator(self) -> str:
        """The estimator name the statistics are computed with."""

        return self.orientation_estimator or "pc1"

    @property
    def resolved_min_components(self) -> int:
        """The rank floor the PLS cross-validation runs with (1 when hash-omitted)."""

        return self.min_components or 1

    @property
    def resolved_latent_coordinates(self) -> str:
        """The coordinate system the PLS latent space is measured in."""

        return self.latent_coordinates or "scores"

def check_intersim_available(rscript: str = "Rscript") -> InterSIMAvailability:
    """Check whether Rscript and the R InterSIM package are available."""

    rscript_path = which(rscript)
    if rscript_path is None:
        return InterSIMAvailability(
            available=False,
            message=f"Rscript dependency is missing or not on PATH: {rscript}",
        )

    cmd = [
        rscript_path,
        "-e",
        'quit(status = if (requireNamespace("InterSIM", quietly = TRUE)) 0 else 1)',
    ]
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        details = _format_process_output(proc)
        return InterSIMAvailability(
            available=False,
            message="R package InterSIM is not installed or cannot be loaded." + details,
            rscript_path=rscript_path,
        )

    return InterSIMAvailability(
        available=True,
        message="Rscript and R package InterSIM are available.",
        rscript_path=rscript_path,
    )

def run_intersim(
    params: InterSIMParams,
    *,
    rscript: str = "Rscript",
    check_dependency: bool = True,
) -> InterSIMResult:
    """Invoke R InterSIM and return aligned omics matrices plus cluster metadata."""

    if check_dependency:
        availability = check_intersim_available(rscript)
        if not availability.available:
            raise InterSIMDependencyError(availability.message)
        rscript_cmd = availability.rscript_path or rscript
    else:
        rscript_cmd = which(rscript) or rscript

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="motco-intersim-") as tmp:
        output_dir = Path(tmp)
        proc = subprocess.run(
            _build_rscript_command(params, output_dir=output_dir, rscript=rscript_cmd),
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise InterSIMRuntimeError(
                f"InterSIM R process failed with exit code {proc.returncode}."
                f"{_format_process_output(proc)}"
            )
        return _load_result(output_dir, params=params)

def generate_semisynthetic_trajectory(
    params: SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams,
    *,
    reference: IntersimReference | None = None,
) -> SemiSyntheticTrajectoryDataset:
    """Generate a semi-synthetic trajectory dataset using the numpy generator."""

    _validate_params(params)
    ref = reference if reference is not None else load_reference()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(params.seed)

    if params.group_stage_sizes is not None:
        group_a_sizes, group_b_sizes = (list(row) for row in params.group_stage_sizes)
    else:
        stage_sizes = _stage_sizes(params)
        group_a_sizes, group_b_sizes = _group_stage_sizes(stage_sizes, params)

    methyl_a = _baseline_methyl(rng, ref, params)
    deltas_a = (params.delta_methyl, params.delta_expr, params.delta_protein)
    transform_meta: dict[str, Any]
    if params.construction == "stage_span":
        # Draws nothing: B keeps A's indicators and effects, so the stream is the
        # ``none`` stream and B's plant is added to its cell means below.
        methyl_b, deltas_b, transform_meta = methyl_a.copy(), deltas_a, {}
    else:
        methyl_b, deltas_b, transform_meta = _transform_group_b(rng, ref, params, methyl_a)

    indicators_a = _derive_group(methyl_a, ref)
    indicators_b = _derive_group(methyl_b, ref)

    plant: _StageSpanPlant | None = None
    if params.construction == "stage_span":
        plant = _stage_span_plant(ref, params, indicators_a, deltas_a, group_a_sizes, group_b_sizes)
        transform_meta = plant.transform
    shifts_b = plant.shifts if plant is not None else None

    gen_a = _generate_group(rng, ref, indicators_a, deltas_a, group_a_sizes)
    gen_b = _generate_group(rng, ref, indicators_b, deltas_b, group_b_sizes, shifts=shifts_b)
    population_trajectories = _build_population_trajectories(
        ref, params, indicators_a, indicators_b, deltas_a, deltas_b, shifts_b=shifts_b
    )

    methylation, expression, proteomics, metadata = _assemble(
        ref, params, gen_a, gen_b, group_a_sizes, group_b_sizes
    )
    truth = _build_truth(params, indicators_a, indicators_b, deltas_a, deltas_b, transform_meta)
    if params.group_stage_sizes is not None:
        truth["group_stage_sizes"] = {
            params.group_labels[0]: list(group_a_sizes),
            params.group_labels[1]: list(group_b_sizes),
        }
    if plant is not None:
        truth.update(plant.truth)

    return SemiSyntheticTrajectoryDataset(
        methylation=methylation,
        expression=expression,
        proteomics=proteomics,
        metadata=metadata,
        truth=truth,
        population_trajectories=population_trajectories,
    )

snf and pls build genuine latent spaces (the measurement substrate for trajectory geometry); concat is a standardized-feature-concatenation baseline, not a constructed latent space. See the module docstring for the latent-space architecture.

Source code in src/motco/simulations/evaluation.py 
def integrate_semisynthetic_dataset(
    dataset: SemiSyntheticTrajectoryDataset,
    params: SimulationEvaluationParams,
    *,
    preprocessor: FittedOmicsPreprocessor | None = None,
    observed_blocks: Mapping[OmicsLayer, pd.DataFrame] | None = None,
) -> LatentIntegrationResult:
    """Construct the molecular latent space from aligned omics layers.

    ``snf`` and ``pls`` build genuine latent spaces (the measurement substrate
    for trajectory geometry); ``concat`` is a standardized-feature-concatenation
    baseline, not a constructed latent space. See the module docstring for the
    latent-space architecture.
    """

    _validate_latent_coordinates(params)
    weighting = _validate_block_weighting(params.integration_method, params.integration_params)
    _validate_sparsity(params.integration_method, params.integration_params)
    _validate_dataset(dataset, params.group_col, params.stage_col)
    _require_span_layers_measured(dataset, params.integration_params)
    _require_predictive_stages(dataset.metadata, params)
    layers = _measured_layers(params.integration_params)
    if preprocessor is None:
        preprocessor = fit_omics_preprocessor(dataset, layers, weighting=weighting)
    else:
        try:
            preprocessor.require_layers(layers)
            preprocessor.require_block_weighting(weighting)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise SimulationEvaluationError(str(exc)) from exc
    if observed_blocks is None:
        observed_blocks = preprocessor.transform_dataset(dataset)
    method = params.integration_method
    if method == "concat":
        return _concat_integration(dataset, params.integration_params, observed_blocks)
    if method == "snf":
        return _snf_integration(dataset, params.integration_params)
    if method == "pls":
        return _pls_integration(
            dataset,
            params.integration_params,
            stage_col=params.stage_col,
            observed_blocks=observed_blocks,
            preprocessor=preprocessor,
            min_components=params.resolved_min_components,
            coordinates=params.resolved_latent_coordinates,
        )
    if method == "pca":
        return _pca_integration(dataset, params.integration_params, observed_blocks)
    if method == "pls_within_group":
        return _pls_within_group_integration(
            dataset,
            params.integration_params,
            group_col=params.group_col,
            stage_col=params.stage_col,
            observed_blocks=observed_blocks,
        )
    if method == "pls_residual_pca":
        pls = _pls_integration(
            dataset,
            params.integration_params,
            stage_col=params.stage_col,
            observed_blocks=observed_blocks,
            preprocessor=preprocessor,
            min_components=params.resolved_min_components,
        )
        return pls_residual_pca_from_pls(dataset, pls, params)
    raise SimulationEvaluationError(f"Unsupported integration_method: {method!r}.")

def build_simulation_trajectory_design(
    metadata: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    group_col: str = "group",
    stage_col: str = "stage",
) -> SimulationTrajectoryDesign:
    """Build full/reduced model matrices, LS means, and two-group contrast."""

    _validate_metadata(metadata, group_col, stage_col)
    design_frame = metadata[[group_col, stage_col]].reset_index(drop=True).copy()
    design_frame[group_col] = design_frame[group_col].astype(str)
    design_frame[stage_col] = design_frame[stage_col].astype(str)
    group_levels = _sort_levels(pd.unique(design_frame[group_col]).tolist())
    stage_levels = _sort_levels(pd.unique(design_frame[stage_col]).tolist())
    if len(group_levels) != 2:
        raise SimulationEvaluationError(f"Expected exactly two groups, found {len(group_levels)}: {group_levels}.")
    if len(stage_levels) < 2:
        raise SimulationEvaluationError(
            f"Expected at least two stages, found {len(stage_levels)}: {stage_levels}."
        )
    _validate_group_stage_combinations(design_frame, group_col, stage_col, group_levels, stage_levels)

    model_full = get_model_matrix(design_frame, group_col=group_col, level_col=stage_col, full=True)
    model_reduced = get_model_matrix(design_frame, group_col=group_col, level_col=stage_col, full=False)
    ls_means = build_ls_means(group_levels, stage_levels, full=True)
    n_stages = len(stage_levels)
    contrast = [[group_index * n_stages + stage_index for stage_index in range(n_stages)] for group_index in range(2)]
    return SimulationTrajectoryDesign(
        model_full=model_full,
        model_reduced=model_reduced,
        ls_means=ls_means,
        contrast=contrast,
        group_levels=group_levels,
        stage_levels=stage_levels,
    )

docs.title: motco.simulations.evaluate_semisynthetic_trajectory(dataset, params=None, *, latent=None)
docs.text:
Evaluate one semi-synthetic trajectory dataset through MOTCO routines.

latent optionally supplies an integration already built for this dataset with the same integration_method and integration_params (from :func:integrate_semisynthetic_dataset), so evaluations that differ only in measurement settings — the orientation estimator, say — share one space fit. Omitted (the default), the integration is built here.

Source code in src/motco/simulations/evaluation.py 
def evaluate_semisynthetic_trajectory(
    dataset: SemiSyntheticTrajectoryDataset,
    params: SimulationEvaluationParams | None = None,
    *,
    latent: LatentIntegrationResult | None = None,
) -> SimulationEvaluationResult:
    """Evaluate one semi-synthetic trajectory dataset through MOTCO routines.

    ``latent`` optionally supplies an integration already built for this
    dataset with the same ``integration_method`` and ``integration_params``
    (from :func:`integrate_semisynthetic_dataset`), so evaluations that differ
    only in measurement settings — the orientation estimator, say — share one
    space fit. Omitted (the default), the integration is built here.
    """

    params = params or SimulationEvaluationParams()
    _validate_evaluation_params(params)
    _require_span_layers_measured(dataset, params.integration_params)
    _require_predictive_stages(dataset.metadata, params)
    start = perf_counter()

    weighting = _block_weighting(params.integration_params)
    preprocessor = fit_omics_preprocessor(dataset, _measured_layers(params.integration_params), weighting=weighting)
    observed_blocks = preprocessor.transform_dataset(dataset)
    if latent is None:
        latent = integrate_semisynthetic_dataset(
            dataset,
            params,
            preprocessor=preprocessor,
            observed_blocks=observed_blocks,
        )
    elif latent.metadata.get("integration_method") != params.integration_method:
        raise SimulationEvaluationError(
            f"Supplied latent integration was built with {latent.metadata.get('integration_method')!r}, "
            f"not integration_method={params.integration_method!r}."
        )
    elif _integration_coordinates(latent) != params.resolved_latent_coordinates:
        raise SimulationEvaluationError(
            f"Supplied latent integration is in {_integration_coordinates(latent)!r} coordinates, "
            f"not latent_coordinates={params.resolved_latent_coordinates!r}."
        )
    elif _integration_block_weighting(latent) != weighting:
        raise SimulationEvaluationError(
            f"Supplied latent integration was built with block_weighting={_integration_block_weighting(latent)!r}, "
            f"not the requested {weighting!r}."
        )
    elif _integration_sparsity(latent) != _sparsity_record(params.integration_params):
        raise SimulationEvaluationError(
            f"Supplied latent integration was built with sparsity={_integration_sparsity(latent)!r}, "
            f"not the requested {_sparsity_record(params.integration_params)!r}."
        )
    design = build_simulation_trajectory_design(
        dataset.metadata,
        group_col=params.group_col,
        stage_col=params.stage_col,
    )

    observed_deltas, observed_angles, observed_shapes, observed_spectra = estimate_difference(
        Y=latent.matrix,
        model_matrix=design.model_full,
        LS_means=design.ls_means,
        contrast=design.contrast,
        return_spectra=True,
        orientation_estimator=params.resolved_orientation_estimator,
    )
    config_spectrum = _config_spectrum_block(observed_spectra, design.group_levels)
    shape_available = len(design.stage_levels) >= 3
    pair_statistics = _extract_pair_statistics(
        observed_deltas,
        observed_angles,
        observed_shapes,
        shape_available=shape_available,
    )

    p_values: dict[str, float] = {}
    null_distributions: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None
    null_summary: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    if params.permutations > 0:
        dist_delta, dist_angle, dist_shape, dist_eigengap = RRPP(
            latent.matrix,
            design.model_full,
            design.model_reduced,
            design.ls_means,
            design.contrast,
            permutations=params.permutations,
            n_jobs=params.n_jobs,
            progress=params.progress,
            seed=params.seed,
            return_eigengaps=True,
            orientation_estimator=params.resolved_orientation_estimator,
        )
        null_values = _extract_null_distributions(
            dist_delta,
            dist_angle,
            dist_shape,
            shape_available=shape_available,
        )
        p_values = {
            statistic: _empirical_p_value(null_values[statistic], observed)
            for statistic, observed in pair_statistics.items()
            if statistic in null_values and np.isfinite(observed)
        }
        null_summary = _summarize_null_distributions(null_values)
        # Only the summary survives: the per-permutation eigengaps are discarded
        # here, exactly as the per-permutation statistics are.
        config_spectrum["permutation_pooled_eigengap"] = _summarize_permutation_eigengaps(
            dist_eigengap
        )
        if params.include_null_distributions:
            null_distributions = null_values

    runtime_seconds = perf_counter() - start
    runtime_metadata: dict[str, Any] = {
        "runtime_seconds": runtime_seconds,
        "permutations": params.permutations,
        "n_jobs": params.n_jobs,
        "seed": params.seed,
        "progress": params.progress,
        "shape_available": shape_available,
    }
    if params.orientation_estimator is not None:
        runtime_metadata["orientation_estimator"] = params.orientation_estimator
    if params.min_components is not None:
        runtime_metadata["min_components"] = params.min_components
    if params.span_capture is not None:
        runtime_metadata["span_capture"] = params.span_capture
    if params.latent_coordinates is not None:
        runtime_metadata["latent_coordinates"] = params.latent_coordinates
    latent_checkpoint = _LATENT_CHECKPOINTS.get(params.integration_method)
    # Span capture reads the linear map the statistics were measured in; the
    # nonlinear or unrecorded spaces (``snf``, ``pls_within_group``) have none
    # and record nothing.
    span_map = latent.linear_map if params.span_capture else None
    realized_geometry = calculate_realized_geometry(
        dataset,
        preprocessor=preprocessor,
        observed_blocks=observed_blocks,
        latent_matrix=latent.matrix if latent_checkpoint is not None else None,
        group_col=params.group_col,
        stage_col=params.stage_col,
        latent_checkpoint=latent_checkpoint or "pls_latent",
        orientation_estimator=params.resolved_orientation_estimator,
        latent_map=span_map,
    ).to_dict()
    # The fitted estimator and standardized joint matrix live only inside this
    # call: attribution consumes them here, and only the compact JSON-safe
    # record survives into the result.
    attribution_diagnostics = _attribution_diagnostics(dataset, params, latent)

    return SimulationEvaluationResult(
        observed_deltas=observed_deltas,
        observed_angles=observed_angles,
        observed_shapes=observed_shapes,
        pair_statistics=pair_statistics,
        p_values=p_values,
        latent_matrix_metadata=latent.metadata,
        # Drop the raw indicator arrays — they are not JSON-serializable for the
        # study's JSONL persistence; the per-stage/group counts and transform
        # notes (which are) are retained for downstream characterization.
        truth_metadata={k: v for k, v in dataset.truth.items() if k != "indicators"},
        runtime_metadata=runtime_metadata,
        evaluation_params=params,
        group_levels=design.group_levels,
        stage_levels=design.stage_levels,
        contrast=design.contrast,
        null_distributions=null_distributions,
        realized_geometry=realized_geometry,
        attribution_diagnostics=attribution_diagnostics,
        null_summary=null_summary,
        config_spectrum=config_spectrum,
    )

def enumerate_type_i_grid(
    *,
    baseline_generator_params: SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams,
    evaluation_params: SimulationEvaluationParams | None = None,
    axes: Mapping[str, Sequence[Any]] | None = None,
    n_replicates: int = 1,
    base_seed: int = 0,
) -> SimulationGrid:
    """Enumerate a null Type I grid with baseline plus one-factor-at-a-time axes."""

    # A zero effect is the null dataset under every construction, so the null
    # cells carry none (``construction``/``span_layers``, the alignment and the
    # span scale cleared).
    null_generator = replace(
        baseline_generator_params,
        trajectory_mode="none",
        group_effect_size=0.0,
        construction=None,
        span_layers=None,
        span_alignment=None,
        span_support=None,
        span_scale=None,
    )
    cells = [
        make_simulation_cell(
            phase="type_i_baseline",
            generator_params=null_generator,
            evaluation_params=evaluation_params,
            n_replicates=n_replicates,
            base_seed=base_seed,
            metadata={"varied_axis": None, "varied_value": None},
        )
    ]
    for axis, values in (axes or {}).items():
        baseline_value = _get_axis_value(null_generator, evaluation_params, axis)
        for value in values:
            if _to_jsonable(value) == _to_jsonable(baseline_value):
                continue
            generator_params, eval_params = _apply_axis_value(
                null_generator,
                evaluation_params or SimulationEvaluationParams(),
                axis,
                value,
            )
            generator_params = replace(
                generator_params,
                construction=None,
                span_layers=None,
                span_alignment=None,
                span_support=None,
                span_scale=None,
            )
            cells.append(
                make_simulation_cell(
                    phase="type_i_ofat",
                    generator_params=generator_params,
                    evaluation_params=eval_params,
                    n_replicates=n_replicates,
                    base_seed=base_seed,
                    metadata={"varied_axis": axis, "varied_value": value},
                )
            )
    return SimulationGrid(cells=tuple(cells), metadata={"grid_type": "type_i"})

Because it runs before cell construction, the resolved settings enter the cell id and parameter signature rather than being applied after the fact. cell_metadata is merged into every emitted cell's metadata.

def enumerate_power_grid(
    *,
    baseline_generator_params: SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams,
    evaluation_params: SimulationEvaluationParams | None = None,
    trajectory_modes: Sequence[str],
    effect_sizes: Sequence[float],
    axes: Mapping[str, Sequence[Any]] | None = None,
    n_replicates: int = 1,
    base_seed: int = 0,
    evaluation_resolver: CellEvaluationResolver | None = None,
    cell_metadata: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> SimulationGrid:
    """Enumerate power cells from trajectory modes, effect sizes, and optional axes.

    ``evaluation_resolver`` may specialize the evaluation parameters per cell
    (for example, to enable attribution diagnostics only on selected cells).
    Because it runs *before* cell construction, the resolved settings enter the
    cell id and parameter signature rather than being applied after the fact.
    ``cell_metadata`` is merged into every emitted cell's metadata.
    """

    if not trajectory_modes:
        raise SimulationGridError("trajectory_modes must contain at least one mode.")
    if not effect_sizes:
        raise SimulationGridError("effect_sizes must contain at least one value.")
    cells: list[SimulationCell] = []
    eval_params = evaluation_params or SimulationEvaluationParams()
    extra_metadata = dict(cell_metadata or {})

    def resolve(phase: str, mode: str, effect_size: float) -> SimulationEvaluationParams:
        if evaluation_resolver is None:
            return eval_params
        return evaluation_resolver(phase, mode, float(effect_size))

    for mode, effect_size in itertools.product(trajectory_modes, effect_sizes):
        generator = replace(
            baseline_generator_params,
            trajectory_mode=mode,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            group_effect_size=float(effect_size),
        )
        primary_eval = resolve("power_primary", mode, float(effect_size))
        cells.append(
            make_simulation_cell(
                phase="power_primary",
                generator_params=generator,
                evaluation_params=primary_eval,
                n_replicates=n_replicates,
                base_seed=base_seed,
                metadata={
                    "trajectory_mode": mode,
                    "effect_size": float(effect_size),
                    "varied_axis": None,
                    **extra_metadata,
                },
            )
        )
        for axis, values in (axes or {}).items():
            ofat_eval = resolve("power_ofat", mode, float(effect_size))
            baseline_value = _get_axis_value(generator, ofat_eval, axis)
            for value in values:
                if _to_jsonable(value) == _to_jsonable(baseline_value):
                    continue
                generator_params, axis_eval_params = _apply_axis_value(
                    generator,
                    ofat_eval,
                    axis,
                    value,
                )
                cells.append(
                    make_simulation_cell(
                        phase="power_ofat",
                        generator_params=generator_params,
                        evaluation_params=axis_eval_params,
                        n_replicates=n_replicates,
                        base_seed=base_seed,
                        metadata={
                            "trajectory_mode": mode,
                            "effect_size": float(effect_size),
                            "varied_axis": axis,
                            "varied_value": value,
                        },
                    )
                )
    return SimulationGrid(cells=tuple(cells), metadata={"grid_type": "power"})

def run_simulation_replicate(
    cell: SimulationCell,
    replicate_index: int,
    *,
    evaluator: Evaluator | None = None,
    error_policy: ErrorPolicy = "raise",
) -> SimulationReplicateResult:
    """Run one replicate, using a fake evaluator in tests or the default harness in production."""

    _validate_error_policy(error_policy)
    replicate_seed = derive_replicate_seed(cell, replicate_index)
    generator_params = replace(cell.generator_params, seed=replicate_seed)
    evaluation_seed = cell.evaluation_params.seed if cell.evaluation_params.seed is not None else replicate_seed
    evaluation_params = replace(cell.evaluation_params, seed=evaluation_seed)
    evaluator = evaluator or _default_evaluator
    start = perf_counter()
    try:
        result = evaluator(generator_params, evaluation_params)
    except Exception as exc:
        if error_policy == "raise":
            raise
        return SimulationReplicateResult(
            cell_id=cell.cell_id,
            phase=cell.phase,
            replicate_index=replicate_index,
            replicate_seed=replicate_seed,
            generator_seed=generator_params.seed,
            evaluation_seed=evaluation_params.seed,
            parameter_signature=parameter_signature(cell),
            status="failed",
            runtime_metadata={"runtime_seconds": perf_counter() - start},
            cell_metadata=dict(cell.metadata),
            error_type=type(exc).__name__,
            error_message=str(exc),
        )

    attribution = dict(result.attribution_diagnostics or {})
    attribution_status = str(attribution.get("status", "not_requested"))
    return SimulationReplicateResult(
        cell_id=cell.cell_id,
        phase=cell.phase,
        replicate_index=replicate_index,
        replicate_seed=replicate_seed,
        generator_seed=generator_params.seed,
        evaluation_seed=evaluation_params.seed,
        parameter_signature=parameter_signature(cell),
        status="completed",
        p_values=_finite_mapping(result.p_values),
        pair_statistics=_finite_mapping(result.pair_statistics),
        realized_geometry=result.realized_geometry,
        truth_metadata=result.truth_metadata,
        runtime_metadata=result.runtime_metadata,
        cell_metadata=dict(cell.metadata),
        integration_metadata=dict(result.latent_matrix_metadata),
        attribution_status=attribution_status,
        attribution_diagnostics=attribution,
        null_summary={
            statistic: dict(entry) for statistic, entry in (result.null_summary or {}).items()
        },
        config_spectrum=dict(result.config_spectrum or {}),
        diagnostic_error_type=attribution.get("error_type"),
        diagnostic_error_message=attribution.get("reason") if attribution_status == "failed" else None,
    )

Source code in src/motco/simulations/grid.py 
def run_simulation_grid(
    grid: SimulationGrid,
    *,
    config: SimulationRunConfig | None = None,
    evaluator: Evaluator | None = None,
) -> list[SimulationReplicateResult]:
    """Run a grid locally with optional JSONL persistence and resume support."""

    config = config or SimulationRunConfig()
    if config.persistence_format != "jsonl":
        raise SimulationGridError("Only JSONL persistence is currently supported.")
    completed = (
        _completed_index(config.output_path)
        if config.output_path and config.resume and not config.overwrite
        else {}
    )
    records: list[SimulationReplicateResult] = []
    for cell in grid.cells:
        signature = parameter_signature(cell)
        for replicate_index in range(cell.n_replicates):
            key = (cell.cell_id, replicate_index)
            existing_signature = completed.get(key)
            if existing_signature is not None:
                if existing_signature != signature:
                    if not config.overwrite:
                        raise SimulationGridError(
                            f"Existing result for {cell.cell_id} replicate {replicate_index} has a different "
                            "parameter signature. Set overwrite=True to rerun."
                        )
                else:
                    continue
            record = run_simulation_replicate(
                cell,
                replicate_index,
                evaluator=evaluator,
                error_policy=config.error_policy,
            )
            records.append(record)
            if config.output_path is not None:
                append_replicate_results(config.output_path, [record])
    return records

def read_replicate_results(path: Path) -> list[SimulationReplicateResult]:
    """Read replicate records from a JSONL file."""

    if not path.exists():
        return []
    records = []
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line in handle:
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            records.append(_replicate_result_from_dict(json.loads(line)))
    return records
