gate cell mean SE reading bound verdict contamination, unadjusted − oracle − 2·SE anchor 0.4255 0.0115 0.4025 ≥ 0.25 holds |projection, unadjusted − oracle| − 2·SE anchor 0.5091 0.0057 0.4978 ≥ 0.2 holds e = 0.5 0.5207 0.0057 0.5093 ≥ 0.2 holds e = 1.0 0.5113 0.0056 0.5002 ≥ 0.2 holds oracle truth precision e = 1.0 0.9845 — 0.9845 ≥ 0.5 holds

The construction is informative. The covariate fills the unadjusted top-20 where nothing else competes (0.475 against the oracle's 0.050 at the anchor), and it bends the unadjusted contrast in every cell. The planted drivers are recoverable: the oracle's top-20 at e = 1.0 is 98.5 % drivers.

docs.title: 3. Criteria
docs.text:
All readings are adjusted − oracle, paired over the cell's 500 replicates, with 2 paired SEs.

criterion cell mean SE reading bound verdict contamination (+2·SE) anchor 0.0008 0.0028 0.0064 ≤ 0.05 holds e = 0.5 −0.0050 0.0013 −0.0024 ≤ 0.05 holds e = 1.0 −0.0003 0.0003 0.0003 ≤ 0.05 holds residual confounding (|mean| + 2·SE) anchor −0.0032 0.0012 0.0056 ≤ 0.0509 holds e = 0.5 −0.0025 0.0011 0.0047 ≤ 0.0521 holds e = 1.0 −0.0022 0.0011 0.0044 ≤ 0.0511 holds truth precision (−2·SE) e = 0.5 0.0384 0.0135 0.0115 ≥ −0.05 holds e = 1.0 0.0047 0.0019 0.0009 ≥ −0.05 holds sign stability (−2·SE) e = 0.5 0.0341 0.0039 0.0263 ≥ −0.05 holds e = 1.0 0.0166 0.0040 0.0087 ≥ −0.05 holds top-k frequency (−2·SE) e = 0.5 −0.0110 0.0050 −0.0210 ≥ −0.10 holds e = 1.0 −0.0087 0.0044 −0.0174 ≥ −0.10 holds

The residual-confounding bound is 0.10 × the unadjusted arm's |mean projection difference| in the same cell (0.5091, 0.5207, 0.5113), so adjustment removes over 99 % of the confounding the unadjusted contrast carries. The adjusted arm's truth precision and sign stability sit slightly above the oracle's, plausibly because the adjustment also removes the features' chance within-cell association with the five noise covariates, which the oracle keeps; the check does not test that explanation. Top-k frequency is 0.009–0.011 below the oracle's, a tenth of its margin: the six refitted coefficients per replicate add some spread to the per-feature ranks.

The adjusted contrast is not the oracle's contrast. Their cosine is 0.55 at the anchor and 0.74 / 0.79 at e = 0.5 / 1.0, and their top-20 overlap 0.28 / 0.50 / 0.50; the unadjusted arm's are lower (0.49 / 0.69 / 0.74 and 0.17 / 0.43 / 0.44). Estimating the coefficients on n = 80 moves the per-feature contrast; the criteria ask whether that movement reintroduces the confounder or loses drivers, and it does neither.

docs.title: 4. Verdict and consequence
docs.text:
Verdict: adjusted_attribution_validated. Both confounding gates and the recoverability gate hold, and every criterion holds at every cell. The decision file's consequence, verbatim: "covariate-adjusted attribution is validated at the case study's configuration; item 12 (the plasmode demonstration on SEA-AD astrocyte cohort_30) may start on the released version (0.14.0)".

  • Item 12 is proposed next, pinned to MOTCO 0.14.0. Its proposal fixes the detection rate, the recovery thresholds and the null-making step on the real blocks. The Phase 6 attribution leg stays withheld until it reports.
  • motco analyze. With declared covariates, --attribution reports covariate-adjusted drivers; the record's attribution.adjustment block names the means it used. The validation status in docs/api/analysis.md now cites this report.

docs.title: 5. Descriptive readings
docs.text:
None of these enters the verdict.

  • The unadjusted arm. Read against the same bounds, it fails contamination at the anchor (0.4485 against 0.05) and residual confounding everywhere (0.52–0.53 against about 0.05). Its truth precision is higher than the oracle's (+0.084 / +0.013): injected features that are also drivers get a boost and are counted as correct, which is why the contamination metric counts only injected non-drivers.
  • The PLS-captured component. Contamination holds (≤ 0.019). Residual confounding reads 0.045 / 0.037 / 0.023 against 0.019 / 0.019 / 0.031. On the means, adjustment removes 85 / 89 / 97 % of the captured component's confounding, short of 90 % at the anchor and e = 0.5. The captured view projects the adjusted means through a basis fitted without the covariates, so a share of the injection direction that lies in that basis is reconstructed with the signal. The driver report uses the observed component (design D9).
  • The residual component. Contamination holds. On the means, adjustment removes 90 / 93 / 94 % of its confounding, but the 2-SE readings, 0.049 / 0.040 / 0.025, exceed the bounds 0.032 / 0.033 / 0.020; truth precision at e = 0.5 reads −0.052 against −0.05. The residual is observed minus captured, so it inherits the captured view's remainder with the opposite sign.
  • The transitions. Both transition blocks hold every criterion at every cell, with margins wider than the principal block's (residual confounding 0.003 against about 0.028).
  • The angle-rejected units. Restricted to units whose adjusted analysis rejects angle at 0.05 (23 / 128 / 333 units), every criterion holds (largest contamination reading 0.0137; truth precision at e = 0.5 −0.0131).
  • Rank-deficient replicates. None in any unit. All six covariates are numeric, so no resample can drop a factor level.

docs.title: 6. Limitations and scope
docs.text:
• Structural analogue. The blocks are InterSIM omics (367 methylation and 131 expression features, 498), not SEA-AD's 10,000 RNA and ATAC features. Item 12 runs on the real blocks.
  • One table, one stage effect. Only the astrocyte table (item 12's cohort) at δ = 2.0 is measured. At SEA-AD's own stage signal (held-out AUROC 0.63–0.70) the stage transitions are near zero and every arm's contrast is noise; how attribution behaves there is item 12's question.
  • Numeric covariates only. The rank-deficient path for a rare factor level is unit-tested, not measured here.
  • The covariate model. Covariates enter additively and linearly, as in the trajectory models; the interpretation boundary in every adjusted result says so. Adjustment removes only declared covariates.
  • The amended gates. The contamination gate is read at the anchor only. At the orientation cells, removal is judged by the projection, which does not depend on the top-k, while contamination there is a criterion without a gate.
  • The observed principal block. The verdict reads one component and one block. The PLS-captured and residual views hold contamination but not the 90 % residual-confounding bound at every cell (§5).

docs.title: Operating characteristics at the ADNI design — 2026-11-02
docs.text:
This report measures size and power of the real-data analysis at the ADNI case study's design (openspec change adni-design-operating-characteristics, spec adni-design-validation; roadmap Next changes item 9). The case study (adni_sexdiff) reads its angle and shape non-rejections as uninformative under its reading rule 3, because no power statement existed at its design. This check supplies one.

Every number below is read from results/adni-design-2026-11-02/: - run/adni_design_decision.json, run/size_readings.csv, run/adni_design_rates.csv, run/adni_design_rank_strata.csv, run/merge.json, run/decide.json, run/settings.json, run/PROVENANCE.txt; - calibration/calibration.json (every calibration iteration); - the smoke smoke/ (R = 20 × 99 permutations, indicative).

run/records/ and the 1.66 MB run/adni_design_replicates.csv stay on ing; run/PROVENANCE.txt names them with their sha256. Rates are rejection rates at p ≤ 0.05 over R = 500 replicates at 999 permutations.

Run. - One SLURM array on ing (job 932122, partition 512x1024, n11 excluded, 175 shards of 40 units), from the clean worktree of feat/adni-design-operating-characteristics at db2e30a. Its git tree 3ec28936… equals the workstation's, and the change's tests passed there. - All 175 tasks ended COMPLETED 0:0 between 15:23Z and 16:48Z on 2026-11-02. 7,000 of 7,000 units, 0 failures. - 174.6 elapsed core-hours (planned about 200, range 105–265); the units' own timers sum to 152.7 h. - The afterany job 932123 ran merge and decide. The decision file's settings hash aa7964ab… equals settings.json's.

Verdict: non_rejections_uninformative, read verbatim from adni_design_decision.json ("indicative": false). - "size": "holds": true, "exceeding": []. All six readings sit at or below the 0.0695 bound. - "informative_from" is null for delta, angle and shape: no target statistic reaches the 0.80 floor at any effect.

In one paragraph. - The design. ADNI's sex × stage table (n = 1,501) was rebuilt with two blocks and six covariate columns of ADNI's kinds: a confounded numeric, a factor in two drop-first columns, a phase-like binary nuisance injected into one block, and two noise columns. The stage signal was calibrated to ADNI's held-out AUROC, and the run used a seed family no committed check uses. Every unit ran the case study's primary as issued: analyze_trajectories with the six covariates, the rank floor of 2 and net displacement. - Size. It holds at both controls. The six readings are 0.034–0.068 against 0.0695. - Power. None of the three statistics has useful power. Magnitude/delta reaches 0.530 at a doubled stage effect in one group (e = 1.0). Orientation/angle and shape/shape stay at the null rate (0.034–0.076) at every effect. - Rank. The CV-selected rank sits at the cap, 19, in 95–100 % of units at every cell, against ADNI's 8. - Consequence. adni_sexdiff keeps its rule 3, now citing these measured rates, in its own change. The Phase 6 exit review (roadmap item 10) reads ADNI as a design without power for any of the three statistics.

docs.title: 1. Construction
docs.text:
scripts/adni_design_check.py composes the case-study construction by import (case_study_type_i_check, built on the D10 construction of covariate_type_i_check):

  • Generator. The semi-synthetic generator at ADNI's table [[237, 310, 125], [223, 448, 158]], three stages, methylation (367 CpGs) and expression (131 genes), joint magnitude, p_dmp 0.1, and one weakened per-omic stage effect δ.
  • Covariates, in model order (six design columns, as covariates.design_columns records them):
  • z: D10's numeric covariate, confounded with group × stage and injected along a fixed direction over 20 % of the joint features at s_z (ADNI's age).
  • category[c1], category[c2]: D10's three-level covariate on the same linear predictor, declared as a factor and not injected (ADNI's apoe4[1], apoe4[2]).
  • phase: binary, drawn per sex × stage cell at ADNI's ADNI2GO shares (F 0.603 / 0.623 / 0.424, M 0.561 / 0.507 / 0.481; adni_sexdiff results/motco_input/). It is injected into the expression block only as a dense offset s_p · sd_f · d_f · phase, with d_f i.i.d. N(0, 1) drawn once from the base seed. It enters the model as a numeric 0/1 column (ADNI's phase[ADNI2GO]). The expression block's 131 features stand for p180's 133.
  • x1, x2: i.i.d. N(0, 1), never injected (ADNI's education, statin[1]).
  • Seeds. Every seed derives from base seed 2032 and the replicate index, so the 14 cells of a replicate share the baseline draw, the covariates, the phase draw and the permutation draws, and differ only in the surgery.
  • Analysis. One adjusted analysis per unit: the six covariates in the trajectory model, min_components = 2, net displacement, the harness CV knobs (3 × 4 folds, 5 repeats, max_components 20), 999 permutations and the replicate's RRPP seed. There is no latent adjustment and no residual correction, as in ADNI's primary (κ ≈ 1.003 at n = 1,501 would be immaterial).
  • Cells. The anchor; translation at e = 1.0; magnitude at e = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0; orientation and shape at e = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
Twelve iterations on anchor units (R = 20 × 99 permutations, two arms), all in calibration/calibration.json, met the three predeclared criteria at δ = 0.02, s_z = 0.1, s_p = 1.75. The iterations and why this one was chosen are tabulated in the change's design.md (Calibration). In short:

  • At D10's s_z = 3 the first component followed z (|ρ| 0.94) and the AUROC sat at 0.77–0.88.
  • At s_z = 0.3 the AUROC kept a floor near 0.645 that δ barely moved.
  • At s_z = 0.1 the floor fell, and the phase offset steered the basis without adding stage signal: raising s_p from 1.5 to 2.5 moved the AUROC from 0.602 to 0.604.

The calibrated construction, as realized at the paper-grade run's 500 anchor units (calibration_realized in the decision), beside ADNI's primary:

quantity construction (anchor, R = 500) ADNI primary held-out CV stage AUROC, mean 0.606 (q05–q95 0.576–0.633; band 0.55–0.65) 0.600 (0.580–0.616 across CV-selected analyses) first latent component |Spearman| with phase, median 0.578 (threshold 0.4) 0.542 first latent component |Spearman| with the confounded numeric, median 0.078 0.061 (age) CV-selected rank 19 in 494 of 500 (2, 11, 18 in two each) 8 pooled relative eigengap, median 0.330 0.744 angle null q95, median 51.0° 35.4° phase offset in the injected block: median |d|, PC1 |corr| 1.126, 0.994 p180: 1.12, 0.73 phase offset in the other block 0.031, 0.015 NMR: 0.21, 0.13

The construction matches ADNI on the calibrated quantities (AUROC, the basis following phase, the size of the offset) and differs on the latent geometry. The CV selects every component it is offered (rank 19 against 8). The stage means are less one-dimensional (eigengap 0.33 against 0.74), and the angle null is wider (51° against 35°). The offset is the injected block's whole first axis, where ADNI's p180 has other structure of its own.

The paper-grade run has no unadjusted arm. At calibration the unadjusted arm rejected delta at 0.15 and shape at 0.45 at the anchor, so the construction confounds (criterion 3).

docs.title: 2. Size
docs.text:
size_readings.csv, bound α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/R) = 0.0695 at R = 500, so at most 34 rejections of 500 hold:

control delta angle shape anchor (e = 0) 17 / 500 = 0.034 30 / 500 = 0.060 20 / 500 = 0.040 translation (e = 1.0) 17 / 500 = 0.034 27 / 500 = 0.054 34 / 500 = 0.068
  • Every reading holds. Translation shape holds at the largest count the bound allows (34). Under the rule's design (D8), a valid test fails at most one of six readings about 17 % of the time at exact α, so one reading near the bound is expected.
  • delta is conservative (0.034 at both controls). Six covariate columns at n = 1,501 cost almost nothing in residual df, so the liberal delta the SEA-AD configuration showed at n = 80 (residual_df_shrinkage) does not arise here.
  • The size sentence, verbatim: "Size holds at the ADNI design: all six readings at or below the one-sided bound".

docs.title: 3. Power
docs.text:
adni_design_rates.csv (target pairs), SE the binomial standard error, R = 500 at every effect:

target e rate (SE) CV-selected rank magnitude / delta 0.1 0.034 (0.008) 19 in 497 0.25 0.056 (0.010) 19 in 498 0.5 0.134 (0.015) 19 in 500 1.0 0.530 (0.022) 19 in 500 orientation / angle 0.25 0.070 (0.011) 19 in 488; 2–3 in 4 0.5 0.056 (0.010) 19 in 468; 2–3 in 12 0.75 0.076 (0.012) 19 in 418; 2–3 in 53 1.0 0.058 (0.010) 19 in 352; 2–3 in 96 shape / shape 0.25 0.062 (0.011) 19 in 487 0.5 0.048 (0.010) 19 in 487 0.75 0.034 (0.008) 19 in 475 1.0 0.046 (0.009) 19 in 472
  • Magnitude/delta. It is the only statistic whose rate rises with the effect, but it stays below the floor. At e = 1.0 (group B's per-omic stage effect twice group A's) delta rejects 0.530. The magnitude surgery also raises the stage AUROC, from 0.614 at e = 0.1 to 0.683 at e = 1.0 (cv_mean_auroc_mean).
  • Orientation/angle and shape/shape. Both sit at the null rate at every effect: 0.056–0.076 and 0.034–0.062. These surgeries permute or relocate differential features whose stage effect is δ = 0.02. At an AUROC near 0.60 that moves the group's stage means by too little for a test whose null angle q95 is about 51°.
  • Rank strata (adni_design_rank_strata.csv; descriptive). The orientation surgery pushes more units to rank 2–3 as e grows (4 → 96 of 500), but those units do not reject more often. At e = 1.0: 2 / 96 = 0.021 at rank 2–3, 1 / 8 at 4–7, 26 / 396 = 0.066 at 8+. At e = 0.75: 3 / 53 = 0.057 at 2–3, 35 / 444 = 0.079 at 8+. The Phase 6 pattern, where power rises above rank 3, does not appear, because there is no power to stratify. Magnitude sits at rank 8+ in 499–500 units per effect. The strata's replicates sum to the pooled R in every cell.
  • Off-target rates (descriptive). They lie at 0.022–0.078: magnitude by angle 0.050–0.060 and by shape 0.028–0.042; orientation by delta 0.022–0.050 and by shape 0.030–0.058; shape by delta 0.030–0.044 and by angle 0.050–0.078. Only one of the 24 off-target readings lies above 0.0695: shape e = 0.75 read by angle (0.078), which does not enter the verdict.

docs.title: 4. Verdict, statements and consequences
docs.text:
Verdict: non_rejections_uninformative. Size holds at both controls and no target statistic has an informative effect. The decision file's statements, verbatim:

  • delta: "At the ADNI design delta reaches at most 0.530 (SE 0.022, R = 500) at e = 1 of the magnitude construction, at CV-selected rank 19 (median 19); a non-rejection is uninformative up to the construction maximum (e = 1; floor 0.80)."
  • angle: "At the ADNI design angle reaches at most 0.076 (SE 0.012, R = 500) at e = 0.75 of the orientation construction, at CV-selected rank 2–19 (median 19); a non-rejection is uninformative up to the construction maximum (e = 1; floor 0.80)."
  • shape: "At the ADNI design shape reaches at most 0.062 (SE 0.011, R = 500) at e = 0.25 of the shape construction, at CV-selected rank 2–19 (median 19); a non-rejection is uninformative up to the construction maximum (e = 1; floor 0.80)."

Consequences.

  • adni_sexdiff. It keeps reading rule 3 in its own change, now as a measurement rather than an absence of one. Its angle and shape non-rejections are uninformative: at this design and stage signal neither statistic detects the generator's strongest orientation or shape construction above the null rate. Its delta non-rejection (p 0.112) is uninformative too, by the same rule: delta reaches 0.53 only at a doubled stage effect in one group.
  • Size holds at both controls, and delta is conservative there (0.034).
  • So the sensitivity arms' delta rejections near α (forced rank 6, p 0.047; nmr_all_columns, 0.045) are not explained by a liberal null at this design. They remain the arm-setting dependences the case study reads them as.
  • MOTCO. The documentation states the measured rates beside the SEA-AD statement. Nothing under src/motco/ changes, and the version stays 0.13.0.
  • Roadmap item 10 (Phase 6 exit review). It reads both case studies as size-controlled designs without power for orientation and shape. ADNI also has no useful power for size.

docs.title: 5. Limitations and scope
docs.text:
• Structural analogue. The blocks are InterSIM omics, not metabolomics: 367 methylation and 131 expression features (498) against p180's 133 and NMR's 165 (298). The block shares differ: methylation / expression 74 / 26 % against NMR / p180 55 / 45 %. The generator's latent geometry differs from ADNI's: the CV rank is at the cap (19 against 8), the eigengap is 0.33 against 0.74, and the phase offset is the injected block's whole first axis (0.99 against 0.73). No statement is made about metabolite-level behaviour.
  • One table. Only the intersection cohort's table (n = 1,501) is measured. The CN / LMCI / AD arm (n = 1,130) is inferred, not measured.
  • One strength. The run used one calibrated stage signal (δ = 0.02, s_z = 0.1, s_p = 1.75). The calibration matched AUROC, the basis following phase and the offset size. It did not match the rank, which the design records but does not tune to.
  • The covariate model. Covariates enter additively and linearly: one confounded numeric (z, weakly injected at s_z = 0.1), one confounded factor (category, declared, not injected), one injected binary nuisance and two noise columns.
  • The primary only. The latent-adjusted, residual-corrected and forced-rank arms, and ADNI's export variants, were not run, so their operating characteristics at this design stay inferred.

docs.title: The angle RRPP null is strongly non-pivotal — and that is what makes the test work
docs.text: Run date: 2026-09-01 Code revision: 899179586c6c04c97e3485bcf19e504309320ba8 (branch feat/diagnose-angle-null-pivotality, parent bc0d42c, the merge of the orientation sign-anchor fix) Configuration: examples/trajectory_power_study/angle_pivotality_diagnostic.json Records: results/angle-pivotality-2026-09-01/merged.jsonl (500 replicates, 0 failures, 199 permutations each) Tables: results/angle-pivotality-2026-09-01/report/ — pivotality_association.csv, pivotality_rejection_split.csv, pivotality_standardized.csv Provenance: results/angle-pivotality-2026-09-01/PROVENANCE.txt Change: openspec/changes/diagnose-angle-null-pivotality Answers: Phase 5 readiness item 1 (blocking) Environment: Python 3.11.15, numpy 2.3.5, pandas 2.3.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scipy 1.16.3; no R at runtime

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The Phase 4 hypothesis is confirmed: within a replicate, the RRPP permutation null for angle moves almost one-for-one with that replicate's own observed angle. Regressing each replicate's own 95th-percentile null on its observed statistic gives a slope of 0.811 in the orientation cell at effect 1.00 and 0.87–0.96 in every other cell measured. The statistic is not pivotal, and the effect is large.

This fully accounts for the rejection inversion. Among the 100 orientation replicates at effect 1.00, the 32 that fail to reject have a larger mean observed angle (60.8°) than the 68 that reject (46.5°) — but their own critical values differ by far more: 103.6° versus 15.8°. The outcome is decided by the critical value, not by the observed statistic, and the pattern is confined to angle.

The proposed remedy does not follow. The readiness worklist anticipated that a confirmed association would mean "a pivotal statistic or a studentized test." Both are ruled out by measurement:

  • Within-replicate studentization is a no-op. Standardizing observed and null by the same constants is a strictly monotone transform of both sides of the comparison; the permutation p-value is identical. This is a theorem, not an empirical finding, and it is pinned by tests/test_pivotality.py::test_within_replicate_studentization_leaves_the_p_value_unchanged.
  • Cross-replicate standardization gains nothing. Recalibrating each replicate as z = (observed − null_mean) / null_sd against the pooled null-control z distribution moves orientation angle power from 0.68 to 0.70 — two replicates, against a Monte Carlo standard error of 0.047.
  • Freezing the null is catastrophic. Replacing the per-replicate critical value with a single fixed threshold calibrated on the null cell (its 95th-percentile observed angle, 153.2°) drops orientation angle power from 0.68 to 0.01.

The per-replicate null is not a defect that costs power. It is adaptation to a latent-space noise level that varies enormously across replicates, and it is worth roughly 67 points of power relative to any fixed threshold. The tracking is the price of that adaptation.

Verdict: angle is strongly non-pivotal, the non-pivotality explains the inversion, and it is load-bearing rather than corrigible. The remaining shortfall is a property of the design point, not of the statistic or its calibration.

docs.title: Provenance: this reads the same records that produced the shortfall
docs.text:
The diagnostic was configured to hold every generator, integration, and evaluation parameter at the Phase 4 pilot's values, and it does so exactly. Comparing per replicate against the sign-fix re-run (results/orientation-signfix-2026-08-28/merged.jsonl):

  • 400 of 500 records match on all four cells they share — identical generator seeds, identical delta, angle, and shape statistics to 1e-8 relative, identical p-values to 1e-12.
  • Orientation angle power reproduces at 0.68, delta at 0.65, shape at 0.99 — the sign-fix operating point, replicate for replicate.
  • The fifth cell (magnitude at effect 1.00, absent from the sign-fix re-run) matches Phase 4 on all 100 generator seeds and on delta and shape in 100 of 100 replicates; angle differs in 15 of 100, which is the sign-anchor correction and nothing else.

So the numbers below are not a re-derivation on fresh draws. They are a decomposition of the same replicates that yielded 0.68.

docs.title: Cells
docs.text:
enumerate_study emits five cells, not the three requested: it unconditionally adds a none Type I baseline and a translation negative control. Both are retained deliberately — they supply the null-control reference distribution the cross-replicate counterfactual calibrates against.

Cell Phase n Role orientation @ 1.00 power_primary 100 the shortfall magnitude @ 1.00 power_primary 100 comparator; its delta reaches power 1.00 translation @ 1.00 power_primary 100 null control that behaved normally in Phase 4 translation @ 1.00 type_i_baseline 100 mandated negative control none type_i_baseline 100 mandated zero-effect baseline

docs.title: 1. The association
docs.text:
Slope of each replicate's own null 95th percentile on its own observed statistic. Both axes carry the same units within a statistic, so the slope reads directly: how much of a one-unit increase in the observed statistic is matched by an increase in the critical value it must beat.

Cell delta angle shape none (zero effect) 0.339 0.931 0.449 translation @1.00 (type_i_baseline) 0.237 0.925 0.373 translation @1.00 (power_primary) 0.152 0.960 0.348 magnitude @1.00 0.030 0.874 −0.000 orientation @1.00 0.018 0.811 0.058

Bold marks each statistic in the cell where it carries signal, plus angle throughout.

Read the columns, not the rows. Under the zero-effect null every statistic tracks its own null to some degree, and that is expected: observed and permuted values are exchangeable draws from the same distribution, so a replicate with an unstable latent space produces both a large observed statistic and a large null. Tracking under the null is not evidence of a problem.

What separates a usable statistic is what happens when signal is added. For delta, the slope in its own cell collapses from 0.339 to 0.030; for shape, from 0.449 to 0.058. The signal moves the observed statistic while leaving the null where it was — which is exactly what a test needs. For angle in its own cell the slope barely moves, 0.931 → 0.811. Roughly four fifths of any orientation signal that reaches the observed angle also reaches the bar it has to clear.

Correlations, with Fisher-z 95% intervals (pivotality_association.csv, null_target = q95), confirm the association is not a small-sample artifact — every interval excludes zero:

Cell angle correlation 95% interval none +0.634 [+0.500, +0.738] translation @1.00 (type_i_baseline) +0.609 [+0.469, +0.719] translation @1.00 (power_primary) +0.562 [+0.411, +0.683] orientation @1.00 +0.526 [+0.367, +0.655] magnitude @1.00 +0.473 [+0.305, +0.613]

The same table reports the association against the null's mean and sd, which track more weakly (orientation angle: slopes 0.306 and 0.349, correlations +0.585 and +0.563). The upper tail moves more than the centre — which is why the summary retains quantiles and not just moments: the alpha-level critical value is not recoverable from the mean and sd of a bounded, skewed angular null.

docs.title: 2. It accounts for the inversion
docs.text:
From pivotality_rejection_split.csv, orientation at effect 1.00, α = 0.05:

Statistic n reject n fail mean observed (reject) mean observed (fail) mean critical (reject) mean critical (fail) angle 68 32 46.5° 60.8° 15.8° 103.6° delta 65 35 3.069 0.547 1.025 1.048 shape 99 1 0.0705 0.0103 0.0233 0.0266

The angle row is inverted — non-rejecting replicates carry the larger observed statistic — and it is the only inverted row in any signal-carrying cell. For delta and shape the critical value is essentially constant across the split (ratios 1.02× and 1.14×) while the observed statistic separates by 5.6× and 6.9×. For angle the observed statistic separates by only 1.3× while the critical value separates by 6.6×.

Per-replicate angle critical values in this cell span 5.0° to 176.6°, a 35-fold range. That dispersion, not the observed angle, decides the outcome.

The Phase 4 report recorded this inversion pre-sign-fix as 66.7° versus 52.5°. Post-fix it is 60.8° versus 46.5°: the inversion survived the correction, exactly as the sign-anchor report predicted, and it now has a mechanism.

One further inverted row appears — angle in the translation Type I baseline (6.9° rejecting vs 14.0° non-rejecting). It rests on 4 rejections out of 100 and should be read as noise, not as a second finding.

docs.title: 3. Why no remedy recovers the power
Within-replicate studentization is a no-op
docs.text: Dividing the observed statistic and every null draw by the same constant is strictly monotone on both sides of the comparison that defines the permutation p-value. The p-value cannot change. This closes off the reading that a "studentized angle test" is available but unimplemented.

docs.title: Cross-replicate standardization: +0.02
docs.text:
pivotality_standardized.csv reports, per cell and statistic, the as-specified rejection rate beside the rate obtained by comparing each replicate's z = (observed − null_mean) / null_sd against the 95th percentile of the pooled null-control z distribution:

Cell Statistic As specified Standardized Control? orientation @1.00 angle 0.68 0.70 no orientation @1.00 delta 0.65 0.64 no orientation @1.00 shape 0.99 0.99 no magnitude @1.00 delta 1.00 1.00 no magnitude @1.00 angle 0.00 0.00 no none angle 0.05 0.05 yes translation @1.00 (type_i_baseline) angle 0.04 0.04 yes translation @1.00 (power_primary) angle 0.03 0.06 yes

The controls hold their nominal level under both rules, so the counterfactual is calibrated. It simply does not help: two replicates on orientation angle, against a Monte Carlo standard error of 0.047. The reason is visible in §1 — the null's sd tracks the observed statistic too (slope 0.349), so standardizing removes the nuisance and a comparable share of the signal with it.

The cross-replicate counterfactual is a diagnostic, not a deployable test. It borrows a reference z distribution from null-control cells, which do not exist alongside a real dataset. It is reported to measure how much power the tracking costs, never as a procedure to adopt.

docs.title: A fixed threshold destroys the test
docs.text:
The null cell's observed angle distribution has a median of 5.1° and a 95th percentile of 153.2° — it is extraordinarily heavy-tailed. Using that 95th percentile as one fixed critical value for every replicate, orientation at effect 1.00 rejects 1 time in 100, against 0.68 as specified. Only 1 of the 32 non-rejecting replicates carries an observed angle above it.

This is the finding that reframes the item. The per-replicate null is not a tax on power; it is worth about 67 points of it. A replicate-specific critical value is the only thing that makes a latent angular statistic testable at all when latent-space stability varies this much across draws.

docs.title: 4. What the shortfall actually is
docs.text:
The 32 non-rejecting replicates are the high-noise draws: their latent trajectory geometry is unstable enough that a real effect-1.00 orientation change (cell median observed angle 41.8°, IQR [23.5°, 70.3°]) falls inside their own permutation null. The test is behaving correctly — it is declining to call an angle significant when that angle is not resolvable in the space it was measured in.

The instability is invisible to every integration diagnostic currently persisted. Within the orientation cell:

  • Selected PLS dimensionality is 3 in 93 of 100 replicates (2 in the remaining 7).
  • CV mean AUROC is 1.0000 in every replicate, rejecting and non-rejecting alike.
  • Correlation of log(null q95) with selected dimensionality is +0.139; with CV mean AUROC, −0.179.

So the driver of the null width is not latent dimensionality and not stage-separation quality. Nothing the harness records today identifies which replicates will be resolvable, which means Phase 5 cannot condition on it and cannot report it as a covariate.

docs.title: 5. Phase 5 consequence
docs.text:
angle proceeds as specified.

The statistic and its permutation test are sound. Type I level is nominal in every control cell under both decision rules (0.03–0.05 for angle), RRPP p-values remain exact under exchangeability whether or not the statistic is pivotal, no substitute statistic is available, and the two candidate remedies were measured and found to be respectively inert and destructive. There is no calibration defect to fix and nothing to replace.

This decision deliberately does not settle the 0.80 power floor. This diagnostic measured one design point (n = 300, four stages, ~660 features, PLS at 3 latent dimensions) and cannot say whether the gap closes with more samples per group-stage cell. That question belongs to readiness item 4, and it now has a concrete lever: the dispersion of the per-replicate angle null. Power for orientation is governed by how tightly latent trajectory geometry is determined by the data, so the design-point study should measure how the spread of null_summary["angle"]["q95"] contracts with samples per group-stage cell, not just how the rejection rate moves.

docs.title: Consequences for the other readiness items
docs.text:
• Item 2 (orientation → shape). Unchanged in substance, but the diagnostic removes one candidate explanation: shape in the orientation cell is nearly pivotal (slope 0.058, critical values 0.0233 vs 0.0266 across the rejection split), so its 0.99 rejection rate is not a null-tracking artifact. The response is real in the latent space and item 2's framing as a projection-versus-construction question stands.
  • Item 3 (latent dimensionality). Cannot be settled with the diagnostics currently recorded. Selected dimensionality is effectively constant and CV AUROC is saturated at 1.0, and neither correlates with the null width. Re-sizing the latent space needs a direct measure of latent trajectory-geometry stability, which the harness does not yet compute.
  • Item 4 (design point). Inherits the 0.80-floor question, with the null-dispersion lever above.

docs.title: Reproducing
docs.text:
# ~26 minutes on 16 cores; 500 work units. Do NOT pass --n-jobs.
for i in $(seq 0 15); do
  uv run python scripts/run_study_shard.py \
    --config examples/trajectory_power_study/angle_pivotality_diagnostic.json \
    --out-dir results/angle-pivotality-2026-09-01 \
    --shard-index "$i" --n-shards 16 --error-policy record &
done
wait
uv run python scripts/motco_study.py merge --out-dir results/angle-pivotality-2026-09-01
uv run python scripts/angle_null_pivotality.py \
  --merged  results/angle-pivotality-2026-09-01/merged.jsonl \
  --out-dir results/angle-pivotality-2026-09-01/report

The shard and merged JSONL are gitignored as regenerable; the report/ tables and PROVENANCE.txt are committed. Every number in §1, §2, and the standardized table in §3 is a cell of one of those three committed tables. The record-identity check in the provenance section and the fixed-threshold and metadata-correlation figures in §3 and §4 are derived from merged.jsonl directly, by this:

from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from motco.simulations.grid import read_replicate_results

recs = read_replicate_results(Path("results/angle-pivotality-2026-09-01/merged.jsonl"))
orient = [r for r in recs
          if (r.cell_metadata or {}).get("trajectory_mode") == "orientation"
          and r.phase == "power_primary"]
null_cell = [r for r in recs
             if r.phase == "type_i_baseline"
             and (r.cell_metadata or {}).get("trajectory_mode") in (None, "none")]

# §3 — one fixed critical value calibrated on the null cell's observed angles
threshold = np.quantile([r.pair_statistics["angle"] for r in null_cell], 0.95)   # 153.22 deg
obs = np.array([r.pair_statistics["angle"] for r in orient])
print(threshold, (obs > threshold).mean())                                       # 0.01 vs 0.68 as specified

# §4 — the null width against the persisted integration diagnostics
q95 = np.log([r.null_summary["angle"]["q95"] for r in orient])
lv = [float(r.integration_metadata["selected_lv"]) for r in orient]
auroc = [float(r.integration_metadata["cv_mean_auroc"]) for r in orient]
print(np.corrcoef(q95, lv)[0, 1], np.corrcoef(q95, auroc)[0, 1])                 # +0.139, -0.179

docs.title: Case-study configuration diagnosis — 2026-10-30
docs.text:
This report diagnoses the size excess that the case-study configuration Type I check found at the SEA-AD case study's configuration (openspec change case-study-configuration-diagnosis, spec case-study-configuration-diagnosis). It covers two findings: the covariate-adjusted model's delta, and the stage latent adjustment's anchor angle and shape.

Every number below is read from results/case-study-diagnosis-2026-10-30/: - case_study_diagnosis_decision.json, diagnosis_contrasts.csv, decide.json; - per run in delta0.1/ and delta0.05/: diagnosis_rates.csv, diagnosis_rank_table.csv, diagnosis_reproduction.json, merge.json, settings.json, PROVENANCE.txt; - the smoke records smoke-delta0.1/, smoke-delta0.05/ and smoke-decision/.

diagnosis_pvalues.csv, merged.jsonl and records/ stay on ing; each PROVENANCE.txt names them with their sha256. Rates are rejection rates at p ≤ 0.05 over R = 500 replicates at 999 permutations. The bound is the parent check's one-sided α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/R) = 0.0695, i.e. at most 34 rejections in 500.

Run. - Two 50-shard SLURM arrays on ing (partition 512x1024, n11 and the heavily loaded n3 excluded), from the clean worktree of feat/case-study-configuration-diagnosis at 5c30c51. The git tree is 4fe2050d…, identical to the workstation, and the diagnosis tests passed there. - Job 930358 ran the δ = 0.1 parent and job 930408 the δ = 0.05 parent: 50 / 50 tasks COMPLETED 0:0 in each, 10.7 + 14.4 = 25.1 recorded core-hours (34 planned). - 1,000 units per parent (the zero-effect anchor and the translation control at e = 1.0, × 500 replicates). Each unit ran four analyses and twelve RRPP-only arms, with 0 arm failures. - Every unit passed three hard checks: - the reconstruction of the fitted covariate-blind projection matched the analysis's latent scores (maximum error 2.7e-13 against the 1e-9 tolerance); - X − X0 and Y − Y0 were rank one in z (maximum residual 6.5e-16); - the script's z_noise5 equalled analyze_trajectories exactly.

Reproduction. The diagnosis regenerated the parent's data, covariates, CV folds and RRPP seeds. z_noise5 reproduces the parent's adjusted arm, and latent_stage_cv its latent_stage arm, with 0 mismatches over 3,000 + 3,000 p-values per parent (diagnosis_reproduction.json, status holds in both runs). So every derived arm below sits on the parent's exact units, and the decision's gate is open.

Verdicts. Both are read verbatim from case_study_diagnosis_decision.json ("decision": "diagnosed", "indicative": false): - Covariate-adjusted delta: residual_df_shrinkage. The column contrast C2 (z_noise5 vs z_noise0) is significant (one-sided p = 0.015). The residual-df corrected case-study model holds the bound for every statistic at both controls in both runs, and its own column contrast C4 is not significant (p = 0.156). - stage latent adjustment: residualized_basis. At a forced rank of 2, with no cross-validation, it still exceeds on anchor angle in both runs (0.084 / 0.082), although its shape now holds.

In one paragraph. - The design. The diagnosis reran the parent check's exact units: - on the covariate-blind basis, it crossed the confounded covariate z (estimated in the model, or its injection removed exactly from the latent scores) with 0, 2 or 5 pure-noise covariates; - each of those six arms was rerun with the Freedman–Lane residuals rescaled by κ = √(n / (n − p_red)); - the stage latent adjustment ran at the CV floor of 2, at floor 1 and at a forced rank of 2. - delta rises with the column count and the correction removes it. Pooled over the four control readings (2,000 units), delta rises 0.0545 → 0.0595 → 0.066 with z in the model and 0.0525 → 0.0545 → 0.060 under the oracle. The corrected arms read 0.0475–0.0545, with no arm above the bound in any reading. - Estimating z costs no delta size. C3 (z_noise0 vs oracle_noise0) has p = 0.39. - What this means. The case study's delta excess is the Freedman–Lane null's residual-df shrinkage at ten reduced-model columns and n = 80. It is not the covariate's confounding. - The stage arm. Its anchor angle excess sits at rank 2 itself. Its shape excess sits in the CV rank's tail, and a fixed rank of 2 cures shape but not angle. - Consequences. The case study's primary waits for a MOTCO change offering the corrected permutation, validated by its own Type I and power check. The stage sensitivity arm stays inadmissible at this configuration, at a fixed rank too.

docs.title: 1. Construction
docs.text:
scripts/case_study_diagnosis.py (design D1) binds each run to one committed run directory of the parent check (--parent).

Parent binding. - It refuses a parent whose settings.json fails its recorded hash. - It also refuses one whose settings case_study_type_i_check.build_settings does not rebuild from the recorded arguments to the same hash. - The diagnosis's own settings.json carries the parent's settings, path and hash: ca57cc38… against parent 899ce29a… at δ = 0.1, and 6c5d447a… against 97eb6d90… at δ = 0.05.

The parent's construction is unchanged: - the Phase 6 SEA-AD design, [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]] with n = 80, methylation + expression; - the per-omic stage effect weakened to δ = 0.1 or 0.05; - z = 0.5·g + 1·s + 2·g·s + ε, injected at s_z = 10 along a fixed direction; - five i.i.d. N(0, 1) noise covariates x1–x5; - the rank floor of 2, the harness CV knobs and the net-displacement estimator.

Arms (design D2–D6). Every arm of a unit shares its data and its RRPP seed.

arm latent scores covariates in both trajectory models p_red κ oracle_noise0 Y0 none 4 — oracle_noise2 Y0 x1, x2 6 — oracle_noise5 Y0 x1–x5 9 — z_noise0 Y z 5 — z_noise2 Y z, x1, x2 7 — z_noise5 Y z, x1–x5 (the case study's model) 10 — <arm>_corrected as <arm> as <arm> as <arm> √(80 / (80 − p_red)): 1.026–1.069 latent_stage_cv own basis, stage adjustment, CV at floor 2 (the parent's arm) z, x1–x5 10 — latent_stage_floor1 own basis, stage adjustment, CV at floor 1 (descriptive) z, x1–x5 10 — latent_stage_rank2 own basis, stage adjustment, forced rank 2, no CV z, x1–x5 10 —
  • Y and the factorial. Y is the latent score matrix of one analyze_trajectories call with the six covariates on the covariate-blind basis. The six factorial arms are inference-only on that basis: the analysis's design, _covariate_adjusted_design, estimate_difference and serial RRPP.
  • The oracle (design D3).
  • X0 is D10's build at s_z = 0 with the same seeds.
  • The fitted covariate-blind map is reconstructed from the block scalers, the PLS centring and ddof = 1 scaling, and the PLS rotations, and checked against the analysis's latent scores.
  • Y0 is X0 through that map. It equals Y minus z times a fixed latent vector, which the tests check against the analytic injection.
  • The correction (design D5). Each corrected arm runs RRPP on ŷ_red + κ·e_red with the arm's models and seed: the same permutation indices, the uncorrected observed statistics, and p-values by the analysis's rule.

Contrasts (design D7) are paired on the same units: - For a contrast of arm B against arm A, replicate r contributes d_r: the readings (2 runs × 2 controls) that B rejects and A does not, minus the reverse. - The one-sided p-value is P(Σ ε_r d_r ≥ Σ d_r) over independent equiprobable signs, computed exactly by convolution. Each replicate is one cluster because its four readings share the covariates, noise columns and RRPP seed. - The predeclared delta contrasts are: - C1: oracle_noise5 vs oracle_noise0 - C2: z_noise5 vs z_noise0 - C3: z_noise0 vs oracle_noise0 - C4: z_noise5_corrected vs z_noise0_corrected

Smoke (design D10; smoke-*, R = 20 × 99 permutations; the design.md "Smoke and shard plan" record): - 40 / 40 units per parent with 0 failures, and indicative verdicts unresolved / residualized_basis; - a separate R = 4 × 999 run reproduced 24 + 24 p-values per parent with 0 mismatches; - one unit took 20.5 s on a workstation core (1.11× a parent unit). On ing the mean unit took 31 s (δ = 0.1, n2 and n4) and 42 s (δ = 0.05, n2).

  • Its angle excess sits at rank 2: 35 / 344 = 0.102 and 34 / 383 = 0.089. The tail rejects less (4 / 91 and 2 / 61 at rank ≥ 4).
  • Its shape excess sits in the tail: 10 / 65 and 7 / 56 at rank 3, 9 / 91 at rank ≥ 4, against 27 / 344 and 27 / 383 at rank 2.

docs.title: 5. What the arms show
docs.text:
The case study's delta excess is residual-df shrinkage. The mechanism the proposal named predicts three things, and the run shows all three: - The uncorrected rate rises with the reduced model's column count in both families. - With z: 0.0545, 0.0595, 0.066 at p_red 5, 7, 10. - Under the oracle: 0.0525, 0.0545, 0.060 at p_red 4, 6, 9. - The proposal's normal-tail estimate was 0.067 at six columns and 0.056 at none. - The corrected rate is flat and at or below α. - With z: 0.049, 0.048, 0.0545. - Under the oracle: 0.048, 0.0475, 0.0505. - No corrected arm exceeds the bound on delta in any reading; z_noise5_corrected's largest is 30 / 500. - angle is not inflated. The z arms read 0.042–0.050.

C2 is significant at 0.015. C1 points the same way but stops at 0.065 (net 15 against C2's 23). C4 keeps a residual net of 11 (p = 0.156), so the uniform κ removes most, though not visibly all, of the column trend. C3 is flat (p = 0.39, net 4), so estimating a covariate confounded with the group × stage cells costs no delta size here.

The C2 discordance comes from the translation control: 21 readings against 0, while the anchor readings balance at 20 against 18. That fits a null narrowed by the reduced model's columns, which a constant location offset in group B leaves otherwise untouched. The parent's single excess (translation delta at δ = 0.1, 36 / 500) belongs to this pattern.

The correction costs some angle and shape rejections. z_noise5_corrected reads angle 0.042 and shape 0.0465, against 0.0455 and 0.0615 uncorrected. A uniformly widened null is conservative for the two statistics that were not inflated. That is a power question for the follow-up change (design D5 deferred the leverage-adjusted alternative to it).

The oracle is not a size-α reference for angle. - Removing z's injection exactly from the latent scores, while leaving z out of the model, gives angle 0.0725–0.083 in every reading, corrected or not. Every z arm holds angle. C3 on angle is 23 against 82 in the opposite direction. - The basis is fitted on features that contain z, and only a z column in both models absorbs whatever that basis selected along z. That is a candidate explanation, not a tested one: the smoke probes (design.md, "Smoke and shard plan") found no z-aligned content in Y0's within-cell or interaction pattern on 10–20 units. The mechanism stays open. - The smoke had flagged the oracle rows for delta (5–7 / 20). At R = 500 the oracle's delta is 0.0525–0.060, so that was noise at R = 20. The angle inflation is real. - The delta verdict reads only paired contrasts, and C1 is within the oracle family. Neither depends on the oracle being size-α. Only C3's absolute meaning does, and C3 is flat on delta.

The stage latent adjustment fails on angle at rank 2, not through its rank tail. - With the rank forced to 2 and no cross-validation, which removes both the rank tail and the per-training-set nuisance coefficients, anchor angle still reads 0.084 / 0.082. - Under CV, its rank-2 units reject angle at 0.102 / 0.089. The parent's latent_stage angle excess is therefore a property of the residualized basis. - shape behaves differently: its excess came with the CV rank's tail, and at rank 2 it holds (0.068 / 0.064). - Floor 1 changes little: anchor angle 0.082 / 0.080 and shape 0.082 / 0.068, with 11–12 % of units at rank 1.

docs.title: 6. Verdicts and consequences
docs.text:
Read verbatim from case_study_diagnosis_decision.json.

Gate. "reproduction": {"status": "holds"}, with 3,000 / 0 compared / mismatching per arm and run. No run was a smoke run, so "indicative": false.

Covariate-adjusted delta: residual_df_shrinkage. - Conditions: - "column_contrast_significant": {"C1": false, "C2": true} - "corrected_case_study_model_holds": true - "corrected_column_contrast_significant": false - "collinear_contrast_significant": false - p-values C1 0.0645, C2 0.0153, C3 0.3863, C4 0.1561. - For MOTCO. A change offering the residual-df corrected permutation: - opt-in, with every output byte-identical when it is absent; - its own Type I and power check, comparing the uniform κ with the leverage-adjusted residuals of design D5, and reporting the angle and shape cost seen here. - For sead_sexdiff. - The primary stays withheld until that change is released and validated; then the primary is re-issued under it. - Until then, the primary's delta p-values read against a realized size of about 0.066 at six covariate columns. That is now attributed to the reduced model's column count, not to the covariate's confounding. - Its angle and shape p-values are size-controlled (0.042–0.068 in z_noise5). - Nothing in sead_sexdiff changes under this report.

stage latent adjustment: residualized_basis. - "rank2_not_holding" lists anchor angle at δ = 0.1 (0.084) and δ = 0.05 (0.082). latent_stage_rank2 holds every other reading. - For sead_sexdiff. The stage sensitivity arm stays inadmissible at this configuration, at a fixed rank of 2 too. Its angle rejections are not interpretable there. A rank-2 stage arm would hold shape, but the verdict is on the arm, so it is not adopted. - For MOTCO. Separating the per-training-set coefficients from the residualized basis would need a core switch (design, Risks). It is not proposed, because the forced-rank arm already has neither the rank tail nor CV.

docs.title: 7. Limitations and scope
docs.text:
The parent check's four limitations carry over unchanged:

  • Astrocyte primary cohort sizes only. [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]] with n = 80. The microglia cohort (n = 76) and the other cohorts' tables were not run. The shrinkage scales with p_red / n, so a cohort with fewer donors at the same covariate set is expected to be more liberal, not less.
  • Additive-linear covariate effects. z enters the features additively along one fixed direction and the trajectory model linearly.
  • One confounded covariate beside five independent ones. The five noise covariates are i.i.d. normals, uncorrelated with one another and with the design, unlike the case study's age, education, PMI, RIN and library sizes. The column-count mechanism does not depend on their joint distribution, but its size at the real covariates is inferred.
  • Structural-analogue blocks. These are InterSIM-calibrated methylation and expression analogues (498 measured features), not the case study's TMM log2-CPM blocks of 5,000 features each.

And those of the diagnosis itself:

  • latent_stage_rank2 confounds two things. It removes the CV rank's tail and the per-training-set nuisance coefficients together. Under residualized_basis neither is the cause of the angle excess, but the arm cannot say which of them carried the parent's shape excess. The rank table places that excess in the tail.
  • The oracle's absolute rates. The oracle arms are a valid within-family reference for the column contrast C1, not a size-α baseline for angle (§5).
  • No new replicates. The diagnosis reuses the parent's 500 replicates per strength, so the parent's own excess (two rejections over the bound) is explained rather than re-measured. The R = 1,000 replication was not needed under this verdict and stays deferred.
  • The correction is minimal. The uniform κ restores the unbiased residual variance but not the leverage structure, and C4's residual net of 11 (p = 0.156) leaves room for that. The follow-up change measures both corrections' size and power.
  • No package change. Nothing under src/motco/ changed: the correction is computed in the script from the public RRPP, and MOTCO stays at 0.12.0. The case study's pin is untouched.
  • What stays on ing. The 45,000-row diagnosis_pvalues.csv (2.5 MB per run), merged.jsonl and records/ stay there, named with their sha256 in each PROVENANCE.txt. case_study_diagnosis.py merge regenerates every committed table from records/.

docs.title: Case-study configuration Type I check — 2026-10-29
docs.text:
Paper-grade size check of the real-data analysis (motco analyze, MOTCO 0.12.0) at the SEA-AD case study's configuration — the rank floor of 2, six numeric covariate design columns, a weak stage signal and a nuisance covariate the covariate-blind basis follows (openspec/changes/case-study-configuration-type-i/, spec case-study-configuration-validation). It is the measurement the case-study section cites for its primary analysis and for its stage latent-adjusted sensitivity arm. Every number below is read from results/case-study-type-i-2026-10-29/ (delta0.1/ and delta0.05/: case_study_type_i_decision.json, case_study_type_i_rates.csv, case_study_type_i_replicates.csv, case_study_type_i_pvalues.csv, merge.json, settings.json, PROVENANCE.txt; case_study_type_i_overall_decision.json; calibration/calibration.json; smoke-delta0.1-sz10/, smoke-delta0.05-sz10/; merged.jsonl and records/ stay on ing as each PROVENANCE.txt records). Rates are rejection rates at p ≤ 0.05 over the R = 500 available replicates at 999 permutations; the bound is the one-sided α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/R) = 0.0695, i.e. at most 34 rejections in 500.

Run: two 50-shard SLURM arrays on ing (partition 512x1024, n11 excluded) from the clean worktree of feat/case-study-configuration-type-i at ffd6249 (tree hash ececcb83…, identical to the workstation): job 930122 for δ = 0.1 (50 / 50 tasks completed, 15.2 core-hours) and job 930172 for δ = 0.05, whose stalled and slow shards were moved twice (jobs 930224 and 930266; 35.4 recorded core-hours, about 15 of them productive). 1,000 units per strength (the zero-effect anchor and the translation control at e = 1.0 × 500 replicates), three analyses per unit, 6,000 analyses in all, 0 arm failures, every latent_stage arm available.

Decision: diagnose_configuration_excess at δ = 0.1 and primary_validated at δ = 0.05, hence diagnose_configuration_excess under the predeclared conjunction (case_study_type_i_overall_decision.json). The adjusted arm — the case study's primary — holds the bound for every statistic at both controls at δ = 0.05 and for five of six at δ = 0.1, exceeding it on the translation control's delta by two rejections (36 / 500 = 0.072 against 0.0695). The latent_stage arm — the case study's sensitivity arm and the predeclared fallback — exceeds the bound at the anchor on angle (0.090 / 0.084) and shape (0.092 / 0.078) at both strengths, so it is not admissible either.

In one paragraph. At the Phase 6 SEA-AD design with the per-omic stage effect weakened to δ = 0.1 and 0.05 and a numeric covariate z confounded with group, stage and their interaction injected at s_z = 10 — calibrated so that the covariate-adjusted analysis reads a held-out CV stage AUROC of 0.70 / 0.69 (the cohorts read 0.64–0.70) and the covariate-blind basis spends its first component on z (median |Spearman| 0.92; the real basis reads 0.84) — each of 1,000 units per strength was analysed three times on the same data, CV folds and permutation draws at the rank floor of 2 with the net-displacement estimator: with z and five pure-noise covariates in the trajectory model (adjusted), with no covariates (unadjusted) and with the six covariates under the stage latent adjustment (latent_stage). The unadjusted arm confirms that the construction confounds (anchor delta 0.672 / 0.686, shape 0.252 / 0.222). The adjusted model removes almost all of it: anchor delta 0.068 / 0.064, angle 0.048 / 0.048, shape 0.056 / 0.054, translation delta 0.072 / 0.060, angle 0.042 / 0.044, shape 0.068 / 0.068. Its delta sits at or just above the bound in every reading (0.066 pooled over the four control readings, 34–36 rejections where 34 are allowed) and its shape at the bound at translation; angle is comfortably under it but its RRPP null is wide (median q95 109–113°). The stage latent adjustment removes the nuisance axis from the basis (|ρ| 0.08) at the price of a heavier rank tail (up to 11), a lower AUROC (0.66 / 0.62) and anchor angle and shape rates of 0.078–0.092. Under the rule written before the run, the case study's primary is withheld pending diagnosis of a small delta inflation at six design columns and n = 80, and its stage sensitivity arm's angle and shape rejections are not interpretable at this configuration.

docs.title: 1. Construction and calibration
docs.text:
The check composes two validated constructions by import (scripts/case_study_type_i_check.py, design D1):

  • The D10 covariate construction (scripts/covariate_type_i_check.py, covariate Type I report): a null semi-synthetic dataset at the Phase 6 small-n design (three stages, group_stage_sizes = [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]], n = 80, methylation + expression, joint magnitude), a numeric covariate z = 0.5·g + 1·s + 2·g·s + ε and its effect injected into every feature along a fixed direction over 20 % of the joint features, X_f += s_z·sd_f·w_f·z, on the M-value scale. The three-level categorical covariate D10 draws stays in the RNG stream but is neither declared nor injected (s_c = 0): the case study enters six numerics and no factor, and without a factor no CV training set can lose a level (design D2).
  • The weakened stage signal of the rank-floor check (report): one --delta applied to delta_methyl, delta_expr and delta_protein, with p_dmp at the Phase 6 value 0.1 so the translation surgery keeps its pool headroom.

Beside z the check declares five pure-noise covariates x1–x5 (i.i.d. N(0, 1) from their own seed, never injected), so the trajectory model carries six numeric design columns, as the case study's does. Cells are the zero-effect anchor and the translation negative control at e = 1.0 (design D4). Seeds depend on the replicate index only, so both cells and all three arms of a replicate share the baseline draw, the covariate values and the RRPP seed; the adjusted and unadjusted latent spaces are asserted identical per unit (they share the covariate-blind basis), so an adjusted excess is attributable to the trajectory model and an unadjusted excess to confounding. All three arms run at min_components=2, the harness CV knobs (3 × 4 folds, 5 repeats, max_components 20, random_state 1203), 999 permutations and the net-displacement estimator.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
Three criteria were fixed before any run (design D3): the adjusted arm's mean held-out CV AUROC inside [0.60, 0.75] (the SEA-AD cohorts read 0.636–0.697); the unadjusted arm's median first-component |Spearman ρ| with z at least 0.8 (the real basis reads 0.84); and the unadjusted arm rejecting above α on at least one statistic at the anchor, so the gate is not vacuous. The knobs were δ and s_z. Six iterations (calibration/calibration.json; R = 20, 99 permutations, base seed 2026):

# δ s_z adjusted mean AUROC unadjusted median |ρ| unadjusted anchor rates (delta / angle / shape) met 1 0.10 3 0.691 0.565 0.55 / 0.05 / 0.30 no (|ρ|) 2 0.15 3 0.744 0.571 0.55 / 0.05 / 0.35 no (|ρ|) 3 0.10 10 0.699 0.876 0.55 / 0.10 / 0.25 yes 4 0.10 20 0.699 0.918 0.65 / 0.10 / 0.30 yes 5 0.05 10 0.692 0.873 0.60 / 0.05 / 0.25 yes 6 0.05 20 0.693 0.917 0.65 / 0.10 / 0.25 yes

At D10's s_z = 3 the basis does not follow z (median |ρ| 0.57, which is the regime of the 2026-10-16 check). At s_z ≥ 10 it does, and the realized stage AUROC is then set by the injected covariate rather than by δ — 0.69–0.70 at both δ = 0.05 and 0.10 — because z is confounded with stage. The criteria did not conflict. The settled strengths are s_z = 10 (the smallest injection meeting the threshold, so the nuisance is the case study's rather than a harsher one) at δ = 0.10 and δ = 0.05, the rank-floor check's pair; the user approved two paper-grade runs with the decision as their conjunction.

Realized at paper grade (anchor, R = 500): adjusted mean AUROC 0.702 (q05 0.641, q95 0.771) at δ = 0.1 and 0.688 (0.628, 0.756) at δ = 0.05; unadjusted median |ρ| 0.917 (q05 0.697, q95 0.985) and 0.918 (0.693, 0.985); unadjusted anchor rates delta 0.672 / 0.686, angle 0.104 / 0.098, shape 0.252 / 0.222. All three criteria hold in both runs (calibration.met: true in each decision file).

docs.title: Smoke profiles
docs.text: smoke-delta0.1-sz10/ and smoke-delta0.05-sz10/ (R = 20, 99 permutations, both cells, three arms): 40 / 40 units at each strength, 0 arm failures, the latent_stage arm available in every unit. Both smoke decisions were primary_validated; the latent_stage arm's anchor shape rate of 0.35 (7 / 20) at both strengths was recorded in the design as the warning sign to carry into the paper-grade run, and the paper-grade run confirmed an excess on shape (0.092 / 0.078) and on angle (0.090 / 0.084) at R = 500. One unit took 57 s locally at 999 permutations and 47–55 s on an ing EPYC core.

docs.title: 3. What the arms show
docs.text:
The construction confounds, and the trajectory model removes almost all of it. The unadjusted arm rejects delta in two thirds of the null units and shape in a quarter; the adjusted arm, on the identical latent scores (asserted per unit), brings delta to 0.060–0.072, shape to 0.054–0.068 and angle to 0.042–0.048. The covariate Type I check of 2026-10-16 measured the same model at three design columns (z plus the two indicator columns of a three-level factor), a saturated stage signal (AUROC 1.000), the unfloored rank rule and a nuisance the basis did not follow (|ρ| 0.64): adjusted delta 0.040, angle 0.062, shape 0.034. Here, at six columns, the case study's AUROC and a basis that follows the nuisance, delta reads 0.064–0.072 in every control reading, at or above the 34-rejection limit, and shape reads 0.068 at translation in both runs; angle is lower than in 2026-10-16. The excess that trips the rule — two rejections on one control at one strength — is one Monte Carlo SE wide, but the pooled delta of 0.066 over 2,000 units, every reading above α, is what the diagnosis should take as its starting point: a small delta inflation of the covariate-adjusted model at six design columns and n = 80, which the three-column check did not show.

The adjusted arm's angle null is wide. The median q95 of the RRPP angle null is 109° (δ = 0.1) and 113° (δ = 0.05) in the adjusted arm against 36° in the unadjusted arm on the same basis and 57–59° in the latent_stage arm (case_study_type_i_replicates.csv, angle_null_q95). With six covariates in the reduced model the permuted residuals carry little stage structure, so the permuted net displacements point almost anywhere; angle is size-controlled at this configuration but, as the design-guidance δ arm found at δ ≤ 0.1, it has no power to spend.

The stage latent adjustment is inadmissible at this configuration. It does what it is built to do — the first component's |ρ| with z falls from 0.92 to 0.08 — and its translation control holds (0.048–0.064), but at the anchor it rejects angle 0.090 / 0.084 and shape 0.092 / 0.078, about three Monte Carlo SE above α in each of the four readings. Beside it, the basis changes: the held-out AUROC falls to 0.659 / 0.622 (from 0.702 / 0.688), the CV rank's tail lengthens (rank ≥ 4 in 91 / 500 and 61 / 500 anchor units against 6 / 500 and 1 / 500 in the adjusted arm; maximum 11), and the smallest training-set residual df inside the CV is 31 (cv_min_training_df; full-sample residual_df 71: n − 1 − 2 stage indicators − 6 covariates). The 2026-10-20 latent-adjustment check measured the same conditioning at the unfloored rule, eight covariates including a factor and a saturated stage signal (δ = 2.0): stage held delta 0.031, angle 0.067, shape 0.058 against 0.0706, while its covariate-blind baseline arm rejected shape at 0.078. The excess here therefore belongs to the weak-signal, floor-2, six-numeric regime, not to the conditioning as such; the per-training-set residualization at 31 residual df and the rank tail are the two things to look at first.

Rank and signal. The adjusted arm selects rank 2 in 366 / 500 (δ = 0.1) and 407 / 500 (δ = 0.05) anchor units and rank 3 in most of the rest; no unit selected rank 1 (the floor binds). The rank-floor check at the same strengths without covariates measured the floor-2 arm's anchor at delta 0.044 / 0.042, angle 0.060 / 0.054 and shape 0.038 / 0.036 (δ = 0.1 / 0.05), so the covariate-adjusted model, not the floor, carries the delta and shape readings here.

docs.title: 4. Decision, consequence and what to diagnose
docs.text:
Decision, read verbatim from results/case-study-type-i-2026-10-29/case_study_type_i_overall_decision.json: "decision": "diagnose_configuration_excess", "admissible": [], runs delta0.1 → diagnose_configuration_excess and delta0.05 → primary_validated. The rule, written before the run (proposal, design D5): primary_validated when the adjusted arm holds every statistic at both controls in every run; otherwise adopt_latent_stage when the latent_stage arm does; otherwise diagnose_configuration_excess. The adjusted arm fails the conjunction on one reading (translation delta at δ = 0.1, 36 / 500) and the latent_stage arm fails on four (anchor angle and shape at both strengths).

Consequence for the case study. Under diagnose_configuration_excess the primary analysis of sead_sexdiff (covariates in the trajectory model, floor 2, net displacement, 999 permutations) is withheld pending diagnosis: it does not rest on a validated size at its configuration, and it cannot move to the stage latent adjustment, which is not admissible here either. Concretely for the readers of its results, until the diagnosis is done: the primary's delta p-values should be read against a realized size of about 0.066 rather than 0.05 (a p-value near 0.05 is not a rejection at the nominal level; a p-value well below it is unaffected in kind); its angle and shape p-values are size-controlled in this check (0.042–0.068), with angle's null so wide that a non-rejection is uninformative; and the stage sensitivity arm's angle and shape rejections are not interpretable at this configuration. Nothing in sead_sexdiff changes under this report; the diagnosis is its own change there and here.

What to diagnose (named by the rule; none of it is done here):

  1. The adjusted arm's delta (0.060–0.072, pooled 0.066). Candidates, in the order they should be excluded: the degrees-of-freedom cost of six columns at n = 80 (the same seeds and construction at one, three and six noise columns, which isolates the column count from the confounding); the LS-mean reference row and the RRPP reduced model under covariates at these cell sizes (the design's reference_row is the pooled mean; the reduced model keeps the covariates); and the bound itself at R = 500 (a replication at R = 1,000 on the same seed family would halve the SE, at about 30 core-hours per strength).
  2. The latent_stage arm's anchor angle and shape (0.078–0.092). Candidates: the per-training-set nuisance coefficients at cv_min_training_df 31 (the residualized CV rank's tail reaches 11, and angle/shape at rank ≥ 4 should be tabulated against rank 2–3); and the interaction of the residualized basis with the rank floor, which the 2026-10-20 check never measured (it ran at floor 1).

docs.title: 5. Limitations and scope
docs.text:
Four limitations the spec requires the report to carry, then the scope:

  • Astrocyte primary cohort sizes only. The check uses the astrocyte cohort_30 cell sizes [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]] (n = 80) that every Phase 6 check uses; the microglia cohort (n = 76) and the other cohorts' tables were not run, and size at their cell sizes is inferred, not measured.
  • Additive-linear covariate effects. z enters the features additively along one fixed direction and the trajectory model linearly; non-linear or interaction effects of real covariates on the features are outside the construction.
  • One confounded covariate beside five independent ones. The confounding rests on z alone; the five noise covariates are i.i.d. normals, uncorrelated with one another and with the design, unlike age, education, PMI, RIN and library sizes. The configuration matched is the column count, the floor and the nuisance regime, not the covariates' joint distribution (design D2 records the alternatives considered).
  • Structural-analogue blocks. The blocks are InterSIM-calibrated methylation and expression analogues (498 measured features), not the case study's TMM log2-CPM blocks of 5,000 features each; the per-omic δ is a generator strength, and the regime is matched on the realized AUROC and |ρ|, not on the feature space.

Scope:

  • No power is claimed at this configuration (the design-guidance pilot's δ arm measured none at δ ≤ 0.1), and the group_stage conditioning, a floor-1 arm and the microglia sizes were not run.
  • No change under src/motco/: every record field the check reads exists in 0.12.0, so the release and the case study's pin are untouched (design D9).
  • The two strengths are independent runs with their own decision files; the conjunction rule and the number of runs were fixed with the user after calibration and before submission (design D3 record). The δ = 0.05 run's shards were moved twice between nodes (PROVENANCE.txt); shards are resumable and a unit recorded in any shard file is never re-run, so the move changes which node computed a unit and nothing else.
  • The replicate-level tables (case_study_type_i_replicates.csv, case_study_type_i_pvalues.csv) are committed for both runs; merged.jsonl and records/ stay on ing under the worktree named in each PROVENANCE.txt, and case_study_type_i_check.py merge regenerates every table from records/.

docs.title: Corrected-permutation check — 2026-10-30
docs.text:
This report validates the residual-corrected RRPP null that MOTCO 0.13.0 offers as the opt-in residual_correction (openspec change residual-df-corrected-permutation, spec corrected-permutation-validation). It is the follow-up that the case-study configuration diagnosis named with its residual_df_shrinkage verdict, and roadmap item 8.

Every number below is read from results/corrected-permutation-2026-10-30/: - corrected_permutation_decision.json, size_readings.csv, decide.json; - per run in type-i-astrocyte-delta0.1/, type-i-astrocyte-delta0.05/, type-i-microglia-delta0.1/, type-i-microglia-delta0.05/ and power/: corrected_permutation_rates.csv, merge.json, settings.json and PROVENANCE.txt, plus corrected_permutation_pvalues.csv for the Type I runs and corrected_permutation_contrasts.csv for the power run; - the raw accounting sacct.txt, finish_git.txt and finish_sha256.txt; - the smoke records smoke-*/ and smoke-decision/.

records/ and the power run's 2.6 MB corrected_permutation_pvalues.csv stay on ing; each PROVENANCE.txt names them with their sha256. Rates are rejection rates at p ≤ 0.05 over R = 500 replicates at 999 permutations.

Run. - Five SLURM arrays on ing (partition 512x1024, n11 excluded), from the clean worktree of feat/residual-df-corrected-permutation at a2f1a1f. Its git tree 4d8a22fb… equals the workstation's, and the change's tests passed there. - Jobs 930470, 930520, 930570 and 930620 ran the four Type I runs (50 shards each) and job 930670 the power run (140 shards). All 340 tasks ended COMPLETED 0:0, between 14:00Z and 14:59Z on 2026-10-30. - 1,000 units per Type I run and 7,000 for power, each analysed three times (no correction, df, leverage). There were 0 arm failures, and no unit's arms disagreed on latent scores, rank or statistics. - 164.1 elapsed core-hours (planned 160); the units' own timers sum to 123.1 h. - The afterany job 930817 fast-forwarded the worktree to ea9bacc, which adds only the decision code's clustered sensitivity (finish_git.txt: nothing changed under src/ or in the construction scripts). It then ran merge per run and decide. The five settings hashes in the decision file equal those of the five settings.json files.

Verdict: adopt_df, read verbatim from corrected_permutation_decision.json ("indicative": false). - "holds": {"df": true, "leverage": true}, and "failing" is empty for both corrections. - The tie-break found no significant paired difference between them on any target pair, so the rule chose df. - "uncorrected_excess_reproduced": false. The fresh seed family did not reproduce the uncorrected delta excess; the uncorrected arm failed on pooled shape and on one angle reading instead.

In one paragraph. - The design. The case study's configuration was rebuilt on a seed family no committed check uses: - six covariate columns, the rank floor of 2, net displacement and the weak stage signal; - both case-study cohort tables at δ = 0.1 and 0.05, with the anchor and translation controls; - one power run at the Phase 6 stage effect.

Every unit ran analyze_trajectories three times on the same data, latent basis and RRPP seed, under no correction, df and leverage. - Size. Both corrections hold every reading and every pooled rate. df reads 0.029–0.058 pooled per table and statistic against 0.0597, and at most 32 / 500 per reading against 39 / 500. - The uncorrected null. It is liberal on pooled shape in both tables (0.0685 and 0.0675) and on the power design's anchor angle (43 / 500), but not on delta (0.046 and 0.045). - Cost. The correction costs 0.014–0.054 of power on the target statistics. On angle and shape (0.024–0.034) that is of the order of the uncorrected arm's own excess at the controls. - leverage. It is indistinguishable from df: at most 3 discordant units in either direction on any target. - Consequence. sead_sexdiff re-issues both cell types' primaries with --residual-correction df, pinned to 0.13.0, in its own change. MOTCO documents df as validated at this configuration and keeps it opt-in.

docs.title: 1. Construction
docs.text:
scripts/corrected_permutation_check.py (design D5–D7) builds every unit with the parent check's code (case_study_type_i_check.build_unit) and settings, with four overrides: base seed 2031, the named cohort table, the profile's δ, and the profile's cells.

Fixed across runs (each run's settings.json): - the Phase 6 replicate: three stages, methylation + expression, joint magnitude and p_dmp 0.1; - the confounded covariate z = 0.5·g + 1·s + 2·g·s + ε, injected at s_z = 10 into a fifth of the features along a fixed direction; - five i.i.d. N(0, 1) noise covariates x1–x5, so the trajectory model declares six covariate columns and p_red = 10; - the rank floor of 2, net displacement, the harness CV knobs, 500 replicates and 999 permutations.

Fresh family (design D7). Base seed 2031 is used by no committed check. Every seed derives from it and the replicate index, including the injection direction, the covariates, the generator and RRPP. The diagnosis chose the remedy on the parent's base seed 2026, so a test on those replicates would have been circular.

Runs.

The two tables are the cohort_30 tables of the case study's result.json files (sha256 recorded in each settings.json). The two controls of a replicate, and the power run's 14 cells, share that replicate's seeds.

Arms. Each unit calls analyze_trajectories with identical parameters except residual_correction ∈ {None, "df", "leverage"}. The unit then asserts that the three latent-score arrays, the selected ranks and the statistics are exactly equal. A difference would raise and fail the shard; none occurred.

Calibration (descriptive, from the uncorrected arm at the anchor; calibration in the decision file):

The construction was calibrated on the astrocyte table and not re-tuned. The microglia table also reads inside the band.

Rule (design D8; rule in the decision file). A correction holds size when both tiers hold: - pooled, per cohort table × statistic over the table's four Type I readings: rate ≤ α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/2000) = 0.0597, i.e. at most 119 / 2,000; - per reading, over the four Type I runs' two controls and the power run's two controls, each for three statistics (30 readings): rate ≤ α + 3·√(α(1 − α)/500) = 0.0792, i.e. at most 39 / 500.

The uncorrected arm goes through the same rule descriptively. A replicate-clustered pooled sensitivity was added on 2026-10-30, before any paper-grade result. It is descriptive and never changes the verdict (design, "Smoke and shard plan").

Smoke (smoke-*, R = 20 × 99 permutations). Every unit completed with 0 failures, and the indicative verdict was no_correction_holds. The only failing entries were the pooled shape readings, 9–10 / 80, in every arm including the uncorrected one; at R = 20 that was read as noise. At R = 500 the corrected arms hold shape and the uncorrected arm does not (§2).
