  • The design effects are 1.75–2.04, so the four readings of a table carry about 980–1,140 independent replicates' worth of information, not 2,000. The smoke had predicted that (design, "Smoke and shard plan").
  • The verdict does not depend on it. "clustered_sensitivity_holds" is {"none": false, "df": true, "leverage": true}, the same split as the predeclared rule.

docs.title: 3. The uncorrected null
docs.text:
uncorrected_excess_reproduced: false. The flag asks whether the uncorrected pooled delta exceeds 0.0597 in either table. It reads 0.046 (astrocyte) and 0.045 (microglia). On the parent's family the same model read 0.066 pooled (z_noise5 in the diagnosis, §2).

As predeclared (design, Risks), the correction's size verdict stands either way, and no rule was re-tuned. The evidence that column count drives the delta excess remains the diagnosis's within-family contrast C2 (p = 0.015). This check runs every arm at the same six covariates, so it has no column contrast and cannot re-test that mechanism.

The uncorrected null is still liberal at this configuration, on other statistics. The descriptive uncorrected block lists three failing entries: - pooled shape 0.0685 (astrocyte) and 0.0675 (microglia) against 0.0597. They also fail the clustered sensitivity. The parent family read 0.0615 for the same model (diagnosis, §2). - power anchor angle, 43 / 500 = 0.086 against 39 / 500, at the Phase 6 stage effect.

Every corrected arm holds all three: df reads shape 0.058 and 0.052 pooled and power anchor angle 32 / 500. So the narrowed Freedman–Lane null shows up on different statistics in different seed families and designs: - delta on the parent family; - shape on this family's Type I runs; - angle at this family's strong-signal anchor.

The correction removes the excess in each case, because it widens the null for every statistic at once.

docs.title: 4. Power cost
docs.text:
From power/corrected_permutation_rates.csv: rejection rates on each mode's target statistic, as none / df / leverage, by effect.

mode / statistic effect 1 effect 2 effect 3 effect 4 magnitude / delta 0.02: 0.082 / 0.056 / 0.056 0.05: 0.238 / 0.19 / 0.192 0.1: 0.536 / 0.482 / 0.478 0.25: 0.94 / 0.926 / 0.928 orientation / angle 0.25: 0.182 / 0.154 / 0.154 0.5: 0.29 / 0.256 / 0.26 0.75: 0.436 / 0.412 / 0.412 1.0: 0.732 / 0.706 / 0.706 shape / shape 0.25: 0.1 / 0.074 / 0.074 0.5: 0.148 / 0.118 / 0.116 0.75: 0.208 / 0.182 / 0.182 1.0: 0.296 / 0.264 / 0.262

Pooled over each mode's four effects (2,000 paired readings in 500 replicate clusters; power/corrected_permutation_contrasts.csv, scope mode, role descriptive). "None only" counts the readings the uncorrected arm rejects and the correction does not, and p is the clustered one-sided sign-flip p-value for that direction. Targets are in bold.

mode statistic none df none only p leverage none only p magnitude delta 0.449 0.4135 71 8.5e-22 0.4135 71 8.5e-22 magnitude angle 0.0625 0.046 33 4.8e-07 0.0465 32 9.5e-07 magnitude shape 0.044 0.0285 31 1.9e-06 0.0285 31 3.8e-06 orientation delta 0.2965 0.256 81 8.3e-25 0.2575 78 6.6e-24 orientation angle 0.41 0.382 56 4.4e-16 0.383 54 8.9e-16 orientation shape 0.4725 0.441 63 2.2e-19 0.4425 60 1.7e-18 shape delta 0.273 0.232 82 3.3e-24 0.231 84 8.3e-25 shape angle 0.056 0.0435 25 3.0e-08 0.0435 25 3.0e-08 shape shape 0.188 0.1595 57 5.6e-17 0.1585 59 1.4e-17
  • The cost is one-directional. No reading in any cell is rejected by a correction and not by the uncorrected arm (every df-only and leverage-only count in the contrast file is 0). That is expected: the observed statistics are identical, and only the null widens.
  • angle and shape.
  • The orientation angle power falls by 0.024–0.034 per effect, from 0.732 to 0.706 at e = 1.0.
  • The shape shape power falls by 0.026–0.032, from 0.296 to 0.264 at e = 1.0.
  • Off-target angle and shape fall too, towards or below α: magnitude angle 0.0625 → 0.046 and magnitude shape 0.044 → 0.0285.
  • delta. The magnitude delta power falls by 0.026, 0.048, 0.054 and 0.014 at e = 0.02, 0.05, 0.1 and 0.25. That is the largest absolute cost, in the rising part of the power curve.
  • The comparison arm is itself liberal here. At the power run's controls the uncorrected arm rejects more than df by 0.012 / 0.022 / 0.018 (anchor delta / angle / shape) and 0.016 / 0.012 / 0.014 (translation). The angle and shape costs above are of that order. A rate difference against an arm whose null is too narrow therefore overstates the power a size-valid test gives up. It is reported as measured, against no correction, as the spec requires.

The diagnosis saw the same direction at the null on the parent family: z_noise5_corrected read angle 0.042 and shape 0.0465, against 0.0455 and 0.0615 uncorrected.

docs.title: 5. Tie-break
docs.text:
leverage against df on the power run's target pairs, pooled over each mode's four effects (decision file tie_break; contrast file role tie_break):

target leverage rejections df rejections leverage only df only p (gain) p (loss) magnitude / delta 827 827 3 3 0.656 0.656 orientation / angle 766 764 2 0 0.25 1.0 shape / shape 317 319 1 3 0.938 0.313

No gain or loss reaches p ≤ 0.05, so "choice": "df" (design D9). The two corrections disagree on at most 3 of 2,000 readings in either direction on any target, and their size readings differ by at most 3 / 500 per reading and 3 / 2,000 pooled.

The per-sample multipliers do differ from κ; each analysis's range is in its record's measurement.residual_correction, kept in records/. Even so, at these tables the two corrections almost never reach different rejection decisions.

docs.title: 6. Verdict and consequences
docs.text:
Read verbatim from corrected_permutation_decision.json:

{"verdict": "adopt_df", "indicative": false, "holds": {"df": true, "leverage": true},
 "failing": {"df": [], "leverage": []}, "uncorrected_excess_reproduced": false}

Consequence (the decision file's consequence): "sead_sexdiff re-issues both cell types' primaries with --residual-correction df, pinned to the release that contains it (0.13.0), in its own change; MOTCO documents df as validated at this configuration and keeps it opt-in".

For sead_sexdiff. - The covariate-adjusted primary, withheld since the case-study Type I check, is re-issued for both cell types with --residual-correction df under MOTCO 0.13.0, in its own change. - Under df its delta, angle and shape p-values are size-controlled at this configuration: pooled 0.029–0.058 per table and statistic, at most 32 / 500 per reading. - delta is conservative under df here (0.029 and 0.031 pooled). A delta non-rejection therefore stays weak evidence, as before. - The earlier caveats stand: the angle null is too wide to inform a non-rejection, and the CV-selected rank is reported beside any angle result. - The stage latent-adjusted arm is not touched by this check and stays inadmissible at this configuration (diagnosis, residualized_basis).

For MOTCO. - residual_correction="df" (--residual-correction df) is documented as validated at the case study's configuration. It stays opt-in, and without it every output equals 0.12.0's. - leverage holds size too, and it is kept. It is not the validated choice, because it earned no paired advantage. - Whether df should become the analysis default is a separate, later change. A default flip changes every covariate-adjusted output and needs its own fixture re-issue (tasks, "Workflow follow-up").

docs.title: 7. Limitations and scope
docs.text:
• cohort_50 tables not run. The case study's sensitivity tables, for example microglia cohort_50 at n = 63 with κ = 1.090, were not run. The shrinkage grows with p_red / n, so the uncorrected null is expected to be more liberal there and the correction to matter more. The correction's size there is inferred, not measured.
  • Additive-linear covariates. z enters the features additively along one fixed direction, and the trajectory model linearly. The five noise covariates are i.i.d. normals, unlike the case study's age, education, PMI, RIN and library sizes. The correction depends on n and the reduced rank only, but its size at the real covariates is inferred.
  • Structural-analogue blocks. The blocks are InterSIM-calibrated methylation and expression analogues (498 measured features), not the case study's TMM log2-CPM blocks of 5,000 features each.
  • Calibration on the astrocyte table only. δ and s_z were calibrated on the astrocyte table by the parent check and not re-tuned. The microglia runs read inside the band (§1), so this did not bite, but it was not designed for.
  • Power on one table and one strength. The power run uses the astrocyte table at δ = 2.0, where the statistics have power. The weak-signal runs hold only null controls, so the cost at the case study's stage signal is not measured.
  • The delta excess was not replicated. The mechanism rests on the diagnosis's C2 (§3). The uncorrected arm's pooled delta on this family is at α, which means that df is conservative for delta here.
  • What stays on ing. records/ (4.0 MB per Type I run, 26 MB for power) and the power run's 63,000-row corrected_permutation_pvalues.csv (2.6 MB) stay there, under /home1/tgonza/MOTCO/results/corrected-permutation-2026-10-30/ with the SLURM logs. They were moved there from the run's worktree on 2026-10-31, and their digests were rechecked. Each PROVENANCE.txt names them with their sha256. corrected_permutation_check.py merge regenerates every committed table from records/.

docs.title: Covariate-adjustment Type I check — 2026-10-16
docs.text:
Paper-grade size check of covariate-adjusted motco analyze at the Phase 6 SEA-AD design (openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-16-covariate-adjusted-trajectories/, spec covariate-adjustment-type-i). It is the gate the case study must pass before it reports covariate-adjusted trajectory results. Every number below is read from results/covariate-type-i-2026-10-16/ (covariate_type_i_decision.json, covariate_type_i_rates.csv, covariate_type_i_pvalues.csv, merged.jsonl). Rates are rejection rates at p ≤ 0.05 over 500 replicates × 999 permutations (Monte Carlo SE about 0.0097 at 0.05).

Run: 180 replicates on the workstation, then the remaining 320 on ing as SLURM array 921167 (60 shards, all COMPLETED). The code is c3ee13a plus this change's working tree, and the script and analysis.py hashes in PROVENANCE.txt were verified identical on both machines. Decision: covariates_validated.

In one paragraph. On null datasets at the SEA-AD MTG design, a numeric and a categorical covariate were made to depend on group, stage and their interaction, and their effect was injected into the features. Without adjustment the analysis rejects too often: shape at 0.364, delta at 0.098 and angle at 0.096. With both covariates declared, all three statistics hold the predeclared bound 0.05 + 2·√(0.05·0.95/500) = 0.0695: delta 0.040, angle 0.062 and shape 0.034. The two arms share every latent space (asserted per replicate), so the difference comes entirely from the trajectory model. The case study may report covariate-adjusted results under the conditions in §5.

docs.title: 1. Construction
docs.text:
• Data. generate_semisynthetic_trajectory at the phase6_small_n settings: three stages, group_stage_sizes = [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]], p_dmp = 0.1, ρ = 0, joint magnitude, group_effect_size = 0 (null). Only the methylation (367 CpGs, converted to M-values) and expression (131 genes) blocks are measured; both are analysed with the identity transform. Base seed 2026. Generator, covariate and RRPP seeds are derived per replicate.
  • Covariates. With g the group indicator and s the stage index (0–2):
  • numeric z = a_g·g + a_s·s + a_gs·g·s + ε, with ε ~ N(0, 1);
  • categorical: three levels from a multinomial logit with level logits k·c·η (k = 0, 1, 2) on the same linear predictor η.
  • Values: a_g = 0.5, a_s = 1, a_gs = 2 and c = 0.5.
  • Across replicates, the numeric covariate's group × stage interaction contrast (z̄_B,2 − z̄_B,0) − (z̄_A,2 − z̄_A,0) has mean 3.98 (SD 0.58). The covariates therefore bend the groups' trajectories differently, not only shift them.
  • Injection. X_f += s_z·sd_f·w_f·z + s_c·sd_f·Σ_k u_{k,f}·1[cat = k].
  • sd_f is the feature's pooled SD on the analysed scale.
  • w and the u_k are unit directions, each on a random 20 % of the 498 joint features, drawn once from the base seed.
  • Strengths: s_z = 3 and s_c = 2.
  • Arms. Each replicate is analysed twice with analyze_trajectories, using its defaults: net displacement, CV rank with the harness knobs, and the same RRPP seed.
  • adjusted: covariate_cols = ["z", "category"], category categorical. The design columns are z, category[c1] and category[c2].
  • unadjusted: no covariates.
  • The latent scores and selected rank were identical in both arms for all 500 replicates. CV selected rank 2 in 264 replicates and rank 3 in 236.
  • Rule. Per statistic, the adjusted rate over the R available replicates must be ≤ α + k·√(α(1 − α)/R), with α = 0.05 and k = 2. covariates_validated requires all three statistics to hold. The unadjusted arm is reported only and does not enter the decision.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
The design's first strengths (a_s = 0.5, a_gs = 0.75, s_z = 0.5, s_c = 0.3) did not confound: in the R = 20 smoke run, the unadjusted arm rejected at about α, which would have made the gate vacuous.

Raising s_z alone, even to 30, did not help. The injection carries z's within-cell noise along w in the same proportion as its cell-mean pattern, so the RRPP null widens together with the signal. The confounding signal-to-noise is a_gs relative to the covariate's noise SD.

The calibrated values above were chosen on probe replicates and confirmed by the smoke profile (R = 20, 99 permutations): unadjusted shape 0.45. The categorical logit scale keeps the factor mixed within cells, so complete-cell alignment cannot trip the full-rank guard. All values are recorded in the decision file.

docs.title: 2. Rates against the bound
docs.text:
From covariate_type_i_rates.csv. Rate (MC SE); R = 500 for every statistic, no failed replicate; bound 0.0695.

statistic adjusted verdict unadjusted (descriptive) delta 0.040 (0.0088) holds 0.098 (0.0133) angle 0.062 (0.0108) holds 0.096 (0.0132) shape 0.034 (0.0081) holds 0.364 (0.0215)

Stability. Split into five consecutive blocks of 100 replicates, the adjusted rates are:

  • delta: 0.07, 0.04, 0.05, 0.00, 0.04;
  • angle: 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.11, 0.05;
  • shape: 0.06, 0.02, 0.03, 0.02, 0.04.

The angle rate of 0.062 comes from one block at 0.11; the other four blocks sit at 0.05. At p < 0.05 instead of p ≤ 0.05, the convention of the earlier Type I reports, the rates are 0.040, 0.060 and 0.034. The decision is the same.

Against the no-covariate anchor. The parent Phase 6 study's pls_cv × net_displacement anchor (no covariates, independent seeds; net-displacement Type I report) had delta 0.026, angle 0.050 and shape 0.020. The adjusted arm here is 0.01–0.015 higher on each statistic but within the bound. That is plausible for a model with three more columns at n = 80, where RRPP is exact only asymptotically. It is recorded here and not judged by the rule.

docs.title: 3. What the unadjusted arm shows
docs.text: The construction confounds, mostly through shape: an interaction between the covariate and stage bends one group's path relative to the other's. With 36 % false shape rejections, an unadjusted SEA-AD shape result under comparable confounding could not be told apart from a donor-composition difference. delta and angle inflate about two-fold. The adjustment removes all three inflations, which is the property the gate tests.

docs.title: 4. Scope and limits
docs.text:
• The check covers additive, linear covariate effects that are correctly specified in the model. A covariate whose true effect is non-linear, or interacts with group or stage, is outside it.
  • The latent space is covariate-blind. In this construction the covariate effect is correlated with stage, so PLS may spend capacity on it; that case is measured here rather than assumed away. A covariate effect much larger than the stage signal is not.
  • This is one design: n = 80, two blocks, 498 features, three covariate design columns. More covariate columns at the same n use more residual degrees of freedom; this check does not bound that cost.
  • There is no power claim. Adjustment costs degrees of freedom and, in the presence of confounding, also removes confounded signal; the operating studies' power numbers were measured without covariates.

docs.title: 5. Consequence for the case study
docs.text:
The decision is covariates_validated. The SEA-AD case study may report covariate-adjusted motco analyze results (MOTCO ≥ 0.8.0) under these conditions:

  • keep the covariate set parsimonious (each factor level is a column);
  • report the record's covariates block (design columns, missing policy and dropped donors) beside the results;
  • carry the additive-linear and covariate-blind-basis limitations above;
  • keep the earlier binding statements unchanged: the CV-selected rank is reported beside angle, and non-rejections are uninformative.

docs.title: Design-guidance pilot — findings report (2026-10-28)
docs.text:
Change: design-guidance-grid · Configs: examples/trajectory_power_study/design_guidance_{core,arms}_{magnitude,geometry}_pilot.json · Code revision: 7c218c6 (branch feat/design-guidance-grid) · Records: results/design-guidance-pilot-2026-10-28/<profile>/ (report/, PROVENANCE.txt) and results/design-guidance-pilot-2026-10-28/figures/ · Grade: pilot, 100 replicates × 199 permutations; every rate below carries its Monte Carlo standard error at R = 100 (SE ≤ 0.05) and the anchor bound is α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/R) = 0.0936. This report proposes the slice to rerun at paper grade; it makes no paper-grade claim.

Run: four SLURM arrays on ing (partition 512x1024, one CPU and 4 GB per task, BLAS single-threaded, STUDY_N_JOBS unset, --error-policy record), jobs 929160–929163, 124 array tasks, 47,200 units at 199 permutations, 124 / 124 tasks COMPLETED 0:0, 0 failed records, 0 censored surgeries, 345.3 recorded unit core-hours (362.4 by sacct wall-sum), 3 h 51 m wall. Code: 7c218c6 on a clean worktree of feat/design-guidance-grid. The four PROVENANCE.txt files carry the launch lines, hashes and timings.

In one paragraph. Under the production measurement (pooled PLS, CV rank floored at 2, net displacement), magnitude/delta is the well-powered component: at n = 80 with three stages and two blocks it rejects 0.23 ± 0.04 at e = 0.05 and 0.59 ± 0.05 at e = 0.1, at n = 200 0.72 ± 0.04 and 0.94 ± 0.02, and e = 0.25 is saturated (≥ 0.98) at every column; a third block raises every sub-saturation rate (0.49 / 0.81 at n = 80), and a fourth stage changes little. Shape/shape rises monotonically with n, e and block count: 0.24 / 0.40 / 0.55 at n = 200 (two blocks, e = 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0), 0.50 / 0.72 / 0.85 at n = 500, 0.82 / 0.92 / 0.97 at n = 1000, and ≤ 0.20 at n = 80 with two blocks (0.52 at e = 1.0 with three). Orientation/angle is governed by n and block count, not by the effect size: with two blocks it stays at 0.05–0.22 for n ≤ 200 and reaches 0.41–0.62 only at n = 1000; with three blocks 0.35–0.46 at n = 200 and 0.75–0.87 at n = 1000; its response is flat or non-monotone in e (at five of the six two-block columns with n ≥ 200 the e = 1.0 rate is below the e = 0.5 rate), and across the arms the e = 1.0 rate tracks the CV-selected rank (0.97 at median rank 5, 0.81 at rank 7, 0.12 at the baseline's rank 3), the pattern the Phase 6 study recorded. The held-out CV stage AUROC is 1.000 at every core column and every arm except the stage-effect arm, where δ = 0.05 and 0.1 give 0.553 and 0.729 — bracketing the SEA-AD cohorts' 0.64–0.70 — and there no statistic has power at any effect at n = 200 (magnitude ≤ 0.03, orientation ≤ 0.07, shape ≤ 0.09). Size holds at 26 of 28 distinct anchors; the two excess verdicts are both exactly 0.10 against the bound 0.0936 (delta at n = 80 / four stages / three blocks, angle at the n = 200 baseline), the count chance predicts over 84 anchor tests at R = 100 (2.4), and the baseline column's independent Type I-phase draw gives angle 0.03. Translation's angle is within the pilot bound at every column (0.01–0.09). The paper-grade slice proposed in §7 is the three-stage core at n ∈ {80, 200, 500} × {two, three blocks} (36,000 units, about 350–400 core-hours).

Pre-flight: the fast suite at the same tree (ruff, mypy, 1510 passed / 1 skipped), the 2 × 19 smoke of all four profiles on ing (880 / 880 units, 0 failures) and 16 timed units at 199 permutations (openspec/changes/design-guidance-grid/notes.md).

Shared design (one baseline, one seed root base_seed 1028, one matched-seed family design-guidance): n = 200, three stages, group_ratio 0.5, p_dmp 0.1, ρ = 0, every per-omic δ 2.0, magnitude_kind: joint; pooled PLS on methylation + expression with the stage-supervised double-CV rank (cv1_splits 3, cv2_splits 4, 5 repeats, ≤ 20 components, random_state 1203), orientation_estimator: net_displacement, min_components: 2, 199 RRPP permutations, n_jobs 1. The production measurement is named in every profile, not defaulted. Attribution and the Phase 4 gate are off; the only predeclared rule is the advisory anchor_decision (α 0.05, k = 2, delta/angle/shape).

  • Core (design grid n_samples {80, 200, 500, 1000} × n_stages {3, 4} × layers {methylation + expression, all three}): magnitude at e ∈ {0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25} (98 cells, 9,800 units); orientation, shape and translation at e ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0} (162 cells, 16,200 units).
  • Arms (explicit points, one setting moved off the baseline): group ratio {0.65, 0.8}; stage proportions 0.5/0.3/0.2; p_dmp {0.05, 0.15}; joint δ {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0}; ρ {0.5, 0.8}. Magnitude 80 cells / 8,000 units; geometry 132 cells / 13,200 units.

The magnitude and geometry siblings share their seed family, so at every design column their zero-effect anchors evaluate the same datasets with the same RRPP draws (the smoke verified identical p-values at every column). This report reads the geometry profile's anchor and uses the magnitude profile's only as the reproduction check in §2; the two are never pooled.

docs.title: 2. Unit and failure accounting
docs.text:
• Units. 9,800 / 16,200 / 8,000 / 13,200 records, each (cell_id, replicate_index) present exactly once: duplicates 0, missing 0, unexpected 0, parameter-signature mismatches 0 in every profile (PROVENANCE.txt, computed against the enumerated grids).
  • Failures. 0 failed records in every profile. The design risk — stage-stratified double CV failing or selecting erratically in the n = 80, four-stage cells of 10 samples — did not materialize: those columns completed every unit and selected rank 3–4 (§4).
  • Censored surgeries. 0 (report/realized_surgery.csv: censored_fraction 0 at every orientation, shape and translation cell), as the headroom check at enumeration predicted.
  • Anchor reproduction (design D2). Keyed by design column (generator parameters without the mode and effect, plus the evaluation parameters) and replicate, the 28 distinct anchor columns give 2,800 keys: 2,700 hold one record from each sibling (16 core and 11 non-baseline arm columns × 100 replicates) and 100 hold eight (the baseline column: its design-point anchor and its type_i_baseline-phase anchor in each of the four profiles). Records sharing a key and the same (generator_seed, evaluation_seed) have identical p-values in every case (3,300 pairwise comparisons, 0 mismatches; observed statistics agree to 4 × 10⁻¹¹), so the siblings share both data and RRPP draws and the magnitude profile's anchors reproduce the geometry profile's exactly. The baseline column's Type I-phase anchor is a separate seed derivation (type_i_baseline phase, p-values identical across the four profiles), which gives that column a second, independent 100-replicate size reading (§5). This report reads the geometry profiles' design-point anchors; nothing is pooled.

docs.title: 6. The originally planned grid and what was run instead
docs.text:
The project's originally planned simulation grid (Table 1) crossed every row below; crossing them is infeasible (3,456 null combinations before any power cell), its mean shifts (0.01–0.2) sit far below the InterSIM stage effect the generator operates on (δ = 2.0), its "power" rows do not map to trajectory components, and two of them are null scenarios. Each factor's disposition:

Table 1 factor Disposition Where, and why Sample size Run Core axis n_samples ∈ {80, 200, 500, 1000}, crossed with stages and blocks. Group ratio Run Arm: group_ratio 0.65 and 0.8 off 0.5. Number of stages Run Core axis n_stages ∈ {3, 4}. Two-stage designs are dropped: with two stage means the configuration is a segment, shape is undefined by construction (nothing to bend) and angle reduces to the segment direction, so the three-component guidance cannot be read there; the case study has three stages. Stage proportions Run Arm: 0.5/0.3/0.2 off equal thirds. Differential-feature proportion Run Arm: p_dmp 0.05 and 0.15 off 0.1. 0.2 is excluded because at three stages it fails the surgery-headroom check (orientation saturates at e = 0.89, translation at 0.52). Shared stage shift Run, rescaled Arm: the joint per-omic δ ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} off InterSIM's 2.0. Table 1's 0.01–0.2 are on a scale the generator never reaches; 0.05–0.1 is where the rank-floor check found the SEA-AD stage-signal regime. Noise level Dropped Redundant with the stage shift: features are standardized before the PLS fit, so σ and δ enter the measurement only through δ/σ, which the δ arm already sweeps. Group-specific mean shift Run The translation mode (a constant location offset of group B) at e ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0} in both geometry profiles, read as the negative control for all three statistics; the magnitude mode covers a group-specific size change. Covariance scaling Deferred To the group-specific-dispersion change (change B): an opt-in generator field scaling group B's covariance and a null-only Type I study crossing spread {1, 1.5, 2, 3} × group ratio {0.2, 0.5, 0.8}. It is a size question, not a power row. Correlation scaling Deferred Same change and the same reason: it changes group B's dispersion, not its trajectory. Feature filtering Dropped Supervised filtering (by group or stage) biases the permutation null unless it is repeated inside every permutation, so MOTCO documents it as forbidden; label-blind filtering is upstream preprocessing and changes what is measured, not the validity of the test. Integration method Dropped PLS is the production measurement (docs/roadmap.md); SNF with the Euclidean statistics is deferred pending graph-native statistics; MOFA is out of scope; concat is a diagnostic baseline, not a constructed latent space.

docs.title: 7. Proposed paper-grade slice
docs.text:
The pilot answers the design question descriptively at every column; what the paper needs at paper grade (500 replicates × 999 permutations, SE ≤ 0.022, anchor bound 0.0695) is the slice where the rates are neither saturated nor at the null, at the sizes the planned analyses have. Proposed, as two sibling profiles sharing one seed family exactly as here (the anchor reproduction check is then bit-exact):

  • Columns: n_samples ∈ {80, 200, 500} × three stages × layers ∈ {methylation + expression, all three} — six columns. Three stages are the case-study and planned AD design; the four-stage columns tracked the three-stage ones for magnitude and shape (within 0.13 at every n, within SE at n ≥ 500) and differ for orientation only within the rank-driven scatter, so a second stage count buys little at twice the cost. n = 1000 is dropped: magnitude and shape are saturated there and the pilot's n = 1000 rates stand as pilot-grade values.
  • Effects: magnitude at e ∈ {0.02, 0.05, 0.1} (0.01 resolves only at n = 1000; 0.25 is saturated at every column); orientation and shape at e ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0} (1.0 kept so that orientation's non-monotone response is measured at paper grade with the selected rank recorded per cell); translation at e = 1.0 as the negative control; a zero-effect anchor per column.
  • Units and cost: magnitude profile 6 × (1 + 3) × 500 = 12,000 units; geometry profile 6 × (1 + 3 + 3 + 1) × 500 = 24,000; 36,000 in total. From the pilot's unit timings (10–30 s at n ≤ 500 with 199 permutations, the RRPP adding 2–5 s) a 999-permutation unit costs about 25 s at n = 80 to 50 s at n = 500 with three blocks: about 350–400 core-hours, in line with the latent-adjustment power comparison, on about 150 shards of ≤ 2.5 h on 512x1024.
  • Predeclared rules: acceptance.anchor_decision at α 0.05, k 2 (bound 0.0695 at R = 500); acceptance.type_i entries for translation's angle with bound: upper at every column; no power targets — the slice is guidance, not a gate. The report states rates ± SE, each column's stage AUROC and selected rank, and the design-guidance figure.
  • Second priority, if budget allows: the stage-effect arm δ ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0} at the baseline column (3 columns × 11 cells × 500 = 16,500 units, about 150 core-hours), because that is where power transitions and the CV rank inflates. δ ≤ 0.1 is the null regime at n = 200 and need not be rerun; the rank-floor check already sized it at n = 80 at paper grade.

Not proposed, with reasons: the ρ arm (continuity raises shape and e = 1.0 orientation power and lowers magnitude power; it is an assumption about the baseline geometry, and the design-point pilot chose ρ = 0 as the most general claim — a follow-up sensitivity if the case study's trajectories trend); group ratio, stage proportions and p_dmp (main effects measured at pilot grade move power in the expected direction; the orientation jump at group ratio 0.65 should be understood through the selected rank before it is rerun); the four-stage and n = 1000 columns (above).

Guidance statement the slice would support. delta is the component a cohort of n = 80–200 can detect (e ≥ 0.1 at n = 80, e ≥ 0.05 at n = 200, with two blocks); shape reaches 0.72–0.85 at n = 500 with two blocks (e = 0.5–1.0) and 0.84 at n = 200 with three blocks at e = 1.0, but stays ≤ 0.55 at n = 200 and ≤ 0.20 at n = 80 with two blocks; an angle non-rejection is uninformative at n ≤ 200 with two blocks, and any angle reading carries its selected rank. None of this holds when the stage signal is at the SEA-AD level: there the pilot measured no power for any component at n = 200.

docs.title: 8. Limitations
docs.text:
• Pilot precision. 100 replicates: SE ≤ 0.05 on every rate, and the anchor bound (0.0936) is loose; a column whose anchor sits between 0.07 and 0.09 is neither cleared nor flagged at this grade. Translation's angle rate is read against the bound and flagged, never claimed.
  • Block count is confounded with feature count. The two-block columns measure 498 features (methylation + expression); the three-block columns add the protein block. The contrast is "more blocks and more features", not block count alone; block weighting is roadmap item 5.
  • Structural analogue. The InterSIM blocks are a structural analogue of a real multi-omic design (498 measured features, cross-omic coupling through the reference maps), not an emulation of SEA-AD's RNA/ATAC.
  • Stage signal. The core columns run at δ = 2.0, where the held-out stage AUROC is saturated; only the δ arm reaches the regime of a real analysis, and only at n = 200 with three stages and two blocks.
  • One-at-a-time arms measure main effects off one baseline; interactions with sample size are not measured.
  • Orientation's effect-size response is confounded with the CV-selected rank. The e = 1.0 angle rate tracks the rank the stage-supervised double CV retains (§3.2, §3.4), and the rank is recorded, not controlled; the pilot describes the dependence and does not explain it.
  • The δ arm scales every surgery. Magnitude multiplies δ and the relocation surgeries move sites whose effect is δ, so "no power at δ ≤ 0.1" is partly the construction (group differences proportional to the stage effect), and it is measured at n = 200 with three stages and two blocks only.
  • Two anchor excesses at 0.10 are unresolvable at R = 100, and the baseline column's second anchor (the Type I-phase draw) is also a 100-replicate reading; the paper-grade slice resolves both columns.

docs.title: Design-guidance paper-grade slice — findings report (2026-10-29)
docs.text:
Change: design-guidance-paper-grade-slice (MOTCO 0.12.0). Supersedes at its columns: the pilot-grade rates of the design-guidance pilot (2026-10-28) at n ∈ {80, 200, 500}, three stages, two or three blocks, and at the joint stage effect δ ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}; the pilot's four-stage, n = 1000 and remaining arm columns stand at pilot grade. Reads: results/design-guidance-slice-2026-10-29/ (report/ and PROVENANCE.txt per profile, figures/, reproduction/).

The slice reruns the pilot report §7 proposal at paper grade: the three-stage core at the sample sizes the planned analyses have, under the production measurement (pooled PLS with the stage-supervised double-CV rank floored at 2, net-displacement orientation, joint magnitude), 500 replicates × 999 permutations (SE ≤ 0.022 on every rate; anchor bound 0.0695 at R = 500), in the pilot's seed family so that every column evaluates the pilot's datasets at its first 100 replicates. It is guidance, not a gate: the predeclared rules are the advisory anchor decision and a column-scoped Type I rule for translation's angle; there is no power target. The second-priority stage-effect arm (§8) was run on the user's decision once the slice's numbers were in.

In one paragraph. Size holds at every column under both predeclared rules. delta is the component a small cohort detects: 0.62 at n = 80 and 0.94 at n = 200 at e = 0.1 with two blocks (0.84 and 0.99 with three), and 0.63 at n = 500 even at e = 0.02 with two blocks. shape is monotone in n, effect and block count: ≤ 0.20 at n = 80 with two blocks, 0.56 at n = 200 and 0.85 at n = 500 at e = 1.0, and 0.48 / 0.86 / 0.97 with three blocks. angle is governed by n and block count with a flat, non-monotone response in effect (0.10–0.15 at n = 80 and 0.16–0.24 at n = 200 with two blocks; 0.36–0.43 at n = 500; 0.24–0.31 / 0.41–0.49 / 0.66–0.74 with three), every reading at a CV-selected rank of 2 or 3. All of it at a stage signal that is saturated (held-out CV AUROC ≥ 0.9998 at every cell), which is what the stage-effect arm relaxes.

docs.title: Translation (negative control), all statistics at every effect
4. Stage signal and selected rank
docs.text: The held-out CV stage AUROC (design_point_stage_signal.csv, the number that compares with a real analysis) is ≥ 0.9998 in mean and 1.000 at the q33–q67 range at every cell of both profiles: the stage signal is saturated at the core stage effect δ = 2.0, as in the pilot. The CV selects rank 2 or 3 at every cell (median 2 at 36 of the 42 geometry cells and 3 at the others, the n = 80 / two-block column and the e ≥ 0.5 orientation cells at n = 200 and 500 with two blocks among them; never above 3). With a saturated stage signal and two or three retained components, orientation is measured in a two- or three-dimensional latent space whose second axis carries little signal, and angle power is governed by how much of the group difference that second axis resolves — by n and the block count — rather than by the size of the orientation surgery (§9).

docs.text: Stated in §2: the sibling profiles reproduce each other's anchors at every column with identical p-values (3,000 / 3,000), and each slice profile reproduces the pilot's datasets at replicate indices 0–99 at every column (600 / 600 per profile, seeds and observed statistics identical, p-values not comparable across 999 and 199 permutations and excluded from the verdict). Pilot and slice replicates are never pooled.

docs.title: 7. Design-guidance statement
docs.text:
For a two-group, three-stage design measured as the production pipeline measures it, at the core stage effect (δ = 2.0; a saturated stage signal) and with the structural-analogue blocks:

  • Size. Every statistic holds its nominal size at every sample size and block count (anchor ≤ 0.062 against 0.0695), and the location-only control holds the angle bound at every column at e = 1.0. A rejection beside a location difference still warrants care at n = 80 with two blocks, where the smaller location offsets gave angle 0.074–0.078.
  • delta (magnitude) is the component a small cohort detects. With two blocks: e = 0.1 at 0.62 (n = 80), 0.94 (n = 200) and 1.00 (n = 500); e = 0.05 at 0.23, 0.69 and 0.96; e = 0.02 at 0.04, 0.23 and 0.63. A third block raises every rate: 0.84 / 0.99 / 1.00 at e = 0.1, 0.51 / 0.88 / 0.99 at e = 0.05, 0.11 / 0.43 / 0.83 at e = 0.02.
  • shape needs n or blocks. With two blocks it stays ≤ 0.20 at n = 80, reaches 0.42–0.56 at n = 200 (e = 0.5–1.0) and 0.75–0.85 at n = 500; with three blocks 0.32–0.48 at n = 80, 0.67–0.86 at n = 200 and 0.89–0.97 at n = 500. A shape non-rejection at n = 80 is uninformative.
  • angle (orientation), every reading at a selected rank of 2–3: 0.10–0.15 at n = 80 and 0.16–0.24 at n = 200 with two blocks (a non-rejection is uninformative there), 0.36–0.43 at n = 500 with two blocks; 0.24–0.31, 0.41–0.49 and 0.66–0.74 with three blocks. The rate does not increase with the orientation effect between e = 0.25 and 1.0; what moves it is n and the block count. Report the cohort's selected rank beside any angle result.
  • Blocks. Measuring the third block raises delta, shape and angle power at every n — by 0.2–0.3 at the mid-range cells — at no cost in size; block count is confounded with feature count (§9).

None of this is claimed below the core stage effect; the stage-effect arm (§8) measures how the statement degrades as δ falls toward the SEA-AD regime.

The arm is the slice profile at n = 200, three stages and two blocks with the joint per-omic stage effect delta_methyl = delta_expr = delta_protein at δ ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0} as explicit design points. δ = 0.25 is its configuration baseline — so no column repeats the slice, whose n = 200 / two-block column is the δ = 2.0 reference in the table — and its Type I baseline phase is a fresh 500-replicate draw at δ = 0.25.
