  • Size holds at every δ. Anchor ≤ 0.062 (the δ = 0.25 shape) against 0.0695 and size_holds at all three points; translation's angle at e = 1.0 meets the column-scoped rule at 0.048–0.054; no translation rate at any effect exceeds 0.062. The Type I baseline phase at δ = 0.25 gives anchor 0.026 / 0.062 / 0.036 and translation 0.036 / 0.056 / 0.034 (e = 0.1, magnitude profile) and 0.028 / 0.054 / 0.060 (e = 1.0, geometry profile) — all under the upper bound; the two-sided entry flags the conservative 0.026 and 0.028 rates, not an excess.
  • The stage signal stays strong down to δ = 0.25 (held-out CV AUROC 0.997, against 0.64–0.70 in the SEA-AD cohorts and 0.55 / 0.73 at the pilot's δ = 0.05 / 0.1), so the arm covers the upper part of the transition; the orientation surgery at e = 1.0 is the only cell that erodes it (0.950 at δ = 0.25).
  • The CV rank inflates as δ falls: a median 11 components at δ = 0.25 (up to 19), 4 at δ = 0.5, 3 at δ = 1.0 and 2 at δ = 2.0; at the orientation e = 1.0 cells 16, 9, 4 and 3.
  • delta and shape lose their power with δ. At e = 0.1 delta falls from 0.94 (δ = 2.0) to 0.51, 0.31 and the null (0.08); e ≤ 0.05 is at the null for δ ≤ 0.5 and 0.20 at δ = 1.0 and e = 0.05. shape is at the null for δ ≤ 0.5 and reaches 0.17 at δ = 1.0 and e = 1.0 against 0.56 at δ = 2.0.
  • angle does not follow δ monotonically. At e ≤ 0.5 it sits at the null for every δ ≤ 1.0 (0.06–0.11), but at e = 1.0 it reads 0.46 and 0.47 at δ = 0.5 and 1.0 — above the 0.18 at δ = 2.0 — with ranks 9 and 4 against 3. This is the rank confound of §9 in the other direction: a weaker stage signal makes the CV retain more components, which gives the largest orientation surgery room to be resolved, while a saturated signal collapses the latent space to two or three stage-driven axes. At δ = 0.25 (rank 16) the e = 1.0 rate is 0.13.
  • Against the pilot arms (100 × 199) the arm's rates are within 0.06 (delta), 0.04 (angle) and 0.03 (shape) at every cell and the median ranks agree; the arm supersedes them at these three columns.

Reproduction. The two arm profiles' anchors reproduce each other at all three columns, 1,500 / 1,500 pairs with identical p-values (reproduction/siblings_stage_effect.csv). Against the pilot arms profiles the committed --by-column tool pairs nothing (pilot_stage_effect_*.csv, 0 pairs): it keys a column on its full design point, and the pilot arms' points carry seven axes (the other one-factor arms at their baseline values) against the arm's three. The seed identity holds nonetheless — the profile tests assert it at enumeration for every arm cell (replicates 0–99) — and a projected join of the records on (δ, replicate index), restricted to the pilot columns whose other axes sit at the baseline, confirms it on the data: 300 / 300 pairs per profile (100 at each δ), with generator seeds, selected ranks and observed delta/angle/shape identical on every pair (reproduction/pilot_stage_effect_*_projected.csv; p-values not comparable across 999 and 199 permutations). An option to project the column key onto named axes is the natural follow-up for the tool.

Guidance below the core stage effect (n = 200, three stages, two blocks): at δ = 0.25 no component has power at any effect in the enumerated ranges except a weak e = 1.0 orientation reading (0.13 at rank 16); at δ = 0.5–1.0 only delta at e = 0.1 (0.31–0.51) and angle at e = 1.0 (0.46–0.47, at ranks 9 and 4) leave the null; shape needs the core stage effect. A real design's held-out stage AUROC places it on this axis: 1.000 reads as δ ≥ 0.5, 0.997 as δ ≈ 0.25, and the SEA-AD level (0.64–0.70) sits below the arm, where the pilot measured no power for any component at δ ≤ 0.1.

docs.title: 9. Limitations
docs.text:
• Translation at three effects. A configuration has one effect list, so translation ran at e ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}; the predeclared rule judges e = 1.0 only, and the two smaller offsets are descriptive controls (above the bound for angle at n = 80 with two blocks). A per-mode effect list in the engine is the documented alternative.
  • Block count is confounded with feature count (498 measured features with two blocks against 498 plus the protein block with three): the block effect is a measurement contrast on the same datasets, not a claim about protein data.
  • Structural analogue. The blocks are InterSIM-calibrated structural analogues of methylation, expression and protein data; the rates transfer to a real design only through the stage signal and the feature counts, not through any biology.
  • Saturated stage signal. At δ = 2.0 the held-out CV stage AUROC is 1.000 everywhere, far above the SEA-AD cohorts (0.64–0.70); the statement in §7 holds for a strongly staged design, and §8 is the only part of this report that speaks to weaker staging.
  • The rank confound of orientation power. angle is measured in the CV-selected latent space (rank 2–3 here) and its power follows n and the block count rather than the orientation effect; a flat or non-monotone response in e is a property of the measurement, not evidence that larger orientation differences are harder to detect. The latent-rank ladder (2026-09-08) and the pilot report §4 document the mechanism; every angle reading above carries its rank.
  • Scope. Three stages, ρ = 0, equal groups, p_dmp 0.1, n ≤ 500. The pilot's four-stage, n = 1000, group-ratio, stage-proportion, p_dmp and ρ columns stand at pilot grade (100 × 199) and are not rerun here. Group-specific dispersion is not in the generator (change B of the pilot's follow-ups).

docs.title: Geometry audit: statistics, constructions, and documentation
docs.text: Run date: 2026-09-01 Code revision: cd583a7 (branch main, the merge of diagnose-angle-null-pivotality) Records read: results/angle-pivotality-2026-09-01/merged.jsonl (500 replicates) and results/phase4-2026-08-27/merged.jsonl (1,900 units) — read-only; no new study cells were run New computation: three targeted experiments — a deterministic estimator check, and replicate regenerations from persisted generator_seeds pushed through the identical PLS integration. Every regenerated statistic was matched against its persisted record (angles to 1e-8, shapes to 4+ decimals) before any conclusion was drawn. Scope: stats/ (trajectory, permutation, design, pls, snf, attribution), simulations/ (semisynthetic, generator, evaluation, preprocessing, diagnostics, specificity, pivotality, grid), all six reports under docs/reports/, the OpenSpec spec set, and the test suite Affects: Phase 5 readiness items 1–5 Environment: Python 3.11.15, numpy 2.3.5, pandas 2.3.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scipy 1.16.3; no R at runtime

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The statistical core — RRPP, the design coding, the Procrustes solver, the sign-anchor fix, the M-value contract, the matched-seed and signature machinery — is sound, and the 2026-09-01 pivotality diagnosis is correct as far as it goes. The audit found that it stops one step short, and found four further defects:

  • F1. The per-replicate angle null width that the pivotality report calls "invisible to every integration diagnostic currently persisted" is in fact predicted (Spearman −0.81 on the 16 extreme replicates) by the relative eigengap of the latent stage-mean configuration — and that eigengap is near zero by construction, because the baseline draws independent per-stage indicator programs whose stage means form a near-regular simplex.
  • F2. The orientation and translation effect axes are silently censored by the relocation clamp: the orientation surgery saturates at e ≈ 0.69, and 80 of 100 replicate pairs at e = 0.75 and e = 1.00 are byte-identical datasets with identical statistics. The flat top of the orientation power curve is partly guaranteed by construction.
  • F3. The shape reflection contract is ambient-dimension-dependent: "reflections retained as distinct" is true only where the trajectory configuration spans the full space (the PLS latent checkpoint) and silently vacuous at every pre-integration checkpoint, so the Phase-4 localization table compares two different statistics across its rows. Measured on regenerated pilot replicates, however, reflection is ruled out as the orientation→shape mechanism (allowing reflections changes the latent shape distance in 0 of 100 replicates) — the latent shape response is genuine projection-induced deformation.
  • F4. The tested angle statistic (PC1-axis divergence) and its attribution machinery (per-adjacent-transition contrasts) decompose different orientation quantities for ≥ 3 stages; the planned "signed principal orientations" extension was never implemented.
  • F5 (synthesis). The load-bearing assumption surgery mode ⇒ target latent statistic fails at five compounding layers, and angle is the only statistic exposed at all five — which is why every fix so far (sign anchor, studentization candidates, more replicates) moved it by points rather than tens of points. The deepest layer is the independent-indicator baseline, which makes the orientation estimand itself nearly degenerate per draw.

Plus a set of documentation and spec defects (D1–D9), including README examples that raise on execution and a stale GPA description in CLAUDE.md.

A remediation plan, expressed as proposed OpenSpec changes in priority order, closes the report.

docs.title: F1 — The angle-null width has a measurable driver
docs.text: The pivotality report established that the RRPP null for angle tracks its own observed statistic (slope 0.811), that the tracking is load-bearing, and that "nothing the harness records today identifies which replicates will be resolvable" — selected dimensionality and CV AUROC both saturate and neither correlates with the null width. That last gap is closed here: the missing quantity is the relative eigengap (λ₁−λ₂)/Σλ of the centered stage-mean configuration in the latent space, computable per replicate (and per permutation) from matrices already in hand.

docs.title: Evidence: recomputed from the committed pivotality records
docs.text:
The 8 narrowest-null and 8 widest-null orientation replicates were regenerated from their persisted generator_seeds and pushed through the identical PLS integration (cv1_splits=3, cv2_splits=4, n_repeats=5, max_components=20, random_state=1203). Fidelity first: every recomputed observed angle matched the persisted pair_statistics["angle"] (e.g. 8.56 vs 8.56, 138.46 vs 138.46), so this is the study pipeline reproduced bit-for-bit, not an approximation.

Per replicate, the relative eigengap of the pooled latent stage-mean configuration against the recorded null width:

Group mean eigengap (pooled config) mean recorded angle q95 8 narrowest nulls 0.097 6.6° 8 widest nulls 0.046 174.0°
  • Spearman(log q95, pooled eigengap) = −0.81; Pearson on log–log = −0.88. (Correlations computed within the 16 selected extremes; a full-cell run over all 100 replicates confirms the association — see the addendum at the end of this section.)
  • A 2× separation in eigengap maps to a 26× separation in null width.
  • The replicates whose per-group eigengap is near zero (0.002–0.013) are exactly the ones carrying huge observed angles (138°–157°). Observed statistic and null co-vary because both are driven by the same anisotropy — that shared dependence is the measured 0.811 slope, mechanistically.

docs.title: The construction sets the eigengap near zero
docs.text:
_baseline_methyl draws independent Bernoulli(p_dmp) indicators per stage ("intentionally not forced continuous", per the module docstring). Independent stage programs of equal expected size put the stage means at the vertices of a near-regular simplex: every pairwise distance is statistically identical, the configuration is nearly isotropic, and PC1 — the orientation estimator — is decided by the few-percent random asymmetry of the draw.

Direct measurement (200 indicator draws at k = 4 stages, p_dmp = 0.2): median relative eigengap 0.026 (q5 0.005, q95 0.050), against 1.0 for a straight trajectory; net displacement is ~⅓ of path length. PC1's estimator variance scales like noise/eigengap, so per-replicate angle nulls spanning 5°–177° are the expected behavior of this construction. The heavy near-180° null mass (21/700, unchanged by the sign fix) follows from the same degeneracy: once the axis itself wanders, the sign anchor cannot stabilize the angle.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
1. Readiness items 1 and 3 asked for exactly this quantity. It is one SVD of a k×d matrix per configuration, computable per replicate and per permutation, and on real data it doubles as an "orientation resolvability" qualifier for reporting.
  2. The item-4 design-point question changes shape. More samples shrink the noise on stage means, so power does rise with n — but the required n scales like the inverse square of the eigengap, and the gap's lower tail (draws near perfect isotropy) is what caps the power curve. Sample size buys those replicates almost nothing; the baseline's continuity (F5) is the stronger lever.
  3. The spec expectation that "null configurations never approach antiparallel" (trajectory-orientation-invariance) is enforced only by a small-noise 2-D test (tests/test_trajectory_orientation.py:109). The production operating regime violates its spirit lawfully, because noise there is not small relative to the anisotropy.

docs.title: Addendum: full-cell confirmation
docs.text: The same computation over all 100 orientation replicates (no selection): Spearman(log q95, pooled eigengap) = −0.75 (Pearson log–log −0.62), so the association is a property of the cell, not of the extremes. The eigengap also predicts the outcome: replicates that reject angle average gap 0.053, replicates that fail average 0.035. The observed angle tracks the smaller per-group gap (Spearman −0.33), consistent with the shared-anisotropy mechanism. The same run carries the F3 reflection probe over the whole cell: allowing reflections changes the latent shape distance in 0 of 100 replicates (mean improper/proper ratio 1.000), and the reflection-allowed observed shape still exceeds the recorded shape-null q95 in 99 of 100.

docs.title: F2 — The orientation and translation effect axes are censored
docs.text: _relocate_rows clamps the relocation count to the destination pool: k = min(round(e·|src_pool|), |dst_pool|). With p_dmp = 0.2 and four stages, ~59% of CpGs are stage-active and only ~41% are inactive, so the orientation surgery saturates at e ≈ 0.69. The translation mode's candidate pool (stage-inactive CpGs on untouched genes) is smaller still.

docs.title: Evidence: the Phase-4 records' own truth metadata
docs.text:
Mode e = 0.25 0.50 0.75 1.00 orientation, realized relocations (mean) 54.4 108.9 146.9 149.3 orientation, nominal (uncensored) 54 108 163 217 translation, realized set size (mean) 18.0 34.3 37.7 38.2 translation, nominal 18 37 55 73

Because matched seeds share the generator seed across effect sizes and the clamp makes k identical whenever it binds, 80 of 100 replicate pairs at e = 0.75 and e = 1.00 are byte-identical datasets with identical angle statistics (same generator_seed, angle equal to 1e-9). The Phase-4 "0.67 vs 0.68" comparison between those cells differs on 20 replicates of fresh information.

The other modes are clean: shape/relocate realizes ≈ its nominal count at every effect (18.2 / 36.5 / 54.6 / 72.8 against nominal 18 / 37 / 55 / 73 — its per-stage source pool is smaller than the destination pool), and magnitude scales δ with no pool at all.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The flat top of the orientation power curve is partly guaranteed by construction, and the preregistered monotonicity gate is near-vacuous between the top cells.
  • "Power at effect 1.00" actually characterizes an e ≈ 0.69-equivalent construction.
  • A Phase-5 grid inheriting this axis would duplicate ~80% of its compute between those cells while reporting them as independent measurements.
  • The realized sizes are recorded (truth_metadata.transform) — they have never been surfaced in a report. This is the Phase-2 lesson ("report realized geometry, not requested labels") recurring one level further upstream, at requested-effect → realized-surgery.

docs.title: F3 — The reflection contract is rank-dependent; reflection is not the orientation→shape mechanism
docs.text: The shape spec and the Procrustes audit state that "reflections are retained as distinct shapes by default." That is true precisely when the trajectory configuration spans the full ambient space (dimension ≤ k−1) and silently false otherwise: when the configuration is rank-deficient, the determinant correction in _proper_procrustes_distance flips a null-space singular vector, which costs nothing in the objective — the "proper rotation" constraint is vacuous and the estimator returns the reflection-allowed distance.

docs.title: Evidence: the production estimator on deterministic configurations
docs.text:
A bent 4-stage planar trajectory vs its mirror image, embedded by zero-padding:

Ambient dimension shape distance, config vs mirror 2 0.431 3 0.000 10 0.000 660 0.000

A rank-3 configuration vs its mirror: positive in 3-D, 0.000 in ≥ 4-D. So at every pre-integration checkpoint (population_native, population_standardized, observed_standardized: hundreds of dimensions, configurations of rank ≤ 3) shape is reflection-invariant, while at pls_latent (3 dims, rank-3 configurations) it is reflection-sensitive. The invariance test pins only the 2-D full-rank case, so the suite passes while the contract fails in the very spaces the realized-geometry checkpoints use. The Phase-4 localization table therefore compares two different statistics across its rows.

docs.title: Evidence: but reflection does not explain orientation→shape
docs.text: The natural suspicion — that orientation→shape "first becomes material at the PLS checkpoint" because a mirror-like difference is invisible pre-integration and visible in 3-D — was tested on the regenerated pilot replicates. Allowing reflections in the latent space changed the shape distance by 0.0% in 100 of 100 (the optimal alignment is already a proper rotation), and the reflection-allowed distance still exceeded the replicate's recorded shape-null q95 in 99 of 100. The recomputed proper distances matched the persisted observed shapes to four decimals. The latent shape response is genuine configuration deformation.

docs.title: What that leaves for readiness item 2
docs.text: With reflection eliminated, the remaining account is the one the Phase-4 report labeled "a property of a rank-3 stage-supervised space": an orthogonal (rotation-only) difference between two feature-space programs does not survive a rank-3 projection as a rotation — only rotations within the retained subspace do. At e = 1 the two groups' programs are nearly disjoint, so their relative rotation lies mostly outside any shared 3-D subspace, and its image under the projection returns as deformation, which the shape statistic (nearly pivotal, per the pivotality tables) then detects at rate ~0.99. Under this account the response is an expected property of measuring an out-of-subspace rotation in a rank-limited space — predeclarable for Phase 5 as a projection artifact, and testable: it should shrink as retained rank grows toward the joint program rank.

docs.title: F4 — The angle test and its attribution decompose different orientations
docs.text:
_estimate_orientation returns PC1 of the k-stage configuration signed by net displacement: the tested angle is a principal-axis divergence. stats/attribution.py explains per-adjacent-transition normalized contrasts (d/‖d‖ per transition). These coincide only for k = 2. For a bent trajectory PC1 is not any transition direction — and under the random-simplex baseline (F1) the divergence between the two notions is maximal: transition directions are well-defined per step while PC1 is nearly degenerate.

Two documentation consequences: the orientation-invariance spec's purpose line ("a difference in direction of progression") and its "known angle is recovered" scenario hold only for straight trajectories; and the roadmap's Phase-3 plan to extend attribution with "signed principal orientations" was not implemented. Nothing here is a wrong computation — but a significant 4-stage angle is currently interpreted through a decomposition of a related, different quantity.

docs.title: F5 — Synthesis: why the assumed feature→latent mapping kept failing
docs.text:
The study's load-bearing assumption — surgery mode ⇒ its target latent statistic — fails at five distinct layers:

  1. Requested → realized surgery. The clamp censors the orientation and translation axes (F2). The effect knob is not the effect delivered.
  2. Methylation surgery → multi-omic geometry. The CpG→gene→protein OR-derivation converts a pure methylation relocation into a mixed multi-omic program change (documented in Phase 2 — this layer is understood).
  3. Feature geometry → standardized joint geometry. Pooled per-feature scaling, and magnitude scaling only one of three blocks, mix size into direction (documented — the 39.9° population angle of the magnitude construction).
  4. Joint geometry → latent geometry. The stage-supervised space saturates at rank k−1 and retains ~6% of the group orientation contrast; rotation-only differences that lie outside the retained subspace re-enter as deformation (F3's mechanism for orientation→shape). Angles between projections are not angles between originals.
  5. Latent geometry → statistic. PC1 on a near-isotropic configuration is an ill-determined estimand; observed statistic and permutation null co-vary through the shared anisotropy (F1), which is the measured 0.811 tracking.

delta survives all five because path length is a sum of norms — insensitive to axis identity, projection rotation, and configuration anisotropy. shape survives because the constructed bend is large and its null is nearly pivotal. angle is structurally exposed at every layer, which is why every fix so far moved it by points rather than tens of points.

The deepest of the five is the baseline. "Intentionally not forced continuous" was a defensible generality choice, but it makes the orientation estimand itself nearly meaningless at the population level: a trajectory with independent stage programs has no direction to differ in. It is also the less biologically representative case for staged progression, where successive stages share and accumulate programs and the configuration has a dominant trend — precisely the regime where PC1 is well-conditioned and angle nulls are tight. A baseline-continuity axis (from fully independent to strongly trending indicator draws) would turn the orientation question from "which replicates got lucky draws" into a designed, monotone operating characteristic — while keeping the current isotropic baseline as the stress-test endpoint.

docs.title: D — Documentation and spec defects
docs.text: ID Location Issue D1 CLAUDE.md:73 Says shape uses "iterative Procrustes GPA" — superseded 2026-08-04 by strict pairwise OPA; contradicts the audit report and the code. D2 README.md:52–57 motco simulate example passes --prop-affected-features, which the CLI does not accept, and the comment says the command "requires R + InterSIM" while the parser help says "numpy generator, no R" (cli.py:321). D3 README.md:304–315 Python example imports generate_semisynthetic_trajectory_from_intersim and passes prop_affected_features — neither exists in src/ anymore; the example raises on execution. D4 docs/roadmap.md:28 The resolved shape-invariance item is filed under "Not yet established". D5 openspec/specs/semisynthetic-trajectory-generator/spec.md:5 Purpose line still says datasets are generated "from InterSIM outputs"; the requirements below it correctly say no R at runtime. D6 grid.py:328, showcase.py:71–74 Matched-seed docstrings claim family cells generate "the same dataset" / that "the only thing that changes is group B's transform". Only the baseline indicators and group assignment match: the transforms consume different RNG amounts, so all sampled values differ across modes (the sole common-random-numbers pair is none↔magnitude, whose transforms draw nothing). The pivotality config note "the comparison across modes is on the same generator draws" overstates likewise. D7 CLAUDE.md / evaluation.py vs docs/roadmap.md CLAUDE.md and the evaluation docstring call SNF a "production latent-space method" while rung 2 found SNF leaks independently and the roadmap defers SNF pending graph-native statistics (Phase 7). One message should win. D8 evaluation.py:368, design.py Stage levels sort as strings; ordering silently breaks at n_stages ≥ 10 ("10" < "2"). Latent hazard only, but path length and shape depend on stage order. D9 README.md:270, shape spec Shape described as removing "orientation differences" with reflections retained — needs the F3 rank qualifier to be true as stated. Resolved 2026-09-03 by unify-shape-reflection-policy: rather than adding the qualifier, the policy was unified — reflections are aligned away at every ambient dimension, and README, spec, and docstrings now say so.

docs.title: S — Audited and found sound
docs.text:
• S1 — RRPP. The reduced model (additive group+stage) is the right null for the interaction; permuting whole residual rows is exchangeable under the generator's homoskedastic cells; keeping the latent space fixed under permutation is defensible because integration is group-blind (stage-supervised only) — and empirically Type I holds. The add-one right-tail p-value is applied consistently.
  • S2 — Design coding. get_model_matrix / build_ls_means / contrast indexing are mutually consistent (drop-first dummies, group-major LS-mean rows).
  • S3 — Procrustes solver. The rotation solution and determinant handling are algebraically correct; the independent recomputation reproduced all 16 persisted shape statistics exactly.
  • S4 — Orientation sign anchor. Net-displacement anchoring is the right convention; its one degeneracy (closed trajectories) is documented. The remaining instability is the axis, not the sign (F1).
  • S5 — M-value contract. Applied uniformly across preprocessing, concat, SNF, and diagnostics; the rung-ladder conclusion is honored in the production path.
  • S6 — Study machinery. Parameter signatures (including n_jobs), resumable sharding, seed derivation, and record persistence reproduce byte-identically — verified by regenerating replicates from persisted seeds and matching statistics to 1e-8.
  • S7 — The pivotality report's logic. The studentization no-op argument, the fixed-threshold catastrophe, and the "tracking is load-bearing" reading are all correct. F1 extends it with the missing covariate; it contradicts nothing.
  • S8 — Magnitude path. The one construction/estimator pair with no unexplained behavior: the estimator is more specific than the (deliberately mixed) construction, as reported.

docs.title: Remediation plan
docs.text: Proposed as OpenSpec changes, in priority order. P1–P2 are small, additive, and unblock the Phase-5 design-point work; P3 is contract hygiene the paper-grade study's cross-checkpoint claims depend on; P4 is the substantive scientific decision; P5–P6 are cleanups that can land any time.

docs.title: P1 — record-latent-config-spectrum (F1 → readiness items 1, 3, 4)
docs.text:
Persist the eigenspectrum of the centered stage-mean configuration — pooled and per group — in every evaluation record, beside null_summary.

  • Scope: evaluation.py (compute after estimate_difference, from obs_vect already in hand), grid.py record schema (version bump so resume signatures cannot mix contracts), study report tables (power stratified by eigengap for orientation cells).
  • Also record the per-permutation eigengap summary (quantiles over the RRPP draws) — one SVD of a k×d matrix per permutation, negligible next to estimate_difference.
  • Acceptance: the pivotality analysis re-run over new records shows log(null q95) regressing on the recorded eigengap with the association found here; the Phase-5 report contract gains the stratified power table.
  • Non-goal: no change to any statistic or test.

docs.title: P2 — fix-effect-axis-censoring (F2 → readiness item 4 precondition)
docs.text:
Make the requested-vs-realized surgery relationship explicit and non-degenerate.

  • Decide the policy per mode: fail loudly when the clamp would bind (preferred for study configs), or renormalize the axis to realized fractions, or raise headroom (e.g. lower p_dmp for the orientation cell, or relocate within the active set). The current silent min() is the one indefensible option.
  • Surface transform.orientation_relocated / translation_set_size in summarize_rejection_rates and the study report; annotate or dedupe cells whose realized construction is identical in distribution.
  • Acceptance: enumerating the Phase-4 grid under the new policy either errors on the censored cells or reports distinct realized effects per cell; no two power cells share > 5% identical replicates.
  • Note: changes generator semantics → parameter signatures will (correctly) refuse to resume old shards.

docs.title: P3 — unify-shape-reflection-policy (F3 → readiness item 2, Phase-5 report contract)
docs.text:
Landed 2026-09-03, taking the preferred option below: the determinant correction is gone, SHAPE_STATISTIC_VERSION = 2 guards resume compatibility, and the follow-up probe ships as scripts/latent_rank_probe.py (results under results/latent-rank-probe-2026-09-03/).

Pick one reflection policy that holds at every checkpoint.

  • Preferred: allow reflections everywhere (drop the determinant correction). Measured cost on real replicates: zero (100/100 identical distances); benefit: one statistic across all checkpoints, matching the standard identification of reflections in shape spaces whose dimension exceeds configuration rank.
  • Alternative: keep the proper-rotation estimator but document the rank threshold in the spec and annotate every cross-checkpoint comparison with its regime.
  • Either way: add mirror-pair tests at ambient dimension > rank (the current suite pins only 2-D), and update trajectory-shape-invariance spec + README + docstrings.
  • Include the item-2 follow-up probe: re-measure latent shape at forced larger n_components; if the orientation→shape response decays toward the population value, predeclare it as a projection artifact.

docs.title: P4 — add-baseline-continuity-axis (F5 → the 0.80-floor question, readiness item 4)
docs.text:
Add a generator axis controlling stage-program continuity, from independent (current behavior, the stress-test endpoint) to strongly trending (e.g. Markov persistence of indicators across stages, or cumulative programs).

  • The design decision to make explicitly: orientation power is then reported as a function of baseline continuity, and the honest scientific claim becomes "MOTCO resolves orientation differences when the trajectory has a direction to differ in" — with the eigengap (P1) as the observable that carries that statement to real data.
  • Realized-geometry diagnostics already in place will show how continuity moves the eigengap distribution.
  • This is the change most likely to move the orientation operating characteristics by tens of points; n-scaling alone attacks the noise term while the gap's lower tail persists.

docs.title: P5 — align-orientation-attribution (F4)
docs.text: Either add a principal-orientation component to attribution (contrast of the PC1 axes reconstructed through the fitted loadings, beside the existing per-transition contrasts), or narrow the documented estimand of angle to "principal-axis divergence" and state explicitly that attribution explains transitions. Small; matters for how a significant orientation result is interpreted in Phase 6.

docs.title: P6 — docs-sync-audit (D1–D9)
docs.text: One documentation batch: CLAUDE.md GPA line (D1), README simulate example and Python examples (D2, D3), roadmap bullet placement (D4), semisynthetic spec purpose line (D5), matched-seed docstring wording in grid.py/showcase.py and the pivotality config note (D6), one consistent SNF status message (D7), the stage-label natural-sort guard plus test (D8 — the one code change in the batch), and the reflection qualifier in shape descriptions (D9, folds into P3 if that lands first).

docs.title: Sequencing and cautions
docs.text:
• P1 + P2 before any new power runs; P3 before Phase-5 report drafting; P4 decides the Phase-5 design point; P5/P6 anytime.
  • Caution on latent-space sizing (item 3): any group-aware supervision or sizing puts group information into the measurement space and voids the fixed-latent-space RRPP conditioning that currently makes the permutation test defensible (S1). That road requires integrating inside the permutation loop or a proof of invariance — do not take it casually.
  • The zero-effect anchor, n_jobs-in-signature, and matched-seed machinery need no changes.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text:
All three experiments read committed study records and re-derive datasets from persisted seeds; none re-runs RRPP.

1. Reflection rank-dependence (pure estimator check):

import numpy as np
from motco.stats.trajectory import _estimate_shape

config = np.array([[0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 0.2], [2.0, -0.1], [3.0, 0.8]])
mirror = config * np.array([1.0, -1.0])
for d in (2, 3, 10, 660):
    A = np.hstack([config, np.zeros((4, d - 2))])
    B = np.hstack([mirror, np.zeros((4, d - 2))])
    V = np.vstack([A, B])
    print(d, _estimate_shape(V, [[0, 1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6, 7]])[0, 1])
# 2 → 0.431;  3, 10, 660 → 0.000

2. Eigengap vs recorded angle-null width (regeneration from persisted seeds):

import json
import numpy as np
from motco.simulations.semisynthetic import SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams, generate_semisynthetic_trajectory
from motco.simulations.evaluation import (
    SimulationEvaluationParams, integrate_semisynthetic_dataset, build_simulation_trajectory_design)
from motco.stats.trajectory import estimate_betas

PLS = {"cv1_splits": 3, "cv2_splits": 4, "n_repeats": 5, "max_components": 20, "random_state": 1203}
recs = [json.loads(l) for l in open("results/angle-pivotality-2026-09-01/merged.jsonl")]
orient = [r for r in recs if (r.get("cell_metadata") or {}).get("trajectory_mode") == "orientation"
          and r.get("phase") == "power_primary"]

def relgap(cfg):
    X = cfg - cfg.mean(0, keepdims=True)
    e = np.linalg.svd(X, compute_uv=False) ** 2
    return (e[0] - e[1]) / e.sum()

for r in orient:  # or a subset
    ds = generate_semisynthetic_trajectory(SemiSyntheticTrajectoryParams(
        seed=int(r["generator_seed"]), trajectory_mode="orientation",
        n_samples=300, n_stages=4, group_effect_size=1.0, p_dmp=0.2))
    latent = integrate_semisynthetic_dataset(ds, SimulationEvaluationParams(
        integration_method="pls", integration_params=PLS, permutations=0))
    design = build_simulation_trajectory_design(ds.metadata)
    Y = latent.matrix.to_numpy(float)
    stages = ds.metadata["stage"].to_numpy()
    pooled = np.vstack([Y[stages == s].mean(0) for s in sorted(set(stages))])
    # sanity: estimate_difference here reproduces r["pair_statistics"] exactly
    print(r["generator_seed"], relgap(pooled), r["null_summary"]["angle"]["q95"])

The reflection probe (F3) is the same regeneration with the group LS-mean configurations (build_ls_means @ betas), _center_scale_unit on each, and the Procrustes residual computed with and without the determinant correction.

3. Effect-axis censoring (record scan):

import json
from collections import defaultdict
import numpy as np

rows = defaultdict(list)
for l in open("results/phase4-2026-08-27/merged.jsonl"):
    r = json.loads(l)
    cm = r.get("cell_metadata") or {}
    tr = (r.get("truth_metadata") or {}).get("transform") or {}
    if cm.get("trajectory_mode") == "orientation":
        rows[cm["effect_size"]].append(tr.get("orientation_relocated"))
for e in sorted(rows):
    print(e, np.mean([v for v in rows[e] if v is not None]))
# 0.25 → 54.4, 0.5 → 108.9, 0.75 → 146.9, 1.0 → 149.3 (nominal 54/108/163/217)

The 80/100 duplication figure comes from joining orientation power_primary records on replicate_index across effects 0.75 and 1.00 and counting pairs with equal generator_seed and equal pair_statistics["angle"] (tolerance 1e-9).

docs.title: Per-feature interaction scan — findings report (2026-11-09)
docs.text:
Change: interaction-feature-scan (MOTCO 0.20.0). Reads: results/interaction-scan-2026-11-09/ (interaction_scan_decision.json, simulation/ and plasmode/ scan, block-balance, comparator, false-hit and recovery tables, accounting.json, reproduction.json, settings.json, plasmode-fidelity/fidelity.json, PROVENANCE.txt, sacct.txt). Concept page: measurement visibility.

Every test MOTCO had pooled the group × stage difference over many dimensions: - delta, angle and shape see only the part of a difference inside the fitted stage-PLS span; - the split interaction test sums interaction energy over its parts.

Neither sees a difference confined to a few features. The SEA-AD plasmode planted one, a ramp to 3 within-stage SDs on 20 of 10,000 features in one group, and all six tests rejected it at the null rate (plasmode, split test). motco.stats.interaction.interaction_feature_scan tests each feature's interaction F on its own and combines the features by their maximum. Its global p-value is the permutation p-value of the largest F. Each feature gets a Westfall–Young step-down max-T adjusted p-value, under RRPP's Freedman–Lane draws and residual corrections. A hit is a feature with adjusted p ≤ 0.05.

In one paragraph. The scan is validated: scan_validated. It holds size and familywise control, and it sees the sparse difference every other test misses.

  • Size holds everywhere. The six simulation control rates read 0.048–0.058, against a per-cell bound of 0.0695. On real noise at the case study's configuration (six covariates, 10,000 features) the scan reads 0.042.
  • Familywise control holds under the plasmode's partial null. At e = 2.0 and 3.0, a feature outside the planted set was a hit in 0.042 of units at both strengths.
  • It sees the sparse plant. At e = 3.0 the scan rejects in every unit (1.000), against 0.016–0.048 for the six existing tests on the same units. At e = 2.0 it rejects in 0.692.
  • It names the planted features. At e = 3.0, 0.995 of the hits are planted features and half the plant is found (recall 0.525). The 20 largest F hold 0.887 of the plant, against attribution's committed 0.432.
  • The null maxima are not balanced across blocks. On the SEA-AD export each block holds half the features, but ATAC gives 0.618 of the null maxima. In the simulation, methylation holds 0.737 of the features and gives 0.50. The verdict is unaffected, but the familywise threshold leans on one block.

docs.title: 1. Configuration and provenance
docs.text:
• The parent. Both profiles rerun the split-test validation's units (results/span-split-2026-11-05/). Each profile's settings are rebuilt through scripts/span_split_check.py at the parent's grade and must equal the committed settings.json. The sha256 of that file and of the parent's split and production (or trajectory) tables are bound in the settings and re-checked at every step.
  • Simulation profile. The latent-space comparison's three designs: n200, seaad, and seaad_weak at the calibrated δ = 0.11. Each has methylation + expression (498 features), fourteen cells and base seed 2035.
  • Replicates. The anchor and translation ran 500 replicates, every other cell 100, all at 999 permutations: 6,600 units.
  • Each unit is the parent's unit unchanged: one pls_cv fit and evaluation, and the split test. The scan then runs on the split test's features and models at the unit's RRPP seed. Those features are the fit's standardized features in the PLS input coordinates, a per-feature affine map the scan ignores.
  • Recorded per unit: the scan's counts, its maximum and block, the global p-value, hits per block, the per-block share of null maxima, and hits on population-null features. A feature is population-null when its population B − A difference is constant across stages.
  • Plasmode profile. The SEA-AD plasmode's units: the astrocyte cohort_30 export under the plasmode's contract, within-stage label permutation, and the 20-feature plant (10 per block) with its seeds (base seed 2034, paper stream).
  • Cells: the anchor, e = 2.0 and e = 3.0 at 500 × 999, 1,500 units.
  • Each unit is one analyze_trajectories at the case study's configuration: six covariates, rank floor 2, net displacement, df, harness CV. The split test and the scan are on and attribution is off. The plasmode's consistency check runs on every unit, and its latent check on the anchor.
  • Planted counts are recorded as counts only, with no feature names.
  • Rejection. The scan rejects at adjusted p ≤ 0.05 in both profiles. The six existing tests use their parent's rule (p < 0.05 in the simulation, p ≤ 0.05 in the plasmode), so every rate pairs with the parent's.
  • Code: 359f57f on feat/interaction-feature-scan, in a clean detached worktree on ing.
  • Cluster: partition 512x1024, arrays 936835 (simulation, 200 shards) and 936836 (plasmode, 150 shards), each throttled to 64 tasks. They ran on n1–n4 with n11 excluded and BLAS pinned to one thread. The fidelity gate passed on the cluster's export copy (rank 5, AUROC 0.635556).
  • Pre-flight:
  • the fast suite (2,528 passed);
  • a local smoke of both profiles at 2 × 19;
  • a timing run at 999 permutations: the scan alone takes 0.72 s at 80 × 10,000, under 1 % of a plasmode unit.

Details are in PROVENANCE.txt and openspec/changes/archive/2026-11-09-interaction-feature-scan/notes.md.

docs.title: 2. Accounting and reproduction
docs.text:
• Units: 8,100 of 8,100 complete, 0 failed, 0 duplicates; all 350 array tasks completed. Every plasmode anchor unit passed the latent check.
  • Compute: 69.6 recorded core-hours (simulation 22.6, plasmode 47.0), against the projection of 63 (budget 75), in 71 minutes of wall time. Unit medians were 11.5 s (simulation; the scan takes 0.067 s, 0.66 % of unit seconds) and 86 s (plasmode).
  • Reproduction. Both profiles reproduced the split-test validation exactly, in count and rejections:
  • Simulation: 252 rows, the three split parts' pseudo-F and delta/angle/shape for every design and cell, under p < 0.05.
  • Plasmode: 18 rows, the same per cell, under p ≤ 0.05.

The scan therefore pairs unit by unit with the split test and the trajectory statistics, and through them with the latent-space comparison and the plasmode.

docs.title: 3. The decision
docs.text:
interaction_scan_decision.json, rule version 1. S1–S3 use the stage-span paper grade's count-plus-ceiling rule. At R = 500 the per-cell bound is 0.0695, and the exceedance probability per rate is 0.030.

Criterion What m Rates Exceedances (allowed) Above ceiling Holds S1 simulation size: global scan at the anchor and translation of every design 6 0.048–0.058 0 (1) 0 yes S2 real-noise size: global scan at the plasmode anchor 1 0.042 0 (0) 0 yes S3 strong familywise control: units with a hit outside the planted set at e = 2.0 and 3.0 2 0.042, 0.042 0 (1) 0 yes G sparse gain at e = 3.0: the scan against the best of six existing tests, by more than 2 pooled SE — 1.000 against 0.048 (span) — — yes

S1. The six control rates:

Design Anchor Translation n200 0.056 0.052 seaad 0.054 0.048 seaad_weak 0.056 0.058

Translation is a constant group offset, which has no interaction, so it is a null for the scan.

S3. The 21 of 500 units with a false hit at each planted strength are the same replicates as the anchor's 21 global rejections (checked unit by unit on the per-unit records). Within a replicate the labels and the RRPP seed are shared across cells, and the plant changes only 20 features. So the null features' maxima are the anchor's, and step-down removes the planted features from the suffix only once they are rejected.

G. At e = 3.0 the existing tests read delta 0.026, angle 0.036, shape 0.016, and the split test's total 0.042, span 0.048 and complement 0.018. The comparator is the largest of the six, chosen after the fact, which is the conservative choice. The difference is 0.952 with a pooled SE of 0.0096.

Verdict: scan_validated. The consequence: a case study may report the per-feature interaction scan, read as the measurement-visibility page states. No verdict reopens Phase 6 or changes its attribution leg. The plasmode's attribution_leg_failed stands, and the scan is a new test with its own claim.

docs.title: 4. Real noise: power and recovery on the plasmode
docs.text:
Cell Scan delta angle shape total span complement Recall Hit precision Top-20 precision Attribution top-20 (adjusted: observed / residual) e = 2.0 0.692 0.030 0.034 0.020 0.042 0.046 0.022 0.059 0.966 (346 units) 0.473 0.168 / 0.227 e = 3.0 1.000 0.026 0.036 0.016 0.042 0.048 0.018 0.525 0.995 (500 units) 0.887 0.344 / 0.432
  • Source and grade. Everything except the last column comes from this run, 500 × 999 on the same units. The last column is the plasmode's committed attribution planted-set precision (2026-11-02, 500 × 999, B = 200), on the same metric.
  • Definitions. Recall is the planted features found, divided by 20. Hit precision is the planted share of hits, over units with any hit. Top-20 precision is the planted share of the 20 largest F.
  • The proposal's back-of-envelope calculation held. It assumed Gaussian noise and a Bonferroni bar, and was not a measurement. It gave each planted feature power 0.06 at e = 2.0 and 0.51 at e = 3.0, with at least one detected in 0.71 and 1.00 of units. The measured recall, 0.059 and 0.525, is the per-feature power. The global rates are 0.692 and 1.000.
  • e = 2.0 is detectable but thin. The median unit has one hit. The scan says that the groups differ by stage on some feature, and names about one of the 20.
  • Ranking. The scan's ranking recovers the plant better than attribution's at both strengths, without a latent space and without needing a prior global rejection.

docs.title: 5. Block balance
docs.text:
If every feature were equally likely to give a draw's maximum, a block's share of null maxima would equal its share of features. It does not:

Profile Cell Block Share of features Share of null maxima plasmode anchor ATAC 0.500 0.618 plasmode anchor RNA 0.500 0.382 simulation anchor (n200, seaad, seaad_weak) methylation 0.737 0.501, 0.506, 0.506 simulation anchor (n200, seaad, seaad_weak) expression 0.263 0.499, 0.494, 0.494
  • In the simulation, the methylation share stays at 0.497–0.523 in every cell. Methylation features are strongly correlated through the generator's coupling, so they act as fewer independent tests and win the maximum less often.
  • On the SEA-AD export, ATAC takes more maxima than its share. Its per-feature null F has the heavier tail, or its features are less correlated. The shares are near-identical across the plasmode's cells (0.6178, 0.6178, 0.6177), because the plant changes 20 of 10,000 features.
  • Consequence. Validity is unaffected: S2 and S3 hold on this export. But the common familywise threshold is set more by ATAC's null than by RNA's, so a difference of a given size is somewhat harder to detect on RNA features than per-block thresholds would make it. At e = 3.0 the hits are still balanced (5.27 ATAC, 5.30 RNA per unit, against 10 planted per block).
  • Follow-up. The design named per-block maxima as the follow-up if the balance were materially off. On the export it is (0.62 / 0.38).

docs.text:
The global scan beside the split test's parts and the production statistics, on the same units. The rates are this run's: the scan is judged at p ≤ 0.05 and the others at p < 0.05. Anchors and translations are at 500 replicates, other cells at 100.

The full table, every design and cell, is simulation/comparator_table.csv.

  • The design's prediction was half wrong. It said the scan would trail the complement on the dense φ = 90 rotation, which spreads over hundreds of features. That holds at e = 0.25 on the SEA-AD table (0.16 against 0.31). At e = 0.5 the scan ties the complement at n = 200 (1.00) and beats it on the SEA-AD table (0.96 against 0.68). At n = 200 it also beats the complement at e = 0.25 (0.76 against 0.29). With 498 features the search costs little.
  • The scan is weak where a difference spreads thinly over many features. Magnitude reads 0.09 / 0.01 against delta's 0.74 / 0.21, and the weak SEA-AD bend 0.20 against shape's 0.70.
  • It is strong on in-span rotation: 1.00 against angle's 0.47 on the SEA-AD table at e = 0.25.
  • The tests are complementary: each targets a different spread of the difference across features.
  • At the weak design nothing has power, the scan included. The non-control cells read 0.07–0.08 against controls of 0.056–0.058: the stage-span plants scale with a stage signal that barely exists there.

docs.title: 7. Simulation false hits
docs.text:
The rate of units with a hit on a population-null feature (a feature whose population B − A difference is constant across stages), among the units at cells that have such features (R = 100):

  • n200: 0.02–0.04 over the eight signal cells with population-null features.
  • seaad: 0.00–0.03 over the same eight cells.
  • seaad_weak: 0.00–0.08, where the plant is negligible and the global rate itself is 0.07–0.08.

At the anchor and translation every feature is population-null, so the rate is the global rate (§3, S1). At the φ = 30° and 60° rotations no feature is population-null. These are the generator-noise analogue of S3. They are descriptive and stay within α + 2 SE at R = 100 (0.094) in every cell.

docs.title: 8. What follows
docs.text:
• Case-study use. Under scan_validated, sead_sexdiff may apply the scan to both SEA-AD cell types in its own change. It must pin MOTCO 0.20.0 and fix its multiplicity policy across the scan, the split test and the trajectory statistics before any real-label analysis.
  • Reading. A hit names a feature whose covariate-adjusted group difference changes across stages, with the familywise error rate over the scanned features controlled at 0.05. A scan without hits is uninformative unless power is shown. At the plasmode's design that power is 0.69 for a 20-feature ramp to 2 SDs and 1.00 at 3 SDs.
  • Possible follow-ups, each its own change if proposed:
  • per-block maxima, since the export's null maxima split 0.62 / 0.38;
  • a moderated statistic, if a case study needs more than the measured per-feature power: 0.06 at 2 SDs, 0.53 at 3 SDs.
  • Phase 6. Its attribution leg stays failed (item 12). The scan answers a different question, which features differ and not why the latent trajectory differs, and it is not a rescue of that rule.

docs.title: 9. Limitations
docs.text:
• The plant is stylized: 20 features, one group, a stage ramp. G is a statement about the documented gap, not about realistic power.
  • Real-noise size and familywise control are conditional on one data matrix (the cohort_30 export) and two effect sizes. The simulation gives unconditional size, but at 498 features, not 10,000.
  • The F is the plain per-feature F, not a variance-moderated one. At n = 80 it is noisy (§4).
  • The null maxima are imbalanced across blocks (§5). The threshold leans on the block with the heavier null tail.
  • Hits are detections, not drivers. Correlated neighbours of a differing feature can be hits too, and the scan says nothing about the latent trajectory.
  • The scan has no geometry. It says which features differ by stage, never how the trajectories differ.

docs.title: Interaction scan by block — findings report (2026-11-10)
docs.text:
Change: interaction-scan-block-maxima (MOTCO 0.23.0). Reads: results/interaction-scan-blocks-2026-11-10/ (interaction_scan_blocks_decision.json, the simulation/, plasmode/ and plasmode_unequal/ scan, block, false-hit, paired, minP and allocation tables, accounting.json, reproduction.json, settings.json, PROVENANCE.txt, sacct.txt). Parent: the interaction-scan validation. Concept page: measurement visibility.

The per-feature interaction scan (MOTCO 0.20.0) takes one maximum F over every feature, so its familywise bar is set by whichever block tends to give the largest null F. On the SEA-AD export each block holds half the features, but ATAC gave 0.618 of the null maxima (parent, §5). With blocks of unequal size the larger block would set the bar almost alone.

The by-block combination (interaction_feature_scan(..., blocks=), motco analyze --interaction-scan-by-block) runs the scan's step-down max-T within each block, on the same draws, and splits the familywise error equally over the K blocks that have a non-degenerate feature (Bonferroni). A feature's adjusted p-value is K times its within-block adjusted p-value, capped at 1. The global p-value is K times the smallest block global p-value, capped at 1. A hit is a feature with adjusted p ≤ 0.05, so at K = 2 each block is tested at 0.025.

In one paragraph. The by-block scan is validated: by_block_validated. It holds size and familywise control, it keeps the joint scan's global power on both exports, and on an export with a small block it names more of the small block's planted features.

  • Size holds everywhere. The six simulation control rates read 0.046–0.058, against a per-cell bound of 0.0695. On real noise the global rates read 0.040 on the SEA-AD export and 0.044 on the unequal export.
  • Familywise control holds under the plasmode's partial null. A feature outside the planted set was a hit in 0.040 (SEA-AD export) and 0.044 (unequal export) of units, at both planted strengths.
  • No global power is lost. On the SEA-AD export both arms reject in 0.692 of units at e = 2.0 and in every unit at e = 3.0. On the unequal export the by-block scan rejects in 0.892 at e = 2.0, against the joint scan's 0.760.
  • The small block gains. On the unequal export (RNA cut to 500 of 5,000 features) the by-block arm finds more planted RNA features in 296 of 500 units at e = 2.0 and fewer in none. RNA recall rises from 0.069 to 0.158 at e = 2.0 and from 0.570 to 0.755 at e = 3.0.
  • The large block pays. ATAC recall falls from 0.076 to 0.058 at e = 2.0 and from 0.575 to 0.500 at e = 3.0 on the same export. On the SEA-AD export, with equal blocks, detection moves from ATAC to RNA at the same total.
  • Bonferroni costs little at K = 2. The block maxima correlate weakly (median Spearman 0.18–0.20 on the exports, at most 0.05 in the simulation), and a minP combination would have rejected at most 2 more units out of 500 in any cell.

docs.title: 1. Configuration and provenance
docs.text:
• Arms. Every unit runs two scans on the same inputs and draws: joint (the 0.20.0 scan, no labels) and by_block (labels from block__feature). Both reject at adjusted p ≤ 0.05.
  • Scan-only units. No unit fits a latent space. The scan reads the unweighted pooled-standardized features and the covariate-adjusted full and reduced models, built by the analysis's own input helper.
  • Simulation profile. The interaction-scan validation's 6,600 simulation units: the latent-space comparison's three designs (n200, seaad, and seaad_weak at δ = 0.11), methylation + expression (498 features, 0.263 of them expression), fourteen cells, base seed 2035. The anchor and translation ran 500 replicates, every other cell 100, all at 999 permutations. The settings were rebuilt through interaction_scan_check.simulation_settings and equal the parent's committed ones.
  • Plasmode profile. The interaction-scan validation's 1,500 SEA-AD plasmode units: the astrocyte cohort_30 export (5,000 RNA + 5,000 ATAC features) under the plasmode's contract, within-stage label permutation, the 20-feature plant (10 per block), base seed 2034, paper stream, the case study's six covariates and df. Cells: the anchor, e = 2.0 and e = 3.0 at 500 × 999.
  • Unequal profile (plasmode_unequal). The same export and units with RNA reduced to 500 of its 5,000 features: the first 500 positions of a seeded permutation (seed 455583459), kept in export order and recorded by the sha256 of the feature list. The plant still puts 10 features in each block. This is the unequal-size case the change is for, and it has no parent.
  • Records hold seeds, statistics and counts only.
  • Code: fe87330 on proposal/interaction-scan-block-maxima, in clean worktrees on the workstation and on ing.
  • Compute. The simulation profile ran on the workstation (AMD Ryzen 7 5800X, 8 workers). The two plasmode profiles ran on ing as arrays 937733 and 937734 (10 shards each, all on n4, n11 excluded, BLAS pinned to one thread), queued behind the production latent-space arrays. Job 937821 merged both and ran decide.
  • Pre-flight: a local smoke of all three profiles at 2 replicates per cell × 99 permutations, a serial timing at 999 permutations (projection 2.0 core-hours), and the change's test modules on ing (164 passed).

Details are in PROVENANCE.txt and openspec/changes/archive/2026-11-11-interaction-scan-block-maxima/notes.md.

docs.title: 2. Accounting and reproduction
docs.text:
• Units: 9,600 of 9,600 complete, 0 failed, 0 duplicates (6,600 simulation, 1,500 per plasmode profile); all 20 array tasks and the merge job completed.
  • Compute: 2.89 recorded core-hours (simulation 1.57, plasmode 0.94, unequal 0.38), against the projection of 2.0. Unit medians were 0.81 s (simulation), 2.23 s (plasmode) and 0.91 s (unequal). The parent run, which fitted a latent space in every unit, took 69.6.
  • Reproduction. The joint arm reproduced the interaction-scan validation exactly at the written precision, under p ≤ 0.05:
  • Simulation: 168 rows, the scan table's count, rejections and median hits, the block balance's mean hits and null-maximum share, and the population-null false-hit count and rejections, for every design and cell.
  • Plasmode: 11 rows, the same scan and block-balance columns, and the recovery table's false-hit count and rejections, recall, hit precision and top-20 precision.

The by-block arm therefore pairs unit by unit with the joint scan of the parent run, and through it with the split test and the plasmode.

interaction_scan_blocks_decision.json, rule version 1. S1–S3 use the stage-span paper grade's count-plus-ceiling rule. At R = 500 the per-cell bound is 0.0695, and the exceedance probability per rate is 0.030.

S1. The six control rates, with the joint arm's on the same units beside them:

Design Anchor (by block / joint) Translation (by block / joint) n200 0.052 / 0.056 0.052 / 0.052 seaad 0.046 / 0.054 0.048 / 0.048 seaad_weak 0.050 / 0.056 0.058 / 0.058

S2 and S3.

In each arm the count of units with an outside hit at e = 2.0 and 3.0 equals the anchor's count of global rejections (20 and 22 by block, 21 and 28 joint). The parent run found the same pattern and checked on its per-unit records that these are the same replicates: the labels and RRPP seed are shared across a replicate's cells and the plant changes only 20 features. Here only the counts are compared.

P. The paired global rejections (paired_table.csv):

Export Cell Both Joint only By block only Neither p_loss SEA-AD e = 2.0 337 9 9 145 0.593 SEA-AD e = 3.0 500 0 0 0 1.000 unequal e = 2.0 372 8 74 46 1.000 unequal e = 3.0 500 0 0 0 1.000

On the unequal export at e = 2.0 the by-block arm gains 74 units and loses 8 (descriptive gain p-value 8.2 × 10⁻¹⁵). The global rate rises from 0.760 to 0.892.

G. On the unequal export, per unit, the by-block arm's planted RNA hits minus the joint arm's (plasmode_unequal/allocation_table.csv):

Cell Gains Losses Ties Mean difference p_sign e = 2.0 296 0 204 +0.894 7.9 × 10⁻⁹⁰ e = 3.0 429 0 71 +1.854 7.2 × 10⁻¹³⁰

Verdict: by_block_validated. The decision's consequence: the by-block scan is validated for exports whose blocks differ in size or noise. It controls the familywise error over all scanned features at 0.05, split equally across the blocks, keeps the joint scan's global power and names more features of the small block. Only two blocks were measured. The joint scan stays the default, and the by-block combination stays opt-in.

docs.title: 4. Where the hits go: recall per block
docs.text:
Recall is the planted features found in a block divided by its 10. Hit precision is the planted share of the block's hits, over units with a hit in the block (block_table.csv).

Export Cell Block Recall (joint → by block) Mean hits (joint → by block) Hit precision (joint / by block) SEA-AD e = 2.0 ATAC 0.063 → 0.058 0.67 → 0.61 0.948 / 0.951 SEA-AD e = 2.0 RNA 0.056 → 0.060 0.58 → 0.63 0.979 / 0.978 SEA-AD e = 3.0 ATAC 0.523 → 0.500 5.27 → 5.04 0.994 / 0.994 SEA-AD e = 3.0 RNA 0.527 → 0.547 5.30 → 5.50 0.997 / 0.997 unequal e = 2.0 ATAC 0.076 → 0.058 0.83 → 0.61 0.932 / 0.951 unequal e = 2.0 RNA 0.069 → 0.158 0.69 → 1.60 0.995 / 0.989 unequal e = 3.0 ATAC 0.575 → 0.500 5.82 → 5.04 0.991 / 0.994 unequal e = 3.0 RNA 0.570 → 0.755 5.70 → 7.57 0.999 / 0.997
  • On the SEA-AD export the blocks are equal in size, so the change only redistributes. The by-block arm finds slightly fewer ATAC and slightly more RNA features. The total is unchanged: the mean of the two blocks' recall is 0.059 in both arms at e = 2.0, and 0.525 against 0.524 at e = 3.0. The per-unit allocation table agrees: RNA gains in 22 units and loses in none at e = 2.0, 89 against 6 at e = 3.0, while ATAC loses in 25 and 99 (plasmode/allocation_table.csv). The joint arm's totals equal the parent's committed recall (0.0594 and 0.525).
  • On the unequal export the small block gains much more than the large block loses. The mean of the two blocks' recall rises from 0.07 to 0.11 at e = 2.0 and from 0.57 to 0.63 at e = 3.0. Under the joint scan, a 500-feature RNA block faced a bar set by 5,500 features, 0.92 of whose null maxima came from ATAC. By block, RNA faces its own bar at 0.025.
  • Hit precision stays at 0.93 or above in both arms, in every block and cell.
  • The by-block ATAC rows are the same on both exports in every recall, hit, precision and false-hit column. That is as it should be: the within-block step-down reads only the block's own features and the shared draws, K is 2 on both exports, and ATAC and its plant are the same.

docs.title: 5. Block balance
docs.text:
The joint arm's share of null maxima per block, against its share of features, and the rate of units with a false hit in each block at the anchors, per arm (block_table.csv). Under the by-block scan each block's false-hit rate should be near α/K = 0.025.

Profile Design Block Share of features Share of null maxima (joint) False-hit units, joint False-hit units, by block plasmode — ATAC 0.500 0.618 0.034 0.030 plasmode — RNA 0.500 0.382 0.014 0.016 plasmode_unequal — ATAC 0.909 0.920 0.052 0.030 plasmode_unequal — RNA 0.091 0.080 0.004 0.016 simulation n200 methylation 0.737 0.501 0.038 0.036 simulation n200 expression 0.263 0.499 0.018 0.016 simulation seaad methylation 0.737 0.506 0.030 0.022 simulation seaad expression 0.263 0.494 0.024 0.024 simulation seaad_weak methylation 0.737 0.506 0.036 0.028 simulation seaad_weak expression 0.263 0.494 0.022 0.024
  • The joint scan spends its error unevenly. On the unequal export nearly all of its false hits fall in ATAC (0.052 against RNA's 0.004). On the SEA-AD export ATAC takes 0.034 against RNA's 0.014.
  • By block, the error is shared. Every by-block rate at the plasmode anchors is 0.016 or 0.030, on both exports.
  • In the simulation the joint shares were already near even, since correlated methylation features act as fewer tests (methylation's share of null maxima is 0.497–0.523 in every cell). There the two arms differ little.

docs.title: 6. What dependence between blocks would have bought: minP
docs.text:
The decision rule uses Bonferroni across blocks, which ignores dependence between the block maxima. The run measured a minP combination descriptively: each block maximum's tail probability under the block's own null maxima, combined by the smallest (minp_table.csv).

Profile Cell Joint Bonferroni (by block) minP Median Spearman of block maxima plasmode anchor 0.042 0.040 0.044 0.196 plasmode e = 2.0 0.692 0.692 0.694 0.196 plasmode e = 3.0 1.000 1.000 1.000 0.196 plasmode_unequal anchor 0.056 0.044 0.048 0.184 plasmode_unequal e = 2.0 0.760 0.892 0.896 0.182 plasmode_unequal e = 3.0 1.000 1.000 1.000 0.183
  • On the exports minP rejects at most 2 more units of 500 than Bonferroni (446 → 448 on the unequal export at e = 2.0), and 2 more at each anchor.
  • In the simulation minP equals Bonferroni in 40 of 42 cells and adds one unit of 100 in the other two (seaad orientation e = 0.25 at φ = 60° and 90°). The block maxima are nearly independent there: median Spearman −0.007 to 0.050.
  • Consequence. At K = 2, with weakly correlated block maxima, minP would not change any reading. The design named a minP global test as a follow-up only if the cost were material, and it is not.

docs.title: 7. Simulation: localization and false hits
docs.text:
The two arms' global rates on the simulation units (simulation/scan_table.csv, simulation/paired_table.csv):

  • They agree closely. No cell's rates differ by more than 0.03 (3 units of 100: n200 shape e = 0.25, 0.85 joint against 0.82 by block; seaad_weak orientation e = 0.25 at φ = 30°, 0.08 against 0.05). No cell has more than 6 discordant units.
  • Signal cells keep their power. Each cell where the joint scan had power reads within 0.03 by block: for example 0.76 at n200 orientation e = 0.25, φ = 90° in both arms, and 0.96 → 0.98 at seaad orientation e = 0.5, φ = 90°.
  • At the weak design, where nothing has power, the by-block arm reads 0.05–0.07 in the non-control cells, against the joint arm's 0.07–0.08.

The rate of units with a hit on a population-null feature, over the eight signal cells per design that have such features, at R = 100 (simulation/false_hit_table.csv):

Design Joint By block n200 0.02–0.04 0.02–0.05 seaad 0.00–0.03 0.00–0.01 seaad_weak 0.00–0.08 0.00–0.07

At the anchor and translation every feature is population-null, so the rate is the global rate (S1). These rates are descriptive and stay within α + 2 SE at R = 100 (0.094) in every cell.

docs.title: 8. What follows
docs.text:
• Reading a by-block hit. It names a feature whose covariate-adjusted group difference changes across stages, with the familywise error over all scanned features controlled at 0.05, as for the joint scan. The difference is in who gets the error: each of the K blocks is tested at 0.05/K, whatever its size or noise.
  • When to use it. When the blocks differ in size, or their noise is known to differ. On the unequal export the by-block scan named more planted features of the small block in 296 of 500 units at e = 2.0 and lost none, and it raised the global rate from 0.760 to 0.892. With equal blocks it mostly redistributes detection between them.
  • What it costs. The larger or noisier block's features face a stricter bar: ATAC recall fell from 0.575 to 0.500 at e = 3.0 on the unequal export. With many small blocks each would get only 0.05/K. Only K = 2 was measured.
  • Default. The joint scan stays the default; the by-block combination is opt-in (interaction_scan_by_block, --interaction-scan-by-block). A default flip would change sead_sexdiff's pinned reading and needs its own change.
  • Case-study use. sead_sexdiff may read the scan by block in its own change. It must pin MOTCO 0.23.0 and fix its multiplicity policy across the scan, the split test and the trajectory statistics before any real-label analysis. Its SEA-AD exports have equal blocks, where §4 shows the by-block scan trades ATAC detection for RNA detection at the same total.
  • Not needed: a minP global test at K = 2 (§6).

docs.title: 9. Limitations
docs.text:
• Two blocks only. The Bonferroni split's cost grows with K, and no export with more blocks was run.
  • The unequal export is a construction: a seeded random 500 of the RNA features, with the real noise. It tests a count imbalance with RNA's lighter null tail. A small ATAC block was not run.
  • The plant is stylized: 20 features, 10 per block, one group, a stage ramp. The allocation gain is a statement about that plant.
  • Real-noise size and familywise control are conditional on one data matrix and its subset, and on two effect sizes. The simulation gives unconditional size, at 498 features.
  • Within-block subset pivotality is approximate under Freedman–Lane with covariates, as for the joint scan. S3 measures strong control on real noise in both exports.
  • Hits are detections, not drivers, and the scan has no geometry, as in the parent report.

docs.title: Latent-adjustment power comparison — 2026-10-20
docs.text:
Paper-grade power comparison of covariate-aware latent construction against the 0.8.0 covariate-blind basis at the Phase 6 SEA-AD design (openspec/changes/covariate-aware-latent-construction/, design D9, spec latent-adjustment-validation). It is the companion of the Type I check, which admitted stage conditioning. Every number below is read from results/latent-adjustment-power-2026-10-20/ (latent_adjustment_power_decision.json, latent_adjustment_power_rates.csv, latent_adjustment_power_pvalues.csv, merged.jsonl). Rates are rejection rates at p ≤ 0.05 over the available replicates of 500, at 999 permutations. The Monte Carlo SE is at most 0.024.

Run: 14,000 units of three analyses on ing (SLURM array 923444, 200 shards, 158 recorded core-hours, no failed task), from 979657c plus this change's working tree; file hashes are in PROVENANCE.txt. Advisory verdicts: stage candidate_fails, group_stage candidate_fails.

In one paragraph. stage conditioning gains a lot of orientation power. At the top effect, angle rejects 0.922 against the covariate-blind basis's 0.784 with a covariate-aligned nuisance axis, and 0.931 against 0.642 without one. It fails the predeclared rule for three reasons:

  • it loses shape power at the top shape effect when the nuisance axis is present (0.243 against 0.428);
  • it loses power for small magnitude effects and on delta under shape effects, without the nuisance axis (for example 0.400 against 0.520 at magnitude e = 0.1);
  • its translation control rejects angle at 0.085–0.092, above the bound. The covariate-blind basis is above its own bound there too (0.076–0.086).

group_stage conditioning loses most of the orientation and shape power in both columns: angle 0.344 and shape 0.054 at the top effects with the nuisance axis. With the Type I check's angle excess, it is ruled out. No arm in either column ever selected rank 1. Latent adjustment is therefore not a uniform power improvement. It trades shape and small-magnitude sensitivity for orientation sensitivity in this construction, which §6 turns into conditions for the case study.

docs.title: 1. Construction
docs.text:
• Cells. The zero-effect anchor, the translation control at e = 1.0, and three modes at the Phase 6 effect levels:
  • magnitude (joint) at e = 0.02, 0.05, 0.10 and 0.25, below its saturation;
  • orientation at e = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0;
  • shape at e = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0.
  • The design, blocks and estimator are the Type I check's (§1).
  • Columns.
  • nuisance: the Type I check's calibrated injection (s_z = 40, s_c = 2).
  • clean: s_z = s_c = 0. The same eight covariates are declared, but none affects the features.
  • Matched seeds. The generator, covariate and RRPP seeds depend on the replicate index only. Within a replicate, the two columns share the generated blocks and covariates and differ only in the injection. Every cell starts from the same baseline trajectory, and the arms share the dataset and the RRPP seed. The nuisance column's anchor is therefore the Type I check itself, and its rates reproduce that report's to the third decimal.
  • Arms. baseline (covariates in the trajectory model only, covariate-blind basis), stage and group_stage.
  • Rule (fixed in the hashed settings before the run; the study engine's column_decision convention). Each residualized arm is compared against baseline. The pooled SE is √(SE_arm² + SE_baseline²) and the bound is 0.05 + 2·√(0.05·0.95/R).
  • gain: nuisance column, orientation/angle at e = 1.0: rate_arm − rate_baseline > 2 · pooled SE;
  • protected: nuisance column, magnitude/delta at e = 0.25 and shape/shape at e = 1.0: rate_baseline − rate_arm ≤ 2 · pooled SE;
  • no loss: clean column, every statistic at every effect of every mode: the same loss tolerance;
  • controls: both columns, anchor and translation, every statistic at or below the bound.

D9 also listed magnitude/delta and shape/shape as gain targets. The spec's single gain target is the one applied, because magnitude/delta is at 0.92 or above in every arm and column at its top effect and has little room to gain.

The same 52 (stage) and 38 (group_stage) replicates are unavailable in every cell. Each loses a factor level from a CV training fold, which depends only on the covariates and the folds (Type I report §2). So R = 448 for stage, 462 for group_stage and 500 for baseline throughout.

docs.title: 3. The verdicts
docs.text:
From latent_adjustment_power_decision.json.

stage — candidate_fails.

  • gain: passes. 0.922 against 0.784, difference 0.138 > 0.045.
  • protected: magnitude/delta passes (0.969 against 0.940). shape/shape fails: 0.243 against 0.428, a loss of 0.185 against a tolerance of 0.060.
  • no loss (clean column) fails in eight reads:
  • magnitude/delta at e = 0.02, 0.05 and 0.10: 0.042, 0.121 and 0.400 against 0.076, 0.180 and 0.520;
  • delta under orientation at e = 0.25: 0.029 against 0.066;
  • delta under shape at all four effects: for example 0.214 against 0.298 at e = 1.0.
  • Every other clean-column read holds. That includes shape/shape, which gains: 0.250 against 0.128 at e = 1.0.
  • controls: translation/angle exceeds in both columns (0.092 and 0.085 against 0.0706). Every other control holds.

group_stage — candidate_fails. The gain fails (0.344 against 0.784) and shape/shape fails as a protected pair (0.054 against 0.428). Nine clean-column no-loss reads fail, all under orientation or shape effects. Seven controls exceed the bound: anchor angle in both columns at 0.082, anchor shape in the clean column, and translation angle and shape in both columns.

Pooled over the 14 cells of each column, as a share of the available units:
