PC1's low-tercile collapse (Phase 6 0.114; the Phase 6 report's "the cohort's own eigengap carries an orientation statement") is gone: net displacement does not need a well-determined principal axis. At e ≤ 0.75 its Phase 6 terciles are flat (0.08–0.21).

Rank still gates power at the Phase 6 maximum. Computed from merged.jsonl (integration_metadata.selected_lv): at Phase 6 orientation e = 1.0, 257 of 500 replicates retain more than three components (as in the parent study).

selected rank replicates PC1 net displacement ≤ 3 243 0.082 0.280 > 3 257 0.506 0.996

At e ≤ 0.75 every replicate retains at most three components and power is 0.084–0.178. The estimator raises power in both rank strata. The headline 0.648 is the mixture, and it depends on how often CV retains the group-specific variation the maximal construction creates, which the Phase 6 report found a six-donor change moves from 51 % to 8 %. At Phase 5 the rank is 2–4 throughout and power does not depend on it.

docs.title: 5. Acceptance targets (baseline column, descriptive)
docs.text:
From acceptance_report.csv. The profiles declare upper-bound Type I and specificity targets on the baseline column; the gate is off and the column rule does not read them.

  • Phase 6: all eleven targets met.
  • Phase 5: ten of eleven met. translation/shape in the type_i_baseline cell is 0.070 against 0.0695 (one rejection over), failing both type_i_control and specificity[translation, shape]. That cell is independently seeded, measured in the baseline column, and shape does not depend on the orientation estimator. The Type I study's Phase 5 type_i_baseline translation cell recorded the same rate (0.036 / 0.056 / 0.070), and the matched-seed translation cells here are 0.030–0.046 on shape at every effect. It is a Monte Carlo excursion at the bound in a statistic this comparison does not touch, not an estimator effect.

docs.title: 6. Consistency checks
docs.text:
From consistency_checks.json (scripts/net_displacement_power_checks.py, checks version 2).

(a) delta and shape are identical between the two columns. The estimator enters only _estimate_orientation, so the two columns' delta and shape cannot differ. Over 8,500 paired records per design (17,000 comparisons): 0 p-value mismatches at both designs. Observed statistics are bit-identical in 11,668 (Phase 6) and 9,221 (Phase 5) comparisons and differ in the rest by at most 9.0 × 10⁻¹¹ and 5.4 × 10⁻¹⁰ relative: BLAS rounding across separate processes, inside the checks' 1 × 10⁻⁹ tolerance and never enough to move a p-value.

(b) The baseline column reproduces the parent studies. It shares their generator seeds, evaluation parameters and RRPP seed, so wherever a parent record of the same mode, effect and replicate exists, its seed and p-values must be equal.

design parent records compared seed / p-value mismatches observed bit-identical max rel. diff. Phase 6 phase6-small-n-2026-10-09 6,500 0 / 0 5,285 3.1 × 10⁻⁸ Phase 6 phase6-small-n-magnitude-2026-10-09 2,000 0 / 0 1,167 3.1 × 10⁻⁸ Phase 5 phase5-2026-09-10 6,500 0 / 0 2,981 4.7 × 10⁻¹⁰ Phase 5 phase5-magnitude-2026-10-08 1,500 0 / 0 897 5.1 × 10⁻¹¹

8,000 of 8,500 (Phase 6) and 7,500 of 8,500 (Phase 5) baseline records have a parent. The uncovered cells are the new ones the design names: Phase 6 magnitude 0.75; Phase 5 magnitude 0.5 and 0.75. The 2,000 magnitude records of phase5-2026-09-10 are excluded from the comparison: that run generated magnitude under magnitude_kind: all, so its magnitude datasets differ despite equal seeds. The joint-construction parent phase5-magnitude-2026-10-08 covers magnitude 0.25 and 1.0.

The PC1 column's numbers are therefore the parent studies' recorded rates (e.g. Phase 6 orientation/angle 0.300, Phase 6 shape/angle 0.138), and the two columns are paired measurements of the same 500 datasets per cell.

Checks history. The first pass (checks version 1, db5ab69) exited 1 on both designs for two reasons, both in the checks rather than the records: (a) required bit-identical observed statistics and flagged the rounding above; (b) compared the Phase 5 joint-magnitude cells against the magnitude_kind: all parent (4,000 spurious p-value mismatches, all in magnitude). 1ccded5 adds the 1 × 10⁻⁹ tolerance and pairs parent records only within one magnitude construction (truth_metadata.transform.magnitude_kind); no record changed.

docs.title: 7. Decision and interpretability
docs.text:
comparison_decision.json (rule version 1; inputs phase6/report/column_decision.json sha256 c980fafb…, phase5/report/column_decision.json sha256 bdc3135e…):

  • Phase 6 candidate_qualifies (gain); Phase 5 candidate_qualifies (no_loss);
  • verdict adopt_net_displacement.

The verdict selects the follow-up change: flip SimulationEvaluationParams.orientation_estimator's production default to net_displacement in a separate change that re-pins the committed signatures, as default-joint-magnitude-construction did. Until that change lands, the default and every committed result stay PC1.

What angle means changes. Under net displacement, angle is the angle between the two groups' net displacement vectors (last stage mean − first stage mean) in the latent space, not between their principal axes. It reads only the endpoint stages. The paper and the case study must describe it that way.

Revised angle statement for the SEA-AD cohort (n = 80, ≥30 nuclei, RNA + ATAC), replacing the angle row of the Phase 6 report §8 once the default flips:

statistic rejection may be reported as evidence? non-rejection may be reported as evidence? angle Yes, that the groups' net directions of change differ. Type I is controlled (anchor 0.050; Type I study 0.048–0.058 in every space). Unlike PC1, the size, shape and location constructions do not move it: 0.024–0.068 at every effect, all within the bound, against PC1's up to 0.138 under shape. The translation construction sits at 0.058–0.068, near the bound, so a rejection alongside a location difference warrants care. The cohort's eigengap no longer conditions the statement. No. Power is 0.084–0.178 at e ≤ 0.75. At the construction maximum it is 0.648 overall, but 0.280 when CV retains three or fewer components (243 of 500 replicates) and 0.996 above that. Report the cohort's selected rank beside any angle result. A non-rejection is uninformative at n = 80.

At the Phase 5 design (n = 1200) angle has power 0.92–0.95 at every effect and is specific: shape → angle falls from 0.80 to 0.02. The orientation construction is still detected by shape (0.998–1.000) and delta (0.80–0.91) at Phase 5, and at Phase 6 by shape (0.464) and delta (0.354) at e = 1.0. Those are properties of the construction and of the other two statistics, which this change does not touch. The delta and shape rows of the Phase 6 statement are unchanged.

The rank-stratified and paired-outcome numbers (§2, §4) come from merged.jsonl:

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from motco.simulations.grid import read_replicate_results
from motco.simulations.study.spectrum import record_design_point

def angle_frame(merged):
    rows = []
    for r in read_replicate_results(Path(merged)):
        if r.phase == "type_i_baseline":
            continue
        rows.append({
            "est": (record_design_point(r) or {}).get("evaluation.orientation_estimator") or "pc1",
            "mode": r.cell_metadata["trajectory_mode"], "e": r.cell_metadata["effect_size"],
            "rep": r.replicate_index, "rej": r.p_values["angle"] < 0.05,
            "lv": r.integration_metadata["selected_lv"],
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

d = angle_frame("results/net-displacement-power-2026-10-14/phase6/merged.jsonl")
o = d[(d["mode"] == "orientation") & (d.e == 1.0)]
print(o.assign(high=o.lv > 3).groupby(["high", "est"]).rej.agg(["mean", "size"]))      # §4 rank table
print(pd.crosstab(*o.pivot(index="rep", columns="est", values="rej").T.values))      # §2 paired counts

docs.title: Net-displacement Type I study — 2026-10-13
docs.text:
Paper-grade, null-only re-measurement of the net-displacement orientation estimator (openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-13-net-displacement-type-i-study/). It settles the Type I question that the orientation measurement probe left open. It runs no power cell, makes no power claim, and changes no production default. Every rate below is read from results/net-displacement-type-i-2026-10-13/{phase6,phase5}/report/ (anchor_decision.csv/.json, design_point_operating.csv, type_i_table.csv, acceptance_report.csv) and results/net-displacement-type-i-2026-10-13/follow_up_decision.json. Rates are rejection rates at p < 0.05 over 500 replicates × 999 permutations (Monte Carlo SE about 0.0097 at 0.05).

Runs: results/net-displacement-type-i-2026-10-13/phase6/ (SLURM array 917290) and …/phase5/ (array 917291) on ing · Code: 9089729 · Anchor decision: size_holds at every column at both designs · Follow-up: paper_grade_power_comparison.

In one paragraph. The probe found the net-displacement anchor angle rate at 0.08–0.10 in every space at both designs, against 0.01–0.05 under PC1, over 100 replicates. At 500 replicates × 999 permutations that excess does not reproduce. Every net-displacement column holds the predeclared bound 0.05 + 2·√(0.05·0.95/500) = 0.0695 on delta, angle and shape, at both designs. The lead arm, pls_cv × net_displacement, has anchor angle 0.050 at Phase 6 and 0.050 at Phase 5. Net displacement does move the anchor angle rate from conservative toward nominal at Phase 6 (PC1 0.024, net displacement 0.048–0.058); it is a size change within the bound, not an excess. The predeclared rule therefore selects the paper-grade power comparison of pls_cv × net_displacement against pls_cv × pc1. One caveat carries forward: under net displacement the translation control's angle rate sits near or above the anchor bound in some columns (Phase 6 concat 0.078), so the comparison should hold that control to the same bound (§5).

docs.title: 1. Design
docs.text:
• Columns: five explicit design points (design_grid.points) on matched datasets:
column integration_method forced_components n_components orientation_estimator pls_cv × pc1 (baseline) pls — (CV) — pc1 pls_cv × nd (lead arm) pls — (CV) — net_displacement pls_forced × nd pls 2(K − 1): 4 / 6 — net_displacement pca × nd pca — 2(K − 1): 4 / 6 net_displacement concat × nd (ceiling reference) concat — — net_displacement

The fixed-basis pls_within_group arm is excluded (the probe identified why its anchor inflates). - Designs: - Phase 6 (examples/trajectory_power_study/net_displacement_type_i_phase6.json): three stages, group_stage_sizes = [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]], methylation + expression, base seed 800, family phase6-small-n. - Phase 5 (net_displacement_type_i_phase5.json): n = 1200, four stages, group_ratio 0.5, all three blocks, base seed 600, family phase5-primary. - Both use p_dmp = 0.1, ρ = 0, joint magnitude and surgery_censoring = error. - Cells (12 per design): per column, the shared zero-effect anchor (none, e = 0) and the translation negative control at e = 1.0, plus the engine's two type_i_baseline cells (independently seeded, measured in the baseline column). - Seeds: every column evaluates the same datasets at each replicate index. evaluation.seed is the constant 3 and is also the RRPP seed, so every column draws the same permutation indices, and the baseline column re-computes the parent studies' records (§4). - Rule: acceptance.anchor_decision (rule version 1): per column and statistic, anchor rate ≤ α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/R) with α = 0.05 and R the available replicates (0.0695 at R = 500). A column is size_holds when all three statistics hold. Advisory; it feeds neither the gate (off) nor the acceptance targets.

delta and shape do not depend on the estimator: in the two pls_cv columns they are the same records' statistics and their rates are identical, as they must be. The fixed-rank and label-free spaces are conservative on delta and shape at both designs; that is a property of those spaces, not of the estimator, and no rule here reads it.

Against the probe. The probe's lead-arm anchor angle rates were 0.100 (Phase 6) and 0.080 (Phase 5) over 100 replicates × 199 permutations, on its own seed root (base seed 900), so its datasets are independent of these. Here the rate is 0.050 at both designs. Split into five consecutive blocks of 100 replicates, the lead arm's Phase 6 anchor angle rate ranges from 0.01 to 0.09 (0.06, 0.09, 0.01, 0.04, 0.05), and at Phase 5 from 0.02 to 0.07 (0.07, 0.04, 0.02, 0.05, 0.07); a 100-replicate rate of 0.08–0.10 is within that sampling spread. The probe's excess was Monte Carlo noise at R = 100, which is what the probe report said it could not exclude.

Net displacement narrows the angle null by a factor of 7–8 in the pls_cv space (Phase 6 84.0° → 12.1°, Phase 5 5.5° → 0.7°) and removes most of its across-replicate dispersion (Phase 6 IQR 115° → 27°), which is the PC1 sign/flip tail the probe described. A narrower null is consistent with size holding: the test calibrates against its own permutation distribution.

Reproduction. The baseline column shares the parent study's generator seeds and evaluation parameters, including the RRPP seed, so it re-computes the parent's records:

  • Phase 6: all 1,000 baseline records (anchor and translation, replicates 0–499) equal results/phase6-small-n-2026-10-09/merged.jsonl in generator seed, p-values and observed statistics. The two type_i_baseline cells carry the parent's cell ids and reproduce its 1,000 records' p-values exactly.
  • Phase 5: all 1,000 baseline records equal results/phase5-2026-09-10/merged.jsonl in generator seed, selected rank and p-values. Observed statistics are bit-identical in 317 records and differ in the rest by at most 2.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ relative (floating point; the parent ran at b8f7daa), never enough to change a p-value. The type_i_baseline cells are new (magnitude_kind enters their ids).

The baseline anchor rates therefore equal the parent studies' recorded rates (Phase 6 0.026 / 0.024 / 0.020; Phase 5 0.036 / 0.046 / 0.048), and the five columns are paired measurements of the same 500 datasets per design.

anchor_decision.json, both designs: size_holds at all five columns. follow_up_decision.json (rule version 1, inputs phase6/report/anchor_decision.json sha256 a0af9d20…, phase5/report/anchor_decision.json sha256 89e8e449…):

  • localization none at both designs (no net-displacement column exceeds).

The verdict selects the next change: a paper-grade power comparison of pls_cv × net_displacement against pls_cv × pc1 at both designs, through the study engine (the estimator is now a contracted design axis, so the comparison is one explicit-points config per design over the Phase 5 / Phase 6 power grids). The anchor-excess diagnosis is not needed. Two points to carry into that change:

  1. Hold the translation control to the anchor bound. Under net displacement the translation angle rate is 0.068 for the lead arm at Phase 6 (bound 0.0695) and 0.058–0.078 in the other spaces; Phase 6 concat (0.078) would exceed the bound if it were judged by it. The lead arm passes at both designs, but by one rejection at Phase 6, so the comparison should declare translation angle as a mandatory control rather than leave it descriptive.
  2. concat stays the ceiling reference, not a candidate, and its p-padding question remains open; this study's null-only design cannot answer it.

docs.title: Orientation measurement probe — 2026-10-12
docs.text:
Exploratory, matched-seed probe (openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-12-orientation-measurement-probe/). It ranks measurement arms for a paper-grade follow-up. It certifies none of them and changes no production default. Every rate below is read from results/orientation-measurement-probe-2026-10-12/ (rate_table.csv, checkpoint_table.csv, advancement_decision.json, summary.md). The motivating evidence in §1 is read from evidence/phase6_checkpoint_evidence.md, produced by scripts/orientation_checkpoint_evidence.py. Rates are rejection rates at p < 0.05 over 100 replicates (Monte Carlo SE about 0.022 at 0.05 and 0.05 at 0.5).

Run: results/orientation-measurement-probe-2026-10-12/ · Driver: scripts/orientation_measurement_probe.py at 49134c3 · Decision: no arm advances (advancement_decision.json, advisory).

In one paragraph. Two levers were crossed on the same datasets: the measurement space (five spaces) and the orientation estimator (PC1 or net displacement). The estimator turned out to be the larger lever. In the production stage-PLS space, net displacement more than doubles orientation/angle power at the Phase 6 SEA-AD design (0.29 → 0.67). At Phase 5 it removes the shape construction's leak into angle (0.89 → 0.02), and it costs no other power or specificity. That arm fails the predeclared rule on one criterion only: its Phase 6 anchor angle rate is 0.100, against a bound of 0.0936. Every net-displacement arm shows a similar anchor excess at both designs (0.08–0.10, against 0.01–0.05 under PC1). At 100 replicates this is suggestive, not established, and it is the question the follow-up must settle first. The alternative spaces do not help on their own terms: - pls_within_group without a per-permutation refit is invalid (anchor angle up to 0.88). - pca and pls_forced at rank 2(K − 1) recover the rotation, but they lose Phase 6 shape power (0.19 → 0.00–0.01) and leak angle into the shape or magnitude cells.

docs.title: 1. Motivating evidence
docs.text:
From evidence/phase6_checkpoint_evidence.md (Phase 6 small-n orientation profile, baseline column, results/phase6-small-n-2026-10-09/merged.jsonl, sha256 6a91a47e…):

e population (native methylation) observed std. PLS latent, rank ≤ 3 PLS latent, rank > 3 angle rate (≤ 3 / > 3) 0.25 41.4° 58.3° 21.6° — 0.034 / — 0.50 60.0° 71.5° 24.8° — 0.058 / — 0.75 75.7° 81.8° 28.5° — 0.090 / — 1.00 90.0° 89.8° 32.1° (n = 243) 76.0° (n = 257) 0.082 / 0.506

The surgery realizes arccos(1 − e) exactly in the population, and the observed standardized space keeps it. The stage-supervised PLS space collapses it unless CV keeps more than three components. The signed anchor angle has a heavy tail: q95 = 137.1° in the observed space and 135.6° in the latent space. On that oracle threshold the signed observed angle separates e = 1 from the anchor in 0.000 of replicates, and its folded counterpart in 0.996 (0.496 in the latent space).

docs.title: 2. Design and provenance
docs.text:
• Arms: five spaces × two estimators, giving ten arms:
  • Spaces: pls_cv (production stage-PLS, CV rank; with PC1 this is the reference arm); pls_forced (stage-PLS at rank 2(K − 1)); pls_within_group (K − 1 components per group, fixed basis, no refit inside RRPP); pca (rank 2(K − 1)); and concat (ceiling reference, never eligible).
  • Estimators: pc1 and net_displacement.
  • Designs:
  • Phase 6 SEA-AD: three stages, group_stage_sizes = [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]], methylation + expression measured.
  • Phase 5: n = 1200, four stages, all three blocks measured.
  • Both use p_dmp = 0.1, ρ = 0, joint magnitude and surgery_censoring = error.
  • Deviation: the Phase 5 design uses the joint magnitude construction, not the methylation-only all pinned in phase5_power_study.json. The reference arm's rates are recomputed here, and every comparison is against them.
  • Cells: the anchor; orientation at e = 0.5 and 1.0; magnitude and shape at e = 1.0. Each cell has 100 replicates × 199 permutations.
  • Seeds: the generator seed is matched across cells per (design, replicate). One RRPP seed per unit is shared by all ten arms, so arms differ only in measurement.
  • Run: SLURM array 912606 on ing, 50 shards. 1,000/1,000 units and 10,000 arm records, with 0 failures. It took 28.2 recorded core-hours, 28 % over the 22 core-hour budget written before launch (PROVENANCE.txt).

docs.title: 4. Where the rotation is lost
docs.text:
From checkpoint_table.csv: median realized angle at orientation e = 1.0, and the median retained rank.

arm Phase 6 latent Phase 6 rank Phase 5 latent Phase 5 rank pls_cv__pc1 63.9° 4 72.0° 3 pls_cv__net_displacement 56.7° 4 6.1° 3 pls_forced__pc1 71.1° 4 89.5° 6 pca__pc1 90.5° 4 90.2° 6 pls_within_group__pc1 90.3° 4 90.2° 6

The population angle is 90.0° and the observed standardized angle is 89.7–90.3° in every arm.

  • Label-free and two-sided spaces keep the full rotation. pca and pls_within_group reproduce the observed angle. The CV stage-PLS space shrinks it.
  • Phase 5 under net displacement. The pls_cv latent angle is only 6.1°, yet the test still rejects in 0.89 of replicates, because its anchor median is 0.3°. In a rank-3 = K − 1 space shared by both groups, the two net displacements are nearly parallel, and a small, consistent rotation is still resolvable.

docs.text:

Advancing set: empty.

docs.title: 6. Findings
docs.text:
1. The estimator, not the space, is the main lever.
  2. In the production pls_cv space, net displacement raises Phase 6 orientation power from 0.29 to 0.67. That is +0.38, against a 2-SE margin of 0.13.
  3. It leaves delta and shape power unchanged at both designs.
  4. It removes the largest specificity failure the probe saw: shape → angle at Phase 5, from 0.89 to 0.02.
  5. This matches the mechanism in §1. The signed PC1 angle's heavy null tail comes from PC1 swapping or flipping on near-isotropic configurations, and net displacement does not have that failure mode.
  6. Net displacement shows an anchor excess at both designs, in every space.
  7. Anchor angle rates are 0.08–0.10 for every non-pls_within_group space, against 0.01–0.05 under PC1.
  8. The four spaces share datasets and permutation draws, so their rates are not independent. In effect, the evidence is about 9/100 per design, where 5/100 is expected.
  9. That is suggestive at 100 replicates, but not established. The pls_cv arm misses the bound by less than one rejection.
  10. The mechanism is not identified. One hypothesis, not tested here: the estimator uses only the first and last stages. RRPP permutes reduced-model residuals across all stages, so if the endpoint stages are noisier than the interior ones, the permutation null would be too narrow.
  11. A fixed pls_within_group basis is not a valid test space without a refit. Anchor angle reaches 0.48–0.88. The basis is fitted to the observed groups' own stage directions, and so it carries their noise. The permuted data are then projected onto that fixed basis, so the null never sees the fitting step. This is the risk design D4 anticipated, and the anchor criterion caught it.
  12. Rank 2(K − 1) recovers orientation but costs shape. At Phase 6, both pca and pls_forced drop shape/shape from 0.19 to 0.00–0.01. They also leak angle into the shape cell (PC1) or the magnitude cell (net displacement). Giving the space more dimensions is not the fix.
  13. concat, the ceiling reference, behaves like the label-free spaces. It reaches power 1.00 under net displacement and has the same anchor excess. The p-padding question remains open.

docs.title: 7. Recommendation for the follow-up study
docs.text:
1. Lead candidate: pls_cv__net_displacement, conditional on Type I. First run an anchor-only Type I study for every net-displacement arm at both designs, at paper-grade size (500 replicates × 999 permutations). If the excess holds, diagnose it before running any power comparison. The endpoint-heteroscedasticity hypothesis in §6 is the first thing to test. If size holds, compare pls_cv__net_displacement against pls_cv__pc1 at paper grade.
  2. Drop fixed-basis pls_within_group. A refit-per-permutation variant would be valid by construction, but it multiplies cost by the permutation count. Pursue it only if net displacement fails.
  3. Do not carry pca or pls_forced as replacements. Their Phase 6 shape loss is disqualifying for a three-statistic claim.
  4. Keep concat as the ceiling. Decide p-padding in the follow-up.
  5. No production change. The PC1 estimator and the CV stage-PLS space remain the defaults. The Phase 6 interpretability statement for the case study stands unchanged.

docs.title: Orientation sign anchor: a real defect that does not explain the orientation shortfall
docs.text: Run date: 2026-08-28 Configuration: examples/trajectory_power_study/orientation_signfix_rerun_100x199.json Records: results/orientation-signfix-2026-08-28/merged.jsonl (1,500 replicates, 0 failures) Baseline for comparison: results/phase4-2026-08-27/merged.jsonl Change: openspec/changes/fix-orientation-sign-anchor Environment: Python 3.11.15, numpy 2.3.5, pandas 2.3.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scipy 1.16.3; no R at runtime

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
_estimate_orientation carried a genuine defect: PC1's sign was anchored on the centered first-stage row, a quantity that vanishes for trajectories that depart and return laterally, leaving the sign to be decided by noise. The defect is real, reproducible, and now fixed by anchoring on net displacement, with an invariance contract in tests/test_trajectory_orientation.py that the previous estimator fails.

The fix does not do what the change proposed it would. Re-running the Phase 4 orientation, shape, and translation cells on byte-identical data shows:

  • Orientation angle power moves from 0.59/0.59/0.64/0.65 to 0.64/0.64/0.67/0.68 — a uniform ~3-point lift that leaves the curve flat and well under the 0.80 floor.
  • The 150–180° mass in null cells is unchanged: 21 of 700 before, 21 of 700 after.
  • The realized-geometry checkpoints substantially stand: population orientation 81.1° → 80.5°, PLS latent 57.5° → 51.1°.

The proposal's central claim — that reported orientation power is an artifact-suppressed underestimate explaining "the shortfall's every symptom" — is contradicted by its own re-run. Phase 5 readiness item 1 stays open and diagnose-angle-null-pivotality is not displaced.

docs.title: The defect and its mechanism
docs.text:
The estimator is a port of Adams & Collyer's phenotypic trajectory analysis (tests/data/reference/evo_649_sm_suppmat.r). Orientation is PC1 of the centered stage configuration (:57); PC1's inherent sign ambiguity is resolved at :64 by a line commented #check startingpoint location, which anchors on the raw first-stage row.

MOTCO centered the configuration first and then anchored on the centered row, computing PC1 · (stage₁ − centroid). That quantity vanishes whenever a trajectory departs and returns laterally along its own principal axis — precisely what a bend produces.

On the constructed four-stage geometry in tests/test_trajectory_orientation.py (BENT_TRAJECTORY), whose first stage projects exactly zero onto its own centered principal axis:

  • the sign flips in 98 of 200 perturbation draws at noise sd 0.01, against a trajectory extent of ~5;
  • two copies carrying no orientation difference are measured at a median 179.4°.

Both are pinned as tests (test_orientation_sign_is_stable_under_small_perturbation, test_bent_identical_trajectories_report_zero_angle), and both fail against the previous estimator.

docs.title: The anchor decision
docs.text:
The sign is now anchored on net displacement, PC1 · (stage_last − stage_first). PC1 itself is unchanged.

Why not the faithful port. Anchoring on the raw first-stage row makes the sign depend on where the trajectory sits relative to the coordinate origin, so a pure translation can reverse it. Four regimes, pinned in test_four_regime_anchor_comparison:

regime truth centered (previous) raw (faithful) net displacement bent 4-stage, identical groups 0° 180° 0° 0° straight 2-stage, groups either side of origin 0° 0° 180° 0° translation control, group B shifted 0° 0° 180° 0° genuine 90° difference 90° 90° 90° 90°

The faithful port trades one failure for two, and one of the two is MOTCO's own translation null control — which Phase 4 passes cleanly at every effect size. Adopting it would break a working control to fix a broken one.

Accepted residual degeneracy. Net displacement vanishes for a closed trajectory whose last stage returns to its first. The evidence below suggests this is not merely theoretical in the study's latent space.

docs.title: Fixture equality — correcting the change's own claim
docs.text:
design.md originally asserted that all three anchors reproduce both committed R fixtures exactly. Measured, that is false for example1. Maximum |angle − R| over every reported pair:

fixture centered (previous) raw (faithful) net displacement results_example2.csv (5 levels) 9.9e-12 9.9e-12 9.9e-12 results_example1.csv (2 levels) 30.60 4.8e-13 30.60

MOTCO has never reproduced example1's t1/t3 and t2/t3 angles: it reports 74.70°/76.49° against R's 105.30°/103.51°, because those pairs straddle the PCA origin and R anchors on the raw row. tests/test_permutation.py has always accepted 180 − exp_angle, which is why this went unrecorded for the project's entire history.

This change neither introduces nor removes that deviation — net displacement reproduces the shipped values exactly. The deviation is itself an instance of the origin-side dependence that rules the raw anchor out. The claim has been corrected in design.md and proposal.md.

docs.title: Corrected operating characteristics
docs.text: Re-run scope follows design.md: orientation, shape, and translation cells, plus the shared zero-effect anchor and both Type I baselines. Generator, evaluation, replicate count, effect sizes, base seed, and matched-seed policy are identical to the Phase 4 pilot; all 1,500 replicate generator seeds were verified byte-identical to Phase 4's, so every comparison below is paired on the same data.

docs.title: Orientation angle power against the 0.80 floor
docs.text:
effect Phase 4 corrected MC SE 0.25 0.590 0.640 ±0.048 0.50 0.590 0.640 ±0.048 0.75 0.640 0.670 ±0.047 1.00 0.650 0.680 ±0.047

Still flat, still short of 0.80 by more than two standard errors. The floor is not met. The study's own gate machinery reaches the same verdict independently: report/phase4_gate_decision.json records decision: hold, mandatory_power[orientation,angle] (top_rate=0.680 < floor=0.800).

docs.title: The translation control still holds
docs.text:
cell Phase 4 corrected translation 0.25 0.030 0.030 translation 0.50 0.070 0.060 translation 0.75 0.050 0.030 translation 1.00 0.050 0.030 none (power anchor) 0.040 0.040 none (Type I baseline) 0.040 0.050 translation (Type I baseline) 0.040 0.040

Nominal level everywhere. The raw-anchor trap was correctly avoided.

docs.title: The null-cell artifact is not eliminated
docs.text:
Pooled none + translation cells (n = 700, true angle exactly 0°):

run <30° 30–60° 60–90° 90–135° 135–150° 150–180° max Phase 4 663 8 1 3 4 21 177.8° corrected 663 7 2 1 6 21 178.7°

Identical in aggregate, with a slightly higher maximum.

The paired replicate-level view shows why. Of the 700 null replicates, 654 are unchanged and 46 flip to their supplement (θ → 180 − θ). Of those flips, 21 cross into >150° and 21 cross out — an exact wash. The corrected anchor does not stop the sign from being noise-decided in the study's latent space; it reshuffles which replicates it happens to. This is the signature of PC1 · (stage_last − stage_first) itself landing near zero — the residual degeneracy accepted above — and it means the study-path artifact has a driver this change does not address.

docs.title: Realized-geometry checkpoints (task 4.5)
docs.text:
checkpoint Phase 4 corrected orientation @ 1.00, population standardized 81.1° 80.5° orientation @ 1.00, observed standardized 81.0° 80.8° orientation @ 1.00, PLS latent 57.5° 51.1°

The previously reported 81°/57° figures are not overturned. Arguments resting on "the construction survives integration" stand.

docs.title: Conclusions
docs.text:
1. The sign-anchor defect was real and is fixed, with an invariance contract the previous estimator fails. This stands on its own as a bug fix.
  2. It is not the cause of the Phase 4 orientation shortfall. Power rises ~4 points and stays flat at 0.69 against a 0.80 floor.
  3. It is not the source of the study-path near-180° null angles, which are unchanged at 21/700.
  4. Phase 5 readiness item 1 remains blocking and open.
  5. diagnose-angle-null-pivotality is not displaced and should proceed on its own terms.
  6. A new open question, raised by this run and not answered by it: what decides the orientation sign in the latent space when net displacement is itself small, and is PC1 direction (not merely its sign) unstable when the top two singular values of the stage configuration are close?

docs.title: What is out of scope here
docs.text: Per design.md, the magnitude cells were not re-run: magnitude's delta conclusion does not depend on the orientation estimator. Its angle and shape control rows therefore carry the previous estimator's values and were not re-measured. The full Phase 4 gate was not re-evaluated for the same reason.

docs.title: Orthonormal span coordinates — findings report (2026-11-09)
docs.text:
Change: orthonormal-span-coordinates (MOTCO 0.19.0). Reads: results/orthonormal-coordinates-2026-11-09/ (orthonormal_coordinates_decision.json; paper_grade/ and weak/ rate, paired and cell tables, accounting.json, reproduction.json, settings.json and the post-hoc population_geometry.csv; PROVENANCE.txt, sacct.txt). Concept page: measurement visibility.

The production statistics are measured in PLS score coordinates, T = X_in·R with R = W·(PᵀW)⁻¹, a sheared image of the fitted span. The stage-span paper grade's leak decomposition (report) found that the shear moves a planted bend's path length by −0.48 % on the SEA-AD table and −0.59 % at four stages. On an orthonormal basis of the same span the bend kept its length to within 0.11 %.

MOTCO 0.19.0 adds the opt-in setting SimulationEvaluationParams.latent_coordinates = "orthonormal". It measures on X_in·Q, Q = qr(x_rotations_), with the same fit, rank and draws. delta, angle and shape do not change under any orthogonal map, so every orthonormal basis of the span gives the same statistics. This run compared the two coordinate systems on matched units under a decision fixed in advance (design.md D7).

In one paragraph. The verdict is power_loss. The orthonormal coordinates hold size and remove the score shear's off-target leak. But they lose target power at the small, unequal and four-stage designs, so production stays on the scores.

  • Size holds. The 60 paper-grade controls read 0.000–0.066 and the 6 weak-design controls 0.010–0.050. None is above its bound.
  • Specificity holds, and the leak goes. At the 45° rotation, off-target shape falls from 0.070 to 0.000 at n = 200 and from 0.086 to 0.000 at four stages. 9 of 90 off-target cells read lower with orthonormal coordinates, and none higher, at two-sided paired p < 0.05.
  • Power is lost. 19 of 45 target cells lose, with one-sided paired p < 0.025; 3 losses are allowed, and 16 are below the Bonferroni ceiling. The largest losses:
  • the SEA-AD table's 45° rotation, angle 0.962 → 0.760;
  • the 22.5° rotation at four stages, 0.744 → 0.519;
  • the e = 0.25 bend, shape 0.724 → 0.518 at n = 80 and 0.678 → 0.482 on the SEA-AD table;
  • the e = 0.1 magnitude on the SEA-AD table, delta 0.542 → 0.416.

No target cell gains. The three-block column loses nothing. - The scores do not win by enlarging the planted effect, except for magnitude. The population-level target angle and shape are the same in both coordinate systems: 43.7°–45.2° for the 45° rotation, and 0.1255–0.1303 for the e = 0.25 bend. The scores' advantage there lies on the sampling side. Where the orthonormal coordinates lose, their angle null is wider: at the SEA-AD anchor its 95th percentile is 34.6° against the scores' 26.1°. For magnitude, the scores do stretch the planted size, by 1.6–5.0 %.

docs.title: 1. Configuration and provenance
docs.text:
• The unit. Each unit generates one dataset and fits stage-supervised PLS once (double-CV rank, floor 2). The two arms share that fit:
  • scores: the fit's production evaluation;
  • orthonormal: pls_orthonormal_from_pls, the same fit in orthonormal coordinates, with no refit.

Both arms run at the unit's RRPP seed with 999 permutations, serially, under net displacement, with span capture on. Each unit checks to 1e-8 that QᵀQ = I and that T = Z·(QᵀR). A unit failing either check is inconsistent, and an inconsistent unit fails the decision's gate. - paper_grade profile. It reuses the stage-span paper grade's units under the planted scale, through stage_span_leak_check.column_cells / unit_params, imported unchanged: - Columns (5): n = 200, n = 80 and the SEA-AD table (all on two blocks), n = 200 on three blocks, and n = 200 at four stages. - Cells (13): the anchor; translation, orientation and shape at e 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5; magnitude at e 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.1. - Size: 500 replicates per cell, 32,500 units. - weak profile. The latent-space comparison's seaad_weak anchor and translation (e = 1.0), at δ = 0.11 from its committed calibration and 500 replicates: 1,000 units, the span-split check's units. It reads size only. - Rejection rule: p < 0.05, as the parents count it. - Code. Revision d776366 on feat/orthonormal-span-coordinates, run from a clean detached worktree on ing. Python 3.11.16, numpy 2.3.5, scipy 1.16.3 and scikit-learn 1.8.0, with BLAS pinned to one thread. - Cluster. Partition 512x1024, n11 excluded: - array 936125 (paper_grade): 650 shards, at most 96 at once; - array 936126 (weak): 20 shards. - Pre-flight. - The change's test modules and the identity suites passed on a compute node (95 tests). - A smoke of both profiles ran. - Timing at 999 permutations gave a projection of about 206 core-hours. The user approved a 300 core-hour cap before submission (notes.md).

Details are in PROVENANCE.txt.

docs.title: 2. Accounting and reproduction
docs.text:
• Units.
  • paper_grade: 32,500 of 32,500 records, of which 12 failed with SemiSyntheticTrajectoryError: 9 in the four-stage orientation cell at e = 0.5 and 3 at e = 0.25. These are the planted-scale fixed point the stage-span paper grade also failed on, in the same cells and counts. A failed unit fails before the fit, so it is missing from both arms, and the pairing uses the 497 and 491 units available there.
  • weak: 1,000 of 1,000.
  • Both profiles: 0 inconsistent units and 0 duplicates. All 670 array tasks ended COMPLETED 0:0 (sacct.txt).
  • Consistency. The largest deviations were 2.0e-15 for the orthonormal basis and 3.4e-13 for the same span, against the 1e-8 tolerance.
  • Cost. 173.3 + 2.5 = 175.8 recorded core-hours. The median unit took 18.2 s (paper grade) and 8.9 s (weak); the PLS fit took 16.6 s, and each arm's RRPP pass 0.70 s. That compares with the 206 projected and the 300 cap.
  • Reproduction (the decision's gate): both passed exactly.
  • paper_grade: the scores arm's available and rejected counts equal the stage-span paper grade's committed design_point_operating.csv in all 195 rows (5 columns × 13 cells × 3 statistics).
  • weak: the counts and rejections equal the span-split check's production_table.csv in all 6 rows.
  • So every scores rate below is the parents' rate. Every orthonormal rate pairs with it on the same datasets, fits and permutation draws.

docs.title: 3. The decision
docs.text:
orthonormal_coordinates_decision.json (rule version 1) returns power_loss. O1 and O2 apply the stage-span paper grade's count-plus-ceiling rule (judge_rates, imported unchanged) to the orthonormal arm.

criterion rule result gate both reproductions pass and no unit is inconsistent passed O1 size anchor and translation, delta/angle/shape: m = 60 at the five columns (allowed 4 above the bound 0.0695, ceiling 0.084), and m = 6 at the weak design (allowed 1, ceiling 0.074) holds: 0 of 60 (0.000–0.066) and 0 of 6 (0.010–0.050) O2 specificity off-target delta/shape of orientation, delta/angle of shape and angle/shape of magnitude, m = 90 (allowed 6, ceiling 0.084) holds: 1 of 90 above the bound, the SEA-AD bend at e = 0.5 on angle at 0.072; range 0.000–0.072 O3 power per target cell (m = 45), one-sided exact paired loss p = P(Binomial(b + c, ½) ≥ b). Holds if at most 3 cells fall below 0.025 (the 95th percentile of Binomial(45, 0.025)) and none below 0.05/45 = 0.0011 fails: 19 below 0.025, 16 of them below the ceiling
  • The same families in the scores arm read 0.002–0.062 at the paper-grade controls and 0.026–0.052 at the weak design. They have 3 of 90 off-target rates above the bound: the 45° rotation's shape at 0.070 (n = 200) and 0.086 (four stages), and the SEA-AD bend's angle at 0.078. These are the paper grade's P3 readings.
  • The weak design's controls. With orthonormal coordinates delta is conservative there: 0.012 (anchor) and 0.010 (translation), against the scores' 0.034 and 0.036. angle reads 0.050 and 0.048, against 0.038 and 0.026.

Consequence (the decision's text): "Production stays on scores: the orthonormal coordinates lose target power against the scores at the failing cells. The report documents the trade-off and the setting stays an opt-in diagnostic."

docs.text:
Each entry gives the scores → orthonormal rate over 500 paired units (497 and 491 in the four-stage orientation cells at e = 0.25 and 0.5). In brackets is b/c: b counts units only the scores reject, c units only the orthonormal coordinates reject. ‡ marks a loss below the ceiling 0.0011 and † a loss below 0.025 that is above the ceiling.

  • The losses sit where the stage program is hardest to resolve. They fall at n = 80, on the SEA-AD table and at four stages: 6, 6 and 5 of their 9 target cells. At n = 200 on two blocks there are 2, and on three blocks none. They are spread across the modes: 7 orientation, 7 shape and 5 magnitude cells.

docs.title: 5. Specificity: the watched cells
docs.text:
The watched cells are the 45° rotation's off-target shape. Before the run, they were the paper grade's two largest P3 readings that the shear could explain.

column scores orthonormal b / c two-sided paired p n = 200 0.070 0.000 35 / 0 5.8e-11 four stages (491 units) 0.086 0.000 42 / 0 4.5e-13

The orthonormal coordinates remove the shear's leak, and not only at the watched cells. Nine off-target cells read lower at two-sided p < 0.05, with b/c in brackets:

  • The rotation's shape:
  • n = 200: 0.046 → 0.004 at e = 0.25 (21/0) and 0.070 → 0.000 at e = 0.5 (35/0);
  • SEA-AD table: 0.022 → 0.002 at both effects (11/1);
  • four stages: 0.030 → 0.000 at e = 0.25 (15/0) and 0.086 → 0.000 at e = 0.5 (42/0).
  • The rotation's delta at four stages: 0.020 → 0.000 at e = 0.5 (10/0).
  • The bend's delta at e = 0.5: 0.034 → 0.012 at n = 200 (11/0) and 0.026 → 0.008 at four stages (11/2).

No off-target cell reads higher. The O2 exceedance, the SEA-AD bend's angle at e = 0.5, reads 0.078 in scores and 0.072 in orthonormal coordinates (two-sided p 0.45). It is not a leak the shear caused.

docs.title: 6. Population geometry: the residuals and the planted effect
docs.text:
The bend's residual. For the planted-scale bend at e = 0.5, B's population path length equals A's. The table gives each arm's median population_latent B − A path-length difference, as a share of A's path (cell_table.csv, median_population_share):

column scores orthonormal n = 200 +0.06 % +0.06 % n = 80 −0.04 % +0.11 % SEA-AD table −0.38 % +0.02 % three blocks +0.09 % +0.06 % four stages −0.60 % +0.07 %
  • The leak check's pattern reproduces at R = 500. The leak check, at R = 100 and 199 permutations, read −0.48 % and −0.59 % in scores against −0.01 % and +0.06 % on the orthonormal span. With orthonormal coordinates the residual stays within 0.11 % at every column.
  • The 45° rotation's residual on the SEA-AD table is −1.60 % in scores against +0.52 % with orthonormal coordinates. The leak check's 100 replicates read −3.35 % and +0.66 %. Its median moved with the replicate set, but its sign and its excess over the orthonormal coordinates did not.

The planted effect is not larger in scores, except for magnitude. population_geometry.csv is a post-hoc descriptive aggregate (PROVENANCE.txt). It gives the median population-level statistics per arm, beside the spectrum of the anchor (cell_table.csv):

column 45° rotation, population angle bend e = 0.25, population shape magnitude e = 0.1, population delta anchor angle null q95 anchor pooled eigengap n = 200 44.98° / 44.97° 0.1272 / 0.1272 3.377 / 3.323 (+1.6 %) 2.59° / 2.58° 0.0881 / 0.0793 n = 80 45.15° / 44.86° 0.1270 / 0.1272 3.402 / 3.263 (+4.3 %) 23.94° / 31.93° 0.0955 / 0.0820 SEA-AD table 43.71° / 45.04° 0.1255 / 0.1257 3.561 / 3.391 (+5.0 %) 26.08° / 34.61° 0.1117 / 0.0984 three blocks 45.04° / 44.97° 0.1274 / 0.1274 4.172 / 4.169 (+0.1 %) 1.55° / 1.55° 0.0892 / 0.0878 four stages 44.81° / 45.06° 0.1289 / 0.1303 5.372 / 5.180 (+3.7 %) 17.09° / 24.46° 0.0562 / 0.0470

Each pair reads scores / orthonormal. The percentage is the scores' excess.

  • Orientation and shape. The planted target is the same in both coordinate systems. On the SEA-AD table the scores' population angle is even the smaller (43.7° against 45.0°), yet the scores reject the rotation in 0.962 against 0.760. So the scores' advantage is not a stretched target.
  • Magnitude. The scores stretch the planted size by 1.6–5.0 % at the columns that lose magnitude power, and by 0.1 % on three blocks, which loses none. The shear's stretch accounts for at least part of the magnitude losses.
  • The null side. Where the orthonormal coordinates lose, their angle null is wider: its 95th percentile rises by 7–9° at n = 80, on the SEA-AD table and at four stages, and the pooled eigengap shrinks. At n = 200 and on three blocks both are nearly unchanged. At the weak design the null widens most, from 53.8° to 100.0° at the anchor. There the median observed null angle also rises, from 21.6° to 46.2° (weak/population_geometry.csv), and the orthonormal angle still holds size (0.050).
  • What the aggregates do not explain. At n = 200 the 22.5° rotation loses 0.880 → 0.720, yet the medians agree: the observed angle is 22.22° / 22.26° and the null q95 4.84° / 4.88°. The loss there lies in the tails of the per-unit null, which the committed medians do not resolve.

docs.title: 7. What follows
docs.text:
• Production and motco analyze stay on score coordinates. The default flip and the motco analyze adoption were owed only to adopt_orthonormal. Neither is opened.
  • latent_coordinates = "orthonormal" stays an opt-in diagnostic in the harness. It is not exposed in motco analyze, in study configurations or with attribution. Without it every output equals 0.18.0.
  • The score shear is a measured trade-off, not a defect to remove.
  • The cost. In scores, the 45° rotation leaks into shape at 0.070–0.086 and the e = 0.5 bend into delta at 0.026–0.034. With orthonormal coordinates these read 0.000 and 0.008–0.012. Elsewhere the off-target rates are alike in both arms; the bend's delta peaks at 0.036 / 0.038 on three blocks at e = 0.1.
  • The gain. In exchange, the scores have up to 0.23 more target power at small n, unequal cells and four stages, with equal size.
  • Reading a rejection. An off-target shape or delta rejection beside a strong angle or shape rejection can be the shear's. At paper grade such a rate stayed within 0.086.
  • Roadmap item 15 is closed with this verdict. The change does not permit a production follow-up. Why the score metric narrows the null at weak or unbalanced designs is open. The aggregates show the association with the null width and the eigengap, but not the mechanism. Any future work on the measurement metric should take the scores' power, not the orthonormal span, as the benchmark.

docs.title: 8. Limitations
docs.text:
• One construction family. Every plant is the stage-span construction under the planted scale, exact in planted-standardized coordinates. A real difference may load differently on the shear's directions, so the size of the trade-off is specific to these plants.
  • Medians. The cell and population tables summarize each cell by medians. The n = 200 rotation loss (§6) shows that they can miss where a loss comes from.
  • population_geometry.csv was written after the decision. It does not bear on the verdict, and it reads the same merged records the decision read.
  • The weak design reads size only. The latent-space comparison found no power there for any plant, so it was not measured.
  • Units that cannot be planted. The 12 four-stage orientation units that cannot be planted at the planted scale are missing from both arms. The four-stage orientation rates are therefore over 497 and 491 units.

docs.title: Phase 4 medium PLS pilot
docs.text:
Partially superseded (2026-08-28) — orientation angle values only. The orientation estimator used for this pilot anchored PC1's sign on the centered first-stage row, which flips the sign for bent trajectories. Every angle figure below therefore carries that defect. The corrected re-run is orientation-sign-anchor-2026-08-28.md; corrected orientation angle power is 0.64/0.64/0.67/0.68 across effects 0.25 → 1.00, against 0.59/0.59/0.64/0.65 here.

The pilot's conclusions are not overturned. The shortfall against the 0.80 floor survives correction, the Type I and translation controls still hold, the magnitude and shape conclusions are untouched, and the realized-geometry figures (81.1° population, 57.5° latent) substantially stand. What changes is the explanation offered below: the "why orientation is flat" section's reasoning is superseded, since the corrected estimator leaves the near-180° null mass unchanged at 21/700.

The original numbers in this report are left exactly as run. Nothing below has been edited.

Run date: 2026-08-27 Configuration: examples/trajectory_power_study/phase4_pilot_100x199.json Code revision: 073bb2f on feat/phase4-medium-pls-pilot (parent fabdc18). The pilot executed from this working tree before it was committed; the per-file fingerprints taken at launch are in results/phase4-2026-08-27/PROVENANCE.txt, and the report outputs regenerate byte-identically from this revision. Environment: Python 3.11.15, numpy 2.3.5, pandas 2.3.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scipy 1.16.3, motco 0.6.0; no R at runtime Supersedes for gate purposes: mvalue-pls-pilot-2026-07-30.md, which predates the corrected shape estimator, realized-geometry diagnostics, and orientation attribution. That report is retained unchanged as historical evidence and is not used for the Phase 5 decision.

docs.title: Phase 5 gate decision: HOLD
docs.text:
Mandatory gate failed: mandatory_power[orientation,angle] — top-effect power 0.650 against the predeclared floor of 0.800. The curve itself is monotone within tolerance; the level is short, and the cause is not yet identified (see "Why orientation is flat").

Every other mandatory gate passed. Nothing here is a Monte Carlo accident: at 100 replicates the standard error at a rate of 0.65 is 0.048, so the observed power is more than three standard errors below the floor. Raising the replicate count would sharpen the estimate without moving it.

The full decision, every observation, and its Monte Carlo standard error are in results/phase4-2026-08-27/report/phase4_gate_decision.json.

docs.title: Run configuration
docs.text:
Parameter Value Integration Pooled PLS, M-value methylation PLS cross-validation cv1_splits=3, cv2_splits=4, n_repeats=5, max_components=20, random_state=1203 Samples per replicate 300 Stages 4 Replicates per cell 100 Permutations per test 199 Effect sizes 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00 Trajectory modes magnitude, orientation, shape, translation Seed policy matched primary seeds, one shared zero-effect anchor Attribution all nonzero primary orientation cells; 100 bootstraps, top_k=20 Significance level 0.05 Cells 19 Total work units 1,900 Failed work units 0 Compute 23.3 core-hours (attribution 0.45% of it)

All 1,900 units completed, every parameter signature matched enumeration, no records were missing or duplicated, and every completed record carried selected-component and realized-geometry metadata. All 400 eligible orientation replicates produced valid attribution diagnostics; none failed.

docs.title: Type I control
docs.text:
Eighteen one-sided control tests were predeclared: the none baseline plus every translation effect level, each contributing one test per statistic. All passed. The one-sided bound at n = 100 is 0.05 + 2·sqrt(0.05·0.95/100) = 0.0936; the largest observed control rate anywhere was 0.09 (translation negative control, shape). No exceedance occurred, so the marginal-exceedance confirmation rule was not engaged.

This is the strongest result in the pilot. Translation — a pure location offset — leaves all three statistics at nominal level at every effect size, which is what a correctly calibrated test must do.

docs.title: Magnitude
docs.text: delta reaches 1.00 at every nonzero effect and is monotone within tolerance. Both mandatory off-diagonal controls pass: magnitude's angle (0.01) and shape (0.00) at effect 1.00 sit below alpha, not merely below the inflation bound. The M-value contract established in July holds under the corrected estimator.

docs.title: Shape
docs.text: shape power is 0.94–1.00 across the sweep and monotone. The corrected pairwise Procrustes estimator detects the constructed interior bend easily, so the detectability requirement the gate encodes is met with room to spare.

docs.title: Orientation — the failing gate
docs.text: angle power is 0.59, 0.59, 0.64, 0.65 across effects 0.25 → 1.00. It is monotone within tolerance but essentially flat: quadrupling the requested effect buys about six points of power. A construction whose power does not respond to its own effect size is not simply underpowered — something other than the requested signal is governing the test. The next section shows the obvious candidate (a sampling noise floor) is contradicted by the records.

docs.title: Why orientation is flat: what the geometry does and does not explain
docs.text:
Realized geometry at effect 1.00, joint scope (report/phase4_geometry.csv). Angles are in degrees; delta and shape are only comparable within a column, never across columns.

Mode Statistic Population (standardized) Observed (standardized) PLS latent magnitude angle 39.9 45.8 32.0 magnitude delta 27.5 27.2 26.8 orientation angle 81.1 81.0 57.5 orientation delta 1.69 1.69 2.19 shape angle 85.0 85.8 65.2 shape delta 8.96 8.89 9.95 translation angle 0.0 16.8 8.9 translation delta 0.0 0.38 0.37

The construction is strong and survives integration: 81° at the population level, still 57° in the latent space, against a null floor of 8.9° (translation, whose population angle is exactly 0°). On a simple detection-threshold reading that separation should yield near-complete power, and it does not.

The obvious explanation is wrong, and the records say so. Within the orientation cell at effect 1.00, the replicates that fail to reject have a larger mean observed latent angle (66.7°) than the ones that reject (52.5°). A noise-floor or underpowered-signal account predicts the opposite ordering. The same inversion appears in shape at effect 1.00 (83.3° non-rejecting versus 61.5° rejecting), while the translation null behaves normally (30.7° rejecting versus 7.8° non-rejecting) — so the inversion is specific to cells that carry real signal, not a general property of the statistic.

Two candidate explanations are ruled out. Latent dimensionality is not responsible: splitting the cell by selected components gives an angle rejection rate of 0.71 at lv = 2 (n = 7) against 0.65 at lv = 3 (n = 93). And it is not Monte Carlo noise: the effect is a 14-degree gap across 65 versus 35 replicates.

What remains is that the RRPP permutation null for angle co-varies with the observed statistic within a replicate — that is, the statistic is not pivotal across replicates, so a replicate whose latent geometry inflates the observed angle inflates its own null by at least as much. The pilot cannot confirm this because include_null_distributions was off, so the per-replicate null quantiles were not persisted. Confirming or refuting it is the first item of pre-Phase-5 work; see Phase 5 readiness.

Until that is settled, the honest statement is: orientation power is 0.65 and the cause is not yet identified. It is not cross-talk (the off-diagonal localization below shows nothing projection-associated for orientation's own statistic), it is not latent dimensionality, and it is not a weak construction.

docs.title: Off-diagonal responses, localized
docs.text:
Off-diagonal rejection is not interpreted as estimator cross-talk by default. Each response is localized against the checkpoint where it first becomes material, on a scale-free quantity compared only against that same checkpoint's own zero-effect null (report/phase4_localization.csv).

Mode → statistic First material checkpoint Reading magnitude → angle population (standardized) construction-present shape → angle population (standardized) construction-present shape → delta population (standardized) construction-present orientation → shape PLS latent projection-associated orientation → delta never material not material magnitude → shape never material not material translation → anything never material not material

Most off-diagonal responses are already present in the analytic population geometry, before any sampling, preprocessing, or projection: they are properties of the constructions Phase 2 documented as mixed, and demanding purity from them would fail a correct estimator. Magnitude's population angle is 39.9° yet its angle rejection rate is 0.01 — the estimator is more specific than the construction, which is the opposite of cross-talk.

One response is genuinely projection-associated: orientation → shape first becomes material at the PLS latent checkpoint (at effects 0.75 and 1.00), where the population and observed shape values are immaterial. Correspondingly, orientation's shape rejection rate is 0.97–1.00. Phase 5 should treat this as an open question about the latent representation, not as evidence about the shape estimator. These labels describe where a response appears, not what caused it.

docs.title: PLS representation
docs.text:
Component selection was extremely stable: the modal selected latent dimensionality was 3 in every one of the 19 cells, with an observed range of 2–3 and mean CV AUROC 1.00 (report/phase4_pls_selection.csv). Nothing in the pilot depends on a fragile component choice.

That stability has a cause worth stating: with four stages, a stage-supervised PLS-DA has at most three informative components, and the double CV saturates there. The latent space is sized to separate stage centroids, which is exactly what the architecture intends — but it is not sized to preserve the group orientation contrast, and the attribution diagnostics quantify the cost.

docs.title: Attribution diagnostics
docs.text:
All 400 eligible orientation replicates produced valid diagnostics (availability 1.00), with 423 truth drivers per replicate among 658 aligned features. Attribution cost 0.45% of total compute.

Metric (observed component, effect 1.00) Value Top-20 precision against generator truth 1.00 Top-20 recall 0.066 Bootstrap sign stability 0.87 Observed-vs-PLS-captured cosine 0.07 PLS-captured norm ratio 0.06 Top-20 precision, PLS-captured component 0.15

Two findings stand out.

The observed-space attribution is exact. Every one of the top 20 observed features is a true generator driver, at every effect size and every transition. Recall is low only because 20 identifiers are being drawn from 423 drivers. Bootstrap sign stability of 0.80–0.87 means the reported directions are stable within a replicate.

The PLS reconstruction retains almost none of the orientation contrast. The cosine between the observed directional contrast and its PLS-captured reconstruction is 0.05–0.08, and the captured norm is ~6% of the observed. Its top-20 precision against truth is 0.01–0.16 — near chance at small effects. Reconstructing a ~660-dimensional directional contrast through a rank-3 model cannot do better, so this is arithmetic, not a bug; but it means the pls_captured view must not be presented as a driver list. For interpretation, the observed component is the trustworthy one.

Cross-replicate top-20 overlap is low (Jaccard 0.02–0.05) and cross-replicate sign agreement is ~0.68. This is expected by construction and is not an instability finding: each replicate index draws a fresh set of differential indicators, so the true driver set genuinely differs between replicates. Matched seeds pair cells within a replicate index, not across them. A cross-replicate stability claim would require holding the driver set fixed, which this design deliberately does not do.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• 100 replicates give a standard error of about 0.05 at a rate of 0.5; small differences between adjacent power points are not resolvable, which is why monotonicity is judged within two combined standard errors.
  • The four modes' 0.00 points come from one shared anchor cell. This is deliberate — at zero requested effect the generator ignores the mode, so separate cells would be byte-identical — but it means the four null rows are one measurement and must not be counted as independent evidence.
  • Matched seeds make requested-effect comparisons paired within a replicate index. Comparisons across replicate indices remain unpaired.
  • The generator-truth definition covers features whose group-stage differential mean change differs between groups, including propagated CpG→gene→protein effects. It does not model correlation-induced drivers, so precision against it is a lower bound on biological plausibility, not a causal claim.
  • Attribution is descriptive. It carries no p-values and no causal interpretation, per the Phase 3 contract.
  • n_jobs is part of each cell's parameter signature because RRPP seeds one RNG stream per worker. This run used the config's n_jobs=1 throughout; parallelism came from concurrent shards. Overriding --n-jobs would change the realized permutation draws and break resume.
  • The pilot executed from the working tree that became commit 073bb2f. Record generation used exactly that code; the localization scaling fix and the n_jobs guard landed afterwards and affect only report generation, and the reports here were regenerated after them and verified byte-identical.

docs.title: Decision and recommended next work
docs.text:
Do not launch the Phase 5 paper-grade study yet. More Monte Carlo precision would not resolve the orientation shortfall — it would only measure a flat 0.65 curve more accurately.

Before Phase 5:

  1. Characterize the orientation noise floor. Translation's 16.8° observed angle at a true 0° is the binding constraint. Establish how the floor scales with samples per group-stage cell and with feature count, and pick a Phase 5 design point where orientation is adequately powered — or revise the power target to what the estimator can achieve at a defensible sample size.
  2. Investigate orientation → shape at the PLS checkpoint. It is the one response that first appears at projection. Determine whether it is a property of a rank-3 stage-supervised space or of the shape statistic measured within it.
  3. Reconsider latent dimensionality for group contrasts. Selection saturates at n_stages - 1 because the supervision target is the stage label. A space sized for stage separation retains ~6% of the group orientation contrast. If orientation is a primary estimand, the latent space that measures it may need a different sizing criterion — this is a design question, not a bug.
  4. Present only the observed component in driver reports. Its top-20 precision is 1.00; the PLS-captured component's is 0.15.

Magnitude, shape, and Type I calibration need no further pilot work. They are ready for Phase 5 as soon as the orientation question is settled.

  uv run python scripts/run_study_shard.py \

docs.text: Run date: 2026-09-08 Configuration: examples/trajectory_power_study/phase5_design_point_pilot.json (sha256 153f53b7…, recorded in full in results/phase5-design-point-2026-09-08/PROVENANCE.txt) Code revision: ff68514 on feat/phase5-design-point-pilot (clean working tree at launch; parent afab7df = main). Record generation and report generation used the same revision. Execution: SLURM array job 878322 on cluster.ing.uc.cl, partition 512x1024 (AMD EPYC 7662 nodes), 100 single-CPU shards, --error-policy record, no --n-jobs, BLAS pinned to one thread. Environment: Python 3.11.16, numpy 2.3.5, pandas 2.3.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scipy 1.16.3, motco 0.6.0, installed from the lockfile with uv 0.12.10; no R at runtime. Answers: readiness item 4 (phase5-readiness.md) — the Phase 5 design point and the 0.80 orientation power floor. Every number below traces to a file under results/phase5-design-point-2026-09-08/report/; the JSONL records are gitignored as regenerable.

docs.title: Design-point decision: CHOSEN — ρ = 0, n = 1200
docs.text:
First design point in preference order (n_samples ascending, then baseline_continuity ascending) whose orientation/angle power at its top effect (1.00) clears the 0.80 floor with 1·SE confirmation: rate 0.88, lower bound 0.85 (report/design_point_decision.json).

The rule was predeclared in the config (acceptance.design_point) and is advisory. Its per-column evaluation (report/design_point_decision.csv):

ρ n orientation angle power at e = 1.00 MC SE 1·SE lower bound status anchor Type I (delta / angle / shape) 0.0 300 0.55 0.050 0.50 fails 0.03 / 0.06 / 0.03 0.5 300 0.24 0.043 0.20 fails 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.01 0.8 300 0.69 0.046 0.64 fails 0.04 / 0.01 / 0.01 0.0 600 0.76 0.043 0.72 fails 0.04 / 0.05 / 0.05 0.5 600 0.46 0.050 0.41 fails 0.02 / 0.00 / 0.02 0.8 600 0.73 0.044 0.69 fails 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.07 0.0 1200 0.88 0.032 0.85 meets 0.04 / 0.04 / 0.03 0.5 1200 0.69 0.046 0.64 fails 0.05 / 0.02 / 0.02 0.8 1200 0.81 0.039 0.77 marginal 0.02 / 0.04 / 0.03

The chosen column's own zero-effect anchor holds nominal level on all three statistics (0.04 / 0.04 / 0.03 against α = 0.05), so the design.md risk — a column that meets the floor on angle while another statistic drifts — did not materialize. ρ = 0 is also the declared isotropic stress-test endpoint and the Phase 4 comparator, so the chosen point carries the most general claim the grid offered: the floor is met without assuming any baseline continuity.

The figure report/design_point_power.png shows the same nine points as curves: orientation angle rejection rate at e = 1.00 versus n_samples, one line per ρ, Monte Carlo error bars, each point annotated with the column's median pooled eigengap. The ρ = 0 line rises steepest (0.55 → 0.76 → 0.88) and is the only one to clear 0.80 with margin; the ρ = 0.5 line lies below it everywhere; the ρ = 0.8 line starts highest at n = 300 and is overtaken by n = 600.

docs.title: Run configuration
docs.text:
Parameter Value Integration Pooled PLS, M-value methylation PLS cross-validation cv1_splits=3, cv2_splits=4, n_repeats=5, max_components=20, random_state=1203 Stages 4 Differential-site density p_dmp 0.1 (Phase 4 used 0.2) Surgery censoring default "error" (fail loud); no cell was censored Design grid ρ ∈ {0.0, 0.5, 0.8} × n_samples ∈ {300, 600, 1200} (9 columns; ρ = 0, n = 300 is the baseline column) Trajectory modes orientation, translation Effect sizes 0.00 (shared anchor per column), 0.25, 0.50, 1.00 Replicates per cell 100 Permutations per test 199 Seed policy one matched primary family across the whole grid; one zero-effect anchor per column Attribution / Phase 4 gate off / off Cells 65 (2 Type I + 63 primary/design) Total work units 6,500 Failed work units 0 Censored surgeries 0 (report/realized_surgery.csv, censored_fraction = 0.0 in all 55 surgery cells) Compute 70.4 core-hours of recorded unit runtime (75.2 CPU-hours billed by sacct), 70 minutes wall on 100 concurrent tasks

All 6,500 units completed with status completed; every (cell, replicate) appears exactly once in merged.jsonl; every record's parameter signature equals the signature enumerated from the committed config; every record carries 199 permutations, n_jobs = 1, config_spectrum, and selected_lv.

docs.title: Type I behaviour, per column
docs.text:
Every column's anchor and every translation cell sits at or below the one-sided bound 0.05 + 2·sqrt(0.05·0.95/100) = 0.0936 on all three statistics; the largest control rate anywhere in the grid is 0.09 (translation delta, ρ = 0, n = 1200, e = 0.25). Type I calibration does not drift with sample size or continuity, which is the property the design.md risk list asked this report to check before adopting a column.

The baseline type_i acceptance targets (report/acceptance_report.json, two-sided |rate − α| ≤ 2·SE) pass on 5 of 6 tests. The one flagged test is the translation control's delta rate of 0.02 — 0.03 below α against a 0.028 bound — i.e. a conservative rate, not an inflation. The Phase 4 report judged these controls one-sided (inflation only); under that reading all six pass. It is reported here as flagged because the config's target is two-sided.

docs.title: Orientation at the baseline column, against Phase 4
docs.text: At ρ = 0, n = 300 the orientation angle curve is 0.45, 0.63, 0.55 across e = 0.25 / 0.50 / 1.00 (report/power_curves.csv). Phase 4 measured 0.59, 0.59, 0.64, 0.65 (0.64–0.68 after the sign-anchor correction) at p_dmp = 0.2. The shape of the curve is the same — no monotone response to the requested effect; adjacent points differ by at most 2.6 combined standard errors and the top effect is not the most powerful — and the level is about 0.1 lower, consistent with halving the differential-site density rather than with any change in the estimator. The off-diagonal pattern is also unchanged: orientation moves shape (0.82–0.93 here, 0.97–1.00 in Phase 4) and delta (0.60–0.69 here, 0.60–0.69 in Phase 4). Item 2 predeclared the shape response as a projection artifact of the rank-3 stage-supervised space; nothing here contradicts that, and at n ≥ 600 the response saturates at 0.96–1.00 in every ρ = 0 and ρ = 0.5 column.

docs.title: What governs orientation power across the grid
docs.text:
The design-point table carries the two recorded covariates readiness item 4 asked for — the pooled configuration eigengap and the dispersion of each replicate's own angle null width (q95). Orientation cells at e = 1.00, from report/continuity_resolved_orientation.csv (identical rows appear in design_point_operating.csv):

ρ n angle power median eigengap (q33–q67) median angle null q95 IQR of q95 SD of q95 0.0 300 0.55 0.052 (0.035–0.067) 40.7° 107.4° 59.1° 0.0 600 0.76 0.048 (0.038–0.066) 18.8° 38.2° 55.5° 0.0 1200 0.88 0.049 (0.038–0.063) 10.8° 13.0° 48.4° 0.5 300 0.24 0.086 (0.071–0.125) 56.6° 116.6° 57.4° 0.5 600 0.46 0.114 (0.090–0.149) 26.2° 42.2° 54.2° 0.5 1200 0.69 0.133 (0.094–0.188) 16.3° 12.1° 29.5° 0.8 300 0.69 0.221 (0.145–0.285) 24.6° 83.3° 60.2° 0.8 600 0.73 0.193 (0.156–0.269) 21.3° 37.6° 54.1° 0.8 1200 0.81 0.186 (0.142–0.234) 15.3° 20.0° 49.9°

Sample size does what item 1 predicted. Along n at fixed ρ = 0 the eigengap is constant (≈ 0.05: the baseline is near-isotropic at every n, as it must be — ρ, not n, sets the configuration's shape) while the median angle null width contracts 40.7° → 18.8° → 10.8° and its IQR collapses 107° → 38° → 13°. Power rises 0.55 → 0.76 → 0.88 with it. The zero-effect anchors show the same contraction (median q95 17.3°, 8.1°, 4.9° at n = 300, 600, 1200; design_point_operating.csv, none rows). This is the mechanism the pivotality report identified — each replicate's critical value tracks its own geometry, and more samples per group-stage cell pin that geometry down — now measured across n rather than inferred at one point.

Continuity does not help at this baseline, and its effect is non-monotone. ρ = 0.5 is worse than ρ = 0 at every n (0.24 / 0.46 / 0.69 vs 0.55 / 0.76 / 0.88), and ρ = 0.8 is above ρ = 0 only at n = 300 (0.69 vs 0.55), then below it (0.73 vs 0.76, 0.81 vs 0.88). This is not what the headroom analysis anticipated, and the covariates say why the simple story fails:

  • The eigengap behaves as designed — it rises from ≈ 0.05 at ρ = 0 to 0.09–0.13 at ρ = 0.5 and 0.19–0.22 at ρ = 0.8, so the stage configuration does acquire a dominant PC1 — and at ρ = 0.5, n = 1200 the anchor's null is the narrowest in the grid (median q95 2.2° against 4.9° at ρ = 0). The null side of the test improves with continuity exactly as the audit predicted.
  • What does not carry over is the signal. Computed from the records (merged.jsonl, pair_statistics.angle; reproduction snippet below), the median observed latent angle for orientation at e = 1.00 is 61° / 73° / 66° at ρ = 0 for n = 300 / 600 / 1200, but only 46° / 35° / 28° at ρ = 0.5 — the same nominal surgery realizes a smaller latent orientation contrast when the baseline trends, and the contrast shrinks as n grows. At ρ = 0.8 the observed angle is back to 64° / 62° / 66°, but the anchor's null is wide again (median q95 54° / 26° / 19°, versus 23° / 9° / 2° at ρ = 0.5), so the larger eigengap buys nothing on the null side there.

So "larger eigengap ⇒ narrower null ⇒ more power" holds only along n at fixed ρ. Across ρ, two things change at once — the realized orientation contrast of the surgery and the null width — and they do not move together. The claim Phase 5 can make is therefore n-conditional, not continuity-conditional: at the chosen point the floor is met at the isotropic endpoint, with an eigengap distribution (median 0.049, terciles 0.038–0.063) that is the real-data observable to report alongside any orientation result. A trending baseline is not a lever Phase 5 should pull to buy orientation power; if anything, the ρ = 0.5 columns are a warning that the orientation surgery's semantics are not ρ-invariant, which belongs in the Phase 5 report contract as a stated limitation of the construction.

docs.title: PLS representation
docs.text:
Selected latent dimensionality (design_point_operating.csv, median/min/max_selected_lv):

column anchors (median, range) orientation e = 1.00 (median, range) ρ = 0, every n 3 (2–4) 3–4 (2–4) ρ = 0.5, every n 3–4 (2–4) 4 (3–6) ρ = 0.8, n = 300 / 600 / 1200 4 (4–7), 4 (4–5), 4 (3–5) 8 (4–14), 7 (4–10), 7 (4–9)

At the chosen point selection saturates at n_stages − 1 = 3 (median 3, range 2–4, orientation cells included), exactly as in Phase 4: the stage-supervised double CV sizes the space for stage separation and does not respond to n. The retained-rank question — whether a space sized for stage centroids should be the space that measures the group orientation contrast — is handed to readiness item 3 unchanged; this pilot recorded rank and did not vary it.

One new observation for item 3: at ρ = 0.8 the orientation surgery at e = 1.00 roughly doubles the selected rank (median 7–8, up to 14) relative to that column's own anchor (median 4), while at ρ ≤ 0.5 it adds at most one component. A strongly trending baseline plus a global feature permutation evidently creates additional stage-predictive directions that the CV retains. It coincides with ρ = 0.8 being the only ρ at which orientation's delta and shape responses fall (0.27–0.46 and 0.43–0.69, versus 0.60–0.88 and 0.91–1.00 at ρ = 0) — consistent with the latent-rank probe's finding that the projection artifact decays as rank grows. It is recorded, not explained, here.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• 100 replicates give a Monte Carlo SE of about 0.05 at a rate of 0.5 and 0.032 at 0.88. The decision's confirmation margin is one SE by predeclaration; the chosen column would also clear a 2·SE margin (0.88 − 0.065 = 0.815) but ρ = 0.8, n = 1200 would not.
  • magnitude and shape were deliberately not run (decided 2026-09-04; both reached power 1.00 at n = 300 in Phase 4 and only gain from larger n). Their operating characteristics at the chosen point are measured in the Phase 5 study itself, not here. The p_dmp change from 0.2 to 0.1 touches every mode, so Phase 4's magnitude and shape numbers are not transferable to this baseline without that measurement.
  • The observed-angle medians in "What governs orientation power" are computed from the gitignored merged.jsonl, not from a committed CSV; the snippet below regenerates them from the records. Every rejection rate, eigengap, null-width, and rank figure comes from committed CSV/JSON.
  • Comparisons along ρ at fixed n are paired at the baseline indicator draw (one matched family, ρ thresholds the same uniform block); comparisons across n are not paired. Neither pairing is exploited by the report's rate estimates, which are per-cell binomials.
  • Each column's 0.00 row is one shared anchor cell; the two modes' nulls in a column are one measurement.
  • The Type I acceptance target is two-sided in this config, which is why a conservative 0.02 control rate is flagged. Phase 4's one-sided reading is the one the readiness worklist uses; both readings pass on inflation.
  • The examples README's pre-run cost estimate (~500 workstation-core-hours) was about 7× too high; it was taken from a rehearsal that oversubscribed BLAS threads. The measured cost is 70 core-hours on EPYC 7662 cores, and about 35 on a modern desktop core (12.5 s / 18.5 s / 27 s per unit at n = 300 / 600 / 1200, single-threaded, 199 permutations). The README is corrected in this change.

docs.title: Decision and hand-off
docs.text:
1. Phase 5 design point: ρ = 0 (independent baseline), n = 1200 (300 samples per group-stage cell), four stages, p_dmp = 0.1, pooled PLS on M-value methylation with CV-selected rank. Orientation angle power at e = 1.00 is 0.88 (1·SE lower bound 0.85) with the column's anchor at nominal level on all three statistics. The 0.80 floor stands; the claim is not revised.
  2. Report the eigengap, not ρ, with any orientation claim. At the chosen point the pooled eigengap is 0.049 (terciles 0.038–0.063). That distribution is what a real cohort must be compared against; the continuity knob is a generator parameter and does not transfer.
  3. Do not use baseline continuity to buy orientation power. ρ = 0.5 lowers power at every n and ρ = 0.8 does not beat ρ = 0 beyond n = 300. The orientation surgery's realized contrast is not ρ-invariant; state this as a construction limitation in the Phase 5 report contract.
  4. Hand the retained-rank question to item 3 with one new fact: rank is 3 at the chosen point regardless of n, and only a strongly trending baseline (ρ = 0.8) moves the CV off n_stages − 1.
  5. Phase 5 must re-measure magnitude and shape at the chosen point, since p_dmp changed.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text:
The run used the committed config at revision ff68514. Locally (about 35 core-hours on a modern desktop core; ~3.5 hours on 22 single-thread shards):

Then, from the repository root:

  --config examples/trajectory_power_study/phase5_design_point_pilot.json \
  --out-dir results/phase5-design-point-2026-09-08

Record-derived observed-angle medians (the only figures above not in a committed CSV):

uv run python - <<'EOF'
import json, collections, statistics
by = collections.defaultdict(list)
for line in open("results/phase5-design-point-2026-09-08/merged.jsonl"):
    r = json.loads(line); cm = r["cell_metadata"]
    if cm["trajectory_mode"] != "orientation" or cm["effect_size"] != 1.0: continue
    dp = cm.get("design_point") or {"generator.baseline_continuity": 0.0, "generator.n_samples": 300}
    by[(dp["generator.baseline_continuity"], dp["generator.n_samples"])].append(r["pair_statistics"]["angle"])
for k in sorted(by): print(k, round(statistics.median(by[k]), 1))
EOF
