docs.title: 1. The exit-gate criteria
docs.text:
Phase 6's purpose is "demonstrate that the validated method answers a meaningful biological question end to end". Its exit gate has two parts. Each is recorded with one of three values: met, not met or unexercised.

criterion status evidence G1 — collaborators can trace each global trajectory claim to stable feature/module drivers unexercised; attribution unavailable at the case-study configuration No claim exists. SEA-AD rejects no statistic in any of its 44 analyses (SEA-AD report, Result and §11), and ADNI's primary rejects none (ADNI report, Summary). Had a claim existed, attribution could not have run on it: analyze_trajectories refuses attribution whenever covariates are declared (src/motco/analysis.py:519–523), and both primaries declare six covariate columns (§4, D6). G2 — collaborators can reproduce the result from documented inputs and configuration met SEA-AD: the re-issue's gates and reproducibility check are byte-identical on the re-issue machine, and every output that reads no p-value reproduces the superseded outputs made on another machine at rounding level, with every rank and CV AUROC equal (SEA-AD report §12). ADNI: adni-sexdiff report --check regenerates the report from the committed outputs and compares it cell by cell (ADNI report, Reproduction). Both run every analysis through one entry point, motco.analysis.analyze_trajectories, and record its motco analyze CLI equivalent. the gate as a whole not met as written G2 is met; G1 is unexercised, not met. the purpose demonstrated up to inference Two real designs are analysed end to end with size measured at both primaries (§2), and their non-rejections are measured or bracketed to be uninformative (§2, §5). The interpretive half, the drivers, has no real-data demonstration (§6).

The vacuous pass is refused. Read literally, "each global trajectory claim" ranges over an empty set, and the gate would pass with nothing traced. This review does not take that reading. The purpose sentence and the conditional Work bullet ("For significant orientation, …") both presuppose a detected difference, and a gate that passes because nothing was found would mean nothing. Nor is G1 recorded as failed: failure would say that attribution was tried on a claim and produced no stable drivers, and nothing of the kind happened.

The Work list.

Work bullet status evidence Predefine cohorts, stages, covariates, missing-data handling, and preprocessing met SEA-AD report, reading rules "predeclared in the proposal before any corrected run"; ADNI report, Reading rules (READING_RULES, "decided by adni-analyze before any run") Fit one pooled, cross-validated PLS representation met SEA-AD report §3 (astrocyte cohort_30: CV rank 5, cv_mean_auroc 0.6356); ADNI report, Primary analysis (CV rank 8, cv_mean_auroc 0.599514) Report magnitude, orientation, and validated shape results with uncertainty met RRPP p-values and null summaries in every analysis (SEA-AD report §3; ADNI report, Primary analysis); size measured at both primaries (§2) For significant orientation, produce observed and PLS-reconstructed feature contrasts, bootstrap stability, and pathway/module enrichment withheld — no claim; unavailable with covariates §4, D1 and D6; §6 Include sensitivity to PLS dimensionality and preprocessing choices met SEA-AD report §4 (twelve forced-rank analyses) and §6 (sixteen preprocessing-variant analyses); ADNI report, Rank sensitivity (forced ranks 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12) and Export sensitivity (six variants) Make the analysis reproducible from raw-input contracts to final figures met SEA-AD report §1 (pin, gates, commands) and §12; ADNI report, Reproduction

docs.title: 2. The evidence ledger
docs.text:
Every size and power statement carries one of three provenance classes:

  • measured: a committed decision file at that design and configuration;
  • bracketed: measured at neighbouring designs whose stage signal or n encloses the cohort's;
  • inferred: from a mechanism, such as κ = √(n / (n − r)) depending on n and the reduced rank r only.

The paper may state a measured or a bracketed statement, naming its class. It may not turn a bracket into a number for the cohort. Rates are rejection rates at p ≤ 0.05; delta / angle / shape in that order.

analysis group design result size power at its stage signal SEA-AD astrocytes cohort_30 (primary) n = 80 (F 11/10/28, M 9/10/12); RNA + ATAC pseudobulk, 5,000 + 5,000 features; six covariate columns; CV rank 5; AUROC 0.6356; df, κ 1.06904 p 0.501 / 0.449 / 0.331; none rejected measured under df on this table: pooled 0.031 / 0.0425 / 0.058, every reading at most 32 / 500 (corrected-permutation report §2) bracketed: every rate 0.010–0.062 at n = 80 and anchor AUROC 0.516 / 0.580 (rank-floor report §3–§4); no statistic above 0.09 at n = 200 and AUROC 0.553 / 0.729 (pilot §3.3–§4, δ arm) SEA-AD microglia cohort_30 (primary cohort of the positive-control cell type) n = 76; CV rank 2; AUROC 0.6852; κ 1.0731 p 0.705 / 0.456 / 0.991; none rejected measured under df on this table: pooled 0.029 / 0.05 / 0.052 (corrected-permutation report §2) bracketed, as above SEA-AD cohort_50, astrocytes and microglia (sensitivity cohorts) n = 74 (rank 2, AUROC 0.6965, κ 1.0753); n = 63 (rank 4, AUROC 0.6565, κ 1.0903) p 0.628 / 0.242 / 0.514 and 0.834 / 0.291 / 0.644; none rejected inferred from κ (SEA-AD report §13) bracketed, as above SEA-AD sensitivity arms 40 analyses: twelve forced ranks, sixteen preprocessing-variant analyses (eight variants × two cohorts), eight latent-adjustment arms, four donor-exclusion analyses no rejection in any inferred (eight-covariate arms at r = 12, exclusion variants at n = 58–70; SEA-AD report §13); the latent_adjusted arm's angle and shape inadmissible (residualized_basis) bracketed, as above ADNI primary n = 1,501 (F 237/310/125, M 223/448/158); p180 + NMR, 133 + 165 features; five covariates in six design columns; CV rank 8; AUROC 0.599514; uncorrected (κ ≈ 1.003); 9,999 permutations p 0.1116 / 0.6879 / 0.7105; none rejected measured: 0.034–0.068 at both controls against 0.0695 (ADNI-design report §2) measured, non_rejections_uninformative: delta at most 0.530 (SE 0.022), angle 0.056–0.076, shape 0.034–0.062 (ADNI-design report §3) ADNI sensitivities 14 analyses: latent_stage; six export variants (nist_bridge, per_run_standardized, nmr_all_columns, raw_scale, log2_plus_one, glog); the CN / LMCI / AD arm (n = 1,130); forced ranks 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12 only delta rejects: at forced rank 6 (p 0.0471) and under nmr_all_columns (p 0.0447) inferred: the arms were not run at the design (ADNI-design report §5) measured only for the primary's construction

The sources of each row's design and result are the SEA-AD report §3, §4, §6, §7, §9 and §13, and the ADNI report's Summary, Primary analysis and sensitivity sections. The ADNI κ is the ADNI-design report's (§1). The residualized_basis verdict is the case-study diagnosis's.

Why SEA-AD's power is a bracket and not a measurement. The SEA-AD cohorts' held-out AUROCs (0.6356–0.6965) lie inside the pilot's δ-arm range (0.553–0.729), where no statistic has power at n = 200. They lie above the rank-floor check's 0.516 / 0.580, where every rate sits at the null at the astrocyte cohort's own table, without covariates. No run was made at n = 80 and AUROC 0.6356–0.6965 with the case study's covariates. The non-rejections are uninformative on both sides of the bracket, but the bracket gives no number for the cohort.

The binding readings, as the case studies predeclared them:

  • SEA-AD primaries (SEA-AD report, reading rules and §11). The angle and shape non-rejections are uninformative at this n, and the angle null is too wide to inform a non-rejection. The delta non-rejections are weak evidence against a size difference, since delta is conservative under df (0.031 / 0.029 pooled). The CV-selected rank, eigengap and null summary are reported beside angle.
  • SEA-AD arms. Each is read beside the primary under its own rules. No rank, preprocessing, latent-adjustment or exclusion dependence was found. The latent_adjusted arm's angle and shape p-values are reported, not read.
  • ADNI primary (ADNI report, READING_RULES). delta is not rejected; the angle and shape non-rejections are uninformative by rule 3, which states that no power statement exists at this design. The ADNI-design check turns that absence into a measurement and extends it to delta: "a non-rejection is uninformative up to the construction maximum" for all three statistics (ADNI-design report §4). adni_sexdiff confirms rule 3 in its own change (§8).
  • ADNI sensitivities. A rejection status that differs from the primary's is dependence on the arm's setting, never a replacement of the primary (READING_RULES 1), and the rank sweep's rules count no ranks that reject (sweep rules 2, 5 and 6; §4, D5).

docs.title: 3. What Phase 6 establishes, withholds, and does not allow to be claimed
docs.text:
Claimable now:

  • An end-to-end, reproducible real-data analysis of two designs through one entry point. SEA-AD (n = 80, RNA + ATAC pseudobulk, 44 analyses) and ADNI (n = 1,501, serum metabolomics, 15 analyses) each ran every analysis through analyze_trajectories. Each had predeclared reading rules, sensitivity to rank and preprocessing, and a reproduction record (§1, G2).
  • Size at both primaries, measured. SEA-AD cohort_30 under df: pooled 0.029–0.058 per cohort table and statistic against 0.0597 (corrected-permutation report §2). ADNI: 0.034–0.068 against 0.0695 (ADNI-design report §2).
  • The null result, stated with its uninformativeness. Neither primary rejects any statistic: SEA-AD astrocyte and microglia cohort_30, and ADNI. The non-rejections are uninformative. At ADNI this is measured: no statistic reaches the 0.80 floor at any construction effect. At SEA-AD it is bracketed, and stated as a bracket (§2).
  • The design finding (§5): at these designs the held-out stage signal, not n, limits power.
  • The configuration lessons. Each is a measured MOTCO result that a real analysis ran into first:
  • where the stage signal is weak, the CV rank needs a floor of 2 (rank-floor report, adopt_floor; MOTCO 0.10.0);
  • with six covariate columns at n = 80, the Freedman–Lane null shrinks with the reduced model's residual df, and the df correction restores size (case-study diagnosis, residual_df_shrinkage; corrected-permutation report, adopt_df; MOTCO 0.13.0);
  • the covariate-blind basis follows technical axes where they dominate the variance (SEA-AD library composition, ADNI assay phase). The axis diagnostics report them, and no statistic is re-read for them. The stage latent adjustment is inadmissible for angle and shape at n = 80 (residualized_basis);
  • the held-out CV stage AUROC is the observable that places a cohort on the power axis (§5).

Withheld, with a named path to lift it:

  • Driver tracing on real data: G1, the Phase 6 Work bullet for attribution, and the roadmap's objective 4. It is withheld because it was never exercised. It has not failed, and it is not waived. Items 11 and 12 lift it, or report it failed on its own terms (§6). The paper's real-data section states it as withheld and names the gap.

Not claimable:

  • Any agreement reading. A non-rejection of delta, angle or shape in either cohort is not evidence that the sexes' trajectories agree in size, direction or shape. Both case studies' rules say so, and the measured or bracketed power says why.
  • The sensitivity-arm rejections as results. ADNI's delta rejections at forced rank 6 (p 0.0471) and under nmr_all_columns (p 0.0447) are setting dependence under the case study's predeclared rules (§4, D5).
  • A numeric power for SEA-AD. The bracket says that the non-rejections are uninformative. It gives no power number at n = 80 and AUROC 0.6356 (§2).
  • Metabolite- or feature-level claims from the structural analogue. Both operating-characteristic constructions use InterSIM blocks (498 features), and the ADNI one differs from ADNI on its latent geometry (§4, D7). They support statements about what the analysis can detect at the design. They support nothing about metabolite-, gene- or peak-level behaviour.

docs.title: 4. Resolution of each deviation
docs.text:
D1 — No global trajectory claim to trace. Claim revision. Neither primary rejects: SEA-AD astrocyte cohort_30 reads p 0.501 / 0.449 / 0.331 and ADNI p 0.1116 / 0.6879 / 0.7105. SEA-AD rejects nothing in any of its 44 analyses. The mechanism is power, not size: size is measured at both primaries, and power is absent at both designs (§2, §5). G1 is recorded as unexercised and the phase closes on the null. No further analysis of either cohort is run to produce a claim. The case studies' predeclared rules forbid that. SEA-AD's reading rules state that "nothing is re-tuned", and ADNI's READING_RULES 9 reads "The analysis is run once at these settings; a second run at other settings is a new proposal". Sources: SEA-AD report, reading rules and §11; ADNI report, Summary and Reading rules.

D2 — The rank-1 angle degeneracy. Method revision (MOTCO 0.10.0). Under the 0.9.0 rule both SEA-AD cohorts selected rank 1. There angle is 0° or 180° by construction, and its RRPP null is a two-point distribution. minimum-latent-rank floors the CV candidates at 2. The rank-floor check returned adopt_floor at δ = 0.05 and 0.1: the floor-2 arm holds 0.0695 at the anchor (delta 0.042 / 0.044, angle 0.054 / 0.060, shape 0.036 / 0.038). The floor defines angle and shape in at least two dimensions; it does not make them powerful. Source: rank-floor report §1–§4; results/rank-floor-2026-10-23/delta0.05/rank_floor_decision.json, results/rank-floor-2026-10-23/delta0.1/rank_floor_decision.json.

D3 — Residual-df shrinkage of the Freedman–Lane null. Method revision (MOTCO 0.13.0); the case study was re-issued with no status change. At the case study's configuration (n = 80, six covariate columns) the covariate-adjusted primary exceeded the bound on translation delta at δ = 0.1: 0.072 against 0.0695 (case-study Type I report, diagnose_configuration_excess). The diagnosis found residual_df_shrinkage. The reduced model's residuals have mean square RSS / n rather than RSS / (n − p_red), with p_red = 10. Pooled delta rises 0.0545 → 0.0595 → 0.066 with one, three and six covariate columns. The opt-in df correction multiplies the residuals by κ = √(n / (n − r)). The corrected-permutation check returned adopt_df, with pooled rates of 0.029–0.058. SEA-AD then re-issued every MOTCO-dependent output under df: every p-value moved up or stayed, and no rejection status changed in any of the 44 analyses (SEA-AD report, Result and §12). ADNI keeps the uncorrected null, because κ ≈ 1.003 at n = 1,501 is immaterial (ADNI-design report §1) and delta is conservative there (0.034, §2).

D4 — The covariate-blind basis follows technical axes, and the stage latent adjustment is inadmissible for angle and shape. Claim revision. SEA-AD: the first latent component of the astrocyte cohort_30 primary tracks ribosomal_mean (|ρ| 0.840858) more closely than stage (ρ 0.491212). In microglia it tracks mitochondrial_pseudobulk (0.843828, against stage 0.688175) (SEA-AD report §5). The positive control, microglia against astrocytes, is a control for the stage signal. It does not hold on the primary basis in cohort_30, through E3 alone (0.6882 against mitochondrial_pseudobulk 0.8438), and it holds on the latent_adjusted basis (E3 0.5279 against tmm_rna 0.4153) (SEA-AD report §10). ADNI: the primary's first component tracks the assay phase (|ρ| 0.542; ADNI report, Axis diagnostics of the primary). The stage latent adjustment that would remove such axes is residualized_basis at n = 80: at a forced rank of 2 it still exceeds the bound on anchor angle (0.084 / 0.082; case-study diagnosis). The claim is revised, not the method: - an axis correlated with a technical variable is a measurement-space finding, reported beside the statistics and never a reinterpretation of them; - the latent_adjusted arm's angle and shape p-values are reported, not read; - the covariate-blind analysis stays the primary in both case studies.

D5 — ADNI's two sensitivity-arm delta rejections. Claim revision: none; the predeclared reading stands. delta rejects at forced rank 6 (p 0.0471), one of six forced ranks. It also rejects under the nmr_all_columns export variant (p 0.0447), one of six export variants (ADNI report, Rank sensitivity and Export sensitivity). Under adni_sexdiff's predeclared sweep and membership rules both are setting dependence. The primary's non-rejection stays the result, and the sweep's rules count no ranks that reject (sweep rules 2, 5 and 6). - A liberal null does not explain them. Size holds at the design, and delta is conservative there (0.034; ADNI-design report §2). - They are not a claim. No multiplicity-controlled rule makes one. - They are not a G1 candidate. Running attribution on them would be the forking path this review closes, and it would meet the gap of D6.

D6 — Attribution is unavailable with covariates. Capability gap → item 11. Two guards block it: - analyze_trajectories raises "Attribution is not available with covariates: it works from unadjusted cell means" whenever covariates are declared (src/motco/analysis.py:519–523, pinned by tests/test_analysis.py:579). - The lower-level analyze_orientation_attribution accepts covariate-adjusted means only as a precomputed mean_table, and then requires bootstrap_replicates = 0, because "row-level bootstrap semantics are unavailable" (src/motco/stats/attribution.py:368–372).

Both case-study primaries declare six covariate columns. So a claim from either primary could not have been traced to stable drivers as the analysis is built today. Unadjusted attribution is no substitute: under a confounded covariate the unadjusted contrast is a different estimand, and the covariate Type I check's unadjusted arm rejected shape at 0.364 on null data (covariate Type I report §2).

D7 — The structural analogue is wider at ADNI. Claim scope. The ADNI-design construction matches ADNI on the calibrated quantities: held-out AUROC 0.606 against 0.600, and first-component |ρ| with phase 0.578 against 0.542. It does not match ADNI's latent geometry: - CV rank 19 in 494 of 500 anchor units, against 8; - eigengap 0.330 against 0.744; - angle null q95 51.0° against 35.4°.

Its blocks are InterSIM omics (498 features), not ADNI's 298 metabolites (ADNI-design report §1, §5). Its measured rates say what the analysis can detect at the design; they say nothing about metabolite-level behaviour. The SEA-AD statements carry the same limitation (the same 498 InterSIM features). The ADNI-design report records it as wider at ADNI, because there the construction's rank sits at the cap and its eigengap is less than half of ADNI's.

docs.title: 5. The cross-study finding and the binding reading
docs.text:
At these designs the held-out stage signal, not n, limits power.

run n held-out stage AUROC best power source ADNI-design check 1,501 0.606 (ADNI 0.600) delta at most 0.530 (SE 0.022), at a doubled stage effect in one group (e = 1.0); angle and shape at the null rate ADNI-design report §1, §3 design-guidance slice (three stages, two blocks) 80 1.000 (mean ≥ 0.9998) delta 0.620 (SE 0.022) at e = 0.1 slice report §3.1, §4 design-guidance pilot, δ arm (δ = 0.05 / 0.1) 200 0.553 / 0.729 no statistic above 0.09 at any effect (magnitude ≤ 0.03, orientation ≤ 0.07, shape ≤ 0.09; R = 100) pilot report §3.3, §3.4, §4

A cohort almost nineteen times larger, at AUROC 0.60, detects a doubled stage effect less often than n = 80 at a saturated stage signal detects a 10 % size change. The SEA-AD cohorts (AUROC 0.6356–0.6965) sit inside the δ arm's bracket, at a smaller n than it measured.

Binding reading, for the paper and for any later real-data use of motco analyze: a non-rejection is informative only where a measured operating characteristic at the cohort's own design and stage signal says so; the held-out CV stage AUROC is reported beside the CV-selected rank with every result. - It extends the Phase 6 statement that already requires the rank beside any angle result, and replaces nothing in it. - It is a reading condition, not a power model. Three regimes do not fit a power curve in AUROC, and none is offered.

docs.title: 6. The withheld leg and its lifting criterion
docs.text:
The gap. The lifting demonstration must run at the configuration in which a real claim would be read: covariates declared, the rank floor, net displacement and, at small n, df. Attribution as built cannot run there (D6: the guards at src/motco/analysis.py:519–523 and src/motco/stats/attribution.py:368–372). Two consequent changes follow, in order, each with its own proposal.

Item 11 — covariate-adjusted attribution in motco analyze (MOTCO). It has three parts: - attribution from covariate-adjusted cell means, evaluated at the record's reference row; - bootstrap stability that refits the adjustment within each resample on the frozen basis; - its own validation that the attribution of an adjusted contrast is stable and unbiased under a confounded covariate.

It is byte-identical without covariates. It would modify real-data-trajectory-analysis and orientation-driver-attribution. Its proposal decides, after a smoke timing, whether the validation needs cluster compute.

Item 12 — the plasmode demonstration (after item 11). It lifts the leg or reports it failed. - Data. The real exported blocks, covariates and design of SEA-AD astrocyte cohort_30, the primary cohort. SEA-AD is open data, while ADNI's are under a data-use agreement. This configuration's size under df is measured. And ADNI's analogue sits at the CV cap, so its latent geometry is the less understood of the two. - Construction. A planted group × stage difference of a declared kind, with a known feature set, is added to the real data at declared strengths. The orientation kind comes first, because the Work bullet is conditioned on orientation. Each plasmode unit is analysed by motco analyze at the case-study configuration with attribution. - Lift criteria. The leg is lifted when all three of these hold: - (i) the unplanted construction holds size at the one-sided bound α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/R); - (ii) the planted difference is detected at a rate fixed in item 12's proposal; - (iii) the planted features are recovered among the attribution's top drivers, with bootstrap sign stability and top-k frequency above thresholds fixed in that proposal before any run.

Otherwise the leg is reported failed on its own terms, with the failing criterion named. - What this review leaves to item 12's proposal. Three things are left open. The first is the detection rate in (ii). The second is the thresholds in (iii), which are fixed there before any run. The third is the null-making step for (i): real sex labels may carry a real difference, so "unplanted" data need one, such as a within-stage label permutation that preserves the covariates. The proposal may also add an unadjusted arm as a descriptive comparison. That arm cannot lift the leg (D6). - Ownership. MOTCO owns the planting construction and the decision rule, as it does for its other validation checks. It reads sead_sexdiff's export through a documented input contract and commits aggregates only. sead_sexdiff supplies the export, and no donor-level data are committed to MOTCO. Item 12's proposal confirms the split.

If item 11 proves harder than expected, the leg stays withheld and the paper reports it so, with the gap named. The closure does not depend on it.

docs.title: 7. Phase 7 stays deferred — unchanged
docs.text: SNF-native trajectory statistics stay deferred on the Phase 5 exit review's §5 grounds. Nothing in either case study bears on SNF: both measured the PLS latent space throughout.

docs.title: 8. Consequent work, in order
docs.text:
1. Item 11 — covariate-adjusted attribution (MOTCO; owed by the withheld leg; §6).
  2. Item 12 — the plasmode demonstration (MOTCO, with sead_sexdiff's export; owed by the withheld leg; §6). It starts after item 11.
  3. adni_sexdiff reading rule 3 (owed by that repository, in its own change). It confirms the rule, now citing results/adni-design-2026-11-02/run/adni_design_decision.json, so that its angle, shape and delta non-rejections are read as measured to be uninformative at its design.
  4. Independent of Phase 6; none of these blocks anything Phase 6 owes:
  5. item 5, optional block weighting;
  6. item 6, defaulting the null-dispersion materiality rule;
  7. item 7(b), group-specific dispersion in the generator and its null study;
  8. item 8's follow-ups: whether df becomes the analysis default, and the cohort_50 tables, whose size under df is inferred and on which no rejection depends;
  9. the toy-fixture decision (cross-cutting engineering work).

sead_sexdiff and adni_sexdiff cite this review in their reports' limitations when they next re-issue. Nothing in either changes now.

docs.title: 9. What this review does not do
docs.text:
• It makes no new measurement and changes no code. Nothing under src/motco/ or tests/ moves, and no release is made.
  • It edits no predeclared artefact: no case-study reading rule, decision file or committed report. It does not rewrite the Phase 6 gate's text, which stays as written beside the status recorded here.
  • It re-reads no case-study result under new rules. Every reading above is the one the case studies predeclared, confirmed or cited.
  • It ends the two cohorts' use as Phase 6 evidence. No further analysis of SEA-AD or ADNI is read as Phase 6 evidence, so a later analysis of either is a new study with its own proposal, not a continuation of this phase. The plasmode of item 12 uses SEA-AD's real blocks as the substrate for a planted signal. It reads no sex × stage result from them.

docs.title: Phase 6 small-n operating study at the SEA-AD design — 2026-10-09
docs.text:
Follows examples/trajectory_power_study/phase5_report_template.md section for section. The study is split into two profiles (spec "Phase 6 small-n study profiles", split rule), so each section reports both runs. Rates and Monte Carlo SEs are read from the two runs' report/ directories. The few figures that are not in report/ (selected-rank breakdowns, anchor reproduction) are computed from merged.jsonl, whose sha256 is in each PROVENANCE.txt, and are marked as such.

Runs: results/phase6-small-n-magnitude-2026-10-09/ (magnitude) and results/phase6-small-n-2026-10-09/ (orientation, shape, translation) · Configs: examples/trajectory_power_study/phase6_small_n_magnitude.json (sha256 41211d61…) and examples/trajectory_power_study/phase6_small_n_study.json (sha256 18cf0fc7…) · Gate decisions: magnitude PROCEED, orientation/shape HOLD (advisory, design D6; from each run's report/phase4_gate_decision.json).

In one paragraph. At the SEA-AD MTG astrocyte design (n = 80, three stages, cells of 9–28, two blocks), the three RRPP tests hold their size. Every Type I cell of the baseline column is at or below α (0.010–0.040, bound 0.0695), and the three-block columns stay inside the bound. The tests differ sharply in power. delta detects a joint size change of 10 % about half the time (0.542) and of 25 % almost always (0.956), and the magnitude construction leaves angle and shape at the floor. angle and shape stay weak even at the strongest orientation and shape constructions the generator can build: 0.300 and 0.228 at e = 1.00, where every differential site has been relocated. They are also not specific. The orientation construction rejects shape (0.464) and delta (0.354) more often than angle, and the shape construction rejects delta (0.330) more often than shape. For the case study, a delta rejection is interpretable evidence that the trajectories differ. A delta non-rejection is evidence against size changes of about 25 % or more. angle and shape rejections are interpretable as evidence of a difference, but not of which kind, and their non-rejections carry no information at n = 80 (section 8).

docs.title: 1. Configuration and provenance
docs.text:
Design point. The study reproduces the SEA-AD MTG astrocyte case-study design fixed on 2026-10-09. Sex is the group (A = F, B = M; the surgery is applied to the smaller group, the conservative assignment, design D4). ADNC is merged into three stages (Not AD + Low / Intermediate / High). The donor table at ≥30 nuclei per donor per omic is group_stage_sizes = [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]] (n = 80). All three InterSIM blocks are generated, but only methylation + expression are measured (integration_params.layers), as the two-block analogue of ATAC + RNA (design D2). Every trajectory surgery acts on methylation indicators, so each mode's construction is present in the measured space. Measurement is pooled PLS on M-value methylation with the committed stage-supervised double-CV rank, and magnitude_kind = joint. p_dmp = 0.1 and ρ = 0 are copied from Phase 5. Only the stage count and sizes change.

Design grid. Both profiles cross the ≥30-nuclei and ≥50-nuclei tables ([[10, 9, 25], [9, 9, 12]], n = 74) with two-block and three-block measurement (layers null), giving four columns. The cohort-size contrast is the baseline vs the ≥50-nuclei column at two blocks. The block-count contrast is the baseline vs the three-block column at n = 80. Columns that differ only in layers evaluate the same generated datasets. The fourth column (≥50 nuclei, three blocks) exists because the engine crosses design-grid axes (design D4, accepted 2026-10-09).

Effect axes. These come from the pilot (results/phase6-small-n-pilot-2026-10-09/NOTES.md; each profile's metadata.effect_axis gives the reason for each point). Magnitude: 0 / 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.25 / 0.50 / 1.00, covering the measured rise and saturation. Orientation, shape and translation: 0 / 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 1.00. For orientation and shape, e = 1.00 is the construction maximum, because _relocate_rows clamps the relocated fraction at 1.

Monte Carlo sizing and seeds. 500 replicates × 999 permutations per cell. Base seed 800 and the matched-seed family phase6-small-n are shared with the pilot. This makes the shared zero-effect anchor the same datasets in the pilot and both profiles, and the family is independent of every Phase 5 record. Both configs derive from phase6_small_n_pilot.json (metadata.derives_from) and name each other as split siblings.

Provenance. See each run's PROVENANCE.txt; the fields the template requires are all present. In summary: - Records were produced at code revision 5325f6d; the reports were rendered at 946e471, which adds only a reporting fix (section 2). - The runs used cluster ing, partition 512x1024, AMD EPYC 7662, with --exclude=n3 and later n3,n4. STUDY_N_JOBS was unset and BLAS was pinned to one thread. - Software: python 3.11.16, motco 0.6.0, numpy 2.3.5, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scipy 1.16.3, uv 0.12.10. - Layout: 100 shards per profile, error policy record, and n_jobs = 1 in every record (each report/report_contract.json). - Magnitude: 30 cells × 500 = 15,000 units, median 11.6 s per unit, 47.6 core-hours. - Orientation/shape/translation: 54 cells × 500 = 27,000 units, median 13.2 s per unit, 102.4 core-hours.

docs.title: 3. Gate decision
docs.text:
The Phase 4 gate is declared as advisory acceptance (design D6). At n = 80 a missed 0.80 power floor is a finding about the case study's design, not a defect.

Magnitude profile — PROCEED (report/phase4_gate_decision.json; rules reduced to magnitude as in the Phase 5 re-measurement): - Mandatory power: magnitude/delta reaches 1.000 at e = 1.00 against the 0.80 floor. - Mandatory controls at e = 1.00, bound α + 2·SE = 0.0695: magnitude/angle 0.008, magnitude/shape 0.002. - Type I inflation: anchor 0.026 / 0.024 / 0.020 (delta / angle / shape); type_i_baseline none 0.016 / 0.028 / 0.018. - Completeness met.

Orientation/shape profile — HOLD (report/phase4_gate_decision.json). Two mandatory power rules fail, and both curves are monotone (tolerated_monotone=True): - orientation/angle: top rate 0.300 against the 0.80 floor. - shape/shape: top rate 0.228 against the 0.80 floor.

Every Type I inflation observation passes (report/phase4_gate.csv): the anchor, type_i_baseline none and translation, and translation at every e (0.010–0.040, bound 0.0695). The descriptive roles (orientation/delta, orientation/shape, shape/delta, shape/angle) are reported in section 6, and completeness is met. No confirmation re-run is required: a HOLD on mandatory power at the top effect is not a marginal exceedance. The HOLD is the measured answer to "can orientation and shape be detected at n = 80?".

docs.title: 4. Type I error
docs.text:
Null claims read the type_i_baseline cells, a separate seed family from the power grid (report/type_i_table.csv):

cell delta angle shape none (type_i_baseline-ca766c21680e) 0.016 ± 0.006 0.028 ± 0.007 0.018 ± 0.006 translation at e = 1.00 (type_i_baseline-74c0457435ca) 0.034 ± 0.008 0.040 ± 0.009 0.018 ± 0.006

Both cells have the same cell ids and signatures in the two profiles and are the same measurement. They are counted once.

The shared zero-effect anchor reads 0.026 ± 0.007 / 0.024 ± 0.007 / 0.020 ± 0.006. It is power_primary-6f04726ce01b in the magnitude profile and power_primary-1a2e4088b485 in the orientation/shape profile (report/report_contract.json resolves it to [magnitude] and to [orientation, shape, translation], counted_as: 1). The two cells hold the same 500 datasets. Generator seeds and selected ranks are identical at all 500 replicate indices, observed statistics agree to within 1.4e-11, and p-values are identical (computed from merged.jsonl). The anchor is therefore one measurement, not one per mode or per profile. Its first 100 replicates also reproduce the pilot's anchor to within 7.3e-12 on the observed statistics, with identical seeds and ranks (p-values differ: 199 vs 999 permutations).

Translation at e > 0, read as a negative control on all three statistics (report/power_curves.csv): 0.014–0.032 for delta, 0.018–0.030 for angle and 0.010–0.030 for shape, at every e.

The two-block measurement is conservative at n = 80. The baseline column's null rates sit at half of α. At three blocks the anchor rates rise to 0.062 ± 0.011 (delta) and 0.056 ± 0.010 (shape), still inside the bound; at ≥50 nuclei and two blocks they fall to 0.010 and 0.008 (report/design_point_operating.csv).

docs.text:
Baseline column (≥30 nuclei, two blocks), report/power_curves.csv, rate ± Monte Carlo SE:

Magnitude. The delta rise sits about 10× higher on the native joint axis than at n = 1200 (Phase 5 re-measurement: 0.836 at e = 0.01, 0.996 at 0.02). e is the per-omic size ratio minus one, so delta has about even odds at a 10 % joint size change and is near certain at 25 %. The pilot (100 × 199) measured 0.58 and 0.93 at the same points, agreeing within pooled SE.

Orientation, with its recorded geometry. The anchor's pooled relative eigengap has median 0.111 and terciles 0.082 / 0.144 (report/design_point_operating.csv, baseline rows). Three stage means always span at most a 2-D subspace. The small eigengap, a near-isotropic triangle whose PC1 is poorly determined, comes from the generator's isotropic endpoint ρ = 0: each stage draws its differential sites independently, so the stage means do not trend. It is not a property of three stages. A real cohort whose stages trend would have a larger eigengap. The Phase 5 continuity sweep found that this does not translate into orientation power under the current construction: the orientation surgery realizes a smaller latent contrast on a trending baseline (design-point report, "Continuity does not help"). The angle null is correspondingly wide and variable: per-replicate q95 median 84° and IQR 115° at the anchor. At the orientation cells:

e median eigengap (terciles) angle null q95 median (IQR) orientation/angle power 0.25 0.135 (0.101 / 0.173) 59° (109°) 0.034 ± 0.008 0.50 0.160 (0.120 / 0.210) 56° (105°) 0.058 ± 0.010 0.75 0.176 (0.135 / 0.222) 65° (114°) 0.090 ± 0.013 1.00 0.167 (0.127 / 0.213) 63° (104°) 0.300 ± 0.020

Orientation angle power within eigengap terciles at e = 1.00 (report/eigengap_stratified_power.csv, power_primary rows):

tercile eigengap range power low 0.013–0.127 0.114 ± 0.025 middle 0.127–0.213 0.449 ± 0.038 high 0.213–0.441 0.337 ± 0.037

At e = 0.75 the same terciles give 0.060 / 0.138 / 0.072. In the low tercile, angle power is at most 0.114 at every e (0.018 / 0.048 / 0.060 / 0.114).

Rank selection. Power at e = 1.00 also depends on the CV-selected rank (merged.jsonl). Elsewhere the rank is 2 or 3 in essentially every replicate. At e = 1.00 in the baseline column, 257 of 500 replicates select more than three components, because relocating every differential site creates group-specific variation that CV retains. Those replicates reject angle at 0.506, against 0.082 for the 243 at rank ≤ 3.

Comparison with the pilots. The Phase 5 design-point and ladder pilots measured orientation angle at 0.88 and 0.85 (n = 1200, four stages). The Phase 6 pilot (100 × 199) measured 0.24 at e = 1.00 and the paper-grade run 0.300 ± 0.020, a difference of 1.3 pooled SE (pilot SE about 0.043).

Shape. shape/shape rises to 0.228 at the construction maximum, against a pilot value of 0.18. The shape null is not the limiting factor (q95 near 0.1 in the pilot records). The construction is small: one interior vertex of a three-vertex path.

docs.title: Cohort-size and block-count contrasts
docs.text:
report/design_point_operating.csv, target statistic per mode, at the points where the curves move:

mode / statistic, e baseline (n = 80, 2 blocks) ≥50 nuclei (n = 74, 2 blocks) three blocks (n = 80) n = 74, 3 blocks anchor delta / angle / shape 0.026 / 0.024 / 0.020 0.010 / 0.022 / 0.008 0.062 / 0.020 / 0.056 0.038 / 0.024 / 0.044 magnitude/delta, 0.05 0.206 ± 0.018 0.198 ± 0.018 0.438 ± 0.022 0.436 ± 0.022 magnitude/delta, 0.10 0.542 ± 0.022 0.502 ± 0.022 0.774 ± 0.019 0.770 ± 0.019 orientation/angle, 0.50 0.058 ± 0.010 0.066 ± 0.011 0.162 ± 0.016 0.144 ± 0.016 orientation/angle, 1.00 0.300 ± 0.020 0.112 ± 0.014 0.294 ± 0.020 0.210 ± 0.018 shape/shape, 0.50 0.090 ± 0.013 0.088 ± 0.013 0.306 ± 0.021 0.276 ± 0.020 shape/shape, 1.00 0.228 ± 0.019 0.138 ± 0.015 0.472 ± 0.022 0.448 ± 0.022

Cohort size (baseline vs ≥50 nuclei, two blocks). Dropping six donors leaves magnitude essentially unchanged (0.206 → 0.198; 0.542 → 0.502, within 1.3 pooled SE). It costs orientation/angle at e = 1.00 most of its power (0.300 → 0.112). That drop is a rank-selection effect, not a smooth sample-size effect. At n = 74 only 39 of 500 replicates select more than three components, against 257 at n = 80, and within each rank class power is similar (0.436 vs 0.506 above rank 3; 0.085 vs 0.082 at or below it; merged.jsonl). shape/shape at e = 1.00 falls from 0.228 to 0.138. Below the construction maximum, orientation and shape are unchanged within SE.

Block count (baseline vs three blocks, n = 80, same datasets). The third standardized block raises every mode's power where the curve is rising: - magnitude/delta at 0.05: 0.206 → 0.438; - orientation/angle at 0.50: 0.058 → 0.162; - shape/shape at 0.50: 0.090 → 0.306.

It also raises the null rates of delta and shape from about half of α to near α (0.026 → 0.062, 0.020 → 0.056), so part of the gain is the two-block measurement's conservatism being removed. Orientation at e = 1.00 is the exception (0.300 vs 0.294): there both columns are dominated by the rank-selection effect above.

Interaction column (n = 74, three blocks). It follows the three-block column within SE, except orientation/angle at e = 1.00 (0.210), where rank selection again carries the difference.

docs.title: 6. Cross-talk
docs.text:
The baseline column's off-diagonals are shown below (report/specificity_matrix.csv at the top effect, report/power_curves.csv per effect, and report/phase4_localization.csv for where each first becomes material).

Magnitude's off-diagonals are mandatory controls. magnitude/angle is 0.008–0.024 and magnitude/shape 0.002–0.024 at every e, against the 0.0695 bound. The joint construction stays size-pure at n = 80, as it was at n = 1200.

Orientation → shape and orientation → delta exceed the target statistic. At e = 1.00 they are 0.464 and 0.354, against angle 0.300; at e = 0.50, 0.196 and 0.160 against 0.058. Under the default materiality rule, the localization table labels both projection_associated: they first exceed the rule in the PLS latent space (shape from e = 0.75, normalized excess 0.055–0.077; delta at e = 1.00, 0.062). That label must not be carried into the paper. The magnitude-construction diagnostic (§1, §4) refuted the projection-associated framing for orientation's cross-talk at n = 1200: the response is present within each omic block, and under the recalibrated (null-dispersion) rule no pair localizes as projection-associated. That rule is opt-in and was not used here. The orientation construction is a per-omic feature relocation, and its shape/delta responses are reported as construction cross-talk. They are descriptive gate roles, not acceptance targets.

Shape's off-diagonals are construction-present. shape → angle (0.138 at e = 1.00) is material in the population-standardized geometry from e = 0.25 (normalized 0.236–0.436). shape → delta (0.330) is material from e = 0.75 (0.054–0.065). Bending one vertex of a three-vertex path changes its direction and length, not only its shape. Shape's construction moves delta more often than shape.

docs.title: 7. Drivers
docs.text:
Orientation attribution ran on the four nonzero orientation power_primary cells, observed component only (report/driver_report.csv; contract echo in report/report_contract.json). For each transition (0→1, 1→2), at e = 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 1.00:

e precision (0→1 / 1→2) recall (0→1 / 1→2) mean selected within-replicate bootstrap sign stability 0.25 0.996 / 0.996 0.375 / 0.379 20 0.787 / 0.786 0.50 1.000 / 1.000 0.194 / 0.193 20 0.813 / 0.810 0.75 1.000 / 1.000 0.131 / 0.132 20 0.835 / 0.835 1.00 1.000 / 1.000 0.101 / 0.102 20 0.855 / 0.856

The top-20 observed drivers are almost always true drivers. Recall falls with e because the truth set grows (every relocated site and its cascade) while k stays at 20. bootstrap_top_k_frequency_mean is 0.040 at every cell. That is top_k / n_features (20 / 498) by construction for a mean over all features, so it carries no information here. The attribution figure is report/phase4_attribution_stability.png ("Within-replicate bootstrap stability (observed component)").

No cross-replicate driver-stability claim is made. Cross-replicate top-k Jaccard and sign agreement (top_k_jaccard, sign_agreement in report/phase4_attribution.csv) are descriptive only: every replicate index draws a fresh differential-indicator set, so the true driver set genuinely differs across replicates and matched seeds pair cells within a replicate index, not across them. A stability claim needs a design that holds the driver set fixed, which this study is not.

Driver precision is high even where angle power is low. Attribution describes the observed directional contrast whether or not the angle test rejects, so in the case study a driver list is descriptive and is not evidence of an orientation difference.

docs.title: 8. Construction limitations and case-study interpretability
docs.text:
• This is a structural analogue, not an emulator. InterSIM blocks are Gaussian/M-value with 367 + 131 measured features against 80 samples. SEA-AD RNA and ATAC pseudobulks after VST are only approximately Gaussian and will have thousands of filtered features. The operating characteristics transfer as statements about the design (n, cell sizes, three stages, two blocks, stage-supervised PLS), not about RNA/ATAC distributions. The case-study repo must report its feature filtering beside any result.
  • Orientation power is eigengap- and rank-conditional. At ρ = 0 the three stage means form a near-isotropic triangle, and its eigengap is small (anchor median 0.111). This is the generator's independent-baseline assumption, copied from Phase 5, not a consequence of three stages. The operating characteristics here are not measured at other baseline geometries, and Phase 5 found the orientation construction's realized contrast is not ρ-invariant. In the low eigengap tercile, angle power is at most 0.114 even at the construction maximum. At the construction maximum, power depends on whether CV retains more than three components, which a six-donor change in the cohort moves from 51 % to 8 % of replicates. The Phase 5 exit condition stands: the cohort's own recorded eigengap, not n, is what carries an orientation statement.
  • The orientation and shape constructions are bounded. e = 1.00 relocates every differential site, so no larger construction exists. The HOLD is a statement that these constructions are not detectable at n = 80, not that the effect axis was too short.
  • The statistics are not mode-specific at n = 80. The orientation construction is detected more often by shape and delta than by angle, and the shape construction more often by delta than by shape. Only magnitude is specific: the joint size change leaves angle and shape at the floor.
  • Deviation from the predeclared targets. The orientation/angle and shape/shape power floors (0.80) are missed. Per design D6 this revises the claim, not the method or the Monte Carlo size. MOTCO's orientation and shape tests are not claimed to have useful power at this design.

Per-statistic interpretability for the SEA-AD cohort (n = 80, ≥30 nuclei, RNA + ATAC):

statistic rejection may be reported as evidence? non-rejection may be reported as evidence? delta Yes, that the two sexes' ADNC trajectories differ. Type I is controlled (0.016–0.034). A rejection is consistent with a size difference, but it does not by itself exclude a direction or shape difference, since those constructions also reject delta at up to 0.35. Yes, against large size differences only. Power is 0.956 for a 25 % joint size change and 0.542 for 10 %. A non-rejection argues against a size difference of about 25 % or more, and is uninformative below that. angle Yes, that the trajectories differ (Type I 0.024–0.040), but not specifically in direction. Orientation constructions reject shape and delta more often, and shape constructions reject angle at up to 0.14. Report it with the cohort's recorded eigengap. If that eigengap falls in the simulated low tercile (below about 0.13), a rejection is still valid at level α, but the test had little chance of one. No. Power is at most 0.300, at the strongest construction the generator can build, and 0.03–0.09 below it. A non-rejection is uninformative at n = 80. shape Yes, that the trajectories differ (Type I 0.018–0.020), but not specifically in shape. The orientation construction rejects shape at 0.464, more than either angle or the shape construction's own 0.228. No. Power is at most 0.228 at the construction maximum. A non-rejection is uninformative at n = 80.

Using the ≥50-nuclei cohort (n = 74) leaves these statements unchanged for delta and makes angle and shape weaker still. Adding a third standardized block would raise power for all three statistics, but the case study has two blocks.

docs.title: 9. Reproduction
docs.text:
Reproduction never passes a worker-count override: n_jobs is part of every cell's parameter signature and both configs' contracts forbid it (the runner exits 2). Parallelize across shards. Avoid nodes under memory pressure: a stalled shard can be cancelled and resubmitted, and the signature-guarded resume skips completed units.

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1

# SLURM (partition/resource flags are cluster-specific); STUDY_N_JOBS must stay unset.
for P in magnitude:phase6-small-n-magnitude-2026-10-09 study:phase6-small-n-2026-10-09; do
  CFG=examples/trajectory_power_study/phase6_small_n_${P%%:*}.json; RUN=results/${P#*:}
  sbatch -p <partition> --cpus-per-task=1 --mem=2G --time=8:00:00 --array=0-99 \
      --export=ALL,STUDY_CONFIG=$(pwd)/$CFG,STUDY_OUT=$(pwd)/$RUN,N_SHARDS=100 \
      scripts/motco_study_array.sbatch
done

# After completion, per profile:
uv run python scripts/motco_study.py merge  --out-dir $RUN
uv run python scripts/motco_study.py report --config $CFG --out-dir $RUN

Each run commits report/ and PROVENANCE.txt and leaves the shard and merged JSONL gitignored. The pilot that fixed the effect axes is results/phase6-small-n-pilot-2026-10-09/ (NOTES.md, PROVENANCE.txt).

docs.title: Plasmode attribution demonstration on SEA-AD astrocytes — 2026-11-02
docs.text:
This report runs the plasmode demonstration (openspec change plasmode-attribution-demonstration, spec plasmode-attribution-demonstration; roadmap Next changes item 12). Phase 6 closed with its attribution leg withheld (exit review §1 G1, §6): neither case study had a global trajectory claim to trace. Item 11 made attribution available with declared covariates and validated it on semi-synthetic data (report). This check plants a known group × stage orientation difference in SEA-AD's real exported blocks, covariates and design, analyses each unit as the case study does, and asks whether the difference is detected and traced back to the planted features. A rule fixed before any unit either lifts the leg or reports it failed.

Every number below is read from results/plasmode-2026-11-02/: - plasmode_decision.json, plasmode_summary.csv, merge.json, settings.json, sacct.txt, PROVENANCE.txt; - fidelity.json, calibration.json (every calibration iteration) and calibration_sacct.txt; - diagnostic/latent_capture.json (the label-free diagnostic in §4) and the indicative smoke in smoke/ (R = 20 × 99 permutations × B = 50).

The per-unit records, merged.jsonl, plasmode_units.csv and plasmode_metrics.csv stay on ing; PROVENANCE.txt names them with their sha256. No file in the repository holds a donor identifier, a label vector or a donor-level value. Readings are over R = 500 units per cell at 999 permutations and B = 200 bootstrap replicates, on the observed component of the principal-orientation block of the covariate-adjusted (primary) arm, unless stated otherwise.

Run. - Calibration: one 40-CPU job on ing (job 932595, n1, 18 min 49 s, COMPLETED 0:0), the fidelity gate first. - Paper grade: one SLURM array on ing (job 932620, partition 512x1024, n11 excluded, 150 shards of 10 units), from a detached worktree of feat/plasmode-attribution-demonstration at dd5981f, whose git tree c0d285a3… equals the workstation's. The export was copied to ing, and its five files' sha256 equal the settings'. - All 150 tasks ended COMPLETED 0:0 between 21:36 and 21:55 (−03:00) on 2026-11-02. 1,500 of 1,500 units, zero consistency failures, zero label redraws. 73.1 elapsed core-hours; the units' own timers sum to 68.3 h (median 178.5 s per unit). - merge and decide ran on ing. The decision file's settings hash 734bb538… equals settings.json's.

Verdict: attribution_leg_failed, read verbatim from plasmode_decision.json ("indicative": false, 500 replicates per cell, adopted calibration iteration 4, cap_reached). The failing criteria are (ii) detection and two parts of (iii): planted-set precision and top-k frequency.

In one paragraph. - The construction. SEA-AD MTG astrocytes cohort_30 (n = 80, RNA and ATAC, 10,000 features), analysed exactly as the case-study primary: six covariates, rank floor 2, net displacement, the df correction. In each unit the sex labels are permuted within stage, which removes any real sex × stage structure. Then 20 random features (10 per block) drift with stage in the donors labelled male, up to e within-stage SDs at the last stage. - Size holds on the real data. At the anchor (no plant) delta, angle and shape reject at 0.042, 0.048 and 0.026, under the bound of 0.0695. - The test does not see the plant. Calibration found no ladder step at which angle rejected: 0 of 40 units at every e from 0.5 to 3.0. At e* = 3.0, the cap, angle rejects in 0.036 of 500 units, the null rate. delta (0.026) and shape (0.016) are flat too. - Why. The measurement lives in a five-dimensional stage-PLS space that holds 99.9 % of the pooled stage displacement, but only 2.2 % of a planted direction: what any random direction in 10,000 dimensions gets (§4). The PLS-captured component recovers none of the plant (planted-set precision 0.001). - Attribution sees part of it, unstably. Over all 500 units at e*, about a third of the observed contrast's top-20 is planted (0.344, against 0.0023 at the anchor), with stable signs (0.957), but each planted feature enters the top-20 in only 6 % of bootstrap resamples. - Consequence. The Phase 6 attribution leg is reported failed, on detection first. The case study's non-rejection says nothing about sex differences carried by a few features; Phase 6 is not reopened and no case-study reading changes.

docs.title: 1. Construction
docs.text:
scripts/plasmode_check.py (fidelity | calibrate | run | merge | decide) reads the export in place and commits aggregates only.

Input contract. The export directory is sead_sexdiff's results/motco_input/cohort_30 (export manifest from ab3423a, read with sead_sexdiff at 2d427b0). The check requires its manifest.json to declare exactly the blocks rna and atac (5,000 TMM log2-CPM features each, identity transform), the groups Female/Male and the stage order 0/1/2, and it reads metadata.csv and covariates.csv. A violation (donor mismatch, unknown stage, not exactly two groups, missing covariate, and others) raises a named error before any analysis. The sha256 of the five files read are part of the settings, so a resume on another export is refused.

Covariates. The primary's six, in its model order: age_at_death, pmi, rin, years_education, log10_n_rna and log10_n_atac. The last two are the base-10 logarithms of n_rna and n_atac, derived in MOTCO as sead_sexdiff's ANALYSIS_LOG10_COLUMNS derives them (src/sead_sexdiff/data.py at 2d427b0); a unit test pins the derivation.

Fidelity gate. The stage-PLS latent space is stage-supervised and covariate-blind, so it does not depend on the sex labels. One analysis on a within-stage permutation, with no permutations and no attribution, had to reproduce the primary's CV-selected rank 5 and mean held-out stage AUROC 0.635556. It did on the workstation and on ing (fidelity.json: rank 5, AUROC 0.6355555…). Every anchor unit was held to the same check, and all 500 passed (rank 5.0, AUROC 0.635556).

Null-making step. Each replicate permutes the sex column within each stage, so the cell table [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]] is kept and every donor's blocks and covariates stay on its own row. A draw equal to the real labels is refused and redrawn; none was. The analysis under the real labels is never run. Size at the anchor is therefore size conditional on this export: the 500 units are label draws on one data matrix.

Plant. In the donors labelled Male under the permuted labels (31 donors), each feature f of a planted set K is shifted by e · c(stage) · σ_f · s_f: - K is 10 RNA and 10 ATAC features drawn uniformly per replicate, s_f a uniform sign; - σ_f is the export's pooled within-stage SD (ddof = 3), so e is in within-stage SD units at the last stage; - c is 0, 0.5 and 1 at stages 0, 1 and 2, so the ramp adds no offset at baseline.

At e* = 3.0 a planted feature in a male donor moves by 1.5 within-stage SDs at stage 1 and 3 SDs at stage 2. The plant is nearly orthogonal to the shared trajectory: its cosine with the pooled stage displacement averages 0.0001 (SE 0.0005). At e = 0 the blocks are the export, byte for byte.

Seeds. Every draw derives from base seed 2034 (no committed check uses it), the stream (paper, calibration or fidelity), the replicate and the purpose (labels, plant, RRPP, bootstrap), never from the strength. The three cells of a replicate share the labels, K, the signs, the RRPP seed and the bootstrap seed.

Arms, on one analysis per unit. - adjusted (primary). analyze_trajectories with the six covariates, covariate-adjusted attribution (B = 200, top-k 20), min_components 2, net displacement, residual_correction="df", the harness CV knobs (random_state 1203) and 999 permutations. - unadjusted (descriptive). The attribution primitive on the analysis's latent_artifacts without covariates, with the same bootstrap seed. It cannot lift the leg. - Each unit first checked that the exposed estimator reproduces the latent scores and that the adjusted means project to the analysis's stage means (to 1e-8 relative); no unit failed.

Metrics per arm, block and component: the planted-set precision |top-20 ∩ K| / 20, the mean bootstrap sign stability and top-k frequency over all 20 planted features, and the share of recovered planted features whose observed sign is the planted one.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
The ladder e ∈ {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0} was climbed with 40 units per step at 99 permutations, attribution off, from the calibration stream. The rule adopts the first step at which angle rejects in at least 0.90 of the units, and otherwise proceeds at the cap. Every iteration is in calibration.json:

e delta angle shape CV-selected rank (count of 40) outcome 0.5 2/40 0/40 1/40 5: 35, 2: 4, 10: 1 climb 1.0 1/40 0/40 1/40 5: 25, 2: 11, 7: 2, 10: 1, 12: 1 climb 1.5 2/40 0/40 0/40 5: 22, 2: 12, 7: 4, 8: 1, 11: 1 climb 2.0 1/40 0/40 0/40 5: 24, 2: 9, 7: 4, 8: 2, 11: 1 climb 3.0 1/40 0/40 0/40 5: 24, 2: 8, 7: 3, 8: 4, 11: 1 cap_reached

So e* = 3.0 and the descriptive cell is 2.0. The user approved the paper grade at the cap, as the rule predeclares, after seeing this table. The smoke (R = 20 at e = 1.0, indicative) had already read angle 2/20.

docs.title: 2. Criteria
docs.text:
criterion cell R mean SE reading bound verdict (i) size, delta anchor 500 0.042 0.0090 0.042 ≤ 0.0695 holds (i) size, angle anchor 500 0.048 0.0096 0.048 ≤ 0.0695 holds (i) size, shape anchor 500 0.026 0.0071 0.026 ≤ 0.0695 holds (ii) detection, angle e = 3 500 0.036 0.0083 0.036 ≥ 0.80 fails (iii) planted-set precision (−2·SE) e = 3 18 0.3083 0.0662 0.1759 ≥ 0.50 fails (iii) sign stability over K (−2·SE) e = 3 18 0.9630 0.0066 0.9498 ≥ 0.90 holds (iii) top-k frequency over K (−2·SE) e = 3 18 0.0646 0.0075 0.0496 ≥ 0.50 fails

The size bound is α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/R) at α = 0.05. Criterion (iii) reads the 18 units at e* whose angle rejects, as predeclared; with detection at the null rate those are mostly chance rejections, which the next section's unconditional readings confirm.

docs.title: 3. Verdict and consequence
docs.text:
Verdict: attribution_leg_failed. Size holds; detection fails at the cap, and so do planted-set precision and top-k frequency. The decision file's consequence, verbatim: "the Phase 6 G1 attribution leg is reported failed, naming the failing criteria; Phase 6 is not reopened and no case-study reading changes".

  • The Phase 6 attribution leg moves from withheld to failed. At the case study's design, the shipped analysis could not be shown to trace a planted orientation difference to its drivers. It fails at detection: a difference the test does not detect is never handed to attribution in the workflow the leg describes.
  • The case-study reading is unchanged and sharpened. The SEA-AD primary's non-rejection was already bracketed as uninformative. It is now also measured to be blind to sex differences confined to a few features: a 3-SD ramp on 20 of 10,000 features is not detected.
  • Size at the case study's configuration holds on the real export, conditionally on it (§1), which complements the semi-synthetic Type I and corrected-permutation reports.

docs.title: 4. Why the test does not see the plant
docs.text:
The trajectory statistics are measured in the stage-PLS latent space, five dimensions fitted to the stage label across all 10,000 features. diagnostic/latent_capture.py fits that space at the primary's rank (forced 5) on the unplanted export and measures, in analysed coordinates, the share of a direction's norm that falls inside it:

  • the pooled stage displacement: 99.94 %;
  • 200 planted directions drawn as the check draws them: median 2.16 % (q05–q95 1.11–3.20 %), against 2.24 % for any random direction (√(5/10,000)).

A planted direction is therefore almost entirely outside the measured subspace. At e = 3 its norm in analysed units is about 13.4 (4.47 per unit of e), and it applies to 31 of 80 donors. Only about 0.3 of those units (2 % of 13.4) can enter the measured subspace, against a pooled stage displacement of 39.7 that lies almost entirely inside it.

Refitting the space on the planted data does not rescue it. The planted cells' CV-selected rank barely moves (mean 4.85 at e = 3, 4.88 at e = 2, against 5.0 at the anchor), the held-out stage AUROC rises only from 0.6356 to 0.6442, and the PLS-captured component of the attribution recovers no planted feature (planted-set precision 0.001 at e = 3, against 0.432 for the residual component). The plant lives in the part of feature space the measurement discards.

docs.title: 5. Descriptive readings
docs.text:
None of these enters the verdict.

  • Unconditional readings at e* (all 500 units): planted-set precision 0.344 (SE 0.009), sign stability over K 0.957 (SE 0.001), top-k frequency over K 0.060 (SE 0.001). They agree with the 18 rejecting units, so the conditioning selected no favourable subset. Where planted features are recovered, their observed sign is the planted one in every case (sign agreement 1.0 over the 478 units with at least one hit).
  • False-recovery reference. At the anchor the planted-set precision is 0.0023 (SE 0.0005) and the sign stability over K 0.699: chance for 20 random features among 10,000. Against it, the observed contrast at e* is about 150 times enriched for the planted set, without being stable.
  • The descriptive cell (e = 2.0). delta / angle / shape reject at 0.030 / 0.034 / 0.020. Unconditionally, planted-set precision is 0.168, sign stability 0.918 and top-k frequency 0.033: the same picture at a lower dose.
  • The unadjusted arm. At e* it recovers more than the adjusted arm: planted-set precision 0.453 over all units (0.375 on the rejecting units), sign stability 0.971, top-k frequency 0.092. Plausibly, refitting six covariate coefficients on n = 80 adds variance to the adjusted contrast, while there is no confounding for it to remove: the within-stage permutation balances the covariates across the permuted groups in expectation. The check does not test that explanation.
  • Components. The PLS-captured component recovers nothing (planted-set precision 0.001 over all units at e*, sign stability 0.691, the anchor's level); the residual component carries the recovery (0.432, 0.955, 0.072).
  • Transitions. The per-transition contrasts recover little (planted-set precision 0.018 for 0->1 and 0.030 for 1->2 over all units at e*), although their signs are stable (0.958 and 0.965). Each transition carries half the ramp, and a single step between two cell means is plausibly noisier than the configuration's principal axis.
  • Degeneracy. The principal axis is flagged near-isotropic in 10.6 % of anchor units and 9.4 % at e = 3 and e = 2.

docs.title: 6. Limitations and scope
docs.text:
• One kind of plant. The plant is sparse (20 random features), linear in stage and confined to one group. That is the kind the stage-PLS measurement is blind to by construction (§4). A dense difference aligned with the stage signal, which rotates the shared trajectory inside the measured subspace, was not tested. Testing it would be a new check with its own predeclared rule, not a rescue of this one.
  • A stylized strength. e* = 3.0 within-stage SDs is the predeclared cap, large for 20 features; the design chose not to extend the ladder after calibration. The result is a statement about traceability of a known signal on real noise, covariates and design, not about power at a realistic effect.
  • Conditional size. Size at the anchor is conditional on this export (§1); the unconditional size at the case study's configuration is in the case-study Type I and corrected-permutation reports.
  • Recovery read on rejecting units. Criterion (iii) reads 18 units, most of them chance rejections. The unconditional readings over 500 units agree with it.
  • One cohort. Only astrocyte cohort_30 is measured. Microglia, cohort_50 and ADNI are not.

docs.title: Predictive-subspace size excess — diagnosis report (2026-11-13)
docs.text:
Change: predictive-size-excess-diagnosis (no package change; MOTCO 0.24.0). Reads: results/predictive-size-excess-2026-11-13/ (predictive_size_excess_decision.json; the rate, paired and cell tables; accounting.json, reproduction.json, preflight.json, settings.json; PROVENANCE.txt, sacct.txt). Parent: the predictive-subspace pilot. Concept page: measurement visibility.

The predictive-subspace pilot read keep_production on one finding. On the SEA-AD plasmode anchor (500 permuted-label replicates of the astrocyte export) all three predictive coordinate systems rejected delta in 65–68 units and shape in 38–39, where production rejected 21 and 13. No simulated design reproduced the excess.

Roadmap open item 2 named a guess. The two predictive directions of the rank-5 fit hold its in-sample stage fit (stage R² 0.84 against a held-out AUROC of 0.636), and the reduced model's residuals in them are not exchangeable across stages, which RRPP's draws assume. Two checks test it on the pilot's own units, labels and RRPP seeds, under a decision fixed before any unit ran (design.md D8):

  • Check W keeps the coordinates and changes the null. RRPP's draws are restricted within stage: the reduced model's residuals are permuted among the donors of each stage, never across stages.
  • Check O keeps the null and changes the coordinates. The fitted stage indicators are computed out of fold: each donor's row comes from a stage-PLS model fitted without it.

In one paragraph. The verdict is both_restore. Each repair alone brings the predictive coordinates' anchor rates within the size rule the pilot applied, so the excess needs both the unrestricted draws and coordinates fitted on the donors they measure.

  • Within-stage draws remove the delta excess entirely. 37–38 units are rejected only under the unrestricted draws, and none only under the within-stage ones; delta falls from 0.130–0.136 to 0.056–0.062. They remove little of the shape excess. shape falls from 0.076–0.078 to 0.064–0.066 (5–6 discordant units, all one way), so it holds the rule by one or two counts and stays at about 2.5 times production's 0.026.
  • The out-of-fold coordinates read 0.016 / 0.014 / 0.034, but at the anchor they carry almost no stage signal: the out-of-fold fit explains a median 0.022 of the stage indicators' variance, against 0.84 in sample.
  • On the real-noise plant the within-stage arms keep delta above production's at e = 0.5 (0.64–0.66 against 0.51), but production gains as much under the same draws (0.63).
  • Without covariates the predictive excess stays, so the six covariates and their df correction do not cause it.
  • The rule's consequence. A follow-up change may propose within-stage draws as an opt-in option and read their size and power before predictive_orthonormal is re-read. The pilot's keep_production stands.

docs.title: 1. Configuration and provenance
docs.text:
• The units. The pilot's 800 plasmode units (predictive_subspace_check.plasmode_settings / plasmode_units, imported unchanged): the anchor at the paper stream's replicates 0–499, and the production selection's real-noise span plant at e ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0} at replicates 0–99. All run at 999 permutations with rejection at p ≤ 0.05. Each unit carries the pilot's label draw (within-stage, base seed 2034), plant and RRPP seed. The configuration is the case study's: six covariates, the df residual correction, net displacement and rank floor 2. The export is the SEA-AD MTG astrocyte cohort_30 (RNA and ATAC, 5,000 features each, 80 donors, cells F 11 / 10 / 28 and M 9 / 10 / 12), read in place through the plasmode's contract.
  • One fit per unit.
  • An anchor unit fits at the plasmode's committed fidelity rank of 5 without cross-validation. The anchor does not move the label-free features, so every anchor unit's CV selects that rank.
  • A plant unit runs the production CV once, and every other arm is forced at the rank it selects (4–14; medians 7, 7 and 5 at e = 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0).
  • The pre-flight required the cross-validated fit on anchor replicates 0 and 1 to select rank 5 at AUROC 0.635556, and to give the forced call's statistics and p-values exactly. It passed on the workstation and on ing.
  • The fourteen arms (design.md D7), each at the unit's RRPP seed with serial draws:
arm coordinates draws covariates role pls_cv scores unrestricted six reference predictive, predictive_orthonormal, predictive_fitted in-sample predictive unrestricted six reference predictive__within_stage, predictive_orthonormal__within_stage, predictive_fitted__within_stage in-sample predictive within stage six check W, decisive fitted_out_of_fold out-of-fold fitted indicators unrestricted six check O, decisive pls_cv__within_stage scores within stage six descriptive fitted_out_of_fold__within_stage out-of-fold fitted indicators within stage six descriptive <reference arm>__no_covariates (four) as named unrestricted none descriptive
  • Within-stage draws. Per draw, each stage's residual rows are permuted among themselves, in declared stage order, from default_rng(the unit's RRPP seed). Everything else is RRPP's: the reduced fit, the df scale and estimate_difference per draw. The driver's loop equals RRPP exactly when every row is in one stratum (a test). One restricted sequence per unit is shared by every within-stage arm.
  • Out-of-fold coordinates. Four stage-stratified, shuffled folds per replicate, seeded from the driver's name, base seed 2037, the replicate and folds. For each fold, fit_plsda_model is fitted on the other three folds' rows of the analysis's PLS input features, at the unit's rank and scaling. The held-out rows then get transform(X_held) · y_loadingsᵀ, the fitted stage indicators in that model's response units. With every donor in training, the same computation returns predictive_fitted to 1e-8 (a test). Each training set holds 15 / 15 / 30 donors by stage.
  • Checks on every unit.
  • The pilot's five consistency checks.
  • same_fit_covariate_free: each covariate-free arm fitted the production model.
  • path_identity: the driver's inference path, under unrestricted draws, returns each reference arm's statistics to 1e-10 and its p-values exactly.
  • Code and host. Revision 7046672 on proposal/predictive-size-excess-diagnosis, run from a clean detached worktree on ing (partition 512x1024, nodes n1 and n3). Python 3.11.16, numpy 2.3.5, scipy 1.16.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0 and pandas 2.3.3, with BLAS pinned to one thread. Preparation job 938594, array 938598 (100 shards) and finishing job 938732; every allocation completed with exit 0:0. 10.92 recorded core-hours, against a projection of about 11.5 and a cap of 20 (PROVENANCE.txt).

docs.title: 2. Accounting and reproduction
docs.text:
• Units. 800 of 800 complete: no failed unit, no failed arm, no inconsistent unit and no duplicate record.
  • Checks. Every applicable check held on every unit. The largest deviations were path_identity 0, same_fit 0, same_fit_covariate_free 0, rank 0 and fitted_labels 5.3e-14. Every covariate-free arm's latent matrix equals its reference arm's exactly.
  • Reproduction: passed. Each of the four reference arms' available and rejected counts, in each of the four cells, for delta, angle and shape, equals the pilot's committed rate_table.csv: 48 of 48 rows. The forced anchor fit therefore reproduces the pilot's cross-validated anchor counts exactly (21 / 24 / 13 for pls_cv, 68 / 11 / 38 for predictive, 67 / 9 / 38 for predictive_orthonormal, 65 / 10 / 39 for predictive_fitted).

docs.title: 3. The decision
docs.text:
Rule version 1 grades each decisive arm on its three anchor readings:

  • restored: the arm holds the stage-span paper grade's count-plus-ceiling rule (judge_rates, m = 3). This is the rule and the family the pilot's S1 failed. At R = 500 a reading exceeds the bound α + 2·SE = 0.0695 above 34 rejections, the ceiling is 36, and one exceedance is allowed.
  • reduced: not restored, and the one-sided exact paired p-value for fewer rejections than the arm's counterpart is at most 0.025 on delta or shape.
  • unchanged: otherwise.

Check W takes the weakest grade of its three arms, and check O the grade of its one arm.

arm delta angle shape exceedances grade pilot's counterpart predictive__within_stage 31 (0.062) 17 (0.034) 33 (0.066) 0 restored 68 / 11 / 38 predictive_orthonormal__within_stage 29 (0.058) 17 (0.034) 32 (0.064) 0 restored 67 / 9 / 38 predictive_fitted__within_stage 28 (0.056) 17 (0.034) 33 (0.066) 0 restored 65 / 10 / 39 fitted_out_of_fold 8 (0.016) 7 (0.014) 17 (0.034) 0 restored 65 / 10 / 39 (predictive_fitted)

Check W is restored, and so is check O. The verdict is both_restore. The gate passed: the reproduction passed, no unit was inconsistent and the pre-flight passed.

The consequence fixed with the rule: "The unrestricted draws are what fails in the predictive subspace on this export, and the out-of-fold reading confirms that the in-sample fit is where the excess lives. A follow-up change may propose within-stage draws as an opt-in option and must read their size and power on the pilot's simulated designs, the weak design and this anchor before predictive_orthonormal is re-read."

docs.title: 4. Check W: what the within-stage draws repair
docs.text:
Paired against each arm's counterpart (the same coordinates under unrestricted draws) on the 500 anchor units. b counts the units only the counterpart rejects, and c the units only the within-stage arm rejects:

arm delta b / c delta p (fewer) shape b / c shape p (fewer) predictive__within_stage 37 / 0 7.3e-12 5 / 0 0.031 predictive_orthonormal__within_stage 38 / 0 3.6e-12 6 / 0 0.016 predictive_fitted__within_stage 37 / 0 7.3e-12 6 / 0 0.016
  • delta. The within-stage null removes the whole excess, and only that. Every unit the restricted draws stop rejecting was one the unrestricted draws rejected, and none goes the other way. Against production's unrestricted rates the within-stage arms still read slightly more (17–19 units against 9–10; two-sided p 0.09–0.25).
  • shape. It barely moves: 5–6 units, all one way. The arms hold the rule at 32–33 rejections against the exceedance threshold of 34. Against production shape stays higher: 26 units against 6–7, two-sided p 0.0005–0.0013. Production itself reads 19 under the same within-stage draws (§7).
  • angle rises from 9–11 to 17 and stays well inside the bound.

So restored is firm for delta and marginal for shape. The rule grades both alike; the follow-up has to read shape again.

docs.title: 5. Check O: what the out-of-fold coordinates show
docs.text:
fitted_out_of_fold reads 8 / 7 / 17 on the anchor. Against predictive_fitted that is 64 / 7 discordant units on delta and 38 / 16 on shape. Against production's unrestricted rates it rejects less delta (20 / 7) and less angle (21 / 4), with shape close (13 / 17).

The reading is weaker evidence than its grade suggests. At the anchor the out-of-fold coordinates carry almost no stage signal. The out-of-fold fit explains a median 0.022 of the stage indicators' variance, against 0.84 in sample on every anchor unit. Its angle null has a median 95th percentile of 94.9°, so the net displacement it measures is close to noise.

What the arm shows is that the excess needs coordinates fitted on the donors they measure. It does not show that a cross-fitted measurement is usable at this design. Under within-stage draws the same coordinates read 23 / 18 / 23 (descriptive), also inside the rule.

docs.title: 6. The plant cells (descriptive)
docs.text:
delta rejection rates at R = 100. The paired tests are one-sided, for a gain against pls_cv:

arm e = 0.25 e = 0.5 e = 1.0 e = 0.5 against pls_cv (b / c, p) pls_cv 0.24 0.51 1.00 — predictive, predictive_orthonormal, predictive_fitted 0.40–0.42 0.79–0.82 1.00 1–2 / 30–32, ≤ 1.2e-7 predictive*__within_stage 0.28–0.29 0.64–0.66 1.00 8–9 / 22–23, 0.005–0.015 pls_cv__within_stage 0.24 0.63 1.00 0 / 12, 0.00024 fitted_out_of_fold 0.81 0.99 1.00 0 / 48, 3.6e-15 fitted_out_of_fold__within_stage 0.82 0.99 1.00 —
  • The within-stage arms keep part of the real-noise gain. At e = 0.5 they read 0.64–0.66, above production's 0.51 (the decision's statement for each restored arm), and below their unrestricted counterparts' 0.79–0.82 (14–16 units, all one way).
  • Production gains under the same draws. It reads 0.63 at e = 0.5 (12 units, all one way). The within-stage draws keep the pooled stage means at their fitted values, which narrows the delta null against a magnitude edit of one group's configuration. Within-stage draws against within-stage draws, the predictive coordinates' advantage is therefore small: 0.64–0.66 against 0.63 at e = 0.5, and 0.28–0.29 against 0.24 at e = 0.25. No paired test of that pair was predeclared, so these are rates only.
  • The out-of-fold arm reads 0.81 and 0.99, above every in-sample arm. The design expected the opposite, a lower bound. The plant is defined by the full sample's stage means. A plausible reading, not tested here: each fold model is fitted on 60 of the same 80 donors, so it recovers the planted direction, while a held-out donor's own noise is not fitted into its coordinates. On that reading the out-of-fold plant rate reflects how the plant is built, not real-noise power. The arm also leaks shape there (0.16 at e = 0.5).

docs.title: 7. Production under within-stage draws (descriptive)
docs.text: pls_cv__within_stage reads 19 / 27 / 19 on the anchor, inside the rule. Against pls_cv the paired counts are 4 / 2 on delta, 0 / 3 on angle and 0 / 6 on shape (two-sided p 0.69, 0.25 and 0.031). Production holds size under either null on this anchor. On the plant it gains delta power under the within-stage draws (§6) and reads more off-target shape (0.11 at e = 0.25 and e = 0.5, against 0.09 and 0.04).

docs.title: 8. The covariate-free arms (descriptive)
docs.text:
arm delta angle shape against the six-covariate counterpart, delta (b / c, two-sided p) pls_cv__no_covariates 41 (0.082) 14 16 3 / 23, 0.0001 predictive__no_covariates 63 (0.126) 14 42 12 / 7, 0.36 predictive_orthonormal__no_covariates 61 (0.122) 14 41 13 / 7, 0.26 predictive_fitted__no_covariates 60 (0.120) 15 44 14 / 9, 0.40
  • The predictive excess does not come from the covariates. Without them the three arms read the same delta and shape excess as with them: no paired difference has p below 0.26.
  • Production without covariates exceeds on delta. It reads 0.082, above the bound of 0.0695, with 23 units against 3. The df correction then follows the four-column reduced model. On this anchor production's delta size depends on having the covariates in the trajectory model. The case study runs with them; this reading is a lead about the covariate-free configuration, not about the case study.

docs.title: 9. Dispersion by stage and the stage fit (descriptive)
docs.text:
On each unit, each stage's mean squared residual norm under the six-covariate reduced model, divided by the pooled value. The table gives medians over the 500 anchor units; stages are 0 / 1 / 2 in declared order, with 20 / 20 / 40 donors.
