coordinates stage 0 stage 1 stage 2 max / min scores 0.805 0.921 1.137 1.41 predictive 1.121 1.178 0.852 1.39 predictive_orthonormal 1.120 1.278 0.802 1.59 predictive_fitted 1.091 1.252 0.830 1.51 out of fold 0.841 0.564 1.293 2.32
  • The size of the inequality does not separate the predictive coordinates from the scores (1.39–1.59 against 1.41).
  • Its direction does. In the scores the largest stage is the widest. In the predictive coordinates it is the narrowest (0.80–0.85), and the two 20-donor stages are wider (1.09–1.28). The in-sample fit tightens the stage with the most donors along the directions it fitted.
  • What the unrestricted draws do with it. They move residuals between stages of unequal dispersion, and the within-stage draws do not. The measured delta excess is consistent with that. The table describes the pattern; it does not test the mechanism.
  • The stage fit. In-sample stage R² is 0.840 on every anchor unit, against a median out-of-fold share of 0.022. On the plant cells the two readings are 0.95 / 0.27, 0.95 / 0.40 and 0.87 / 0.49 at e = 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0. The plant adds stage signal that survives out of fold.

docs.title: 10. Null widths (descriptive)
docs.text:
Median angle null 95th percentile on the anchor:

arm degrees pls_cv 40.2 pls_cv__within_stage 38.8 predictive, predictive_orthonormal, predictive_fitted 11.0–12.1 their within-stage arms 9.3–10.2 fitted_out_of_fold 94.9 fitted_out_of_fold__within_stage 74.1

The predictive coordinates' angle null is narrow, as in the pilot. Within-stage draws narrow it further, and their angle rejections rise from 9–11 to 17, still well inside the bound.

docs.title: 11. What follows
docs.text:
• The verdict's consequence. A separate change may propose within-stage draws as an opt-in option of RRPP, the harness and motco analyze, byte-identical when unset, and must read their size and power on the pilot's simulated designs, the weak design and this anchor. Only its verdict could reopen predictive_orthonormal, under the admissibility rule the roadmap requires.
  • What that change should carry from this reading.
  • shape stays near the bound under within-stage draws on this anchor (0.064–0.066), so its size reading cannot be assumed.
  • Production gains as well. Production gains plant power under within-stage draws (0.51 → 0.63 at e = 0.5), so any comparison of measurement spaces must pair them under the same draws. The predictive coordinates' advantage over production then shrinks to a few points on the plant.
  • The null is a design question, not only a predictive-subspace one. Within-stage draws assume exchangeability within stage only, which is weaker than RRPP's assumption, and they keep the pooled stage means at their fitted values.
  • The pilot's keep_production stands. The predictive values stay opt-in diagnostics. No verdict here validates a test or changes a default.
  • Open item 2 keeps its prediction for ADNI. The guess was confirmed on this export, so the predicted excess should shrink as donors per feature grow. Reading it needs ADNI's export contract.
  • A covariate-free lead. Production without covariates exceeds on delta at this anchor (§8). Whether that holds beyond one fit is unread.

docs.title: 12. Limitations
docs.text:
• One export and one fit. The 500 anchor units share one latent matrix and differ only in the group labels, so every anchor rate is conditional on that fit (as the pilot's were). The out-of-fold arm averages over fold splits, not over donors.
  • The within-stage null mirrors how the plasmode draws its labels. The plasmode permutes the labels within stage, so the restricted draws match the anchor's null by construction. Whether they hold size where residuals are exchangeable across stages, and what they cost in power, is the follow-up's simulation reading.
  • shape holds by one or two counts. At R = 500 the within-stage arms sit at 32–33 against a threshold of 34. A rerun on new label draws could put one of them over it.
  • The out-of-fold arm's restored comes with almost no stage signal (§5), and its plant reading reflects the plant's construction (§6).
  • The plant cells are R = 100 and descriptive. No paired test between the within-stage predictive arms and production under the same draws was predeclared.
  • The rank is chosen on all donors. It is one integer, selected by held-out AUROC and pinned at 5 on the anchor.

docs.title: Predictive-subspace coordinates — findings report (2026-11-12)
docs.text:
Change: predictive-subspace-coordinates (MOTCO 0.24.0). Reads: results/predictive-subspace-2026-11-12/ (predictive_subspace_decision.json; simulation/, weak_size/ and plasmode/ rate, paired and cell tables, accounting.json, reproduction.json, settings.json; PROVENANCE.txt, sacct.txt). Concept page: measurement visibility.

Production uses the CV-selected rank A of the stage-PLS fit for two jobs: it regularizes the fit, and it is the number of dimensions delta, angle and shape are measured in. The stage labels are one-hot, so the fit's Y loadings have rank K − 1 whatever A is, and the fitted stage labels move only along K − 1 directions of the score space: the predictive subspace. MOTCO 0.24.0 measures there on request, in three coordinate systems on one subspace:

  • predictive: the scores projected on it;
  • predictive_orthonormal: the input coordinates on an orthonormal basis of it;
  • predictive_fitted: the fitted stage indicators.

This pilot read the three against production on matched units under a decision fixed in advance (design.md D7).

In one paragraph. The verdict is keep_production. All three coordinate systems read size_excess on the SEA-AD plasmode's real noise.

  • Real noise. On 500 permuted-label replicates of the astrocyte export, production rejects delta in 21 and shape in 13. Each predictive arm rejects delta in 65–68 (0.13–0.136) and shape in 38–39 (0.076–0.078), above the family's ceiling of 0.072. The excess is paired: about 50 units reject only under the candidate, against 5–6 that reject only under production.
  • Simulation. Size holds at every design, the weak one included (500 replicates × 999 permutations).
  • Power. The arms lose no protected power anywhere and gain in 10 of the 18 δ = 2.0 target cells at the Bonferroni threshold. In the stage-effect band, between δ = 2.0 and the weak design, the gains are large: the n = 200 rotation at δ = 0.5 and e = 0.1 goes from 0.06 to 0.94. On the plasmode's real-noise plant delta goes from 0.51 to 0.79–0.82 at e = 0.5.
  • Specificity separates the three. predictive raises production's rotation-into-shape leak in the band. predictive_fitted leaks at δ = 2.0. predictive_orthonormal passes both families.
  • So the subspace's gains are real on simulated noise, and on real noise it does not hold size.

docs.title: 1. Configuration and provenance
docs.text:
• The unit. Each unit builds one dataset, fits the production stage-PLS space once (double-CV rank, floor 2, net displacement) and evaluates these arms on it, serially, at the unit's RRPP seed:
  • pls_cv: production, in the fit's scores;
  • predictive, predictive_orthonormal, predictive_fitted: the three coordinate systems on the predictive subspace of that same fit, built without refitting;
  • forced_k_minus_1: the fit forced to K − 1 = 2 components, the control that lowers the fit rank instead of the measured dimension;
  • predictive_rank_plus_one: predictive on the fit forced to A + 1 components (simulation only).

The arms share data, fit and permutation indices, so the decision compares them by exact paired tests on the discordant units. Every unit also checks that the predictive arms measure the production fit (five checks, design.md D5). - simulation profile. A fresh seed family (base seed 2036; the probe spent 4242 and the earlier runs 2035) on the latent-space comparison's generators and seed derivations, under the planted scale, at 100 replicates × 199 permutations, rejection p < 0.05: - Designs: n200 and seaad (the SEA-AD table) at δ = 2.0; the band n200_delta1, n200_delta0.5, n200_delta0.25 and seaad_delta0.5; seaad_weak at the committed δ = 0.11. - Cells (11 per design): the anchor; translation e = 1.0; magnitude e ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.25}; orientation e ∈ {0.1, 0.25, 0.5} (in units of 90°, φ = 0); shape e ∈ {0.1, 0.25, 0.5}. - The surgery cell: the default feature-set orientation surgery at e = 1.0 on the SEA-AD table at δ = 2.0 (descriptive). - Units: 7,800. - weak_size profile. The comparison's seaad_weak anchor and translation at replicates 0–499 × 999 permutations (base seed 2035): the span-split check's own simulation units. 1,000 units. - plasmode profile. The SEA-AD astrocyte cohort_30 export (RNA and ATAC, 5,000 features each, 80 donors), read through the plasmode's contract, with sex labels permuted within stage by the plasmode's paper stream (base seed 2034). Every arm runs analyze_trajectories at the case-study configuration: six covariates, floor 2, net displacement, df, 999 permutations, rejection p ≤ 0.05. - Cells: the anchor at replicates 0–499, and the production selection's real-noise span plant at e ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0} at replicates 0–99. - The predictive arms run at forced_components = the unit's pls_cv rank. This is the amendment approved before any array unit: the same final fit, without repeating the CV. - Units: 800. - Code. Revision fea0874 on proposal/predictive-subspace-coordinates (MOTCO 0.24.0), run from a clean detached worktree on ing. Python 3.11.16, numpy 2.3.5, scipy 1.16.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0 and pandas 2.3.3, with BLAS pinned to one thread. - Cluster. Partition 512x1024, n4 and n11 excluded. Arrays 938116 (plasmode, 80 × 10 units), 938117 (simulation, 120 × 65) and 938118 (weak_size, 25 × 40). - Pre-flight. A workstation smoke of the three profiles (168 units, 0 failed, 0 inconsistent) projected about 178 core-hours as designed, or about 91 with the amendment. The user approved the amendment and a cap of 120 (openspec/changes/archive/2026-11-12-predictive-subspace-coordinates/notes.md).

Details are in PROVENANCE.txt.

docs.title: 2. Accounting and reproduction
docs.text:
• Units. 7,800 + 1,000 + 800 of 9,600: 0 failed units, 0 failed arms, 0 inconsistent units and 0 duplicates. All 225 array tasks ended COMPLETED (sacct.txt).
  • Consistency. On every unit:
  • the Y loadings had rank min(A, K − 1);
  • the fitted stage labels lay in every predictive arm's column space to 1e-8;
  • every predictive arm fitted production's model;
  • the three predictive arms reported equal span-capture shares;
  • at A ≤ K − 1, predictive reproduced pls_cv's p-values.
  • Cost. 46.3 + 6.1 + 27.4 = 79.8 recorded core-hours, against the projection of 91 and the cap of 120.
  • The simulation unit's median was 20.6 s, of which the production CV took 17.9 s and each arm 0.4 s.
  • The plasmode unit's median was 119.6 s: pls_cv 116.9 s, each other arm about 0.6 s.
  • Reproduction (the decision's gate): passed.
  • weak_size: pls_cv's count and rejections equal the span-split check's committed production_table.csv in all 6 rows.
  • plasmode anchor: pls_cv rejects delta, angle and shape in 21, 24 and 13 of 500 replicates, the plasmode's committed rates (0.042, 0.048, 0.026).
  • plasmode plant: all 9 rows equal the production selection's committed pls_cv rows.
  • Fidelity: all 500 anchor units selected rank 5 at held-out AUROC 0.635556.
  • So every production rate on the real-noise cells is a committed rate, and every candidate rate pairs with it on the same data and draws.

docs.title: 3. The decision
docs.text:
predictive_subspace_decision.json (rule version 1) returns keep_production: no arm qualifies.

criterion rule predictive predictive_orthonormal predictive_fitted gate reproductions, fidelity, no inconsistent unit passed S1 size, simulation anchor and translation, seven designs, m = 42: at most 3 above the bound 0.0936, none above the ceiling 0.13 holds: 2 above holds: 1 above holds: 3 above S1 size, weak_size m = 6 at R = 500: at most 1 above 0.0695 holds: 0.030–0.052 holds: 0.032–0.042 holds: 0.034–0.056 S1 size, plasmode the anchor's three statistics at R = 500, m = 3: at most 1 above 0.0695, none above the ceiling 0.072 fails: delta 0.136, shape 0.076 fails: delta 0.134, shape 0.076 fails: delta 0.130, shape 0.078 S2 protected power 57 target cells (six designs at δ ≥ 0.25, the plasmode plant), one-sided exact paired loss: at most 4 below 0.025, none below 0.05/57 holds: 0 losses holds: 0 losses holds: 0 losses S3 specificity, δ = 2.0 off-target rates, m = 36, the S1 rule (bound 0.0936, ceiling 0.13) holds: 2 above the bound holds: 0 above fails: 4 above the ceiling (0.15–0.24) S3 specificity, band off-target excess over pls_cv, m = 72: at most 4 one-sided exact paired p below 0.025, none below 0.05/72 fails: 9 below 0.025, 2 below the ceiling holds: 0 holds: 0 G gain 18 target cells at δ = 2.0, one exact paired gain p ≤ 0.05/18 holds: 10 cells holds: 10 cells holds: 10 cells arm verdict size_excess → power_loss → specificity_excess → no_gain → qualifies size_excess size_excess size_excess

Consequence (the decision's text): "Production keeps measuring in the fitted span's scores; the three predictive coordinate systems stay opt-in diagnostics, and the measurement-visibility page records what the measured dimension costs and why it was kept."

predictive_orthonormal fails only S1, and only on the plasmode.

docs.title: 4. Size on real noise: the plasmode anchor
docs.text:
Rejections over the 500 anchor replicates (plasmode/rate_table.csv), and the discordant counts against pls_cv (b only pls_cv rejects, c only the arm; plasmode/paired_table.csv):

arm delta angle shape delta b/c shape b/c pls_cv 21 (0.042) 24 (0.048) 13 (0.026) — — predictive 68 (0.136) 11 (0.022) 38 (0.076) 6 / 53 5 / 30 predictive_orthonormal 67 (0.134) 9 (0.018) 38 (0.076) 6 / 52 4 / 29 predictive_fitted 65 (0.130) 10 (0.020) 39 (0.078) 5 / 49 4 / 30 forced_k_minus_1 7 (0.014) 10 (0.020) 5 (0.010) 20 / 6 12 / 4
  • The excess is the subspace's, not a metric's. The three coordinate systems agree to within three rejections in every statistic, while production holds and the forced rank-2 fit is conservative. The two-sided paired p-values for delta are below 1e-9 in all three.
  • The fit is fixed across the anchor's replicates. The latent space is label-free and the anchor does not move the features, so every anchor unit fits the same rank-5 model (AUROC 0.635556, in-sample stage R² 0.840). The predictive arms measure one fixed two-dimensional subspace of it. The permutation null that holds size in five dimensions does not hold it in those two: the anchor's median angle null 95th percentile narrows from 40.2° to 11.0–12.1°, and the observed angle from 20.7° to 3.2–3.5° (plasmode/cell_table.csv).
  • Simulation does not reproduce it. The same arms hold size at every simulated design, including seaad_weak at R = 500 (0.030–0.056). The probe's shape reading there (0.077 over 300 units) did not recur: predictive reads 0.052 at the anchor, against production's 0.050. What the plasmode has and the generator lacks is not identified by this run. Candidates include real noise structure aligned with the stage directions, and the six-covariate design with its df correction. A diagnosis would be its own change.
  • angle moves the other way. On the plasmode every predictive arm rejects angle less often than production (b/c 24/11 for predictive).

docs.title: 5. Power: no loss, gains where the span sees the plant
docs.text:
S2 holds with no loss in any arm or cell. Target rates at δ = 2.0, pls_cv → predictive (b/c against pls_cv; the other two candidates agree within 0.04):

design magnitude e = 0.05 orientation e = 0.1 orientation e = 0.25 shape e = 0.1 shape e = 0.25 n = 200 0.56 → 0.72 (0/16) 0.76 → 0.99 (0/23) 0.90 → 1.00 (0/10) 0.71 → 0.83 (0/12) 0.97 → 1.00 (0/3) SEA-AD table 0.22 → 0.54 (0/32) 0.40 → 0.90 (0/50) 0.41 → 1.00 (0/59) 0.13 → 0.56 (0/43) 0.63 → 0.90 (0/27)

Each candidate passes G in the same 10 cells, with gain p from 1.7e-18 (the SEA-AD table's 22.5° rotation) to 9.8e-4. Magnitude e = 0.1 on the SEA-AD table also gains (0.57 → 0.86).

The band is where the payoff is largest. It is recorded, and did not decide G. Production's CV selects ranks 4 (n200_delta0.5), 11 (n200_delta0.25, q10–q90 8–16) and 5 (seaad_delta0.5) at a held-out AUROC of 0.998–1.000. The predictive arms measure in two of those dimensions.

design cell pls_cv predictive forced_k_minus_1 n = 200, δ = 1.0 orientation e = 0.1 0.10 1.00 0.60 n = 200, δ = 0.5 orientation e = 0.1 0.06 0.94 0.11 n = 200, δ = 0.5 shape e = 0.25 0.22 0.92 0.09 n = 200, δ = 0.25 magnitude e = 0.25 0.35 1.00 0.20 n = 200, δ = 0.25 orientation e = 0.25 0.12 1.00 0.11 SEA-AD table, δ = 0.5 orientation e = 0.25 0.13 0.98 0.15 SEA-AD table, δ = 0.5 shape e = 0.5 0.16 0.82 0.08

Each candidate gains at the Bonferroni threshold 0.05/36 in 29–30 of the 36 band target cells. Pooled over them the paired difference is +0.44 to +0.45, from b/c of about 50 against 1,618–1,660.

Real-noise plant (delta, pls_cv → candidates): e = 0.25, 0.24 → 0.40–0.42; e = 0.5, 0.51 → 0.79–0.82; e = 1.0, 1.00 in every arm. Two of the three cells gain at 0.05/3.

The weak design does not move. Production reads 0.01–0.05 at its nine target cells, and the candidates 0.01–0.07; no gain p is below 0.015. There the fitted span keeps 0.107 of the pooled stage program, and the predictive subspace the same 0.107.

docs.title: 6. Specificity: the metric decides the leak
docs.text:
Production's own off-target rates in the band are high under the planted scale, and the three coordinate systems move them in opposite directions:

design cell off-target pls_cv predictive predictive_orthonormal predictive_fitted n = 200, δ = 1.0 orientation e = 0.5 shape 0.56 0.37 0.03 0.00 n = 200, δ = 0.5 orientation e = 0.25 shape 0.57 0.81 0.04 0.03 n = 200, δ = 0.5 orientation e = 0.5 shape 0.80 0.85 0.41 0.01 n = 200, δ = 0.25 orientation e = 0.5 shape 0.55 0.71 0.16 0.00 SEA-AD table, δ = 0.5 orientation e = 0.5 shape 0.46 0.59 0.24 0.07 n = 200, δ = 0.5 shape e = 0.5 delta 0.06 0.19 0.04 0.06

(descriptive.band_off_target_rates.)

  • predictive keeps the score metric's shear and adds to production's leak: 9 of the 72 band readings have an excess p below 0.025, and the two shape readings of the n = 200 rotations at δ = 0.5 (e = 0.1 and 0.25) fall below the ceiling 0.05/72.
  • predictive_orthonormal and predictive_fitted remove most of production's leak. Neither has a band excess.
  • predictive_fitted leaks at δ = 2.0. In the response metric, rotations at n = 200 read shape 0.19 (e = 0.1) and 0.16 (e = 0.25), and bends read delta 0.15 (e = 0.25) and 0.24 (e = 0.5). All four are above the ceiling 0.13.
  • predictive_orthonormal has 4 off-target readings above the bound over both families (the fewest), and would have been named had it held size.

docs.title: 7. The control arm: lowering the fit rank
docs.text:
forced_k_minus_1 truncates the fit at two components instead of measuring two dimensions of the CV fit (descriptive.control_arm).

  • It keeps less of the stage program in the band. Its pooled-stage capture is 0.48 (n200_delta0.5), 0.34 (n200_delta0.25) and 0.39 (seaad_delta0.5). Production's is 0.88, 0.74 and 0.73, and the predictive subspace's 0.87, 0.67 and 0.73.
  • Its power follows. In the band it rejects at or below production in most target cells, for example 0.11 against production's 0.06 and predictive's 0.94 at the n = 200, δ = 0.5 rotation e = 0.1.
  • At δ = 2.0 it recovers part of the gain. On the SEA-AD table's 22.5° rotation it reads 0.92, against production's 0.41 and predictive's 1.00, where the CV rank is 2–3 and two components hold the program.
  • On the plasmode it is conservative: 0.014 / 0.020 / 0.010.
  • So the later components aim the K − 1 directions, as the probe found. A lower fit rank is the wrong lever, and the predictive subspace keeps what they contribute.

docs.title: 8. Rank plus one: the CV rank sits next to the leak
docs.text:
One more fit component under the predictive coordinates (descriptive.rank_sensitivity):

  • At δ = 2.0 the rotation leaks into shape. At e = 0.5 the off-target shape rate goes from 0.03 to 0.92 at n = 200 and from 0.04 to 0.99 on the SEA-AD table; at e = 0.25, from 0.04 to 0.22 and from 0.05 to 0.56. The two-sided paired p-values are 1e-27 to 8e-6.
  • Target power stays high (0.84–1.00 at δ = 2.0).
  • At n = 200 and δ = 1.0, where the CV rank is 3, the e = 0.5 rotation's leak still grows, from 0.37 to 0.77.
  • Where the CV rank is already 4–11 (δ = 0.5 and 0.25) one more component changes little. The paired p-values there run from 0.14 to 1.0, except 0.019 for the n = 200, δ = 0.5 rotation at e = 0.1.

The CV's rank at δ = 2.0 is one component from a large specificity loss in the predictive coordinates. Any adoption would need a rank rule for a fixed measured dimension.

docs.title: 9. Estimation: observed against population through the same map
docs.text:
Median observed angle beside the population's through each arm's map, in degrees (descriptive.orientation_estimation):

design rotation pls_cv predictive predictive_orthonormal n = 200, δ = 2.0 45° 44.6 / 45.3 43.8 / 45.2 43.4 / 45.0 SEA-AD table, δ = 2.0 45° 42.9 / 43.1 39.7 / 43.4 41.3 / 45.2 n = 200, δ = 0.5 45° 39.2 / 42.3 30.9 / 44.8 32.4 / 44.8 n = 200, δ = 0.25 45° 31.3 / 41.6 17.8 / 43.4 19.5 / 44.8 SEA-AD table, δ = 0.5 45° 38.1 / 39.1 18.6 / 40.8 21.3 / 44.8
  • At δ = 2.0 the predictive arms estimate the angle within about 4°.
  • In the band they detect the rotation but report about half of it. At n = 200 and δ = 0.25 they read 18–20° where the population reads 43–45° through the same map. Production reads 31°, but in more noise dimensions.
  • So a predictive arm is a detector first. Measuring the difference stays with roadmap open item 3.

docs.title: 10. The surgery cell: what the lower dimension gives up
docs.text:
The Phase 6 feature-set orientation surgery at e = 1.0 on the SEA-AD table is largely outside the stage span (descriptive.surgery_cell):

arm delta angle shape group_difference capture pls_cv 0.26 0.66 0.48 0.203 predictive 0.49 0.48 0.61 0.002 predictive_orthonormal 0.52 0.49 0.63 0.002 predictive_fitted 0.51 0.48 0.59 0.002 forced_k_minus_1 0.46 0.49 0.57 0.014 predictive_rank_plus_one 0.32 0.22 0.30 0.001
  • Production reads the surgery's angle through its extra components: a median rank of 4 keeps 0.20 of the group difference, against 0.002 in the predictive subspace.
  • The predictive arms read it at 0.48–0.49 instead of 0.66. Their delta and shape rise instead, which suggests the plant reaches them indirectly through the stage directions.
  • So a difference seen only through the dropped components is no longer read as it was.

docs.title: 11. Rank and AUROC per design
docs.text:
From simulation/cell_table.csv, the anchor's pls_cv row:

design median rank (q10–q90) held-out AUROC in-sample stage R² pooled_stage capture n = 200, δ = 2.0 2 (2–3) 1.000 0.983 0.970 SEA-AD table, δ = 2.0 3 (2–3) 1.000 0.991 0.933 n = 200, δ = 1.0 3 (3–3) 1.000 0.981 0.951 n = 200, δ = 0.5 4 (3–4) 1.000 0.943 0.876 n = 200, δ = 0.25 11 (8–16.1) 0.998 0.970 0.737 SEA-AD table, δ = 0.5 5 (4–6) 1.000 0.964 0.734 SEA-AD table, δ = 0.11 2 (2–5) 0.593 0.444 0.107

The band is where the held-out AUROC is at its ceiling while the rank grows. There the predictive subspace measures two of 4–11 dimensions and gains most.

docs.title: 12. What follows
docs.text:
• Production and motco analyze keep measuring in the fitted span's scores. The paper grade, the default flip and the CLI flag were owed only to propose_paper_grade. None is opened.
  • The three values stay opt-in diagnostics in the harness and motco.analysis, now measured:
  • They hold size in simulation, lose no protected power, and gain large power wherever the span sees the plant.
  • They do not hold size on the SEA-AD plasmode's real noise: delta reads 0.13 and shape 0.08, where production reads 0.042 and 0.026.
  • A case study should not report them as tests.
  • predictive_orthonormal is the coordinate system to keep in view. It fails only the real-noise size, and it removes most of production's own off-target leak in the band. If the plasmode excess is understood and fixed, it is the arm to re-read, with a rank rule for a fixed measured dimension (§8).
  • The real-noise excess is now the open question. The simulation does not reproduce it, so the generator lacks whatever drives it. Roadmap open item 2, the latent plasmode, measures what the span holds on real noise and is the natural place to read it.

docs.title: 13. Limitations
docs.text:
• R = 100 in simulation. Every rate there has an SE of about 0.02 at α; the bound is 0.0936. The real-noise and weak-design size readings are at R = 500.
  • One real data set. The size excess was read on one export, at one configuration (six covariates, df), with a fit that is the same in every anchor unit.
  • The planted scale. The band's off-target rates, production's included, are read under the planted scale. The probe ran the null scale, so its band rates are not comparable.
  • Three stages only. At four stages the CV rank and K − 1 differ differently; the design left them to a paper grade.
  • The band's gains did not decide G. They are recorded with the same test, at Bonferroni over 36 cells.

docs.title: Procrustes Shape Invariance Audit
docs.text:
Date: 2026-08-04

Superseded on the reflection policy (2026-09-03). The reflection rows below record the contract as it stood on this date. unify-shape-reflection-policy (resolving audit finding F3) replaced it: the Procrustes alignment now optimizes over the full orthogonal group, so reflections are aligned away at every ambient dimension and a mirror pair scores zero, not positive. Everything else in this audit — the translation, scale, proper-rotation, and interior-bend cases, and the legacy-GPA comparator — still holds.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: MOTCO now defines trajectory shape as direct pairwise Procrustes residual configuration after removing translation, proper rigid rotation, and positive uniform scale. Reflections are preserved as distinct shapes by default.

docs.title: Deterministic Cases
docs.text:
The audit uses a four-stage, non-collinear two-dimensional trajectory and deterministic transforms:

Case Strict pairwise behavior Legacy leave-one-out GPA diagnostic Translation Zero within tolerance Matches strict reference Uniform scale Zero within tolerance Matches strict reference Proper rotation Zero within tolerance Diverges with a positive residual Reflection Positive by default Recorded as legacy comparator Interior bend Positive Recorded as legacy comparator

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
The production estimator is now the strict pairwise Procrustes calculation. The previous leave-one-out GPA procedure remains represented in tests only as a legacy comparator so the rotation-invariance divergence is visible. R pgpa/pPsup comparison is optional in the test suite and skips when the R environment or package functions are unavailable.

Older operating-characteristic results that depended on the legacy shape implementation should be treated as superseded for shape-specific claims.

docs.title: Production latent-space selection — findings report (2026-11-10)
docs.text:
Change: production-latent-space-selection (run on MOTCO 0.22.0; no package code changed). Reads: results/production-latent-space-2026-11-10/ (production_latent_space_decision.json; simulation/ and plasmode/ rate, paired and cell tables, accounting.json, reproduction.json, settings.json; PROVENANCE.txt, sacct.txt). Concept page: measurement visibility.

Two opt-in settings change the production stage-PLS space without changing its objective:

  • block weighting (block_weighting: equal_variance, MOTCO 0.21.0) multiplies each standardized block by 1/√p_b, so a block's weight no longer grows with its feature count;
  • sparse stage-PLS (sparsity: {scope: block}, MOTCO 0.22.0) lets each component load on a budget of features per block, with the rank and the keep fraction chosen together by the held-out AUROC.

The latent-space comparison (report) kept the stage-PLS span as the production measurement, but it left open how much noise that span carries where real data sit: at SEA-AD's stage signal it keeps 0.10 of the pooled stage program. This check asked whether either setting, or both, holds size, loses no in-span power, and gains power where production has none. It compared four arms on matched units under a decision fixed in advance (design.md D4).

In one paragraph. The verdict is keep_production. No candidate gains power in the regime the decision reads (the weak design and real SEA-AD noise), so neither setting becomes a production candidate.

  • weighted reads no_gain. Size, protected power and specificity hold. Its best gain p-values are 0.105 (the plasmode plant at e = 0.25, delta 0.24 → 0.30) and 0.125 (the weak design's 45° rotation, angle 0.02 → 0.05), against the threshold 0.05/11 = 0.0045.
  • sparse_block and weighted_sparse_block read size_excess. On the plasmode anchor, delta reads 0.11, above the family's ceiling of 0.10 at R = 100. Production reads 0.11 there too: these 100 replicates hold 11 of the 21 delta rejections the 2026-11-02 plasmode found over 500. Both arms also fail the gain criterion. sparse_block's best gain is the plasmode plant at e = 0.5, delta 0.51 → 0.62, p = 0.0096.
  • Where the candidates do gain, the decision does not look. At the δ = 2.0 designs every candidate rejects more often than production where production is below saturation. The largest gain is the SEA-AD table's 22.5° rotation: angle 0.46 → 0.90 (weighted), 1.00 (sparse_block) and 0.99 (weighted_sparse_block). The candidates pick rank 2 where production's CV picks rank 3. These cells are protected-power readings (S2), so the gain counts only as "no loss".

docs.title: 1. Configuration and provenance
docs.text:
• The unit. Each unit builds one dataset and evaluates four arms on it, serially, at the unit's RRPP seed. Every arm is its own stage-PLS fit (double-CV rank, floor 2, net displacement, span capture):
  • pls_cv: production;
  • weighted: block_weighting: equal_variance (every PLS fit with scale=False, so delta is in the weighted metric);
  • sparse_block: sparsity: {scope: block} with the default ladder 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.2 / 0.1 / 0.05;
  • weighted_sparse_block: both.

The arms share the data and the permutation indices, so the decision compares them by exact paired tests on the discordant units. - simulation profile. The latent-space comparison's three designs, seed functions and committed weak δ (base seed 2035), at 100 replicates × 199 permutations, rejection p < 0.05: - Designs: n200 (n = 200, δ = 2.0), seaad (the SEA-AD table, δ = 2.0) and seaad_weak (the SEA-AD table at δ = 0.11, held-out AUROC about 0.6). - Cells (10): the comparison's seven in-span cells by name (anchor; translation; magnitude e = 0.05; orientation e = 0.25 and 0.5 at φ = 0; shape e = 0.25 and 0.5), whose datasets and draws are the comparison's, plus magnitude_e0.25, orient_e1.0_phi0 and shape_e1.0 for a power gradient. Orientation e is in units of 90°, so e = 0.25 is a 22.5° rotation. - Units: 3,000. - plasmode profile. The SEA-AD astrocyte cohort_30 export (RNA and ATAC, 5,000 features each, 80 donors), read through the plasmode's contract with its file hashes checked. Each replicate permutes the sex labels within stage as the plasmode's paper stream does (base seed 2034, replicates 0–99). Each arm runs analyze_trajectories at the case-study configuration: six covariates, floor 2, net displacement, df, attribution off, 999 permutations, rejection p ≤ 0.05. - Cells (4): the anchor and a real-noise span plant at e = 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0: the donors labelled Male at stage s gain e · (x̄_s − x̄), the pooled stage-s mean minus the mean of the stage means. B's centred stage configuration thus gains e times the pooled one, a stage-span magnitude edit on real noise. - Units: 400. - Code. Revision d0a5ddb on proposal/production-latent-space (MOTCO 0.22.0), run from a clean detached worktree on ing. Python 3.11.16, numpy 2.3.5, scipy 1.16.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0 and pandas 2.3.3, with BLAS pinned to one thread. - Cluster. Partition 512x1024, n11 excluded: array 937293 (simulation, 300 shards of 10 units, at most 96 at once) and array 937294 (plasmode, 100 shards of 4 units, at most 64 at once). - Pre-flight. A workstation smoke of both profiles (68 units, 0 failed records) projected about 490 core-hours. The user approved the full ladder at 100 replicates with a cap of 650 core-hours (openspec/changes/archive/2026-11-11-production-latent-space-selection/notes.md). - Amendments before any unit (2026-11-10, notes.md): S3 reads the e ≤ 0.5 cells only, and S1 and S3 use the stage-span paper grade's count-plus-ceiling rule.

Details are in PROVENANCE.txt.

docs.title: 2. Accounting and reproduction
docs.text:
• Units. simulation: 3,000 of 3,000 units, 12,000 records. plasmode: 400 of 400, 1,600 records. Both: 0 failed records, 0 duplicates, 0 fidelity failures. All 400 array tasks ended COMPLETED 0:0 (sacct.txt).
  • Cost. 184.0 + 325.0 = 509.0 recorded core-hours, against the projection of 490 and the cap of 650.
  • simulation: median unit 208.5 s; per arm, pls_cv 13.2 s, weighted 13.2 s, sparse_block 91.5 s, weighted_sparse_block 90.7 s.
  • plasmode: median unit 2,852 s; per arm, 133.8 s, 133.7 s, 1,261 s and 1,268 s.

The sparse arms are 87 % (simulation) and 91 % (plasmode) of the cost: every (rank, fraction) candidate is refitted in every fold. - Reproduction (the decision's gate): both passed. - simulation: the pls_cv arm's count, rejections and failures equal the comparison's committed rate_table.csv in all 63 rows (3 designs × 7 shared cells × 3 statistics). - plasmode: every one of the 100 anchor units' pls_cv arm selected rank 5 at held-out AUROC 0.635556, the plasmode's fidelity values. - So every pls_cv rate on the shared cells is the comparison's rate, and every candidate rate pairs with it on the same datasets and draws.

docs.title: 3. The decision
docs.text:
production_latent_space_decision.json (rule version 1) returns keep_production: no arm qualifies.

criterion rule weighted sparse_block weighted_sparse_block gate both reproductions pass passed S1 size, simulation anchor and translation delta/angle/shape at three designs, m = 18: at most 2 above the bound 0.0936, none above the ceiling 0.12 holds: 0 above (0.00–0.05) holds: 0 above (0.01–0.06) holds: 0 above (0.01–0.06) S1 size, plasmode the anchor's three statistics, m = 3: at most 1 above 0.0936, none above the ceiling 0.10 holds: 0.05 / 0.05 / 0.04 fails: delta 0.11 above the ceiling fails: delta 0.11 above the ceiling S2 protected power 16 target cells at δ = 2.0, one-sided exact paired loss p: at most 2 below 0.025, none below 0.05/16 holds: 0 losses holds: 0 losses holds: 0 losses S3 specificity off-target rates of the δ = 2.0 target cells at e ≤ 0.5, m = 24, under the S1 rule holds: 0 above (0.00–0.08) holds: 0 above (0.00–0.07) holds: 0 above (0.00–0.07) G gain 11 cells (the weak design's 8 targets, the plasmode's 3 plant delta cells), one exact paired gain p ≤ 0.05/11 = 0.0045 fails: best p 0.105 fails: best p 0.0096 fails: best p 0.125 arm verdict size_excess → power_loss → specificity_excess → no_gain → qualifies no_gain size_excess size_excess

Consequence (the decision's text): "Production keeps the stage-PLS space unchanged; block weighting and sparse stage-PLS stay opt-in and are documented as measured."

The pls_cv arm's own controls read 0.00–0.06 at the 18 simulation readings and 0.11 / 0.06 / 0.04 (delta / angle / shape) at the plasmode anchor. Its delta there is above the family's ceiling too (§4).

docs.title: 4. Size, and the plasmode anchor's 0.11
docs.text:
Every arm holds size in simulation: the 72 control readings (18 per arm) run from 0.00 to 0.06, and none is above the bound.

On the plasmode anchor, delta reads:

arm rate b / c against pls_cv pls_cv 0.11 — weighted 0.05 6 / 0 sparse_block 0.11 6 / 6 weighted_sparse_block 0.11 6 / 6

(b counts units only pls_cv rejects, c units only the candidate rejects; plasmode/paired_table.csv.)

  • Production reads 0.11 on these replicates. The pls_cv arm's anchor p-values equal the 2026-11-02 plasmode's per-replicate records at all 100 replicates, with equal seeds (checked after the decision; PROVENANCE.txt). That run's replicates 0–99 hold 11 of its 21 delta rejections over 500 (0.042 over 500, plasmode report). The 0.11 is the replicate subset, not an excess the sparse fit adds.
  • The sparse arms share 5 of their 11 rejections with production. Their anchor space is one label-free fit, the same in every unit (rank 4 at keep fraction 0.05, 250 features per block; plasmode/cell_table.csv), so they reject on different replicates than production at the same rate.
  • The verdict does not depend on it. Without S1 the sparse arms would read no_gain, since every arm fails G. The S1 failure ties production on these permutations; it does not measure an excess of the sparse fit. At R = 100 a rate of 0.11 is about 2.8 SE above α, and the paper grade the decision would have opened is where size is resolved.
  • weighted reads 0.05. Its rejections are a subset of production's (b = 6, c = 0). On the plasmode the weighting is not a rebalancing (§7), so this is the effect of fitting without sklearn's per-fold re-standardization, which also moves the anchor's CV rank from 5 to 7.

docs.title: 5. Gain: the regime the decision reads
docs.text:
G reads the cells where production rejects at or near the null rate (the weak design) and the plasmode plant. Each entry is pls_cv → candidate over 100 paired units, with b/c in brackets and the one-sided gain p after it.

Weak design (SEA-AD table, δ = 0.11):

cell statistic weighted sparse_block weighted_sparse_block magnitude e = 0.05 delta 0.05 → 0.04 (2/1) 0.875 0.05 → 0.05 (0/0) 1 0.05 → 0.07 (2/4) 0.344 magnitude e = 0.25 delta 0.06 → 0.05 (4/3) 0.773 0.06 → 0.07 (1/2) 0.5 0.06 → 0.06 (4/4) 0.637 orientation e = 0.25 angle 0.01 → 0.02 (0/1) 0.5 0.01 → 0.02 (0/1) 0.5 0.01 → 0.03 (0/2) 0.25 orientation e = 0.5 angle 0.02 → 0.05 (0/3) 0.125 0.02 → 0.02 (0/0) 1 0.02 → 0.05 (0/3) 0.125 orientation e = 1.0 angle 0.03 → 0.02 (2/1) 0.875 0.03 → 0.04 (0/1) 0.5 0.03 → 0.04 (2/3) 0.5 shape e = 0.25 shape 0.05 → 0.04 (3/2) 0.813 0.05 → 0.05 (1/1) 0.75 0.05 → 0.01 (4/0) 1 shape e = 0.5 shape 0.03 → 0.06 (1/4) 0.188 0.03 → 0.05 (1/3) 0.313 0.03 → 0.06 (1/4) 0.188 shape e = 1.0 shape 0.02 → 0.04 (1/3) 0.313 0.02 → 0.04 (0/2) 0.25 0.02 → 0.05 (1/4) 0.188

Plasmode span plant (delta):

e weighted sparse_block weighted_sparse_block 0.25 0.24 → 0.30 (5/11) 0.105 0.24 → 0.28 (4/8) 0.194 0.24 → 0.21 (11/8) 0.820 0.5 0.51 → 0.52 (5/6) 0.5 0.51 → 0.62 (4/15) 0.0096 0.51 → 0.49 (11/9) 0.748 1.0 1.00 → 1.00 (0/0) 1 1.00 → 0.99 (1/0) 1 1.00 → 0.99 (1/0) 1
  • The weak design stays at the null rate in every arm. Production reads 0.01–0.06 at its eight target cells, and no candidate moves a cell by more than 0.03. Pooled over the 11 cells the candidates gain 0.019 (sparse_block, b/c 12/33), 0.011 (weighted, 23/35) and 0.004 (weighted_sparse_block, 37/41).
  • The one sizeable gain is sparse_block on the plasmode plant at e = 0.5 (0.51 → 0.62, p = 0.0096). It misses the Bonferroni threshold by a factor of two, and the arm fails S1 regardless.
  • The capture does not rise. At the weak design's anchor the fitted span keeps a median 0.100 of the pooled stage program under pls_cv, 0.098 under weighted, 0.085 under sparse_block and 0.082 under weighted_sparse_block (pooled_stage, simulation/cell_table.csv). Over the design's ten cells the medians run 0.054–0.123 for production and 0.043–0.128 for the candidates, and the held-out stage AUROC 0.548–0.630 and 0.538–0.631. Neither setting finds more of the stage program in the weak regime, which is the mechanism G was meant to reward.

docs.title: 6. Protected power, and where the candidates gain
docs.text:
S2 reads the 16 target cells at the δ = 2.0 designs for losses. There are none: in every candidate and cell c ≥ b. Where production is below saturation the candidates gain:

design cell statistic pls_cv weighted (b/c) sparse_block (b/c) weighted_sparse_block (b/c) n = 200 magnitude e = 0.05 delta 0.74 0.93 (3/22) 0.81 (0/7) 0.93 (3/22) n = 200 orientation e = 0.25 angle 0.84 1.00 (0/16) 1.00 (0/16) 1.00 (0/16) SEA-AD table magnitude e = 0.05 delta 0.23 0.31 (7/15) 0.39 (4/20) 0.31 (7/15) SEA-AD table orientation e = 0.25 angle 0.46 0.90 (1/45) 1.00 (0/54) 0.99 (1/54) SEA-AD table orientation e = 0.5 angle 0.96 1.00 (0/4) 1.00 (0/4) 1.00 (0/4) SEA-AD table shape e = 0.25 shape 0.70 0.87 (10/27) 0.92 (1/23) 0.88 (10/28) SEA-AD table shape e = 0.5 shape 0.95 0.98 (2/5) 0.99 (0/4) 0.99 (1/5) SEA-AD table magnitude e = 0.25 delta 0.95 0.99 (1/5) 0.97 (0/2) 0.99 (1/5)

The other eight cells are at 1.00 in every arm. The two-sided paired p-value is below 0.05 for 13 of these 24 comparisons, and down to 1e-16 for the SEA-AD rotation (descriptive.paired_differences).

  • The gains follow the selected rank. At these cells production's CV picks rank 3 in a large share of units (median 3 on the SEA-AD rotation and bend, q90 3 at n = 200), and every candidate picks rank 2 (median 2, q90 2–2.1 for weighted, 2 for the sparse arms; simulation/cell_table.csv). The capture of the pooled stage program is 0.92–0.98 in every arm there, so the candidates do not see more of the program; they measure it in fewer dimensions. The design-guidance slice found the same association between angle and the CV rank (report §8).
  • weighted and weighted_sparse_block often coincide in simulation. Under weighting the sparse CV keeps the full budget in most units (median keep fraction 1.0 at every δ = 2.0 target cell except the 90° rotation at n = 200 and the SEA-AD 45° rotation), so the two weighted arms often fit the same space and read the same b/c at five of the eight cells above.
  • None of this enters the verdict. The decision protects these cells against loss and looks for gains only where production has none. A gain at a stronger stage signal was not a predeclared reason to change production, and at R = 100 the paired gains are not size-checked at a matched paper grade.

docs.title: 7. Specificity, and what the plasmode's weighted arm measures
docs.text:
S3 (off-target rates of the δ = 2.0 target cells at e ≤ 0.5) holds for every arm with no reading above the bound 0.0936. pls_cv's own off-target rates there read 0.00–0.07. One off-target reading falls in all three candidates: the n = 200 rotation at e = 0.5 leaks into shape in 0.06 of production's units and in none of the candidates' (6/0, two-sided p 0.031).

The e = 1.0 cells' off-target rates are descriptive (descriptive.large_plant_off_target). Production's construction leak there is the stage-span pilot's: the n = 200 full bend's delta reads 0.17 (pls_cv), 0.11 (weighted), 0.15 (sparse_block) and 0.09 (weighted_sparse_block), and the SEA-AD bend's angle 0.12, 0.10, 0.08 and 0.10. No candidate adds a leak there.

At the weak design no off-target rate is read by a criterion. The largest is weighted's shape under the 90° rotation, 0.10 against production's 0.03 (1/8, two-sided p 0.039); weighted_sparse_block reads 0.08 there.

On the plasmode the weighting is not a rebalancing. The export's blocks have 5,000 features each, so equal_variance gives them equal weights. The weighted arm is therefore production fitted with scale=False, without sklearn's per-fold re-standardization. That alone changes the label-free anchor space (rank 5 → 7, held-out AUROC 0.635556 → 0.638444). The plasmode's weighted readings measure that change, not block weighting; the simulation's blocks (367 and 131 features) carry the weighting question.

docs.title: 8. Rank, keep fraction and support
docs.text:
From simulation/cell_table.csv and plasmode/cell_table.csv (medians, q10–q90 in brackets):

  • δ = 2.0 designs. Production's median rank is 2–3, the candidates' 2. sparse_block keeps half the features (median 0.5) at the SEA-AD table's rotations and bends, at both translations, and at n = 200's 45° rotation and full bend; elsewhere it keeps the full budget (median 1.0, q10 0.5 at most cells). AUROC is 1.000 in every arm.
  • Weak design. Production's median rank is 2–3 (q90 5–6); sparse_block's 2–3 (q90 4–5) and weighted_sparse_block's 2. Both sparse arms keep a median 1.0 of the features with q10 0.05–0.1, so a tenth of the units drop to the smallest budgets.
  • Plasmode anchor. The label-free space is identical in every unit: production rank 5, weighted 7, both sparse arms rank 4 at keep fraction 0.05 (250 features per block).
  • Plasmode plant. Production's rank rises to a median 7 at e = 0.25 and 0.5 (q90 10.1 and 9) and falls back to 5 at e = 1.0. sparse_block keeps 0.2 of the features at e = 0.25 (1,000 per block) and 0.5 at e = 0.5 and 1.0 (2,500 per block); weighted_sparse_block keeps 0.5 at every effect.

docs.title: 9. What follows
docs.text:
• Production and motco analyze keep the stage-PLS space unchanged. The paper grade and the default flip were owed only to propose_paper_grade. Neither is opened.
  • Both settings stay opt-in and are now measured.
  • block_weighting: equal_variance holds size, loses no protected power and adds no specificity excess on these designs. It gains no power at a weak stage signal or on the plasmode plant. A case study may declare it as a sensitivity analysis with this reading. Under it delta is in the weighted metric.
  • sparsity: {scope: block} holds size in simulation and reads the plasmode anchor's delta at production's rate on the same replicates; it loses no protected power. It gains no Bonferroni-protected power where the decision looks, and it costs about seven to nine production fits. The plasmode anchor's size is unresolved at R = 100 for every arm, production included.
  • The gain at δ = 2.0 is an open thread, not a finding for production. Every candidate gains up to 0.54 in angle where production's CV selects rank 3 and the candidates select rank 2. That points at the rank rule, not at weighting or sparsity. The latent-rank ladder (2026-09-08) kept the CV rank at the Phase 5 design; whether a stricter rank rule recovers these gains at held size, and what it costs at the weak design, is a question for its own change.
  • Thread 2 of roadmap item 16 (the group-stratified stage space) was sequenced after this selection because it is paired against production. Production is unchanged, so it pairs against pls_cv.

docs.title: 10. Limitations
docs.text:
• R = 100. Every rate has an SE of about 0.02 at α, and the bound is 0.0936. The check decides whether a paper grade is worth its cost; it does not resolve rates near the bound.
  • One kind of each setting. mfa weighting and joint-scope sparsity were not run (proposal, non-goals).
  • The plasmode's weighted arms do not weight. With equal block sizes equal_variance is uniform (§7).
  • Weighted delta is in another metric. Only p-values and rejections are compared across arms (descriptive.delta_metric_note).
  • Convergence. The smoke traced rare ConvergenceWarnings in the weighted sparse arm at the smallest budget (17 of 45,360 power-method calls in one unit; notes.md). They were not counted in the run and do not change a selection measurably in the smoke.
  • The δ = 2.0 gains are paired at 199 permutations on the comparison's datasets. They were not part of a predeclared criterion and are reported as read.

docs.title: Rank-floor check — 2026-10-23
docs.text:
Paper-grade size and power check of the PLS latent-space rank floor (min_components=2, MOTCO 0.10.0) against the unfloored 0.9.0 rule at the Phase 6 SEA-AD design (openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-23-minimum-latent-rank/, design D7, spec rank-floor-validation). It is the gate behind the default flip: motco analyze and the simulation harness select the PLS rank from candidates at or above 2 only once this check names the floor-2 arm admissible. Every number below is read from results/rank-floor-2026-10-23/ (delta0.05/ and delta0.1/: rank_floor_decision.json, rank_floor_rates.csv, rank_floor_replicates.csv, rank_floor_pvalues.csv, merged.jsonl, the last three kept on ing as PROVENANCE.txt records; calibration/; smoke-delta0.05/, smoke-delta0.1/). Rates are rejection rates at p ≤ 0.05 over the available replicates of 500, at 999 permutations.

Run: two SLURM arrays of 100 shards on ing (partition 512x1024): job 925691 for δ = 0.05 and job 925791 for δ = 0.1, 7,000 units each, 100 / 100 tasks completed, 0 arm failures, 53.0 + 45.8 recorded core-hours (29 and 25 s per unit, two analyses at 999 permutations). The code is local main at 0a15d44 plus this change's working tree, rsynced over the cluster checkout and verified by tree hash; file hashes are in each PROVENANCE.txt.

Decision: adopt_floor at δ = 0.05 and adopt_floor at δ = 0.1, hence adopt_floor under the predeclared conjunction. The floor-2 arm holds the bound 0.0695 for every statistic at both controls in both runs.

In one paragraph. At the Phase 6 SEA-AD design with the stage signal weakened until the unfloored rank rule selects rank 1 in 58 % (δ = 0.05) and 42 % (δ = 0.1) of the null replicates (held-out CV AUROC 0.51 and 0.57), each of 7,000 units per strength was analysed twice on the same data and permutation draws, with the 0.9.0 rule and with the rank floor of 2. In the floored arm the zero-effect anchor rejects delta 0.042 / 0.044, angle 0.054 / 0.060 and shape 0.036 / 0.038 (δ = 0.05 / 0.1), and the translation control 0.036 / 0.036, 0.046 / 0.042 and 0.026 / 0.030, all at or below 0.0695 at R = 500. The floor lifted 4,257 and 3,228 rank-1 selections, mostly to rank 2; in the unfloored arm every rank-1 unit measured angle as exactly 0° or 180° with a two-point null that never rejected. Power is at the null in both arms at these strengths, so the check establishes size, not a gain: the floor defines angle and shape where the 0.9.0 rule left them degenerate, and the record's spectrum and null summary say how resolvable they are.

docs.title: 1. Construction and calibration
docs.text:
• Why a new construction. The 0.9.0 latent-adjustment power comparison recorded the CV-selected rank per unit at the Phase 6 construction: no unit in any arm selected rank 1 (roadmap, Next changes item 4), while both SEA-AD cohorts did (held-out AUROC 0.63 / 0.66). The floor changes the measurement only where the unfloored rule selects rank 1, so it is validated where that happens.
  • Data. generate_semisynthetic_trajectory at the Phase 6 small-n design: three stages, group_stage_sizes = [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]] (n = 80), methylation (M-values) and expression measured, 498 features, joint magnitude, p_dmp = 0.1, baseline_continuity = 0, with the stage signal weakened through the per-omic effect sizes delta_methyl = delta_expr = delta_protein = δ, at the Phase 6 value 2.0 for every committed study. Two strengths were run, δ = 0.05 and δ = 0.1 (below). p_dmp stays at 0.1 so every pool-limited surgery keeps its Phase 6 headroom (translation 98 sites available, orientation and shape 242; every cell fits).
  • Cells. The zero-effect anchor; the translation negative control at e = 1.0; magnitude at e = 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25 (the Phase 6 magnitude profile below its saturation); orientation and shape at e = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 (the Phase 6 study profile). 14 cells × 500 replicates = 7,000 units per strength. The generator and RRPP seeds depend on the replicate index only (base seed 2026), so every cell and both arms of replicate r share the baseline draw and the permutation draws.
  • Arms. Each unit is analysed with analyze_trajectories twice, with the harness CV defaults (cv2_splits = 4, cv1_splits = 3, n_repeats = 5, max_components = 20, random_state = 1203), 999 permutations, the same RRPP seed, no covariates and the net-displacement estimator:
  • floor_1: min_components = 1, the 0.9.0 rule (measured, not judged);
  • floor_2: min_components = 2, the candidate default.
  • Rule (predeclared in design D7, pure function rank_floor_decision). For the anchor and the translation control, the floor_2 arm's rate over its R available replicates must be at most α + k·√(α(1 − α)/R) with α = 0.05 and k = 2 (0.0695 at R = 500) for delta, angle and shape. Every statistic holding at both controls gives adopt_floor, otherwise diagnose_floor_excess. With two strengths, adopt_floor requires both runs to hold (settled with the user before submission). The floor_1 arm's rates are reported and never enter the decision; power rows are descriptive.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
The calibration criterion is that the unfloored rule selects rank 1 in at least half of the null (anchor) replicates on a recorded smoke run before any paper-grade run (scripts/rank_floor_check.py calibrate; every iteration is in results/rank-floor-2026-10-23/calibration/calibration.json). Weakening δ alone first raises the selected rank: at δ = 1.0 and 0.5 the held-out AUROC stays at 1.0 and the CV picks 3–6 components, at δ = 0.25 it is 0.92 with 4–11 components, because the stage signal thins across more directions before it fades. It reaches rank 1 only once the signal is near chance.

δ R rank-1 fraction rank distribution mean CV AUROC 2.0 (Phase 6) 20 0.00 2: 8, 3: 12 1.000 1.0 20 0.00 3: 20 1.000 0.5 20 0.00 3: 1, 4: 8, 5: 9, 6: 2 1.000 0.25 20 0.00 4–11 0.920 0.15 50 0.08 1: 4, 2: 12, 3: 8, 4–12: 26 0.702 0.1 20 / 50 0.55 / 0.44 1: 22, 2: 13, 3: 5, 4–10: 10 (R = 50) 0.579 / 0.583 0.05 50 0.58 1: 29, 2: 14, 3: 4, 4: 3 0.525

Both strengths meet the criterion on their smoke replicates (δ = 0.05: 0.70; δ = 0.1: 0.55), and they bracket the SEA-AD regime from the two sides: δ = 0.1 has the cohorts' held-out AUROC (0.58 against 0.63–0.66) with a rank-1 fraction near one half, δ = 0.05 is robustly in the rank-1 regime with almost no stage signal left (AUROC 0.52).

docs.title: Smoke profiles
docs.text: R = 20 at 99 permutations, 14 cells × 2 arms = 560 analyses per strength (smoke-delta0.05/, smoke-delta0.1/). No arm failed; the floor_2 arm selected rank ≥ 2 in every unit while floor_1 measured angle in one dimension in 183 / 280 (δ = 0.05) and 147 / 280 (δ = 0.1) units. Each smoke decision reads diagnose_floor_excess on one statistic at 3 of 20 rejections (0.150 against the R = 20 bound 0.147): anchor angle at δ = 0.05, translation delta at δ = 0.1. At R = 20 one rejection moves a rate by 0.05, so the smoke decisions are calibration and cost evidence, not verdicts. Cost: 26–53 s per unit at 99 permutations locally, 58 s at 999 permutations.

docs.title: 2. Rates against the bound
docs.text:
Rate (Monte Carlo SE) with the floor-2 verdict against α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/500) = 0.0695; the floor-1 arm is descriptive.

docs.title: 3. What the floor changes
docs.text:
• Calibration realized. The unfloored anchor arm selected rank 1 in 289 / 500 replicates at δ = 0.05 (0.578; criterion met) and 210 / 500 at δ = 0.1 (0.420; the smoke replicates' 0.55 was the high side of the R = 50 estimate 0.44, so the paper-grade fraction sits just under one half, as reported before submission). The anchor rank distributions are 1: 289, 2: 120, 3: 59, 4: 18, 5: 10, ≥6: 4 (floor 1) against 2: 346, 3: 91, 4: 27, 5: 23, 6: 7, ≥7: 6 (floor 2) at δ = 0.05, and 1: 210, 2: 131, 3: 66, 4: 27, 5: 25, ≥6: 41 against 2: 275, 3: 104, 4: 37, 5: 39, 6: 22, ≥7: 23 at δ = 0.1.
  • The lift. Over all 7,000 units the unfloored rule selected rank 1 in 4,257 (δ = 0.05) and 3,228 (δ = 0.1); the floor moved those to rank 2 in 3,289 / 2,187, rank 3 in 558 / 499, rank 4 in 184 / 180 and higher in the rest. The two arms select the same rank in 2,635 / 3,633 units; in 108 / 139 units the unfloored modal rank was already ≥ 2 but moved, because outer folds that had chosen rank 1 chose another candidate under the floor. The floor-2 arm selected rank 2 in 4,795 / 3,909 units and rank ≥ 3 in the remainder; it never fell back to a lower rank.
  • angle at rank 1. In every unfloored anchor unit that selected rank 1 the observed angle is exactly 0° (246 and 182 units) or 180° (43 and 28), its null's 95 % quantile is 180° (a two-point distribution) and its smallest p-value is 0.068 / 0.054: the rank-1 angle test never rejects. The unfloored arm's anchor angle rates (0.030 / 0.038) therefore come entirely from its rank ≥ 2 units, where they are 15 / 211 = 0.071 and 19 / 290 = 0.066. Under the 0.9.0 rule a real-data angle p-value of 1.0 at rank 1 says nothing about orientation; this is the degeneracy the floor removes.
  • Null width. The median over anchor replicates of the angle null's 95 % quantile is 84.0° / 61.2° in the unfloored arm (180° in its rank-1 units, 55.9° / 52.4° in its others) against 61.2° / 57.0° with the floor; the null's median SD is 34.0° / 21.0° against 17.8° / 16.3°. In a two-dimensional space with no stage signal the angle null is wide (two near-random directions), which is what a resolvable-orientation reader should see in null_summary.angle.
  • The signal. Mean held-out CV AUROC at the anchor is 0.513 / 0.571 (floor 1) and 0.516 / 0.580 (floor 2): the floor does not change what the CV can find, only the smallest rank it may report.

The angle differences of +0.016 to +0.036, several above two pooled SEs, are the unfloored arm's under-rejection at rank 1 (its angle rates of 0.010–0.042 are below α, as at the anchor), not detection; delta and shape differ by at most ±0.014 between the arms.

docs.title: 5. Decision, limitation and scope
docs.text:
Decision, read verbatim from results/rank-floor-2026-10-23/delta0.05/rank_floor_decision.json and delta0.1/rank_floor_decision.json: "decision": "adopt_floor" in both, with "exceeding": [] and every floor_2 verdict "holds" at the anchor and the translation control. Under the predeclared conjunction the check adopts the floor: MOTCO 0.10.0 keeps min_components=2 as the default of fit_pls_latent_space, SimulationEvaluationParams and TrajectoryAnalysisParams / motco analyze.

Limitation: the floor guarantees two dimensions, not a second axis with signal. When the stage signal supports one component, or none, the second component is the best of the remaining candidates and carries whatever the inner CV preferred among them; angle and shape are then defined but their nulls are wide, and at these strengths their power is at α. A rank-2 selection under the floor is a statement about the measurement space, not evidence of a second biological axis. Read the record's config_spectrum relative eigengap and null_summary.angle together: they say how resolvable orientation is in each analysis, and the selected rank stays the covariate reported beside any angle result. The 0.9.0 rule remains reachable as min_components=1 for comparison.

Scope.

  • The construction weakens the per-omic effect sizes uniformly; p_dmp, the cell sizes, the block set and the joint magnitude are the Phase 6 study's. It reproduces the SEA-AD cohorts' held-out AUROC regime, not their mechanism (a dominant technical axis aligned with stage), which the covariate-aware latent construction addresses.
  • Both arms used the harness CV defaults and no covariates; the floor applies inside the same cross-validation with covariates and latent adjustment, but their interaction was not measured here.
  • Every committed study config, fixture and dated report pins min_components: 1 and is unchanged by the default (tests/test_rank_floor_default_pins.py); the sead_sexdiff cohorts are to be rerun at the floor in their own proposal, pinning MOTCO 0.10.0.
  • Replicates are matched across cells and arms by seed; the two strengths are independent runs with their own decision files, and the report's conjunction rule was fixed with the user before submission.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The Phase 2 gate is resolved at the construction level. MOTCO now records four geometry checkpoints for every generated replicate, which separates exact construction, pooled preprocessing, finite sampling, and PLS projection:

population_native
        ↓ pooled observed-fitted block scaling
population_standardized
        ↓ finite-sample cell-mean error
observed_standardized
        ↓ fitted PLS projection
pls_latent

The generator modes are not required to form a perfectly diagonal mode-by-statistic matrix. Their revised contracts are:

  • Orientation is a pure coordinate relocation in native methylation M-space. The biological CpG→gene→protein cascade makes it a joint multi-omic program relocation with expected magnitude and shape co-movement.
  • Shape/relocate is a free biological bend. It changes the interior-stage program and may also change path length and principal orientation.
  • Shape/magnitude is an interior-stage amplitude perturbation and is intrinsically mixed; retain it as a stress-test construction, not a shape-specific positive control.
  • Magnitude/all is pure within native methylation but scales only one of three omic blocks, so joint standardization can introduce orientation and shape co-movement even though the established production test remains empirically specific.
  • Translation remains the negative geometry control: its exact population delta, angle, and shape stay at numerical zero before and after standardization.

These interpretations replace the assumption that requested mode alone identifies the realized pre-integration geometry. All subsequent operating-characteristic studies must report the realized checkpoint diagnostics alongside rejection rates.

docs.title: Small matched-seed characterization
docs.text:
This implementation check used two matched seeds and three effects. It is sufficient to validate the decomposition and locate construction cross-talk, but it is not a power study and its noisy observed/PLS values must not be treated as stable operating characteristics.

Parameters:

  • seeds: 0,1
  • effects: 0,0.5,1
  • n_samples=80, n_stages=4, p_dmp=0.2
  • PLS CV: one repeat, two inner and outer folds, at most three components
  • no permutations

docs.title: Orientation
docs.text:
Native methylation preserves equal path length and shape while rotating direction. At effects 0.5 and 1.0, its mean realized angles were 57.89° and 73.40°, with delta 0 and shape at numerical zero.

The cascade is the first source of cross-talk. At effect 0.5, native expression showed angle 64.99°, delta 1.12, and shape 0.066; native proteomics showed angle 59.32°, delta 1.36, and shape 0.037. Consequently, standardized joint population geometry was already mixed before sampling or PLS:

Effect Joint population angle Joint population delta Joint population shape 0.00 0.00° 0.00 0.000 0.50 67.41° 1.43 0.029 1.00 85.35° 1.78 0.052

The requested effect maps monotonically to the exact joint angle in this check. The nonzero joint delta and shape are construction/cascade behavior, not PLS leakage.

docs.title: Shape
docs.text:
Both constructions were mixed at the exact-population checkpoint.

For shape_kind=relocate, joint standardized population geometry increased as follows:

Effect Angle Delta Shape 0.00 0.00° 0.00 0.000 0.50 53.88° 1.97 0.050 1.00 85.45° 7.61 0.081

The relocation affects all three native omic layers through the cascade, confirming that it is a free multi-omic bend rather than an isolated Procrustes-shape intervention.

For shape_kind=magnitude, only native methylation changes because the binary cascade indicators remain unchanged. The interior-stage amplitude change nevertheless produces large angle and delta responses in that layer. Joint standardized population geometry was:

Effect Angle Delta Shape 0.00 0.00° 0.00 0.000 0.50 63.54° 4.99 0.064 1.00 75.26° 8.99 0.112

This construction is useful for sensitivity analysis but cannot support a claim of shape specificity.

docs.title: Controls and sampling
docs.text:
The exact none and translation checkpoints remained invariant. Observed standardized statistics were nonzero even for these controls because the two groups are independent finite samples. At n_samples=80, the PLS null angles were particularly unstable, so this run does not update the medium-pilot power conclusions.

Magnitude was pure in native methylation (effect 0.5/1.0 delta 31.97/63.94, angle and shape approximately zero) but became mixed in standardized joint population space (angle 13.56°/22.14°, shape 0.012/0.019). This occurs because methylation is scaled while expression and proteomics retain their baseline trajectories.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text:
Run from the repository root:

uv run python scripts/realized_geometry_characterization.py \
  --seeds 0,1 \
  --effects 0,0.5,1 \
  --n-samples 80 \
  --n-stages 4 \
  --pls-repeats 1 \
  --pls-cv1 2 \
  --pls-cv2 2 \
  --pls-max-components 3 \
  --out-dir /tmp/motco-phase2-small

The driver writes config.json, replicate-level JSONL, a long-form summary CSV, and a monotonicity CSV. For the medium pilot, use the roadmap sample size and effect grid with more matched seeds and the production PLS CV settings.

docs.title: Gate to Phase 3 and the medium pilot
docs.text: Phase 3 orientation-driver attribution can proceed using the revised interpretation: it should explain the joint molecular-program direction captured by PLS, not claim a pure methylation-only rotation. Before the medium pilot, retain all four checkpoint diagnostics and predeclare interpretation against realized geometry rather than requested mode labels alone.

docs.title: Split interaction test — findings report (2026-11-05)
docs.text:
Change: span-split-interaction-test (MOTCO 0.18.0). Reads: results/span-split-2026-11-05/ (span_split_decision.json, simulation/ and plasmode/ split, production, capture and trajectory tables, accounting.json, reproduction.json, settings.json, plasmode-fidelity/fidelity.json, PROVENANCE.txt, sacct.txt). Concept page: measurement visibility.

The latent-space comparison (report) found no measurement space that sees a group difference outside the fitted stage-PLS span without losing power on what the span already sees. This change asks the out-of-span question with its own test instead of a new space. motco.stats.interaction.interaction_split_test splits the group × stage interaction energy of the standardized features exactly into three parts:

  • span: the part inside the fitted span;
  • complement: the part in its orthogonal complement;
  • total: all of it.

Each part is tested by a trace pseudo-F under Freedman–Lane permutation of the reduced model's residuals, with RRPP's draws at the analysis's seed, against a basis that never sees the group labels and is never refitted.

In one paragraph. The split test is validated: split_validated. It holds size on three simulated designs and on the real SEA-AD blocks, and its complement part sees the out-of-span rotation that angle cannot.

  • Size holds everywhere. The 18 simulation control rates read 0.032–0.058 against a per-cell bound of 0.0695, with none above it. On real noise at the case study's configuration (six covariates, rank 5, 10,000 features) the three parts read 0.040, 0.050 and 0.012.
  • The complement sees the out-of-span rotation. A 45° rotation at φ = 90° is rejected in 1.00 (n = 200) and 0.68 (SEA-AD table) of replicates, where angle reads 0.08 and 0.10 on the same units.
  • The parts localize. As the rotation tilts out of the span, the span part's rate falls (1.00 → 0.52 at n = 200) and the complement's rises (0.35 → 1.00).
  • A sparse real-data plant is not seen. The plasmode's 20-feature plant on 10,000 features is rejected by no part above the null rate (0.02–0.05 at 2 and 3 within-stage SDs), as by angle (0.034–0.036). A complement non-rejection at SEA-AD is therefore uninformative about sparse differences of this size.
  • The ratio statistic is what holds size. The uncorrected interaction SS rejects the plasmode's null complement in 0.268 of replicates; the pseudo-F reads 0.012 on the same draws.

docs.title: 1. Configuration and provenance
docs.text:
• Simulation profile. The latent-space comparison's units: three designs (n200, seaad, seaad_weak at the calibrated δ = 0.11), fourteen cells and base seed 2035, imported from scripts/latent_space_comparison.py unchanged. The weak δ was read from the comparison's committed calibration, with its sha256 checked against the comparison's settings.
  • Replicates. The anchor and translation ran 500 replicates, every other cell 100 (the comparison's own units), all at 999 permutations: 6,600 units.
  • Each unit fits pls_cv once and evaluates it with net displacement, rank floor 2 and span capture. It then runs the split test on the fit's standardized features in the PLS input coordinates against qr(x_rotations_), at the unit's RRPP seed, uncorrected and under df.
  • Rejection is p < 0.05, the comparison's rule.
  • Plasmode profile. The SEA-AD plasmode's units: the astrocyte cohort_30 export through plasmode_check's contract, within-stage label permutation, the 20-feature plant (10 per block, at e within-stage SDs) and its seeds (base seed 2034, paper stream).
  • Cells: the anchor, e = 2.0 and e = 3.0 at 500 × 999, 1,500 units.
  • Each unit is one analyze_trajectories at the case study's configuration (six covariates, rank floor 2, net displacement, df) with attribution off and span_split_test on, plus an uncorrected rerun of the split test for the SS diagnostic.
  • Rejection is p ≤ 0.05, the plasmode's rule.
  • Code: b84d23c on feat/span-split-interaction-test, in a clean detached worktree on ing.
  • Cluster: partition 512x1024, arrays 934742 (simulation, 200 shards) and 934743 (plasmode, 150 shards), each throttled to 64 tasks. They ran on n1, n3 and n4 with n11 excluded and BLAS pinned to one thread. The fidelity gate passed on the cluster's export copy (rank 5, AUROC 0.635556; job 934741).
  • Pre-flight:
  • the fast suite (2,377 passed);
  • a local smoke of both profiles;
  • a timing run at 999 permutations;
  • a 1,200-unit local null check. A 40-replicate pre-check had suggested a liberal complement at CV ranks above K − 1; the larger check did not reproduce it, and the design was kept (notes).

Details are in PROVENANCE.txt and openspec/changes/archive/2026-11-05-span-split-interaction-test/notes.md.

docs.title: 2. Accounting and reproduction
docs.text:
• Units. 6,600/6,600 simulation and 1,500/1,500 plasmode units complete, 0 failed, 0 duplicates. All 350 array tasks, the fidelity job and the merge job COMPLETED 0:0 (sacct.txt). Every plasmode anchor unit reproduced the fidelity gate's latent space (rank 5, AUROC 0.635556).
  • Cost. 25.6 + 36.9 = 62.5 recorded core-hours (median 11.1 s per simulation unit and 80.0 s per plasmode unit), against a projection of 113.
  • Reproduction (the decision's gate), both passed:
  • Simulation: pls_cv's count and rejections from the first 199 of each unit's 999 draws equal the comparison's committed rate_table.csv in all 126 rows (3 designs × 14 cells × 3 statistics, replicates 0–99).
  • Plasmode: the delta/angle/shape rates equal the plasmode's committed plasmode_summary.csv in all 9 rows. The anchor reads 0.042 / 0.048 / 0.026, e = 2.0 reads 0.030 / 0.034 / 0.020 and e = 3.0 reads 0.026 / 0.036 / 0.016.
  • So every rate below pairs with the comparison's five arms and with the plasmode on the same datasets, fits and draws.
