docs.title: 4. Localization across alignment and modes
docs.text:
Pseudo-F rejection rate per part, total / span / complement (split_table.csv; 100 replicates per cell, SE ≤ 0.05):

cell n200 seaad magnitude e = 0.05 0.02 / 0.56 / 0.01 0.04 / 0.09 / 0.05 orientation e = 0.25, φ = 0 / 30 / 60 / 90 0.80 / 0.93 / 0.11; 0.63 / 0.81 / 0.22; 0.29 / 0.83 / 0.29; 0.19 / 0.02 / 0.29 0.12 / 0.45 / 0.07; 0.09 / 0.43 / 0.15; 0.08 / 0.49 / 0.27; 0.07 / 0.04 / 0.31 orientation e = 0.5, φ = 0 / 30 / 60 / 90 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.35; 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.78; 1.00 / 0.93 / 1.00; 1.00 / 0.52 / 1.00 0.99 / 0.99 / 0.32; 0.94 / 0.75 / 0.78; 0.66 / 0.41 / 0.72; 0.36 / 0.19 / 0.68 orientation e = 0.5, φ = 90, 20 features 0.90 / 0.79 / 0.78 0.16 / 0.36 / 0.58 shape e = 0.25 / 0.5 0.05 / 0.80 / 0.04; 0.16 / 0.72 / 0.06 0.04 / 0.39 / 0.07; 0.06 / 0.43 / 0.07
  • The parts follow the alignment. For the 45° rotation the span part falls from 1.00 to 0.52 (n = 200) and from 0.99 to 0.19 (SEA-AD table) as φ goes from 0° to 90°, and the complement rises from 0.35 to 1.00 and from 0.32 to 0.68. Magnitude and shape plants, which stay in the stage program, are rejected by the span part and not by the complement (0.01–0.07).
  • The complement also sees in-span plants, partly. At φ = 0 the 45° rotation is rejected by the complement in 0.35 / 0.32 of replicates. The plant keeps 0.97 / 0.93 of its energy in the fitted span (capture_table.csv), and the 3–7 % outside is enough at this size. Through the sample scaler, its rigid rotation also acquires off-span components (the unequal-scales route on the visibility page). A complement rejection therefore means energy outside the fitted span, not a difference outside the stage program (design D10).
  • The span part also sees the out-of-span rotation at n = 200 (0.52 at φ = 90). The production statistics register it there too: shape 0.51 and delta 0.20 on the same units, against angle 0.08. This is the sample-scaler route the comparison reported (§5 of its report).
  • Sparse support. At φ = 90 a 20-feature direction keeps 0.11–0.12 of its energy in the span, against 0.01–0.03 for the dense one. Its complement rate drops from 1.00 to 0.78 (n = 200) and from 0.68 to 0.58 (SEA-AD table), and its span rate rises (0.52 → 0.79 and 0.19 → 0.36).
  • The total part is the weakest for in-span plants (magnitude 0.02, shape 0.05–0.16 at n = 200), because their energy is diluted over all 498 coordinates. The split is what recovers the power: the span part reads 0.56–0.80 on the same plants.
  • At SEA-AD's stage signal (seaad_weak) no part has power for any plant (0.03–0.08), as for every arm of the comparison.

docs.title: 5. The in-span share against capture
docs.text:
Median observed in-span share of the interaction energy beside the median population capture of the planted difference (capture_table.csv):

cell n200 share / capture seaad share / capture seaad_weak share / capture anchor (null) 0.006 / — 0.062 / — 0.292 / — translation (null) 0.171 / — 0.215 / — 0.288 / — orientation e = 0.5, φ = 0 0.832 / 0.971 0.673 / 0.927 0.291 / 0.082 orientation e = 0.5, φ = 90 0.008 / 0.008 0.050 / 0.026 0.297 / 0.005 shape e = 0.5 0.325 / 0.968 0.235 / 0.932 0.312 / 0.095
  • At a strong stage signal the share tracks capture for large plants: 0.83 against 0.97 for the in-span rotation, 0.008 against 0.008 for the out-of-span one at n = 200. Smaller plants sit between their capture and the null share, because the noise's interaction energy is in the same sum.
  • The null share is not zero, and it depends on the fitted rank. The null cells' median shares are 0.006 (n200 anchor, median rank 2), 0.062 (seaad anchor), 0.17–0.22 (the translation cells, median rank 3) and 0.29 at the weak design; at the plasmode anchor (rank 5) it is 0.236 (plasmode/split_table.csv). The local null check split this by rank: a median 0.007 at rank 2 = K − 1 against 0.34 at higher ranks (notes).
  • Why the share is not zero: components beyond K − 1 follow the total covariance, where the noise's interaction energy also concentrates. The local null check found 0.01–0.03 for a basis of the pooled stage means (notes).
  • How to read it: an observed share must be read against the null share at the same rank and design, never against 0. At the weak design the share is the null share whatever the plant: the fitted span is mostly noise (pooled-stage capture 0.07–0.10).

docs.title: 6. The span part against the production statistics
docs.text:
On the units where both apply (production_table.csv), the span part is an omnibus test and the production statistics are targeted:

cell n200 span vs target seaad span vs target magnitude e = 0.05 (delta) 0.56 vs 0.74 0.09 vs 0.21 orientation e = 0.25, φ = 0 (angle) 0.93 vs 0.87 0.45 vs 0.47 shape e = 0.25 / 0.5 (shape) 0.80 / 0.72 vs 1.00 / 1.00 0.39 / 0.43 vs 0.70 / 0.94

The span part matches angle for in-span rotations and trails delta and shape. It does not replace the statistics: it says whether the groups differ inside the span, while delta, angle and shape say how.

docs.title: 7. The complement against the comparison's arms
docs.text:
The comparison's committed angle rates on the same datasets (100 × 199; latent-space-comparison-2026-11-04/rate_table.csv) beside the complement part:

cell n200 complement / concat / pls_cv seaad complement / concat / pls_cv seaad_weak complement / concat / pls_cv anchor 0.03 / 0.05 / 0.04 0.04 / 0.06 / 0.04 0.05 / 0.21 / 0.02 translation 0.05 / 0.05 / 0.04 0.05 / 0.06 / 0.06 0.06 / 0.22 / 0.02 orientation e = 0.5, φ = 90 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.08 0.68 / 0.90 / 0.11 0.07 / 0.23 / 0.01 orientation e = 0.5, φ = 90, 20 features 0.78 / 0.98 / 0.06 0.58 / 0.49 / 0.09 0.06 / 0.26 / 0.01
  • The complement reaches most of concat's out-of-span power and holds size where concat did not. At the weak design concat's angle is liberal (0.21–0.26 in every cell); the complement reads 0.05–0.08 there.
  • On the SEA-AD table concat is more powerful for the dense rotation (0.90 against 0.68). For the sparse one the complement is (0.58 against 0.49).
  • Different questions. concat's angle tests orientation in all coordinates; the complement tests any group × stage difference outside the fitted span, with no geometry.

docs.title: 8. Real noise: the plasmode
docs.text:
cell total span complement delta / angle / shape anchor 0.040 0.050 0.012 0.042 / 0.048 / 0.026 e = 2.0 0.042 0.046 0.022 0.030 / 0.034 / 0.020 e = 3.0 0.042 0.048 0.018 0.026 / 0.036 / 0.016
  • Size holds on real noise at the case study's configuration. The complement is conservative there (6/500), in 9,995 dimensions with six covariates.
  • There is no power for the sparse plant. A shift of 2–3 within-stage SDs on 20 of 10,000 features is rejected by no part above the null rate. The plant keeps a median 2.2 % of its norm in the rank-5 span, the random-direction share (results/plasmode-2026-11-02/diagnostic/latent_capture.json), so it is an out-of-span difference. Its energy is a small fraction of the complement's 9,995 coordinates of noise, and an energy test does not find it. This is design risk R1, and thread 3 (a sparse per-feature scan) is the targeted follow-up.
  • For the case study: a complement non-rejection on SEA-AD says nothing about sparse differences of this size. It is informative only about differences with substantial energy outside the span, like the simulation's dense rotation.

docs.title: 9. The SS diagnostic
docs.text:
Null rejection rates of the uncorrected interaction SS (ss), the interaction SS under df (ss_df) and the pseudo-F (f), at the controls:

profile, cell part f ss ss_df simulation seaad, translation complement 0.052 0.068 0.040 simulation seaad_weak, anchor complement 0.050 0.082 0.038 simulation seaad_weak, translation complement 0.058 0.098 0.048 plasmode anchor total 0.040 0.114 0.040 plasmode anchor span 0.050 0.074 0.048 plasmode anchor complement 0.012 0.268 0.006

D1 predicted this pattern: - Why the uncorrected SS is liberal. The Freedman–Lane residuals are too narrow by √((n − r)/n), and an energy summed over many coordinates concentrates. So the uncorrected SS is liberal in proportion to dimension: 0.268 in the plasmode's 9,995-dimensional complement, 0.068–0.098 in the simulation's 495-dimensional one, and near α in the span. - What corrects it. Rescaling by κ removes the excess (0.006–0.048), and the pseudo-F never had it. This bears on why the analysis's RRPP needs the df correction at the case study's configuration. It does not test why concat's angle was liberal at the weak design, which is a different statistic.

docs.title: 10. What follows
docs.text:
• The split test may be used by a case study under split_validated, with the reading on the measurement visibility page:
  • span = the fitted span;
  • a complement rejection = energy outside it, including the fitted span's misses of the true program;
  • a non-rejection uninformative without power at the design;
  • the share read against the null share.
  • Applying it to SEA-AD is sead_sexdiff's change. It pins MOTCO 0.18.0 and fixes its multiplicity policy over the three parts before any real-label analysis (design open question).
  • Thread 2 (a group-aware space refitted per permutation) now has a benchmark to beat: the complement's 1.00 / 0.68 for the dense out-of-span rotation at size.
  • Thread 3 (a sparse per-feature interaction scan) is the follow-up the plasmode result asks for.

docs.title: 11. Limitations
docs.text:
• The power cells are at R = 100 (SE ≤ 0.05). C3's margins (0.92 and 0.58 against thresholds of 0.054 and 0.111) do not depend on that.
  • Stage-span plants are relative to the configuration. At the weak design they are as weak as the stage program, so its zero power is descriptive. Absolute-scale plants on real noise are the plasmode's, and they are sparse.
  • The plasmode measures one kind of difference (20 features, a monotone stage weight). Dense or moderately sparse real-data differences were not planted.
  • The production angle at the seaad design reads 0.072 (anchor) and 0.070 (translation) at 500 replicates, just above its per-cell bound of 0.0695. This change does not judge that statistic. The two cells share their null datasets, and the comparison read 0.04 / 0.06 there at R = 100.
  • The null in-span share depends on the fitted rank (§5). The share is a descriptive location measure, not a test, and it needs the null reference to be read.

docs.title: Stage-span paper grade — findings report (2026-11-04)
docs.text:
Change: stage-span-paper-grade (MOTCO 0.17.0). Reads: results/stage-span-paper-grade-2026-11-04/. It holds:

  • report/ for each of the three profiles;
  • stage_span_paper_grade_decision.json;
  • leak/, the pre-flight arms and preflight_gate.json;
  • reproduction/, PROVENANCE.txt and sacct.txt.

Concept page: measurement visibility.

The stage-span pilot showed that angle and shape are sensitive once a group difference lies inside the stage-supervised span, but only at pilot grade (100 × 199). It also left the bend's delta leak unexplained. This run states sensitivity given visibility at paper grade (500 × 999) at five columns, with a construction whose leaks are measured.

In one paragraph. The predeclared decision is sensitivity_established.

  • Size. The anchors and the stage-span translation control hold size at every column: 0 of 60 rates above the 0.0695 bound.
  • Capture. Every stage-span plant keeps 0.92–0.97 of its energy in the fitted span. The surgeries keep 0.2–0.8 % at e = 0.5 at the same columns.
  • Power given visibility. A 45° stage-span rotation rejects angle in 0.96–1.00 of replicates and a half-step bend rejects shape in 0.97–1.00, at every column including n = 80 and the SEA-AD table. The surgeries reach 0.08–0.67 at the same effect.
  • Specificity. 3 of 90 off-target rates are above the per-cell bound. The bound rule allows 6, and none is above the Bonferroni ceiling.
  • The planted scale. It solves each edit as a fixed point so that it is exact where the sample scaler looks. That removes the bend's delta leak, now 0.016–0.036.
  • The residual. What remains is the PLS score metric, a sheared map of the span: −0.48 % of A's path on the SEA-AD table and −0.59 % at four stages, for the bend at e = 0.5. It is now documented (measurement visibility, roadmap item 15).
  • Two qualifications.
  • The rotation's off-target shape rises with the angle, reaching 0.086 at four stages at 45°: exactly at that cell's ceiling.
  • 12 of the 1,000 four-stage orientation units have no planted plant and were reported as failures.

docs.title: 1. Configuration and provenance
docs.text:

The five columns, each measured on its span layers:

  • n = 200 (the baseline) and n = 80, at three stages on methylation + expression;
  • the SEA-AD table [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]] on methylation + expression;
  • n = 200 on all three blocks;
  • n = 200 at four stages on methylation + expression.

Shared settings:

  • 500 replicates × 999 permutations; base_seed 1028 in the design-guidance family; evaluation.seed 3, which is also the RRPP seed.
  • The design-guidance generator: p_dmp 0.1, ρ = 0, every per-omic δ 2.0, joint magnitude.
  • The production measurement: pooled PLS with the double-CV rank floored at 2, net_displacement, span_capture on.
  • Code: revision e41c1ae in a clean detached worktree on ing, partition 512x1024 (n1, n3, n4; n2 and n11 excluded, reasons in PROVENANCE.txt), one CPU and 4 GB per task, BLAS pinned to one thread.

Pre-flight before submission:

  • the change's suites (258 passed);
  • a 2 × 19 smoke of all three profiles (192/192 units);
  • 32 random units timed at 999 permutations (mean 17.3 s, about 230 core-hours projected).

Order of work (user decision). The workstation had to shut down before the leak-decomposition script existed. The user chose to submit the paper grade that night under a pre-approved cap of 450 projected core-hours. The leak check and its gate, which the design placed before the paper grade, ran the next morning as a descriptive companion (§6). Its gate holds, so the reordering changed nothing that would have stopped the run. The decision script was committed (cbd3e57) before any rate was read.

docs.title: 2. Unit, failure and reproduction accounting
docs.text:
Units. All 480 array tasks finished COMPLETED 0:0 (22:25–01:13). There are 48,000 records, 48,000 distinct, with no duplicates and 229.0 recorded core-hours (160.9 / 38.1 / 30.0). Every completed record carries net_displacement, min_components 2, n_jobs 1 and span_capture true.

Failures. 12 units failed, all in stage-span orientation at n = 200 / four stages: replicates 311, 409 and 481 at e = 0.25, and 123, 266, 311, 368, 409, 425, 439, 477 and 481 at e = 0.5.

  • Cause. The planted fixed point did not converge: the planted pooled SD cycled in two steps after 200 updates.
  • Diagnosis. In those datasets the configuration with the net displacement removed has two nearly tied singular values (ratio 0.95–0.97, against 0.86 in a replicate that converges). The rotation's second direction is chosen from those two, so it swings with the scale.
  • No cheap fix. Damping the iteration by half-steps rescued 2 of the 12, so the other 10 most likely have no consistent planted plant.
  • Determinism. A local scan of all 1,000 units of the two cells finds exactly these 12.

The user chose to report them as failures, as the design's risk entry anticipated. The two cells' rates use the completed replicates (R = 497 and 491), and every other cell is complete. The failures select against near-tied configurations, so those two cells describe configurations with a well-defined rotation plane.

Reproduction. Run on ing with scripts/anchor_reproduction.py, from reproduction/:

comparison pairs match stage-span magnitude vs geometry anchors (5 columns, --by-column) 2,500 2,499 (seeds, ranks, p-values 2,500) surgery vs stage-span geometry anchors (2 columns) 1,000 1,000 anchors vs the 2026-10-29 slice (n = 200, n = 80, three blocks; 999 permutations both) 1,500 1,499 (p-values 1,500) SEA-AD surgery cells vs the stage-span pilot, replicates 0–99 1,000 1,000 (p-values not comparable) four-stage surgery cells vs the design-guidance pilot, replicates 0–99 1,000 1,000 (p-values not comparable) planted magnitude vs the pilot's stage-span magnitude (n = 200, n = 80, SEA-AD), replicates 0–99 1,200 1,200

Both misses are one anchor dataset (replicate 222 at n = 200), whose observed angle is 0.00019°. It differs by 1.9e-9° between runs, at the limit of the arccos precision near zero, and its p-value is 1.0 everywhere. The planted magnitude cells reproduce the null-scale pilot because scaling about the centroid gives the same plant under either scale.

docs.title: 3. The decision
docs.text:
stage_span_paper_grade_decision.json, rule version 1. Bound rule. For each criterion over m rates:

  • A rate exceeds when it is above α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/R), with R the row's available replicates.
  • The criterion fails if the number of exceedances passes the 95th percentile of Binomial(m, p₂), where p₂ is the exact probability that a Binomial(R, α)/R rate exceeds that bound.
  • It also fails if any rate is above the Bonferroni ceiling at 0.05/m, or if any row is unavailable.

At R = 500, p₂ = 0.0303.

criterion what m allowed observed ceiling holds P1 size anchor (5 columns × 3 statistics) and stage-span translation (5 × 3 effects × 3) 60 4 0 0.084 yes P2 capture median group_difference ≥ 0.90 in every stage-span magnitude, orientation and shape cell 45 cells — 0 below — yes P3 specificity off-target statistics of those cells 90 6 3 0.084 yes

Verdict: sensitivity_established. The three exceedances are listed in §8.

docs.text:
Median group_difference share per cell, with its q10–q90 range across the column's cells:

The bend's shape reads within 0.004, and the scaling's delta within 2.8 % (the population_latent columns of the decision's target_power_and_capture).

Anchor and stage-span translation rejection rates (500 replicates; bound 0.0695):

docs.title: 6. The leak decomposition
docs.text:
scripts/stage_span_leak_check.py ran two arms at 100 × 199 on the five columns (jobs 934447 and 934448, revision b40fb91; 3,500 units each, 0 failed, 32.0 core-hours). It covered the anchor, orientation and shape, under planted at e ∈ {0.1, 0.25, 0.5} and under null at {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}. The null arm reproduces the stage-span pilot's rejection counts at its three columns (63 of 63).

For each unit the check reports B's path length minus A's at six checkpoints. The table gives the median for the bend at e = 0.5, as a share of A's path:

Reading the routes:

  • The scale route. Under the null scale the bend keeps its path length in the null coordinates it is defined in. The planted data's own pooled SD shortens it by 0.65–1.06 %, and the sample scaler sees the same. The planted plant is exact there in every unit (G1), and the scaler follows it.
  • The score-metric route. On an orthonormal basis of the fitted span the planted bend keeps its length to within 0.11 %. In the PLS score coordinates it does not on the SEA-AD table (−0.48 %) or at four stages (−0.59 %).
  • The rotation shows the shear more strongly. The planted 45° rotation on the SEA-AD table reads −3.35 % in scores against +0.66 % on the orthonormal basis.
  • Size is unaffected by either route (§5).

Rates. Under the null scale the bend's delta rate at R = 100 is 0.08 at n = 200 and 0.11 on three blocks at e = 0.5. At e = 1.0 it is 0.17 at n = 200 and 0.33 at four stages. Under the planted scale it is 0.00–0.04 at every column and effect.

Pre-flight gate. preflight_gate.json reads gate_holds:

  • G1. Every planted unit generated, with a planted-scale gap ≤ 1e-8 of A's path.
  • G2. 0 of 60 planted off-target rates above the R = 100 bound (allowed 4, ceiling 0.130).
  • G3. The planted arm's median score-coordinate difference is smaller than the null arm's at every column (−0.28 → +0.01, −0.29 → −0.01, −0.36 → −0.16, −0.35 → +0.05, −0.92 → −0.33, in A's path units).

The gate ran after the paper grade (§1), so it is a diagnostic here, not a condition the run waited on.

docs.text:
Off-target rejection rates of the stage-span cells (500 replicates; bound 0.0695, ceiling 0.084 at R = 500):

The three exceedances (bold) are:

The plant keeps shape exactly in the planted coordinates, so the leak enters through the measurement. The surgeries' low power measures visibility, not the tests.

docs.title: 10. Limitations
docs.text:
• The construction is circular by design. It plants where the measurement looks, so it measures sensitivity given visibility. How much of a real difference the span sees is the latent plasmode's question (roadmap item 13 (b)).
  • The paper grade ran before its pre-flight, on the user's decision. The gate held when it ran (§6), and the decision rule was committed before any rate was read.
  • Excluded configurations. 12 four-stage orientation units have no planted plant (near-tied in-plane directions). The two cells read over 497 and 491 replicates and describe configurations with a well-defined rotation plane.
  • The score-coordinate residual remains. It is −0.48 % and −0.59 % of A's path for the bend at e = 0.5 on the SEA-AD table and at four stages, and −3.35 % for the 45° rotation on the table. It did not produce a delta leak at these effects. Removing it would mean measuring on orthonormal span coordinates, which changes the production measurement and is unvalidated (roadmap item 15).
  • The rotation's off-target shape is at the per-cell bound at 45°, and sits at the ceiling at four stages. Larger stage-span rotations were a non-goal and were not run; they would likely fail P3.
  • The count rule assumes independent rates. Rates within a column share matched-seed noise, so exceedances can cluster (n = 200 reads 0.05–0.06 on every angle cell). Every exceeding row is listed.
  • The surgeries' capture is measured only at pilot grade at n = 200 and n = 80, and not at all on three blocks.
  • Simulator scope. The structural-analogue limitation applies: InterSIM blocks, 498 measured features, ρ = 0.

docs.title: Stage-span pilot — findings report (2026-11-04)
docs.text:
Change: stage-span-constructions (MOTCO 0.15.0). Reads: results/stage-span-pilot-2026-11-04/ (report/ per profile, stage_span_pilot_reading.json, retrofit/, reproduction/, PROVENANCE.txt, sacct.txt). Concept page: measurement visibility.

The production measurement sees a group difference only through its component inside the stage-supervised PLS span (measurement visibility). The simulator's power curves therefore mixed two questions: how much of a planted difference the measurement can see, and how sensitive the test is to what it sees. This pilot separates them. It pairs the feature-set surgeries with a new stage-span construction, which plants group B's difference inside the span of B's own stage configuration, on the same baseline programs and noise. Every replicate records how much of the population difference the fitted basis sees (span_capture). The design is four sibling profiles: {surgery, stage-span} × {magnitude, geometry} at 100 replicates × 199 permutations. Each has three columns at three stages on methylation + expression: n = 200 (baseline), n = 80, and the SEA-AD table [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]]. All four run in the design-guidance seed family, so the surgery siblings reproduce the 2026-10-28 pilot cell for cell.

In one paragraph. Visibility, not sensitivity, limits the surgeries.

  • Capture. The orientation and shape surgeries keep 0.2–1.1 % of their population difference's energy inside the fitted span. That is the share a random direction keeps (rank / 498 = 0.4–0.6 %). The one exception is the full relocation on the unequal SEA-AD table (21.5 %, the "kite" route). The stage-span plants keep 85–97 %. Both magnitude constructions keep 93–97 %.
  • Power given visibility. At e = 0.5 the stage-span orientation (a 45° rotation) rejects angle in 0.95–1.00 of replicates and the stage-span bend rejects shape in 0.98–1.00, at every column including n = 80. The surgeries reach 0.06–0.22 and 0.11–0.40 at the same effect. Seen through the fitted basis, the surgery's full relocation is 4.4° at n = 200, against a population 90°; the stage-span 90° rotation is 90.4°.
  • Magnitude. The two magnitude constructions give the same power to ±0.01 (pooled SE 0.02–0.07).
  • Reading. The predeclared reading returns revise_construction. Its failures sit at e = 1.0: the 90° rotation's capture falls to 0.85 at n = 80, and the full-strength bend leaks into delta (0.17 at n = 200). One further failure is a 0.10 angle reading at n = 200. That reading is inherited from those 100 replicates' shared noise: the shared anchor and every non-angle cell at that column read 0.07–0.10 under both constructions.
  • Proposal. The follow-up should cap the stage-span geometry effects at e ≤ 0.5. Below that every criterion except that inherited reading holds, and the paper grade's 500 replicates should settle it.

docs.title: 2. Unit, failure and reproduction accounting
docs.text:
• Units. 9,200/9,200 records over 92 cells: no duplicates, no failed records, and all 48 array tasks COMPLETED 0:0 (sacct.txt). Every record carries orientation_estimator net displacement, min_components 2, n_jobs 1, span_capture true and the population_latent checkpoint. The run used 45.5 recorded core-hours (median 16.9 s per unit) against a projection of 66.
  • Sibling anchors (reproduction/siblings_*, --by-column). The stage-span profiles' anchors are the surgery profiles' anchor cells, because every zero-effect cell clears the construction. All three comparisons against the surgery geometry anchor pair 300/300 (column, replicate) records with identical seeds, ranks, statistics and p-values.
  • The design-guidance pilot (reproduction/surgery_*_vs_design_guidance_pilot*, --by-cell). This check projects onto n_samples and filters the pilot to three stages and two blocks. The surgery siblings reproduce the 2026-10-28 pilot at every shared cell: 800/800 magnitude pairs (8 cells) and 2,000/2,000 geometry pairs (20 cells), with identical seeds, ranks, statistics and p-values. Span capture changed no statistic. The pilot's other columns and effects are listed with zero pairs.

docs.title: 3. Visibility: how much of each plant the fitted span sees
docs.text:
Median group_difference share over 100 replicates: the share of Σ_s‖d_s‖² inside the fitted span, with d_s the population B − A difference at stage s minus its stage mean. These are energy shares. A random direction keeps rank / 498 = 0.004 at rank 2 and 0.006 at rank 3 (report/span_capture.csv).

  • The surgeries are invisible. The orientation surgery relocates stage-changing CpGs, and the shape surgery relocates one stage's. Both put their difference on features the pooled stage program does not use, so it lands outside the span at the random-direction share. The exception is the full relocation on the SEA-AD table (0.215, median rank 4): with unequal cells the pooled means are weighted and the rhombus becomes a kite.
  • The stage-span plants lie in the population span by construction, and the fitted span keeps 85–97 % of them. Capture falls with n (0.97 at n = 200, 0.93 at n = 80) and with the size of the rotation: a 90° rotation moves B's configuration furthest from the pooled stage means the basis is fitted to.
  • Magnitude scales the shared program, so both constructions sit inside the span (0.93–0.97). They are the same plant up to the cascade's per-feature pattern.
  • Pooled stage means keep 0.97 (n = 200) and 0.93–0.94 (n = 80, SEA-AD) of their energy in the span under every construction. Translation has no stage-varying difference, so its group_difference share is null in every replicate.

Seen through the fitted basis (population_latent, median target statistic). The stage-span rotation reads 22.0–22.5° / 43.7–45.3° / 86.2–90.4° against an intended 22.5° / 45° / 90°. The stage-span bend reads shape 0.125–0.126 / 0.221–0.224 / 0.359–0.365 against an intended 0.125–0.126 / 0.218–0.221 / 0.346–0.351. The surgery's relocation reads 1.1–1.9° at e = 0.25 and 2.0–3.8° at e = 0.5 at every column. At e = 1.0 it reads 4.4–4.8° at the balanced columns and 53.8° on the SEA-AD table. Its population angle is arccos(1 − e) in the methylation block: 41°, 60° and 90° (orientation probe §1).

The surgeries' orientation power is flat or non-monotone in e at the balanced columns (0.17 / 0.22 / 0.12 at n = 200), the pattern the design-guidance pilot recorded. docs.title: 5. Specificity: the stage-span modes move their target, the surgeries a mix
docs.text:
Off-target rates (same tables):

  • Stage-span orientation leaves delta at 0.00 and shape at 0.00–0.07 at every column and effect.
  • Stage-span shape leaves angle at 0.04–0.12 and delta at 0.00–0.08, except at e = 1.0 and n = 200, where delta reads 0.17. The full-strength bend (rescale factor ≈ 0.5) adds enough between-cell variance that the sample scaler departs from the null population scale, so the sample path length moves.
  • Stage-span magnitude moves only delta: angle 0.03–0.09 and shape 0.01–0.05, the same as the surgery's.
  • The surgeries register as a mix, as measurement visibility explains. The full relocation at n = 200 rejects delta 0.22, angle 0.12 and shape 0.21. On the SEA-AD table it rejects 0.31 / 0.67 / 0.52. The full shape surgery is detected more often by delta than by shape: 0.63 against 0.55 at n = 200, and 0.36 against 0.17 on the SEA-AD table.

docs.title: 6. Size
docs.text:
The shared anchor (anchor_decision.json, identical in all four reports, bound 0.0936 at R = 100) reads delta / angle / shape:

anchor_decision reads excess at n = 200 on angle in every profile, because it is the same cell evaluated on the same datasets. These are the design-guidance pilot's baseline anchor datasets at replicates 0–99: the pilot recorded the same 0.10 as one of its two chance-level excesses, and the reproduction above confirms identical p-values. The independent Type I-phase draw at n = 200 (type_i_table.csv, the same cell in all four profiles) reads 0.02 / 0.02 / 0.01. The paper-grade slice held the bound at this column at R = 500 (anchor ≤ 0.062).

At n = 200, every cell that does not target angle reads it at 0.07–0.10 under both constructions. That covers magnitude (0.09 at every effect), translation (0.05–0.10) and stage-span shape (0.09). Those cells share the anchor's noise stream at each replicate index, so an angle reading near the bound at this column is a property of these 100 replicates, not of a construction.

docs.title: 7. The reading
docs.text:
stage_span_pilot_reading.json (rule version 1, bound α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/R) = 0.0936 at R = 100) returns revise_construction:

criterion observations failures R1: stage-span translation at or below the bound, every column, effect and statistic 27 1: n = 200, e = 0.25, angle 0.10 R2: median group_difference ≥ 0.90 in every stage-span magnitude, orientation and shape cell 27 2: orientation e = 1.0 at n = 80 (0.849) and SEA-AD (0.850) R3: off-target rates at or below the bound in those cells 54 3: shape e = 1.0 delta 0.17 (n = 200), angle 0.12 (n = 80) and 0.10 (SEA-AD)

How to read the failures:

  • R2's two failures and R3's delta 0.17 are real properties of the largest effects. A 90° rotation moves B's configuration away from the pooled stage means the basis is fitted to, and capture falls to 0.85 at n = 80. The full-strength bend's between-cell variance shifts the sample scale enough to move delta (§5).
  • R1's failure and R3's two angle readings at 0.10–0.12 are at chance level. At R = 100, each rate exceeds the bound with probability 0.028 when its true value is α, so 2.3 of R1's and R3's 81 bound tests are expected to exceed by chance. R1's failure sits at the n = 200 column, whose angle reads 0.07–0.10 in every non-target cell (§6).
  • Restricted to e ≤ 0.5:
  • R2 holds at every column (capture ≥ 0.924).
  • R3 holds at every column (the largest off-target rate is 0.09, stage-span shape angle at n = 200).
  • R1's only failure is the inherited n = 200 reading.

Descriptive tables in the reading: target power and capture for both constructions (§3–§4), the magnitude delta difference with its pooled SE (§4), and each profile's anchor size as read (§6).

docs.title: 8. Latent retrofit check
docs.text:
retrofit/ (scripts/latent_retrofit_check.py, the n = 200 column, replicates 0–9, 199 permutations): each replicate's own fitted basis, B's latent stage means edited by a 25 % scaling, a 30° rotation, a half-step bend and a half-step offset, each pulled back by the loadings and the minimum-norm preimage.

  • Frozen basis: every edit is recovered to 7.8 × 10⁻¹⁴ in the latent coordinates.
  • Refit from scratch: each edit is detected in its own statistic in 10/10 replicates (delta, angle, shape for magnitude, orientation, shape) and in no other (0/10). The offset is detected in no statistic, except shape in 1/10. Median ranks are 2 at the null fit and 2–3 at the refit.
  • Footprints: 105–170 effective features, 96–97 % of the energy on the truth's stage-active features, 63–67 % on methylation.
  • Agreement with the population plant: each footprint has cosine 0.965–0.984 with the stage-span construction's population plant for the same mode on the same replicate. The loadings preimage is the lower of the two in every mode.

A basis-defined plant and the population-defined plant the construction uses nearly coincide. The circular alternative (design D1, planting in each replicate's own basis) would therefore have bought little, and it would have aligned the plant with that replicate's noise.

docs.title: 9. Proposed paper-grade effect grid, and the revision
docs.text:
The reading is advisory, and the decision belongs to the follow-up change. The evidence supports one revision and one grid:

  • Revision. Cap the stage-span geometry effects at e ≤ 0.5: rotations of at most 45° and bends of at most half a mean step. This is where R2 and R3 hold at every column. The e = 1.0 failures are the construction leaving the regime it was built for. They are not evidence against the measurement, and the paper should not quote the stage-span 90° rotation as a clean orientation-only plant at n ≤ 80.
  • Grid.
  • Stage-span orientation and shape at e ∈ {0.1, 0.25, 0.5}: e = 0.5 already saturates at n ≥ 80, and the informative range is below it.
  • Stage-span translation at {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}, as the control.
  • magnitude at {0.02, 0.05, 0.1} under one construction only: the two are equivalent here.
  • Surgery siblings at the slice's {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}, as the visibility contrast.
  • All at 500 × 999 in the same seed family, so that the n = 200 angle reading near the bound is measured at R = 500 (bound 0.0695), where the slice already held size at that column.
  • Columns. The pilot's three, plus the three-block and four-stage columns the proposal names, to see how capture moves with the span's dimension.

The latent plasmode on the SEA-AD export (a stage-span plant on real noise, which needs a split-sample basis because real data has no population means) is a separate change. So is the paper-grade decision.

docs.title: 10. Limitations
docs.text:
• Pilot grade. At R = 100, rates near the bound are not resolved (SE 0.022 at α). The n = 200 column's datasets carry an angle excess that the slice did not reproduce at R = 500.
  • The stage-span construction is circular by design. It plants where the measurement looks. R2 is a premise check, not a finding, and the construction answers sensitivity given visibility, not how visible a biological difference is. It also bypasses the methylation → expression → protein cascade; the surgeries remain the biologically grounded constructions.
  • One generator regime. These results are at δ = 2.0, three stages, two blocks and ρ = 0. The design-guidance arm showed that a weaker stage signal inflates the CV rank, and a larger span may capture more of the surgeries.
  • The SEA-AD column is the case-study table under the design-guidance generator, not the case-study configuration (no covariates, saturated stage signal).
